headers.toc1: The First Book of Moses, called Genesis
headers.mt1: The First Book of Moses, called Genesis

verses.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.

And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness \add was\add*
upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face
of the waters.
And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.

And God saw the light, that \add it was\add* good: and God
divided the light from the darkness.\f + \fr 1.4  \ft the light from…: Heb. between the light and between the
darkness\f*

And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night.
And the evening and the morning were the first day.\f + \fr 1.5 
\ft And the evening…: Heb. And the evening was, and the morning was
etc.\f*

And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the
waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.\f + \fr 1.6 
\ft firmament: Heb. expansion\f*

And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which \add were\add*
under the firmament from the waters which \add were\add* above the
firmament: and it was so.

And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the
morning were the second day.\f + \fr 1.8  \ft And the evening…: Heb. And the evening was, and the morning was
etc.\f*

And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered
together unto one place, and let the dry \add land\add* appear: and it was so.

And God called the dry \add land\add* Earth; and the gathering
together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that \add it was\add*
good.

And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding
seed, \add and\add* the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind,
whose seed \add is\add* in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.\f + \fr 1.11 
\ft grass: Heb. tender grass\f*

And the earth brought forth grass, \add and\add* herb yielding
seed after his kind, and the tree yielding  fruit, whose seed \add was\add*
in itself, after his kind: and God saw that \add it was\add* good.

And the evening and the morning were the third day.\f + \fr 1.13 
\ft And the evening…: Heb. And the evening was, and the morning was
etc.\f*

And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the
heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs,
and for seasons, and for days, and years:\f + \fr 1.14  \ft the day…: Heb. between the day and between the
night\f*

And let them be for lights in the firmament of the heaven
to give light upon the earth: and it was so.

And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the
day, and the lesser light to rule the night: \add he made\add* the
stars also.\f + \fr 1.16  \ft to rule the day…: Heb. for the rule of the day,
etc.\f*

And God set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light
upon the earth,

And to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide
the light from the darkness: and God saw that \add it was\add* good.

And the evening and the morning were the fourth day.\f + \fr 1.19 
\ft And the evening…: Heb. And the evening was, and the morning was
etc.\f*

And God said, Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving
creature that hath life, and fowl \add that\add* may fly above the
earth in the open firmament of heaven.\f + \fr 1.20  \ft moving: or,
creeping\f*\f + \fr 1.20  \ft life: Heb. soul\f*\f + \fr 1.20  \ft fowl…: Heb. let fowl
fly\f*\f + \fr 1.20  \ft open…: Heb. face of the firmament of heaven\f*

And God created great whales, and every living creature that
moveth, which the waters brought forth abundantly, after their kind,
and every winged fowl after his kind: and God saw that \add it was\add*
good.

And God blessed them, saying, Be fruitful, and multiply, and
fill the waters in the seas, and let fowl multiply  in the earth.

And the evening and the morning were the fifth day.\f + \fr 1.23 
\ft And the evening…: Heb. And the evening was, and the morning was
etc.\f*

And God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature
after his kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth
after his kind: and it was so.

And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle
after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his
kind: and God saw that \add it was\add* good.

And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness:
and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the
fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping
thing that creepeth upon the earth.

So God created man in his \add own\add* image, in the image
of God created he him; male and female created he them.

And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful,
and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion
over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living
thing that moveth upon the earth.\f + \fr 1.28  \ft moveth: Heb.
creepeth\f*

And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb bearing
 seed, which \add is\add* upon the face of all the earth, and every
tree, in the which \add is\add* the fruit of a tree yielding seed;
to you it shall be for meat.\f + \fr 1.29  \ft bearing…: Heb. seeding
seed\f*\f + \fr 1.29  \ft yielding…: Heb. seeding seed\f*

And to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the
air, and to every thing that creepeth upon the earth, wherein \add there
is\add* life, \add I have given\add* every green herb for meat: and it was
so.\f + \fr 1.30  \ft life: Heb. a living soul\f*

And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, \add it
was\add* very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth
day.\f + \fr 1.31  \ft And the evening…: Heb. And the evening was, and the morning was
etc.\f*

Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of
them.

And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made;
and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.

And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because
that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and
made.\f + \fr 2.3  \ft created…: Heb. created to make\f*

These \add are\add* the generations of the heavens and of the
earth when they were created, in the day that the \nd LORD\nd* God
made the earth and the heavens,

And every plant of the field before it was in the earth, and every
herb of the field before it grew: for the \nd LORD\nd* God had not
caused it to rain upon the earth, and \add there was\add* not a man
to till the ground.

But there went up a mist from the earth, and watered the whole
face of the ground.\f + \fr 2.6  \ft there…: or, a mist which went up from,
etc.\f*

And the \nd LORD\nd* God formed man \add of\add* the dust of
the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and
man became a living soul.\f + \fr 2.7  \ft of the dust…: Heb. dust of the
ground\f*

And the \nd LORD\nd* God planted a garden eastward in Eden;
and there he put the man whom he had formed.

And out of the ground made the \nd LORD\nd* God to grow every
tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of
life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of
good and evil.

And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was
parted, and became into four heads.

And the gold of that land \add is\add* good: there \add is\add*
bdellium and the onyx stone.

And the name of the second river \add is\add* Gihon: the same
\add is\add* it that compasseth the whole land of Ethiopia.\f + \fr 2.13 
\ft Ethiopia: Heb. Cush\f*

And the name of the third river \add is\add* Hiddekel: that
\add is\add* it which goeth toward the east of Assyria. And the fourth
river \add is\add* Euphrates.\f + \fr 2.14  \ft toward…: or, eastward to
Assyria\f*

And the \nd LORD\nd* God took the man, and put him into the
garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.\f + \fr 2.15  \ft the man: or,
Adam\f*

And the \nd LORD\nd* God commanded the man, saying, Of every
tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:\f + \fr 2.16  \ft thou…: Heb. eating thou shalt
eat\f*

But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not
eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely
die.\f + \fr 2.17  \ft thou shalt surely…: Heb. dying thou shalt
die\f*

And the \nd LORD\nd* God said, \add It is\add* not good that the
man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.\f + \fr 2.18 
\ft meet…: Heb. as before him\f*

And out of the ground the \nd LORD\nd* God formed every beast
of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought \add them\add*
unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called
every living creature, that \add was\add* the name thereof.\f + \fr 2.19 
\ft Adam: or, the man\f*

And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the
air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not
found an help meet for him.\f + \fr 2.20  \ft gave: Heb. called\f*

And the rib, which the \nd LORD\nd* God had taken from man,
made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.\f + \fr 2.22  \ft made: Heb.
builded\f*

And Adam said, This \add is\add* now bone of my bones, and
flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken
out of Man.\f + \fr 2.23  \ft Woman: Heb. Isha\f*\f + \fr 2.23  \ft Man: Heb.
Ish\f*

Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall
cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.

And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not
ashamed.

Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field
which the \nd LORD\nd* God had made. And he said unto the woman,
Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?\f + \fr 3.1 
\ft Yea…: Heb. Yea, because, etc.\f*

And the woman said unto the serpent, We may eat of the fruit
of the trees of the garden:

But of the fruit of the tree which \add is\add* in the midst
of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye
touch it, lest ye die.
And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:

For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your
eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.

And when the woman saw that the tree \add was\add* good for
food, and that it \add was\add* pleasant to the eyes, and a tree
to be desired to make \add one\add* wise, she took of the fruit thereof,
and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did
eat.\f + \fr 3.6  \ft pleasant: Heb. a desire\f*

And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they
\add were\add* naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made
themselves aprons.\f + \fr 3.7  \ft aprons: or, things to gird about\f*

And they heard the voice of the \nd LORD\nd* God walking in the
garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves
from the presence of the \nd LORD\nd* God amongst the trees of the
garden.\f + \fr 3.8  \ft cool: Heb. wind\f*

And the \nd LORD\nd* God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where
\add art\add* thou?

And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid,
because I \add was\add* naked; and I hid myself.

And he said, Who told thee that thou \add wast\add* naked?
Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest
not eat?

And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest \add to be\add*
with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.

And the \nd LORD\nd* God said unto the woman, What \add is\add* this
\add that\add* thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled
me, and I did eat.

And the \nd LORD\nd* God said unto the serpent, Because thou
hast done this, thou \add art\add* cursed above all cattle, and above every
beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou
eat all the days of thy life:

And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy
seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise
his heel.

Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow
and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy
desire \add shall be\add* to thy husband, and he shall rule over
thee.\f + \fr 3.16  \ft to thy…: or, subject to thy husband\f*

And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the
voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded
thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed \add is\add* the ground
for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat \add of\add* it all the days
of thy life;

Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt
eat the herb of the field;\f + \fr 3.18  \ft bring…: Heb. cause to
bud\f*

In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return
unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou \add art\add*,
and unto dust shalt thou return.

And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother
of all living.\f + \fr 3.20  \ft Eve: Heb. Chavah: that is Living\f*

Unto Adam also and to his wife did the \nd LORD\nd* God make
coats of skins, and clothed them.

And the \nd LORD\nd* God said, Behold, the man is become as
one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his
hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:

Therefore the \nd LORD\nd* God sent him forth from the garden
of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.

So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the
garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every
way, to keep the way of the tree of life.

And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain,
and said, I have gotten a man from the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 4.1 
\ft Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired\f*

And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper
of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.\f + \fr 4.2  \ft Abel: Heb.
Hebel\f*\f + \fr 4.2  \ft a keeper: Heb. a feeder\f*

And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the
fruit of the ground an offering unto the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 4.3 
\ft in process…: Heb. at the end of days\f*

And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the
fat thereof. And the \nd LORD\nd* had respect unto Abel and to his
offering:\f + \fr 4.4  \ft flock: Heb. sheep, or, goats\f*

But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain
was very wroth, and his countenance fell.

And the \nd LORD\nd* said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy
countenance fallen?

If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not
well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee \add shall be\add* his
desire, and thou shalt rule over him.\f + \fr 4.7  \ft be accepted: or, have the
excellency\f*\f + \fr 4.7  \ft unto…: or, subject unto thee\f*

And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the
field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.

And the \nd LORD\nd* said unto Cain, Where \add is\add* Abel
thy brother? And he said, I know not: \add Am\add* I my brother’s
keeper?

And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s
blood crieth unto me from the ground.\f + \fr 4.10  \ft blood: Heb.
bloods\f*

And now \add art\add* thou cursed from the earth, which hath
opened her mouth to receive thy brother’s blood from thy hand;

When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield
unto thee her strength; a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the
earth.

And Cain said unto the \nd LORD\nd*, My punishment \add is\add*
greater than I can bear.\f + \fr 4.13  \ft My…: or, Mine iniquity is greater than that it may be
forgiven\f*

Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the
earth; and from thy face shall I be hid; and I shall be a fugitive
and a vagabond in the earth; and it shall come to pass, \add that\add*
every one that findeth me shall slay me.

And the \nd LORD\nd* said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth
Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the \nd LORD\nd*
set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.

And Cain went out from the presence of the \nd LORD\nd*,
and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.

And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch:
and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the
name of his son, Enoch.\f + \fr 4.17  \ft Enoch: Heb. Chanoch\f*

And unto Enoch was born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael: and
Mehujael begat Methusael: and Methusael begat Lamech.\f + \fr 4.18 
\ft Lamech: Heb. Lemech\f*

And Lamech took unto him two wives: the name of the one \add was\add*
Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.

And Adah bare Jabal: he was the father of such as dwell in
tents, and \add of such as have\add* cattle.

And his brother’s name \add was\add* Jubal: he was the father
of all such as handle the harp and organ.

And Zillah, she also bare Tubal-cain, an instructer of every
artificer in brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal-cain \add was\add*
Naamah.\f + \fr 4.22  \ft instructer: Heb. whetter\f*

And Lamech said unto his wives, Adah and Zillah, Hear my voice;
ye wives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: for I have slain a man
to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt.\f + \fr 4.23  \ft I have…: or, I would slay a man in my wound,
etc.\f*\f + \fr 4.23  \ft to my hurt: or, in my hurt\f*

If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and
sevenfold.

And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called
his name Seth: For God, \add said she\add*, hath appointed me another
seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.\f + \fr 4.25  \ft Seth: Heb. Sheth: that is Appointed, or,
Put\f*

And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called
his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 4.26 
\ft Enos: Heb. Enosh\f*\f + \fr 4.26  \ft to call…: or, to call themselves by the name of the
Lord\f*

This \add is\add* the book of the generations of Adam. In the
day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him;

Male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called
their name Adam, in the day when they were created.

And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat \add a
son\add* in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name
Seth:

And the days of Adam after he had begotten Seth were eight
hundred years: and he begat sons and daughters:

And all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty
years: and he died.

And Seth lived an hundred and five years, and begat Enos:\f + \fr 5.6 
\ft Enos: Heb. Enosh\f*

And Seth lived after he begat Enos eight hundred and seven
years, and begat sons and daughters:

And all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years:
and he died.

And Enos lived ninety years, and begat Cainan:\f + \fr 5.9 
\ft Cainan: Heb. Kenan\f*

And Enos lived after he begat Cainan eight hundred and fifteen
years, and begat sons and daughters:

And all the days of Enos were nine hundred and five years:
and he died.

And Cainan lived seventy years, and begat Mahalaleel:\f + \fr 5.12 
\ft Mahalaleel: Gr. Maleleel\f*

And Cainan lived after he begat Mahalaleel eight hundred and
forty years, and begat sons and daughters:

And all the days of Cainan were nine hundred and ten years:
and he died.

And Mahalaleel lived sixty and five years, and begat Jared:\f + \fr 5.15 
\ft Jared: Heb. Jered\f*

And Mahalaleel lived after he begat Jared eight hundred and
thirty years, and begat sons and daughters:

And all the days of Mahalaleel were eight hundred ninety and
five years: and he died.

And Jared lived an hundred sixty and two years, and he begat
Enoch:

And Jared lived after he begat Enoch eight hundred years,
and begat sons and daughters:

And all the days of Jared were nine hundred sixty and two
years: and he died.

And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah:\f + \fr 5.21 
\ft Methuselah: Gr. Mathusala\f*

And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three
hundred years, and begat sons and daughters:

And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five
years:

And Enoch walked with God: and he \add was\add* not; for God
took him.

And Methuselah lived an hundred eighty and seven years, and
begat Lamech:

And Methuselah lived after he begat Lamech seven hundred eighty
and two years, and begat sons and daughters:\f + \fr 5.26  \ft Lamech: Heb.
Lemech\f*

And all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and
nine years: and he died.

And Lamech lived an hundred eighty and two years, and begat
a son:

And he called his name Noah, saying, This \add same\add* shall
comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the
ground which the \nd LORD\nd* hath cursed.\f + \fr 5.29  \ft Noah: Gr. Noe: that is Rest, or,
Comfort\f*

And Lamech lived after he begat Noah five hundred ninety and
five years, and begat sons and daughters:

And all the days of Lamech were seven hundred seventy and
seven years: and he died.

And Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem,
Ham, and Japheth.

And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face
of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,

That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they \add were\add*
fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.

And the \nd LORD\nd* said, My spirit shall not always strive
with man, for that he also \add is\add* flesh: yet his days shall be an
hundred and twenty years.

There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after
that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they
bare \add children\add* to them, the same \add became\add* mighty
men which \add were\add* of old, men of renown.

And \nd GOD\nd* saw that the wickedness of man \add was\add*
great in the earth, and \add that\add* every imagination of the thoughts
of his heart \add was\add* only evil continually.\f + \fr 6.5  \ft every…: or, the whole imagination: the Hebrew word
signifieth not only the imagination, but also the purposes and desires\f*\f + \fr 6.5 
\ft continually: Heb. every day\f*

And it repented the \nd LORD\nd* that he had made man on the
earth, and it grieved him at his heart.

And the \nd LORD\nd* said, I will destroy man whom I have created
from the face of the earth; both man, and beast, and the creeping
thing, and the fowls of the air; for it repenteth me that I have
made them.\f + \fr 6.7  \ft both…: Heb. from man unto beast\f*
But Noah found grace in the eyes of the \nd LORD\nd*.

These \add are\add* the generations of Noah: Noah was a just
man \add and\add* perfect in his generations, \add and\add* Noah
walked with God.\f + \fr 6.9  \ft perfect: or, upright\f*
And Noah begat three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled
with violence.

And God looked upon the earth, and, behold, it was corrupt;
for all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth.

And God said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before
me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will
destroy them with the earth.\f + \fr 6.13  \ft with the earth: or, from the
earth\f*

Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in
the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.\f + \fr 6.14 
\ft rooms: Heb. nests\f*

And this \add is the fashion\add* which thou shalt make it
\add of:\add* The length of the ark \add shall be\add* three hundred
cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty
cubits.

A window shalt thou make to the ark, and in a cubit shalt thou
finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side
thereof; \add with\add* lower, second, and third \add stories\add*
shalt thou make it.

And, behold, I, even I, do bring a flood of waters upon the
earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein \add is\add* the breath of life,
from under heaven; \add and\add* every thing that \add is\add* in the
earth shall die.

But with thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt
come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons’
wives with thee.

And of every living thing of all flesh, two of every \add sort\add*
shalt thou bring into the ark, to keep \add them\add* alive with thee; they shall be
male and female.

Of fowls after their kind, and of cattle after their kind,
of every creeping thing of the earth after his kind, two of every
\add sort\add* shall come unto thee, to keep \add them\add* alive.

And take thou unto thee of all food that is eaten, and thou shalt
gather \add it\add* to thee; and it shall be for food for thee, and for them.

Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so
did he.

And the \nd LORD\nd* said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy
house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this
generation.

Of every clean beast thou shalt take to thee by sevens, the
male and his female: and of beasts that \add are\add* not clean by
two, the male and his female.\f + \fr 7.2  \ft by sevens: Heb. seven
seven\f*

For yet seven days, and I will cause it to rain upon the earth
forty days and forty nights; and every living substance that I have
made will I destroy from off the face of the earth.\f + \fr 7.4 
\ft destroy: Heb. blot out\f*
And Noah did according unto all that the \nd LORD\nd* commanded him.

And Noah \add was\add* six hundred years old when the flood
of waters was upon the earth.

And Noah went in, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons’
wives with him, into the ark, because of the waters of the flood.

Of clean beasts, and of beasts that \add are\add* not clean,

And the sons of Naphtali; Jahzeel, and Guni, and Jezer, and
Shillem.

These \add are\add* the sons of Bilhah, which Laban gave unto
Rachel his daughter, and she bare these unto Jacob: all the souls
\add were\add* seven.

All the souls that came with Jacob into Egypt, which came
out of his loins, besides Jacob’s sons’ wives, all the souls \add were\add*
threescore and six;\f + \fr 46.26  \ft loins: Heb. thigh\f*

And the sons of Joseph, which were born him in Egypt, \add were\add*
two souls: all the souls of the house of Jacob, which came into Egypt,
\add were\add* threescore and ten.

And he sent Judah before him unto Joseph, to direct his face
unto Goshen; and they came into the land of Goshen.

And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Israel
his father, to Goshen, and presented himself unto him; and he fell
on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.

And Israel said unto Joseph, Now let me die, since I have
seen thy face, because thou \add art\add* yet alive.

And the men \add are\add* shepherds, for their trade hath been to feed
cattle; and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they
have.\f + \fr 46.32  \ft their trade…: Heb. they are men of cattle\f*

And it shall come to pass, when Pharaoh shall call you, and shall
say, What \add is\add* your occupation?

That ye shall say, Thy servants’ trade hath been about cattle
from our youth even until now, both we, \add and\add* also our fathers:
that ye may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd \add is\add*
an abomination unto the Egyptians.

Then Joseph came and told Pharaoh, and said, My father and my
brethren, and their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have, are come
out of the land of Canaan; and, behold, they \add are\add* in the
land of Goshen.

And he took some of his brethren, \add even\add* five men,
and presented them unto Pharaoh.

And Pharaoh said unto his brethren, What \add is\add* your
occupation? And they said unto Pharaoh, Thy servants \add are\add*
shepherds, both we, \add and\add* also our fathers.

They said moreover unto Pharaoh, For to sojourn in the land
are we come; for thy servants have no pasture for their flocks; for the
famine \add is\add* sore in the land of Canaan: now therefore, we pray thee, let thy
servants dwell in the land of Goshen.

And Pharaoh spake unto Joseph, saying, Thy father and thy brethren
are come unto thee:

The land of Egypt \add is\add* before thee; in the best of the
land make thy father and brethren to dwell; in the land of Goshen
let them dwell: and if thou knowest \add any\add* men of activity
among them, then make them rulers over my cattle.

And Joseph brought in Jacob his father, and set him before
Pharaoh: and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.

And Pharaoh said unto Jacob, How old \add art\add* thou?\f + \fr 47.8 
\ft How…: Heb. How many are the days of the years of thy life?\f*

And Jacob said unto Pharaoh, The days of the years of my pilgrimage
\add are\add* an hundred and thirty years: few and evil have the
days of the years of my life been, and have not attained unto the
days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their
pilgrimage.
And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from before Pharaoh.

And Joseph placed his father and his brethren, and gave them a
possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the
land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.

And Joseph nourished his father, and his brethren, and all his
father’s household, with bread, according to \add their\add* families.\f + \fr 47.12 
\ft according…: or, as a little child is nourished: Heb. according to the little
ones\f*

And \add there was\add* no bread in all the land; for the
famine \add was\add* very sore, so that the land of Egypt and \add all\add*
the land of Canaan fainted by reason of the famine.

And Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the
land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the corn which they
bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh’s house.

And when money failed in the land of Egypt, and in the land
of Canaan, all the Egyptians came unto Joseph, and said, Give us
bread: for why should we die in thy presence? for the money faileth.

And Joseph said, Give your cattle; and I will give you for your
cattle, if money fail.

And they brought their cattle unto Joseph: and Joseph gave
them bread \add in exchange\add* for horses, and for the flocks,
and for the cattle of the herds, and for the asses: and he fed them with
bread for all their cattle for that year.\f + \fr 47.17  \ft fed…: Heb. led
them\f*

When that year was ended, they came unto him the second year,
and said unto him, We will not hide \add it\add* from my lord, how that our
money is spent; my lord also hath our herds of cattle; there is not ought
left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands:

Wherefore shall we die before thine eyes, both we and our
land? buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be
servants unto Pharaoh: and give \add us\add* seed, that we may live,
and not die, that the land be not desolate.

And Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh; for the
Egyptians sold every man his field, because the famine prevailed
over them: so the land became Pharaoh’s.

And as for the people, he removed them to cities from \add one\add*
end of the borders of Egypt even to the \add other\add* end thereof.

Only the land of the priests bought he not; for the priests
had a portion \add assigned them\add* of Pharaoh, and did eat their
portion which Pharaoh gave them: wherefore they sold not their lands.\f + \fr 47.22 
\ft priests: or, princes\f*

Then Joseph said unto the people, Behold, I have bought you this
day and your land for Pharaoh: lo, \add here is\add* seed for you, and ye shall
sow the land.

And it shall come to pass in the increase, that ye shall give
the fifth \add part\add* unto Pharaoh, and four parts shall be your own, for
seed of the field, and for your food, and for them of your households,
and for food for your little ones.

And they said, Thou hast saved our lives: let us find grace
in the sight of my lord, and we will be Pharaoh’s servants.

And Joseph made it a law over the land of Egypt unto this
day, \add that\add* Pharaoh should have the fifth \add part;\add*
except the land of the priests only, \add which\add* became not Pharaoh’s.\f + \fr 47.26 
\ft priests: or, princes\f*

And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the country of
Goshen; and they had possessions therein, and grew, and multiplied
exceedingly.

And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years: so the whole
age of Jacob was an hundred forty and seven years.\f + \fr 47.28 
\ft the whole…: Heb. the days of the years of his life\f*

And the time drew nigh that Israel must die: and he called
his son Joseph, and said unto him, If now I have found grace in thy
sight, put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh, and deal kindly
and truly with me; bury me not, I pray thee, in Egypt:

But I will lie with my fathers, and thou shalt carry me out of
Egypt, and bury me in their buryingplace. And he said, I will do
as thou hast said.

And he said, Swear unto me. And he sware unto him. And Israel
bowed himself upon the bed’s head.

And it came to pass after these things, that \add one\add*
told Joseph, Behold, thy father \add is\add* sick: and he took with him his
two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.

And \add one\add* told Jacob, and said, Behold, thy son Joseph
cometh unto thee: and Israel strengthened  himself, and sat upon the
bed.

And Jacob said unto Joseph, God Almighty appeared unto me at
Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,

And said unto me, Behold, I will make thee fruitful, and multiply
thee, and I will make of thee a multitude of people; and will give
this land to thy seed after thee \add for\add* an everlasting possession.

And now thy two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, which were born
unto thee in the land of Egypt before I came unto thee into Egypt,
\add are\add* mine; as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine.

And thy issue, which thou begettest after them, shall be thine,
\add and\add* shall be called after the name of their brethren in their
inheritance.

And as for me, when I came from Padan, Rachel died by me in the
land of Canaan in the way, when yet \add there was\add* but a little
way to come unto Ephrath: and I buried her there in the way of Ephrath; the same
\add is\add* Beth-lehem.
And Israel beheld Joseph’s sons, and said, Who \add are\add* these?

And Joseph said unto his father, They \add are\add* my sons,
whom God hath given me in this \add place\add*. And he said, Bring
them, I pray thee, unto me, and I will bless them.

Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, \add so that\add*
he could not see. And he brought them near unto him; and he kissed
them, and embraced them.\f + \fr 48.10  \ft dim: Heb. heavy\f*

And Israel said unto Joseph, I had not thought to see thy
face: and, lo, God hath shewed me also thy seed.

And Joseph brought them out from between his knees, and he
bowed himself with his face to the earth.

And Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward
Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel’s
right hand, and brought \add them\add* near unto him.

And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid \add it\add*
upon Ephraim’s head, who \add was\add* the younger, and his left
hand upon Manasseh’s head, guiding his hands wittingly; for Manasseh
\add was\add* the firstborn.

And he blessed Joseph, and said, God, before whom my fathers
Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God which fed me all my life long
unto this day,

The Angel which redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads;
and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham
and Isaac; and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the
earth.\f + \fr 48.16  \ft grow: Heb. as fishes do increase\f*

And when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon the
head of Ephraim, it displeased him: and he held up his father’s hand,
to remove it from Ephraim’s head unto Manasseh’s head.\f + \fr 48.17 
\ft displeased…: was evil in his eyes\f*

And Joseph said unto his father, Not so, my father: for this
\add is\add* the firstborn; put thy right hand upon his head.

And his father refused, and said, I know \add it\add*, my
son, I know \add it:\add* he also shall become a people, and he also shall be
great: but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his
seed shall become a multitude of nations.\f + \fr 48.19  \ft multitude: Heb.
fulness\f*

And he blessed them that day, saying, In thee shall Israel
bless, saying, God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh: and he set
Ephraim before Manasseh.

And Israel said unto Joseph, Behold, I die: but God shall be with you, and bring you
again unto the land of your fathers.

Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren,
which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my
bow.

And Jacob called unto his sons, and said, Gather yourselves
together, that I may tell you \add that\add* which shall befall you in the
last days.

Gather yourselves together, and hear, ye sons of Jacob; and
hearken unto Israel your father.

Reuben, thou \add art\add* my firstborn, my might, and the
beginning of my strength, the excellency of dignity, and the excellency
of power:

Unstable as water, thou shalt not excel; because thou wentest
up to thy father’s bed; then defiledst thou \add it:\add* he went
up to my couch.\f + \fr 49.4  \ft thou shalt…: Heb. do not thou excel\f*\f + \fr 49.4 
\ft he went…: or, my couch is gone\f*

Simeon and Levi \add are\add* brethren; instruments of cruelty
\add are in\add* their habitations.\f + \fr 49.5  \ft instruments…: or, their swords are weapons of
violence\f*

O my soul, come not thou into their secret; unto their assembly,
mine honour, be not thou united: for in their anger they slew a man,
and in their selfwill they digged down a wall.\f + \fr 49.6  \ft digged…: or, houghed
oxen\f*

Judah, thou \add art he\add* whom thy brethren shall praise:
thy hand \add shall be\add* in the neck of thine enemies; thy father’s
children shall bow down before thee.

Judah \add is\add* a lion’s whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone
up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him
up?

The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his
feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him \add shall\add* the gathering
of the people \add be\add*.

Binding his foal unto the vine, and his ass’s colt unto the choice
vine; he washed his garments in wine, and his clothes in the blood
of grapes:

His eyes \add shall be\add* red with wine, and his teeth white
with milk.

Zebulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea; and he \add shall
be\add* for an haven of ships; and his border \add shall be\add*
unto Zidon.

Issachar \add is\add* a strong ass couching down between two
burdens:

And he saw that rest \add was\add* good, and the land that
\add it was\add* pleasant; and bowed his shoulder to bear, and became a
servant unto tribute.
Dan shall judge his people, as one of the tribes of Israel.

Dan shall be a serpent by the way, an adder in the path, that
biteth the horse heels, so that his rider shall fall backward.\f + \fr 49.17 
\ft an adder: Heb. an arrow-snake\f*
I have waited for thy salvation, O \nd LORD\nd*.

Gad, a troop shall overcome him: but he shall overcome at the
last.

Out of Asher his bread \add shall be\add* fat, and he shall
yield royal dainties.

Naphtali \add is\add* a hind let loose: he giveth goodly
words.

Joseph \add is\add* a fruitful bough, \add even\add* a fruitful
bough by a well; \add whose\add* branches run over the wall:\f + \fr 49.22 
\ft branches: Heb. daughters\f*

The archers have sorely grieved him, and shot \add at him\add*,
and hated him:

But his bow abode in strength, and the arms of his hands were made
strong by the hands of the mighty \add God\add* of Jacob; (from thence
\add is\add* the shepherd, the stone of Israel:)

\add Even\add* by the God of thy father, who shall help thee; and
by the Almighty, who shall bless thee with blessings of heaven above,
blessings of the deep that lieth under, blessings of the breasts,
and of the womb:

The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings
of my progenitors unto the utmost bound of the everlasting hills:
they shall be on the head of Joseph, and on the crown of the head
of him that was separate from his brethren.

Benjamin shall ravin \add as\add* a wolf: in the morning
he shall devour the prey, and at night he shall divide the spoil.

And he charged them, and said unto them, I am to be gathered
unto my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that \add is\add*
in the field of Ephron the Hittite,

In the cave that \add is\add* in the field of Machpelah, which
\add is\add* before Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought
with the field of Ephron the Hittite for a possession of a buryingplace.

There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried
Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah.

The purchase of the field and of the cave that \add is\add* therein
\add was\add* from the children of Heth.

And when Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons, he gathered
up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the ghost, and was gathered
unto his people.

And Joseph fell upon his father’s face, and wept upon him, and
kissed him.

And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm
his father: and the physicians embalmed Israel.

And forty days were fulfilled for him; for so are fulfilled
the days of those which are embalmed: and the Egyptians mourned for him threescore and
ten days.\f + \fr 50.3  \ft mourned: Heb. wept\f*

And when the days of his mourning were past, Joseph spake unto the
house of Pharaoh, saying, If now I have found grace in your eyes,
speak, I pray you, in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,

My father made me swear, saying, Lo, I die: in my grave which I have
digged for me in the land of Canaan, there shalt thou bury me. Now therefore let me go
up, I pray thee, and bury my father, and I will come again.

And Pharaoh said, Go up, and bury thy father, according as he made thee
swear.

And Joseph went up to bury his father: and with him went up
all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the
elders of the land of Egypt,

And all the house of Joseph, and his brethren, and his father’s
house: only their little ones, and their flocks, and their herds,
they left in the land of Goshen.

And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen: and it was a
very great company.

And they came to the threshingfloor of Atad, which \add is\add*
beyond Jordan, and there they mourned with a great and very sore
lamentation: and he made a mourning for his father seven days.

And when the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw
the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, This \add is\add* a
grievous mourning to the Egyptians: wherefore the name of it was
called Abel-mizraim, which \add is\add* beyond Jordan.\f + \fr 50.11 
\ft Abel-mizraim: that is, The mourning of the Egyptians\f*
And his sons did unto him according as he commanded them:

For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried
him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the
field for a possession of a buryingplace of Ephron the Hittite, before
Mamre.

And Joseph returned into Egypt, he, and his brethren, and all that went
up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.

And when Joseph’s brethren saw that their father was dead,
they said, Joseph will peradventure hate us, and will certainly requite
us all the evil which we did unto him.

And they sent a messenger unto Joseph, saying, Thy father
did command before he died, saying,\f + \fr 50.16  \ft sent: Heb.
charged\f*

So shall ye say unto Joseph, Forgive, I pray thee now, the
trespass of thy brethren, and their sin; for they did unto thee evil:
and now, we pray thee, forgive the trespass of the servants of the
God of thy father. And Joseph wept when they spake unto him.

And his brethren also went and fell down before his face;
and they said, Behold, we \add be\add* thy servants.

And Joseph said unto them, Fear not: for \add am\add* I in the place of
God?

But as for you, ye thought evil against me; \add but\add*
God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as \add it is\add* this
day, to save much people alive.

Now therefore fear ye not: I will nourish you, and your little
ones. And he comforted them, and spake kindly unto them.\f + \fr 50.21 
\ft kindly…: Heb. to their hearts\f*

And Joseph dwelt in Egypt, he, and his father’s house: and
Joseph lived an hundred and ten years.

And Joseph saw Ephraim’s children of the third \add generation:\add*
the children also of Machir the son of Manasseh were brought up upon
Joseph’s knees.\f + \fr 50.23  \ft brought…: Heb. born\f*

And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and God will surely
visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he
sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

And Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel, saying,
God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.

So Joseph died, \add being\add* an hundred and ten years old:
and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

verses.text:
Now these \add are\add* the names of the children of Israel,
which came into Egypt; every man and his household came with Jacob.
Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,
Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,
Dan, and Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

And all the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were
seventy souls: for Joseph was in Egypt \add already\add*.\f + \fr 1.5 
\ft loins: Heb. thigh\f*
And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.

And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly,
and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.
Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.

And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children
of Israel \add are\add* more and mightier than we:

Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply,
and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join
also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and \add so\add* get them
up out of the land.

Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their
burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.

But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied
and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.\f + \fr 1.12 
\ft But…: Heb. And as they afflicted them, so they multiplied, etc\f*

And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with
rigour:

And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter,
and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their
service, wherein they made them serve, \add was\add* with rigour.

And the king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, of which the
name of the one \add was\add* Shiphrah, and the name of the other
Puah:

And he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew
women, and see \add them\add* upon the stools; if it \add be\add*
a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it \add be\add* a daughter,
then she shall live.

But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt
commanded them, but saved the men children alive.

And the king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said unto them,
Why have ye done this thing, and have saved the men children alive?

And the midwives said unto Pharaoh, Because the Hebrew women
\add are\add* not as the Egyptian women; for they \add are\add* lively,
and are delivered ere the midwives come in unto them.

Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people
multiplied, and waxed very mighty.

And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he
made them houses.

And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is
born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save
alive.

And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took \add to
wife\add* a daughter of Levi.

And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he
\add was a\add* goodly \add child\add*, she hid him three months.

And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an
ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put
the child therein; and she laid \add it\add* in the flags by the
river’s brink.
And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him.

And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash \add herself\add*
at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river’s side; and when she
saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.

And when she had opened \add it\add*, she saw the child: and, behold, the
babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This \add is
one\add* of the Hebrews’ children.

Then said his sister to Pharaoh’s daughter, Shall I go and
call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the
child for thee?

And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, Go. And the maid went and
called the child’s mother.

And Pharaoh’s daughter said unto her, Take this child away,
and nurse it for me, and I will give \add thee\add* thy wages. And the
woman took the child, and nursed it.

And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh’s daughter,
and he became her son. And she called his name Moses: and she said,
Because I drew him out of the water.\f + \fr 2.10  \ft Moses: that is, Drawn
out\f*

And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown,
that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens:
and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren.

And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that
\add there was\add* no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the
sand.

And when he went out the second day, behold, two men of the
Hebrews strove together: and he said to him that did the wrong, Wherefore
smitest thou thy fellow?

And he said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest
thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? And Moses feared,
and said, Surely this thing is known.\f + \fr 2.14  \ft a prince: Heb. a man, a
prince\f*

Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses.
But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of
Midian: and he sat down by a well.

Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came
and drew \add water\add*, and filled the troughs to water their father’s
flock.\f + \fr 2.16  \ft priest: or, prince\f*

And the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood
up and helped them, and watered their flock.

And when they came to Reuel their father, he said, How \add is it
that\add* ye are come so soon to day?\f + \fr 2.18  \ft Reuel: called also Jethro, or,
Jether\f*

And they said, An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the
shepherds, and also drew \add water\add* enough for us, and watered
the flock.

And he said unto his daughters, And where \add is\add* he? why
\add is\add* it \add that\add* ye have left the man? call him, that he may
eat bread.

And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses
Zipporah his daughter.

And she bare \add him\add* a son, and he called his name Gershom:
for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.\f + \fr 2.22 
\ft Gershom: that is, A stranger here\f*

And it came to pass in process of time, that the king of
Egypt died: and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage,
and they cried, and their cry came up unto God by reason of the bondage.

And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant
with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

And God looked upon the children of Israel, and God had respect unto
\add them\add*.\f + \fr 2.25  \ft had…: Heb. knew\f*

Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law, the priest
of Midian: and he led the flock to the backside of the desert, and
came to the mountain of God, \add even\add* to Horeb.

And the angel of the \nd LORD\nd* appeared unto him in a flame
of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the
bush burned with fire, and the bush \add was\add* not consumed.

And Moses said, I will now turn aside, and see this great sight,
why the bush is not burnt.

And when the \nd LORD\nd* saw that he turned aside to see,
God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses,
Moses. And he said, Here \add am\add* I.

And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy
feet, for the place whereon thou standest \add is\add* holy ground.

The length of a board \add was\add* ten cubits, and the breadth
of a board one cubit and a half.

One board had two tenons, equally distant one from another:
thus did he make for all the boards of the tabernacle.

And he made boards for the tabernacle; twenty boards for the
south side southward:

And for the other side of the tabernacle, \add which is\add*
toward the north corner, he made twenty boards,

And their forty sockets of silver; two sockets under one board,
and two sockets under another board.
And for the sides of the tabernacle westward he made six boards.

And two boards made he for the corners of the tabernacle in the two
sides.

And they were coupled beneath, and coupled together at the
head thereof, to one ring: thus he did to both of them in both the
corners.\f + \fr 36.29  \ft coupled: Heb. twinned\f*

And there were eight boards; and their sockets \add were\add*
sixteen sockets of silver, under every board two sockets.\f + \fr 36.30 
\ft under…: Heb. two sockets, two sockets under one board\f*

And he made bars of shittim wood; five for the boards of the
one side of the tabernacle,

And five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle,
and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle for the sides westward.

And he made the middle bar to shoot through the boards from the one
end to the other.

And he overlaid the boards with gold, and made their rings
\add of\add* gold \add to be\add* places for the bars, and overlaid
the bars with gold.

And he made a vail \add of\add* blue, and purple, and scarlet,
and fine twined linen: \add with\add* cherubims made he it of cunning
work.

And he made an hanging for the tabernacle door \add of\add*
blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, of needlework;\f + \fr 36.37 
\ft of needlework: Heb. the work of a needleworker or, embroiderer\f*

And the five pillars of it with their hooks: and he overlaid
their chapiters and their fillets with gold: but their five sockets
\add were of\add* brass.

And Bezaleel made the ark \add of\add* shittim wood: two cubits
and a half \add was\add* the length of it, and a cubit and a half
the breadth of it, and a cubit and a half the height of it:

And he overlaid it with pure gold within and without, and made
a crown of gold to it round about.

And he cast for it four rings of gold, \add to be set\add*
by the four corners of it; even two rings upon the one side of it, and
two rings upon the other side of it.

And he made staves \add of\add* shittim wood, and overlaid
them with gold.

And he put the staves into the rings by the sides of the ark,
to bear the ark.

And he made the mercy seat \add of\add* pure gold: two cubits
and a half \add was\add* the length thereof, and one cubit and a
half the breadth thereof.

And he made two cherubims \add of\add* gold, beaten out of one
piece made he them, on the two ends of the mercy seat;\f + \fr 37.7 
\ft on…: or, out of, etc\f*

One cherub on the end on this side, and another cherub on the
\add other\add* end on that side: out of the mercy seat made he the
cherubims on the two ends thereof.\f + \fr 37.8  \ft on the end: or, out of,
etc\f*\f + \fr 37.8  \ft on the other end: or, out of, etc\f*

And the cherubims spread out \add their\add* wings on high,
\add and\add* covered with their wings over the mercy seat, with their
faces one to another; \add even\add* to the mercy seatward were the
faces of the cherubims.

And he made the table \add of\add* shittim wood: two cubits
\add was\add* the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, and a
cubit and a half the height thereof:

And he overlaid it with pure gold, and made thereunto a crown
of gold round about.

Also he made thereunto a border of an handbreadth round about;
and made a crown of gold for the border thereof round about.

And he cast for it four rings of gold, and put the rings upon the
four corners that \add were\add* in the four feet thereof.

Over against the border were the rings, the places for the
staves to bear the table.

And he made the staves \add of\add* shittim wood, and overlaid
them with gold, to bear the table.

And he made the vessels which \add were\add* upon the table,
his dishes, and his spoons, and his bowls, and his covers to cover
withal, \add of\add* pure gold.\f + \fr 37.16  \ft to cover…: or, to pour out
withal\f*

And he made the candlestick \add of\add* pure gold: \add of\add*
beaten work made he the candlestick; his shaft, and his branch, his
bowls, his knops, and his flowers, were of the same:

And six branches going out of the sides thereof; three branches
of the candlestick out of the one side thereof, and three branches
of the candlestick out of the other side thereof:

Three bowls made after the fashion of almonds in one branch,
a knop and a flower; and three bowls made like almonds in another
branch, a knop and a flower: so throughout the six branches going
out of the candlestick.

And in the candlestick \add were\add* four bowls made like
almonds, his knops, and his flowers:

And a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under
two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, according to the
six branches going out of it.

Their knops and their branches were of the same: all of it
\add was\add* one beaten work \add of\add* pure gold.

And he made his seven lamps, and his snuffers, and his snuffdishes,
\add of\add* pure gold.

\add Of\add* a talent of pure gold made he it, and all the
vessels thereof.

And he made the incense altar \add of\add* shittim wood:
the length of it \add was\add* a cubit, and the breadth of it a cubit;
\add it was\add* foursquare; and two cubits \add was\add* the height
of it; the horns thereof were of the same.

And he overlaid it with pure gold, \add both\add* the top
of it, and the sides thereof round about, and the horns of it: also he
made unto it a crown of gold round about.

And he made two rings of gold for it under the crown thereof, by the
two corners of it, upon the two sides thereof, to be places for the
staves to bear it withal.

And he made the staves \add of\add* shittim wood, and overlaid
them with gold.

And he made the holy anointing oil, and the pure incense
of sweet spices, according to the work of the apothecary.

And he made the altar of burnt offering \add of\add* shittim
wood: five cubits \add was\add* the length thereof, and five cubits
the breadth thereof; \add it was\add* foursquare; and three cubits
the height thereof.

And he made the horns thereof on the four corners of it; the
horns thereof were of the same: and he overlaid it with brass.

And he made all the vessels of the altar, the pots, and the
shovels, and the basons, \add and\add* the fleshhooks, and the firepans:
all the vessels thereof made he \add of\add* brass.

And he made for the altar a brasen grate of network under the
compass thereof beneath unto the midst of it.

And he cast four rings for the four ends of the grate of brass,
\add to be\add* places for the staves.

And he made the staves \add of\add* shittim wood, and overlaid
them with brass.

And he put the staves into the rings on the sides of the altar,
to bear it withal; he made the altar hollow with boards.

And he made the laver \add of\add* brass, and the foot of it
\add of\add* brass, of the lookingglasses of \add the women\add*
assembling, which assembled \add at\add* the door of the tabernacle
of the congregation.\f + \fr 38.8  \ft lookingglasses: or, brasen
glasses\f*\f + \fr 38.8  \ft assembling: Heb. assembling by troops\f*

And he made the court: on the south side southward the hangings
of the court \add were of\add* fine twined linen, an hundred cubits:

Their pillars \add were\add* twenty, and their brasen sockets
twenty; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets \add were of\add*
silver.

And for the north side \add the hangings were\add* an hundred
cubits, their pillars \add were\add* twenty, and their sockets of
brass twenty; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets \add of\add*
silver.

And for the west side \add were\add* hangings of fifty cubits,
their pillars ten, and their sockets ten; the hooks of the pillars
and their fillets \add of\add* silver.
And for the east side eastward fifty cubits.

The hangings of the one side \add of the gate were\add* fifteen
cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.

And for the other side of the court gate, on this hand and that hand,
\add were\add* hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their
sockets three.

All the hangings of the court round about \add were\add* of fine
twined linen.

And the sockets for the pillars \add were of\add* brass; the
hooks of the pillars and their fillets \add of\add* silver; and the
overlaying of their chapiters \add of\add* silver; and all the pillars
of the court \add were\add* filleted with silver.

And the hanging for the gate of the court \add was\add* needlework,
\add of\add* blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen:
and twenty cubits \add was\add* the length, and the height in the
breadth \add was\add* five cubits, answerable to the hangings of the
court.

And their pillars \add were\add* four, and their sockets \add of\add*
brass four; their hooks \add of\add* silver, and the overlaying of their
chapiters and their fillets \add of\add* silver.

And all the pins of the tabernacle, and of the court round
about, \add were of\add* brass.

This is the sum of the tabernacle, \add even\add* of the
tabernacle of testimony, as it was counted, according to the commandment
of Moses, \add for\add* the service of the Levites, by the hand of
Ithamar, son to Aaron the priest.

And Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe
of Judah, made all that the \nd LORD\nd* commanded  Moses.

And with him \add was\add* Aholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the
tribe of Dan, an engraver, and a cunning workman, and an embroiderer
in blue, and in purple, and in scarlet, and fine linen.

All the gold that was occupied for the work in all the work
of the holy \add place\add*, even the gold of the offering, was twenty
and nine talents, and seven hundred and thirty shekels, after the
shekel of the sanctuary.

And the silver of them that were numbered of the congregation
\add was\add* an hundred talents, and a thousand seven hundred and threescore and
fifteen shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary:

A bekah for every man, \add that is\add*, half a shekel, after the
shekel of the sanctuary, for every one that went to be numbered,
from twenty years old and upward, for six hundred thousand and three
thousand and five hundred and fifty \add men\add*.\f + \fr 38.26 
\ft every man: Heb. a poll\f*

And of the hundred talents of silver were cast the sockets
of the sanctuary, and the sockets of the vail; an hundred sockets
of the hundred talents, a talent for a socket.

And of the thousand seven hundred seventy and five \add shekels\add*
 he made hooks for the pillars, and overlaid their chapiters, and
filleted them.

And the brass of the offering \add was\add* seventy talents,
and two thousand and four hundred shekels.

And therewith he made the sockets to the door of the tabernacle
of the congregation, and the brasen altar, and the brasen grate for it, and all the
vessels of the altar,

And the sockets of the court round about, and the sockets
of the court gate, and all the pins of the tabernacle, and all the
pins of the court round about.

And of the blue, and purple, and scarlet, they made cloths
of service, to do service in the holy \add place\add*, and made the
holy garments for Aaron; as the \nd LORD\nd* commanded Moses.

And he made the ephod \add of\add* gold, blue, and purple,
and scarlet, and fine twined linen.

And they did beat the gold into thin plates, and cut \add it
into\add* wires, to work \add it\add* in the blue, and in the purple,
and in the scarlet, and in the fine linen, \add with\add* cunning
work.

They made shoulderpieces for it, to couple \add it\add* together:
by the two edges was it coupled together.

And the curious girdle of his ephod, that \add was\add* upon it,
\add was\add* of the same, according to the work thereof; \add of\add*
gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen; as the
\nd LORD\nd* commanded Moses.

And they wrought onyx stones inclosed in ouches of gold, graven,
as signets are graven, with the names of the children of Israel.

And he put them on the shoulders of the ephod, \add that they should
be\add* stones for a memorial to the children of Israel; as the \nd LORD\nd*
commanded Moses.

And he made the breastplate \add of\add* cunning work, like the
work of the ephod; \add of\add* gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet,
and fine twined linen.

It was foursquare; they made the breastplate double: a span
\add was\add* the length thereof, and a span the breadth thereof,
\add being\add* doubled.

And they set in it four rows of stones: \add the first\add*
row \add was\add* a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle: this \add was\add*
the first row.\f + \fr 39.10  \ft sardius: or, ruby\f*
And the second row, an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.
And the third row, a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst.

And the fourth row, a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper: \add they
were\add* inclosed in ouches of gold in their inclosings.

And the stones \add were\add* according to the names of the
children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, \add like\add*
the engravings of a signet, every one with his name, according to the
twelve tribes.

And they made upon the breastplate chains at the ends, \add of\add*
wreathen work \add of\add* pure gold.

And they made two ouches \add of\add* gold, and two gold rings;
and put the two rings in the two ends of the breastplate.

And they put the two wreathen chains of gold in the two rings
on the ends of the breastplate.

And the two ends of the two wreathen chains they fastened
in the two ouches, and put them on the shoulderpieces of the ephod,
before it.

And they made two rings of gold, and put \add them\add* on the
two ends of the breastplate, upon the border of it, which \add was\add*
on the side of the ephod inward.

And they made two \add other\add* golden rings, and put them on the
two sides of the ephod underneath, toward the forepart of it, over
against the \add other\add* coupling thereof, above the curious girdle
of the ephod.

And they did bind the breastplate by his rings unto the rings
of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it might be above the curious
girdle of the ephod, and that the breastplate might not be loosed
from the ephod; as the \nd LORD\nd* commanded Moses.

And he made the robe of the ephod \add of\add* woven work,
all \add of\add* blue.

And \add there was\add* an hole in the midst of the robe, as the
hole of an habergeon, \add with\add* a band round about the hole,
that it should not rend.

And they made upon the hems of the robe pomegranates \add of\add*
blue, and purple, and scarlet, \add and\add* twined \add linen\add*.

A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, round
about the hem of the robe to minister \add in;\add* as the \nd LORD\nd*
commanded Moses.

And they made coats \add of\add* fine linen \add of\add*
woven work for Aaron, and for his sons,

And a mitre \add of\add* fine linen, and goodly bonnets \add of\add*
fine linen, and linen breeches \add of\add* fine twined linen,

And a girdle \add of\add* fine twined linen, and blue, and
purple, and scarlet, \add of\add* needlework; as the \nd LORD\nd*
commanded Moses.

And they made the plate of the holy crown \add of\add* pure
gold, and wrote upon it a writing, \add like to\add* the engravings
of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE \nd LORD\nd*.

And they tied unto it a lace of blue, to fasten \add it\add*
on high upon the mitre; as the \nd LORD\nd* commanded Moses.

Thus was all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of the
congregation finished: and the children of Israel did according to all that the
\nd LORD\nd* commanded Moses, so did they.

And they brought the tabernacle unto Moses, the tent, and all his
furniture, his taches, his boards, his bars, and his pillars, and his
sockets,

And the covering of rams’ skins dyed red, and the covering
of badgers’ skins, and the vail of the covering,

The ark of the testimony, and the staves thereof, and the mercy
seat,

The table, \add and\add* all the vessels thereof, and the
shewbread,

The pure candlestick, \add with\add* the lamps thereof, \add even
with\add* the lamps to be set in order, and all the vessels thereof, and the
oil for light,

And the golden altar, and the anointing oil, and the sweet
incense, and the hanging for the tabernacle door,\f + \fr 39.38 
\ft the sweet…: Heb. the incense of sweet spices\f*

The brasen altar, and his grate of brass, his staves, and all his
vessels, the laver and his foot,

The hangings of the court, his pillars, and his sockets, and the
hanging for the court gate, his cords, and his pins, and all the
vessels of the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of the congregation,

The cloths of service to do service in the holy \add place\add*,
and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and his sons’ garments,
to minister in the priest’s office.

According to all that the \nd LORD\nd* commanded Moses, so the
children of Israel made all the work.

And Moses did look upon all the work, and, behold, they had
done it as the \nd LORD\nd* had commanded, even so had they done
it: and Moses blessed  them.
And the \nd LORD\nd* spake unto Moses, saying,

On the first day of the first month shalt thou set up the tabernacle
of the tent of the congregation.

And thou shalt put therein the ark of the testimony, and cover
the ark with the vail.

And thou shalt bring in the table, and set in order the things that are to be set in
order upon it; and thou shalt bring in the candlestick, and light
the lamps thereof.\f + \fr 40.4  \ft the things…: Heb. the order
thereof\f*

And thou shalt set the altar of gold for the incense before
the ark of the testimony, and put the hanging of the door to the
tabernacle.

And thou shalt set the altar of the burnt offering before the
door of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation.

And thou shalt set the laver between the tent of the congregation
and the altar, and shalt put water therein.

And thou shalt set up the court round about, and hang up the
hanging at the court gate.

And thou shalt take the anointing oil, and anoint the tabernacle, and all that
\add is\add* therein, and shalt hallow it, and all the vessels thereof: and it shall be
holy.

And thou shalt anoint the altar of the burnt offering, and all his
vessels, and sanctify the altar: and it shall be an altar most holy.\f + \fr 40.10 
\ft most holy: Heb. holiness of holinesses\f*
And thou shalt anoint the laver and his foot, and sanctify it.

And thou shalt bring Aaron and his sons unto the door of the
tabernacle of the congregation, and wash them with water.

And thou shalt put upon Aaron the holy garments, and anoint
him, and sanctify him; that he may minister unto me in the priest’s
office.
And thou shalt bring his sons, and clothe them with coats:

And thou shalt anoint them, as thou didst anoint their father,
that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office: for their
anointing shall surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout their
generations.

Thus did Moses: according to all that the \nd LORD\nd* commanded
him, so did he.

And it came to pass in the first month in the second year,
on the first \add day\add* of the month, \add that\add* the tabernacle
was reared up.

And Moses reared up the tabernacle, and fastened his sockets,
and set up the boards thereof, and put in the bars thereof, and reared
up his pillars.

And he spread abroad the tent over the tabernacle, and put
the covering of the tent above upon it; as the \nd LORD\nd* commanded
Moses.

And he took and put the testimony into the ark, and set the
staves on the ark, and put the mercy seat above upon the ark:

And he brought the ark into the tabernacle, and set up the
vail of the covering, and covered the ark of the testimony; as the
\nd LORD\nd* commanded Moses.

And he put the table in the tent of the congregation, upon the
side of the tabernacle northward, without the vail.

And he set the bread in order upon it before the 
d LORD
d*;
as the 
d LORD
d* had commanded Moses.

And he put the candlestick in the tent of the congregation,
over against the table, on the side of the tabernacle southward.

And he lighted the lamps before the 
d LORD
d*; as the 
d LORD
d*
commanded Moses.

And he put the golden altar in the tent of the congregation
before the vail:

And he burnt sweet incense thereon; as the \nd LORD\nd* commanded
 Moses.
And he set up the hanging \add at\add* the door of the tabernacle.

And he put the altar of burnt offering \add by\add* the door
of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation, and offered upon it the burnt
offering and the meat offering; as the \nd LORD\nd* commanded Moses.

And he set the laver between the tent of the congregation
and the altar, and put water there, to wash \add withal\add*.

And Moses and Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their
feet thereat:

When they went into the tent of the congregation, and when they came
near unto the altar, they washed; as the \nd LORD\nd* commanded Moses.

And he reared up the court round about the tabernacle and the
altar, and set up the hanging of the court gate. So Moses finished
the work.

Then a cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the
glory of the \nd LORD\nd* filled the tabernacle.

And Moses was not able to enter into the tent of the congregation,
because the cloud abode thereon, and the glory of the \nd LORD\nd*
filled the tabernacle.

And when the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle,
the children of Israel went onward in all their journeys:\f + \fr 40.36 
\ft went onward: Heb. journeyed\f*

But if the cloud were not taken up, then they journeyed not till the
day that it was taken up.

For the cloud of the \nd LORD\nd* \add was\add* upon the tabernacle
by day, and fire was on it by night, in the sight of all the house
of Israel, throughout all their journeys.

verses.text:
And the \nd LORD\nd* called unto Moses, and spake unto him out of the
tabernacle of the congregation, saying,

Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, If any
man of you bring an offering unto the \nd LORD\nd*, ye shall bring
your offering of the cattle, \add even\add* of the herd, and of the
flock.

If his offering \add be\add* a burnt sacrifice of the herd,
let him offer a male without blemish: he shall offer it of his own voluntary
will at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation before the
\nd LORD\nd*.

And he shall put his hand upon the head of the burnt offering;
and it shall be accepted for him to make atonement for him.

And he shall kill the bullock before the \nd LORD\nd*: and the
priests, Aaron’s sons, shall bring the blood, and sprinkle the blood
round about upon the altar that \add is by\add* the door of the tabernacle
of the congregation.
And he shall flay the burnt offering, and cut it into his pieces.

And the sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire upon the altar,
and lay the wood in order upon the fire:

And the priests, Aaron’s sons, shall lay the parts, the head,
and the fat, in order upon the wood that \add is\add* on the fire which
\add is\add* upon the altar:

But his inwards and his legs shall he wash in water: and the
priest shall burn all on the altar, \add to be\add* a burnt sacrifice,
an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the \nd LORD\nd*.

And if his offering \add be\add* of the flocks, \add namely\add*,
of the sheep, or of the goats, for a burnt sacrifice; he shall bring
it a male without blemish.

And he shall kill it on the side of the altar northward before
the \nd LORD\nd*: and the priests, Aaron’s sons, shall sprinkle his
blood round about upon the altar.

And he shall cut it into his pieces, with his head and his
fat: and the priest shall lay them in order on the wood that \add is\add*
on the fire which \add is\add* upon the altar:

But he shall wash the inwards and the legs with water: and the
priest shall bring \add it\add* all, and burn \add it\add* upon the
altar: it \add is\add* a burnt sacrifice, an offering made by fire,
of a sweet savour unto the \nd LORD\nd*.

And if the burnt sacrifice for his offering to the \nd LORD\nd*
\add be\add* of fowls, then he shall bring his offering of turtledoves,
or of young pigeons.

And the priest shall bring it unto the altar, and wring off
his head, and burn \add it\add* on the altar; and the blood thereof shall be wrung
out at the side of the altar:\f + \fr 1.15  \ft wring…: or, pinch off the head with the
nail\f*

And he shall pluck away his crop with his feathers, and cast
it beside the altar on the east part, by the place of the ashes:\f + \fr 1.16 
\ft his feathers: or, the filth thereof\f*

And he shall cleave it with the wings thereof, \add but\add* shall not divide
\add it\add* asunder: and the priest shall burn it upon the altar,
upon the wood that \add is\add* upon the fire: it \add is\add* a burnt
sacrifice, an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the \nd LORD\nd*.

And when any will offer a meat offering unto the \nd LORD\nd*,
his offering shall be \add of\add* fine flour; and he shall pour
oil upon it, and put frankincense thereon:

And he shall bring it to Aaron’s sons the priests: and he shall
take thereout his handful of the flour thereof, and of the oil thereof, with all the
frankincense thereof; and the priest shall burn the memorial of it upon the
altar, \add to be\add* an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour
unto the \nd LORD\nd*:

And the remnant of the meat offering \add shall be\add* Aaron’s
and his sons’: \add it is\add* a thing most holy of the offerings
of the \nd LORD\nd* made by fire.

And if thou bring an oblation of a meat offering baken in the
oven, \add it shall be\add* unleavened cakes of fine flour mingled
with oil, or unleavened wafers anointed  with oil.

And if thy oblation \add be\add* a meat offering \add baken\add*
in a pan, it shall be \add of\add* fine flour unleavened, mingled
with oil.\f + \fr 2.5  \ft in a pan: or, on a flat plate, or, slice\f*

Thou shalt part it in pieces, and pour oil thereon: it \add is\add*
a meat offering.
