\add it is\add* behind Kirjath-jearim.

And they passed thence unto mount Ephraim, and came unto the
house of Micah.

Then answered the five men that went to spy out the country
of Laish, and said unto their brethren, Do ye know that there is
in these houses an ephod, and teraphim, and a graven image, and a molten
image? now therefore consider what ye have to do.

And they turned thitherward, and came to the house of the young
man the Levite, \add even\add* unto the house of Micah, and saluted
him.\f + \fr 18.15  \ft saluted…: Heb. asked him of peace\f*

And the six hundred men appointed with their weapons of war, which
\add were\add* of the children of Dan, stood by the entering of the
gate.

And the five men that went to spy out the land went up, \add and\add*
came in thither, \add and\add* took the graven image, and the ephod,
and the teraphim, and the molten image: and the priest stood in the
entering of the gate with the six hundred men \add that were\add*
appointed with weapons of war.

And these went into Micah’s house, and fetched the carved
image, the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image. Then said
the priest unto them, What do ye?

And they said unto him, Hold thy peace, lay thine hand upon thy
mouth, and go with us, and be to us a father and a priest: \add is
it\add* better for thee to be a priest unto the house of one man,
or that thou be a priest unto a tribe and a family in Israel?

And the priest’s heart was glad, and he took the ephod, and the
teraphim, and the graven image, and went in the midst of the people.

So they turned and departed, and put the little ones and the
cattle and the carriage before them.

\add And\add* when they were a good way from the house of
Micah, the men that \add were\add* in the houses near to Micah’s
house were gathered together, and overtook the children of Dan.

And they cried unto the children of Dan. And they turned their
faces, and said unto Micah, What aileth thee, that thou comest with such a
company?\f + \fr 18.23  \ft comest…: Heb. art gathered together?\f*

And he said, Ye have taken away my gods which I made, and the
priest, and ye are gone away: and what have I more? and what \add is\add* this
\add that\add* ye say unto me, What aileth thee?

And the children of Dan said unto him, Let not thy voice be
heard among us, lest angry fellows run upon thee, and thou lose thy
life, with the lives of thy household.\f + \fr 18.25  \ft angry: Heb. bitter of
soul\f*

And the children of Dan went their way: and when Micah saw that they
\add were\add* too strong for him, he turned and went back unto his
house.

And they took \add the things\add* which Micah had made, and the
priest which he had, and came unto Laish, unto a people \add that
were\add* at quiet and secure: and they smote them with the edge
of the sword, and burnt the city with fire.

And \add there was\add* no deliverer, because it \add was\add*
far from Zidon, and they had no business with \add any\add* man;
and it was in the valley that \add lieth\add* by Beth-rehob. And they
built a city, and dwelt therein.

And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of
Dan their father, who was born unto Israel: howbeit the name of the
city \add was\add* Laish at the first.

And the children of Dan set up the graven image: and Jonathan,
the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests
to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.

And they set them up Micah’s graven image, which he made,
all the time that the house of God was in Shiloh.

And it came to pass in those days, when \add there was\add*
no king in Israel, that there was a certain Levite sojourning on the
side of mount Ephraim, who took to him a concubine out of Beth-lehem-judah.\f + \fr 19.1 
\ft a concubine: Heb. a woman a concubine, or, a wife a concubine\f*

And his concubine played the whore against him, and went away
from him unto her father’s house to Beth-lehem-judah, and was there
four whole months.\f + \fr 19.2  \ft four whole months: or, a year and four month: Heb. days, four
months\f*

And her husband arose, and went after her, to speak friendly unto her,
\add and\add* to bring her again, having his servant with him, and a
couple of asses: and she brought him into her father’s house: and when the
father of the damsel saw him, he rejoiced to meet him.\f + \fr 19.3 
\ft friendly…: Heb. to her heart\f*

And his father in law, the damsel’s father, retained him; and he
abode with him three days: so they did eat and drink, and lodged there.

And it came to pass on the fourth day, when they arose early
in the morning, that he rose up to depart: and the damsel’s father
said unto his son in law, Comfort thine heart with a morsel of bread,
and afterward go your way.\f + \fr 19.5  \ft Comfort: Heb. Strengthen\f*

And they sat down, and did eat and drink both of them together:
for the damsel’s father had said unto the man, Be content, I pray thee, and tarry all
night, and let thine heart be merry.

And when the man rose up to depart, his father in law urged
him: therefore he lodged there again.

And he arose early in the morning on the fifth day to depart:
and the damsel’s father said, Comfort thine heart, I pray thee. And they
tarried until afternoon, and they did eat both of them.\f + \fr 19.8 
\ft until afternoon: Heb. till the day declined\f*

And when the man rose up to depart, he, and his concubine,
and his servant, his father in law, the damsel’s father, said unto him, Behold, now the
day draweth toward evening, I pray you tarry all night: behold, the
day groweth to an end, lodge here, that thine heart may be merry;
and to morrow get you early on your way, that thou mayest go home.\f + \fr 19.9 
\ft draweth: Heb. is weak\f*\f + \fr 19.9  \ft the day groweth to an end: Heb. it is the pitching time of the
day\f*\f + \fr 19.9  \ft home: Heb. to thy tent\f*

But the man would not tarry that night, but he rose up and
departed, and came over against Jebus, which \add is\add* Jerusalem; and
\add there were\add* with him two asses saddled, his concubine also
\add was\add* with him.\f + \fr 19.10  \ft over against: Heb. to over
against\f*

\add And\add* when they \add were\add* by Jebus, the day was
far spent; and the servant said unto his master, Come, I pray thee, and let us turn
in into this city of the Jebusites, and lodge in it.

And he said unto his servant, Come, and let us draw near to
one of these places to lodge all night, in Gibeah, or in Ramah.

And they passed on and went their way; and the sun went down upon them
\add when they were\add* by Gibeah, which \add belongeth\add* to
Benjamin.

And they turned aside thither, to go in \add and\add* to lodge
in Gibeah: and when he went in, he sat him down in a street of the
city: for \add there was\add* no man that took them into his house
to lodging.

And, behold, there came an old man from his work out of the
field at even, which \add was\add* also of mount Ephraim; and he
sojourned in Gibeah: but the men of the place \add were\add* Benjamites.

And when he had lifted up his eyes, he saw a wayfaring man
in the street of the city: and the old man said, Whither goest thou? and
whence comest thou?

And he said unto him, We \add are\add* passing from Beth-lehem-judah
toward the side of mount Ephraim; from thence \add am\add* I: and I
went to Beth-lehem-judah, but I \add am now\add* going to the house
of the \nd LORD\nd*; and there \add is\add* no man that receiveth
me to house.\f + \fr 19.18  \ft receiveth: Heb. gathereth\f*

Yet there is both straw and provender for our asses; and there is
bread and wine also for me, and for thy handmaid, and for the young
man \add which is\add* with thy servants: \add there is\add* no want
of any thing.

And the old man said, Peace \add be\add* with thee; howsoever
\add let\add* all thy wants \add lie\add* upon me; only lodge not in the
street.

So he brought him into his house, and gave provender unto the
asses: and they washed their feet, and did eat and drink.

\add Now\add* as they were making their hearts merry, behold, the
men of the city, certain sons of Belial, beset the house round about,
\add and\add* beat at the door, and spake to the master of the house,
the old man, saying, Bring forth the man that came into thine house,
that we may know him.

And the man, the master of the house, went out unto them, and
said unto them, Nay, my brethren, \add nay\add*, I pray you, do not
\add so\add* wickedly; seeing that this man is come into mine house,
do not this folly.

Behold, \add here is\add* my daughter a maiden, and his concubine;
them I will bring out now, and humble ye them, and do with them what
seemeth good unto you: but unto this man do not so vile a thing.\f + \fr 19.24 
\ft so vile…: Heb. the matter of this folly\f*

But the men would not hearken to him: so the man took his
concubine, and brought her forth unto them; and they knew her, and
abused her all the night until the morning: and when the day began to
spring, they let her go.

Then came the woman in the dawning of the day, and fell down
at the door of the man’s house where her lord \add was\add*, till it was
light.

And her lord rose up in the morning, and opened the doors
of the house, and went out to go his way: and, behold, the woman
his concubine was fallen down \add at\add* the door of the house,
and her hands \add were\add* upon the threshold.

And he said unto her, Up, and let us be going. But none answered.
Then the man took her \add up\add* upon an ass, and the man rose
up, and gat him unto his place.

And when he was come into his house, he took a knife, and laid
hold on his concubine, and divided her, \add together\add* with her
bones, into twelve pieces, and sent her into all the coasts of Israel.

And it was so, that all that saw it said, There was no such
deed done nor seen from the day that the children of Israel came
up out of the land of Egypt unto this day: consider  of it, take
advice, and speak \add your minds\add*.

Then all the children of Israel went out, and the congregation
was gathered together as one man, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, with the
land of Gilead, unto the \nd LORD\nd* in Mizpeh.

And the chief of all the people, \add even\add* of all the
tribes of Israel, presented  themselves in the assembly of the people
of God, four hundred thousand footmen that drew sword.

(Now the children of Benjamin heard that the children of Israel
were gone up to Mizpeh.) Then said the children of Israel, Tell \add us\add*,
how was this wickedness?

And the Levite, the husband of the woman that was slain, answered
and said, I came into Gibeah that \add belongeth\add* to Benjamin,
I and my concubine, to lodge.\f + \fr 20.4  \ft the Levite: Heb. the man the
Levite\f*

And the men of Gibeah rose against me, and beset the house
round about upon me by night, \add and\add* thought to have slain
me: and my concubine have they forced, that she is dead.\f + \fr 20.5 
\ft forced: Heb. humbled\f*

And I took my concubine, and cut her in pieces, and sent her throughout all the
country of the inheritance of Israel: for they have committed lewdness
and folly in Israel.

Behold, ye \add are\add* all children of Israel; give here your
advice and counsel.

And all the people arose as one man, saying, We will not any
\add of us\add* go to his tent, neither will we any \add of us\add*
turn into his house.

But now this \add shall be\add* the thing which we will do to
Gibeah; \add we will go up\add* by lot against it;

And we will take ten men of an hundred throughout all the
tribes of Israel, and an hundred of a thousand, and a thousand out of ten
thousand, to fetch victual for the people, that they may do, when they
come to Gibeah of Benjamin, according to all the folly that they have
wrought in Israel.

So all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit
together as one man.\f + \fr 20.11  \ft knit…: Heb. fellows\f*

And the tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of
Benjamin, saying, What wickedness \add is\add* this that is done among you?

Now therefore deliver \add us\add* the men, the children of
Belial, which \add are\add* in Gibeah, that we may put them to death,
and put away evil from Israel. But the children of Benjamin would
not hearken to the voice of their brethren the children of Israel:

But the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together
out of the cities unto Gibeah, to go out to battle against the children
of Israel.

And the children of Benjamin were numbered at that time out of the
cities twenty and six thousand men that drew sword, beside the inhabitants
of Gibeah, which were numbered seven hundred chosen men.

Among all this people \add there were\add* seven hundred chosen
men lefthanded; every one could sling stones at an hair \add breadth\add*,
and not miss.

And the men of Israel, beside Benjamin, were numbered four
hundred thousand men that drew sword: all these \add were\add* men
of war.

And the children of Israel arose, and went up to the house
of God, and asked counsel of God, and said, Which of us shall go
up first to the battle against the children of Benjamin? And the
\nd LORD\nd* said, Judah \add shall go up\add* first.

And the children of Israel rose up in the morning, and encamped
against Gibeah.

And the children of Benjamin came forth out of Gibeah, and destroyed
down to the ground of the Israelites that day twenty and two thousand
men.

And the people the men of Israel encouraged themselves, and set their
battle again in array in the place where they put themselves in array
the first day.

(And the children of Israel went up and wept before the 
d LORD
d*
until even, and asked counsel of the 
d LORD
d*, saying, Shall I go
up again to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother? And the

d LORD
d* said, Go up against him.)

And the children of Israel came near against the children
of Benjamin the second day.

And Benjamin went forth against them out of Gibeah the second
day, and destroyed down to the ground of the children of Israel again
eighteen thousand men; all these drew the sword.

Then all the children of Israel, and all the people, went
up, and came unto the house of God, and wept, and sat there before
the \nd LORD\nd*, and fasted that day until even, and offered burnt
offerings and peace offerings before the \nd LORD\nd*.

And the children of Israel enquired of the \nd LORD\nd*, (for the
ark of the covenant of God \add was\add* there in those days,

And Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood
before it in those days,) saying, Shall I yet again go out to battle
against the children of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease? And the
\nd LORD\nd* said, Go up; for to morrow I will deliver them into thine
hand.
And Israel set liers in wait round about Gibeah.

And the children of Israel went up against the children of
Benjamin on the third day, and put themselves in array against Gibeah,
as at other times.

And the children of Benjamin went out against the people,
\add and\add* were drawn away from the city; and they began to smite
of the people, \add and\add* kill, as at other times, in the highways,
of which one goeth up to the house of God, and the other to Gibeah
in the field, about thirty men of Israel.\f + \fr 20.31  \ft to smite…: Heb. to smite of the people wounded as at,
etc\f*\f + \fr 20.31  \ft the house…: or, Beth-el\f*

And the children of Benjamin said, They \add are\add* smitten
down before us, as at the first. But the children of Israel said,
Let us flee, and draw them from the city unto the highways.

And all the men of Israel rose up out of their place, and put themselves in
array at Baal-tamar: and the liers in wait of Israel came forth out of their
places, \add even\add* out of the meadows of Gibeah.

And there came against Gibeah ten thousand chosen men out of all
Israel, and the battle was sore: but they knew not that evil \add was\add*
near them.

And the \nd LORD\nd* smote Benjamin before Israel: and the
children of Israel destroyed  of the Benjamites that day twenty and
five thousand and an hundred men: all these drew the sword.

So the children of Benjamin saw that they were smitten: for the
men of Israel gave place to the Benjamites, because they trusted
unto the liers in wait which they had set beside Gibeah.

And the liers in wait hasted, and rushed upon Gibeah; and the liers in
wait drew \add themselves\add* along, and smote all the city with the
edge of the sword.\f + \fr 20.37  \ft drew…: or, made a long sound with the
trumpet\f*

Now there was an appointed sign between the men of Israel
and the liers in wait, that they should make a great flame with smoke
rise up out of the city.\f + \fr 20.38  \ft sign: or, time\f*\f + \fr 20.38 
\ft and: Heb. with\f*\f + \fr 20.38  \ft flame: Heb. elevation\f*

And when the men of Israel retired in the battle, Benjamin
began to smite \add and\add* kill of the men of Israel about thirty
persons: for they said, Surely they are smitten down before us, as
\add in\add* the first battle.\f + \fr 20.39  \ft to smite…: Heb. to smite the
wounded\f*

But when the flame began to arise up out of the city with a
pillar of smoke, the Benjamites looked behind them, and, behold, the
flame of the city ascended up to heaven.\f + \fr 20.40  \ft the flame of: Heb. the whole consumption
of\f*

And when the men of Israel turned again, the men of Benjamin
were amazed: for they saw that evil was come upon them.\f + \fr 20.41 
\ft was come…: Heb. touched them\f*

Therefore they turned \add their backs\add* before the men
of Israel unto the way of the wilderness; but the battle overtook them; and them which
\add came\add* out of the cities they destroyed in the midst of them.

\add Thus\add* they inclosed the Benjamites round about, \add and\add*
chased them, \add and\add* trode them down with ease over against
Gibeah toward the sunrising.\f + \fr 20.43  \ft with ease…: or, from Menuchah,
etc\f*\f + \fr 20.43  \ft over…: Heb. unto over against\f*

And there fell of Benjamin eighteen thousand men; all these
\add were\add* men of valour.

And they turned and fled toward the wilderness unto the rock
of Rimmon: and they gleaned of them in the highways five thousand
men; and pursued hard after them unto Gidom, and slew two thousand
men of them.

So that all which fell that day of Benjamin were twenty and
five thousand men that drew the sword; all these \add were\add* men
of valour.

But six hundred men turned and fled to the wilderness unto the
rock Rimmon, and abode in the rock Rimmon four months.

And the men of Israel turned again upon the children of Benjamin,
and smote them with the edge of the sword, as well the men of \add every\add*
city, as the beast, and all that came to hand: also they set on fire
all the cities that they came to.\f + \fr 20.48  \ft came to hand: Heb. was
found\f*\f + \fr 20.48  \ft they came…: Heb. were found\f*

Now the men of Israel had sworn in Mizpeh, saying, There shall not
any of us give his daughter unto Benjamin to wife.

And the people came to the house of God, and abode there till
even before God, and lifted up their voices, and wept sore;

And said, O \nd LORD\nd* God of Israel, why is this come to pass in
Israel, that there should be to day one tribe lacking in Israel?

And it came to pass on the morrow, that the people rose early,
and built there an altar, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

And the children of Israel said, Who \add is there\add* among all the
tribes of Israel that came not up with the congregation unto the
\nd LORD\nd*? For they had made a great oath concerning him that came not
up to the \nd LORD\nd* to Mizpeh, saying, He shall surely be put to
death.

And the children of Israel repented them for Benjamin their
brother, and said, There is one tribe cut off from Israel this day.

How shall we do for wives for them that remain, seeing we have
sworn by the \nd LORD\nd* that we will not give them of our daughters
to wives?

And they said, What one \add is there\add* of the tribes of
Israel that came not up to Mizpeh to the \nd LORD\nd*? And, behold, there
came none to the camp from Jabesh-gilead to the assembly.

For the people were numbered, and, behold, \add there were\add*
none of the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead there.

And the congregation sent thither twelve thousand men of the
valiantest, and commanded them, saying, Go and smite the inhabitants
of Jabesh-gilead with the edge of the sword, with the women and the
children.

And this \add is\add* the thing that ye shall do, Ye shall utterly
destroy every male, and every woman that hath lain by man.\f + \fr 21.11 
\ft hath lain…: Heb. knoweth the lying with man\f*

And they found among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead four
hundred young virgins, that had known no man by lying with any male:
and they brought them unto the camp to Shiloh, which \add is\add*
in the land of Canaan.\f + \fr 21.12  \ft young…: Heb. young women
virgins\f*

And the whole congregation sent \add some\add* to speak to the
children of Benjamin that \add were\add* in the rock Rimmon, and to
call peaceably unto them.\f + \fr 21.13  \ft to speak…: Heb. and spake and
called\f*\f + \fr 21.13  \ft call…: or, proclaim peace\f*

And Benjamin came again at that time; and they gave them wives
which they had saved alive of the women of Jabesh-gilead: and yet so they
sufficed them not.

And the people repented them for Benjamin, because that the
\nd LORD\nd* had made a breach in the tribes of Israel.

Then the elders of the congregation said, How shall we do
for wives for them that remain, seeing the women are destroyed out of
Benjamin?

And they said, \add There must be\add* an inheritance for them that be
escaped of Benjamin, that a tribe be not destroyed out of Israel.

Howbeit we may not give them wives of our daughters: for the
children of Israel have sworn, saying, Cursed \add be\add* he that
giveth a wife to Benjamin.

Then they said, Behold, \add there is\add* a feast of the
\nd LORD\nd* in Shiloh yearly \add in a place\add* which \add is\add*
on the north side of Beth-el, on the east side of the highway that goeth
up from Beth-el to Shechem, and on the south of Lebonah.\f + \fr 21.19 
\ft yearly: Heb. from year to year\f*\f + \fr 21.19  \ft on the east…: or, toward the
sunrising\f*\f + \fr 21.19  \ft of the highway: or, on the highway\f*

Therefore they commanded the children of Benjamin, saying,
Go and lie in wait in the vineyards;

And see, and, behold, if the daughters of Shiloh come out
to dance in dances, then come ye out of the vineyards, and catch
you every man his wife of the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the
land of Benjamin.

And it shall be, when their fathers or their brethren come
unto us to complain, that we will say unto them, Be favourable unto them for our sakes: because we
reserved not to each man his wife in the war: for ye did not give
unto them at this time, \add that\add* ye should be guilty.\f + \fr 21.22 
\ft Be favourable…: or, Gratify us in them\f*

And the children of Benjamin did so, and took \add them\add*
wives, according to their number, of them that danced, whom they
caught: and they went and returned unto their inheritance, and repaired
the cities, and dwelt in them.

And the children of Israel departed thence at that time, every
man to his tribe and to his family, and they went out from thence every
man to his inheritance.

In those days \add there was\add* no king in Israel: every
man did \add that which was\add* right in his own eyes.

headers.toc1: The Book of Ruth
headers.mt1: The Book of Ruth

verses.text:
Now it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled, that there was a
famine in the land. And a certain man of Beth-lehem-judah went to
sojourn in the country of Moab, he, and his wife, and his two sons.\f + \fr 1.1 
\ft ruled: Heb. judged\f*

And the name of the man \add was\add* Elimelech, and the name
of his wife Naomi, and the name of his two sons Mahlon and Chilion,
Ephrathites of Beth-lehem-judah. And they came into the country of
Moab, and continued there.\f + \fr 1.2  \ft continued: Heb. were\f*

And Elimelech Naomi’s husband died; and she was left, and her
two sons.

And they took them wives of the women of Moab; the name of the
one \add was\add* Orpah, and the name of the other Ruth: and they
dwelled there about ten years.

And Mahlon and Chilion died also both of them; and the woman
was left of her two sons and her husband.

Then she arose with her daughters in law, that she might return
from the country of Moab: for she had heard in the country of Moab
how that the \nd LORD\nd* had visited his people in giving them bread.

Wherefore she went forth out of the place where she was, and her
two daughters in law with her; and they went on the way to return
unto the land of Judah.

And Naomi said unto her two daughters in law, Go, return each
to her mother’s house: the \nd LORD\nd* deal kindly with you, as ye have
dealt with the dead, and with me.

The \nd LORD\nd* grant you that ye may find rest, each \add of
you\add* in the house of her husband. Then she kissed them; and they lifted
up their voice, and wept.

And they said unto her, Surely we will return with thee unto thy
people.

And Naomi said, Turn again, my daughters: why will ye go with me?
\add are\add* there yet \add any more\add* sons in my womb, that they may be your
husbands?

Turn again, my daughters, go \add your way;\add* for I am too
old to have an husband. If I should say, I have hope, \add if\add*
I should have an husband also to night, and should also bear sons;\f + \fr 1.12 
\ft should have…: or were with an husband\f*

Would ye tarry for them till they were grown? would ye stay
for them from having husbands? nay, my daughters; for it grieveth
me much for your sakes that the hand of the \nd LORD\nd* is gone
out against me.\f + \fr 1.13  \ft tarry: Heb. hope\f*\f + \fr 1.13 
\ft it grieveth…: Heb. I have much bitterness\f*

And they lifted up their voice, and wept again: and Orpah
kissed her mother in law; but Ruth clave unto her.

And she said, Behold, thy sister in law is gone back unto her
people, and unto her gods: return thou after thy sister in law.

And Ruth said, Intreat me not to leave thee, \add or\add*
to return from following after thee: for whither thou goest, I will
go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people \add shall be\add*
my people, and thy God my God:\f + \fr 1.16  \ft Intreat…: or, Be not against
me\f*

Where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried:
the \nd LORD\nd* do so to me, and more also, \add if ought\add* but
death part thee and me.

When she saw that she was stedfastly minded to go with her, then she
left speaking unto her.\f + \fr 1.18  \ft was…: Heb. strengthened
herself\f*

So they two went until they came to Beth-lehem. And it came to pass, when they were
come to Beth-lehem, that all the city was moved about them, and they
said, \add Is\add* this Naomi?

And she said unto them, Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: for the
Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.\f + \fr 1.20  \ft Naomi: that is,
Pleasant\f*\f + \fr 1.20  \ft Mara: that is, Bitter\f*

I went out full, and the 
d LORD
d* hath brought me home
again empty: why \add then\add* call ye me Naomi, seeing the 
d LORD
d*
hath testified against me, and the Almighty hath afflicted me?

So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter in
law, with her, which returned out of the country of Moab: and they
came to Beth-lehem in the beginning of barley harvest.

And Naomi had a kinsman of her husband’s, a mighty man of wealth,
of the family of Elimelech; and his name \add was\add* Boaz.\f + \fr 2.1 
\ft Boaz: Gr. Booz\f*

And Ruth the Moabitess said unto Naomi, Let me now go to the
field, and glean ears of corn after \add him\add* in whose sight
I shall find grace. And she said unto her, Go, my daughter.

And she went, and came, and gleaned in the field after the
reapers: and her hap was to light on a part of the field \add belonging\add*
unto Boaz, who \add was\add* of the kindred of Elimelech.\f + \fr 2.3 
\ft hap…: Heb. hap happened\f*

And, behold, Boaz came from Beth-lehem, and said unto the
reapers, The 
d LORD
d* \add be\add* with you. And they answered
him, The 
d LORD
d* bless thee.

Then said Boaz unto his servant that was set over the reapers,
Whose damsel \add is\add* this?

And the servant that was set over the reapers answered and
said, It \add is\add* the Moabitish damsel that came back with Naomi
out of the country of Moab:

And she said, I pray you, let me glean and gather after the
reapers among the sheaves: so she came, and hath continued even from the
morning until now, that she tarried a little in the house.

Then said Boaz unto Ruth, Hearest thou not, my daughter? Go
not to glean in another field, neither go from hence, but abide here fast by my
maidens:

\add Let\add* thine eyes \add be\add* on the field that they do
reap, and go thou after them: have I not charged the young men that they shall not
touch thee? and when thou art athirst, go unto the vessels, and drink of
\add that\add* which the young men have drawn.

Then she fell on her face, and bowed herself to the ground,
and said unto him, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take
knowledge of me, seeing I \add am\add* a stranger?

And Boaz answered and said unto her, It hath fully been shewed
me, all that thou hast done unto thy mother in law since the death
of thine husband: and \add how\add* thou hast left thy father and thy
mother, and the land of thy nativity, and art come unto a people
which thou knewest not heretofore.

The 
d LORD
d* recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the

d LORD
d* God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust.

Then she said, Let me find favour in thy sight, my lord; for that thou hast
comforted me, and for that thou hast spoken friendly unto thine handmaid,
though I be not like unto one of thine handmaidens.\f + \fr 2.13 
\ft Let me…: or, I find\f*\f + \fr 2.13  \ft friendly: Heb. to the
heart\f*

And Boaz said unto her, At mealtime come thou hither, and
eat of the bread, and dip thy morsel in the vinegar. And she sat
beside the reapers: and he reached her parched \add corn\add*, and she did
eat, and was sufficed, and left.

And when she was risen up to glean, Boaz commanded his young
men, saying, Let her glean even among the sheaves, and reproach her
not:\f + \fr 2.15  \ft reproach…: Heb. shame her not\f*

So she gleaned in the field until even, and beat out that she had
gleaned: and it was about an ephah of barley.

And she took \add it\add* up, and went into the city: and her mother in
law saw what she had gleaned: and she brought forth, and gave to her that she had
reserved after she was sufficed.

And her mother in law said unto her, Where hast thou gleaned
to day? and where wroughtest thou? blessed be he that did take knowledge
of thee. And she shewed her mother in law with whom she had wrought,
and said, The man’s name with whom I wrought to day \add is\add*
Boaz.

And Naomi said unto her daughter in law, Blessed \add be\add*
he of the \nd LORD\nd*, who hath not left off his kindness to the
living and to the dead. And Naomi said unto her, The man \add is\add*
near of kin unto us, one of our next kinsmen.\f + \fr 2.20  \ft one of…: or, one that hath right to
redeem\f*

And Ruth the Moabitess said, He said unto me also, Thou shalt keep
fast by my young men, until they have ended all my harvest.

And Naomi said unto Ruth her daughter in law, \add It is\add*
good, my daughter, that thou go out with his maidens, that they meet
thee not in any other field.\f + \fr 2.22  \ft meet…: or, fall upon
thee\f*

So she kept fast by the maidens of Boaz to glean unto the
end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest; and dwelt with her mother in
law.

Then Naomi her mother in law said unto her, My daughter, shall I not
seek rest for thee, that it may be well with thee?

And now \add is\add* not Boaz of our kindred, with whose maidens
thou wast? Behold, he winnoweth barley to night in the threshingfloor.

Wash thyself therefore, and anoint thee, and put thy raiment
upon thee, and get thee down to the floor: \add but\add* make not thyself
known unto the man, until he shall have done eating and drinking.

And it shall be, when he lieth down, that thou shalt mark the
place where he shall lie, and thou shalt go in, and uncover his feet,
and lay thee down; and he will tell thee what thou shalt do.\f + \fr 3.4 
\ft uncover: or, lift up the clothes that are on\f*

And she said unto her, All that thou sayest unto me I will
do.

And she went down unto the floor, and did according to all that her mother in
law bade her.

And when Boaz had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry,
he went to lie down at the end of the heap of corn: and she came
softly, and uncovered his feet, and laid her down.

And it came to pass at midnight, that the man was afraid,
and turned himself: and, behold, a woman lay at his feet.\f + \fr 3.8 
\ft turned: or, took hold on\f*

And he said, Who \add art\add* thou? And she answered, I \add am\add*
Ruth thine handmaid: spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou
\add art\add* a near kinsman.\f + \fr 3.9  \ft a near…: or, one that hath right to
redeem\f*

And he said, Blessed \add be\add* thou of the \nd LORD\nd*,
my daughter: \add for\add* thou hast shewed more kindness in the latter
end than at the beginning, inasmuch as thou followedst not young
men, whether poor or rich.

And now, my daughter, fear not; I will do to thee all that thou
requirest: for all the city of my people doth know that thou \add art\add*
a virtuous woman.\f + \fr 3.11  \ft city: Heb. gate\f*

And now it is true that I \add am thy\add* near kinsman: howbeit there
is a kinsman nearer than I.

Tarry this night, and it shall be in the morning, \add that\add*
if he will perform unto thee the part of a kinsman, well; let him do the kinsman’s
part: but if he will not do the part of a kinsman to thee, then will I do the part of a
kinsman to thee, \add as\add* the \nd LORD\nd* liveth: lie down until the
morning.

And she lay at his feet until the morning: and she rose up
before one could know another. And he said, Let it not be known that a
woman came into the floor.

Also he said, Bring the vail that \add thou hast\add* upon thee, and
hold it. And when she held it, he measured six \add measures\add*
of barley, and laid \add it\add* on her: and she went into the city.\f + \fr 3.15 
\ft vail: or, sheet, or, apron\f*

And when she came to her mother in law, she said, Who \add art\add*
thou, my daughter? And she told her all that the man had done to her.

And she said, These six \add measures\add* of barley gave
he me; for he said to me, Go not empty unto thy mother in law.

Then said she, Sit still, my daughter, until thou know how the
matter will fall: for the man will not be in rest, until he have
finished the thing this day.

Then went Boaz up to the gate, and sat him down there: and, behold, the
kinsman of whom Boaz spake  came by; unto whom he said, Ho, such
a one! turn aside, sit down here. And he turned aside, and sat down.

And he took ten men of the elders of the city, and said, Sit ye
down here. And they sat down.

And he said unto the kinsman, Naomi, that is come again out of the
country of Moab, selleth a parcel of land, which \add was\add* our
brother Elimelech’s:

And I thought to advertise thee, saying, Buy \add it\add* before the
inhabitants, and before the elders of my people. If thou wilt redeem
\add it\add*, redeem \add it:\add* but if thou wilt not redeem \add it,
then\add* tell me, that I may know: for \add there is\add* none to
redeem \add it\add* beside thee; and I \add am\add* after thee. And he
said, I will redeem \add it\add*.\f + \fr 4.4  \ft I thought…: Heb. I said, I will reveal in thine
ear\f*

Then said Boaz, What day thou buyest the field of the hand
of Naomi, thou must buy \add it\add* also of Ruth the Moabitess,
the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.

And the kinsman said, I cannot redeem \add it\add* for myself, lest I
mar mine own inheritance: redeem thou my right to thyself; for I
cannot redeem \add it\add*.

Now this \add was the manner\add* in former time in Israel concerning
redeeming and concerning changing, for to confirm all things; a man
plucked off his shoe, and gave \add it\add* to his neighbour: and this
\add was\add* a testimony in Israel.

Therefore the kinsman said unto Boaz, Buy \add it\add* for thee. So he drew
off his shoe.

And Boaz said unto the elders, and \add unto\add* all the
people, Ye \add are\add* witnesses this day, that I have bought all that
\add was\add* Elimelech’s, and all that \add was\add* Chilion’s and
Mahlon’s, of the hand of Naomi.

Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased
to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance,
that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren,
and from the gate of his place: ye \add are\add* witnesses this day.

And all the people that \add were\add* in the gate, and the
elders, said, \add We are\add* witnesses. The \nd LORD\nd* make the
woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which
two did build the house of Israel: and do thou worthily in Ephratah,
and be famous in Beth-lehem:\f + \fr 4.11  \ft do thou…: or, get thee riches, or,
power\f*\f + \fr 4.11  \ft be famous: Heb. proclaim thy name\f*

And let thy house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar
bare unto Judah, of the seed which the \nd LORD\nd* shall give thee of this young
woman.

So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went
in unto her, the \nd LORD\nd* gave her conception, and she bare a
son.

And the women said unto Naomi, Blessed \add be\add* the \nd LORD\nd*,
which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name
may be famous in Israel.\f + \fr 4.14  \ft left…: Heb. caused to cease unto
thee\f*\f + \fr 4.14  \ft kinsman: or, redeemer\f*

And he shall be unto thee a restorer of \add thy\add* life,
and a nourisher of thine old age: for thy daughter in law, which
loveth thee, which is better to thee than seven sons, hath born him.\f + \fr 4.15 
\ft a nourisher of: Heb. to nourish\f*\f + \fr 4.15  \ft thine…: Heb. thy gray
hairs\f*

And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became
nurse unto it.

And the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a
son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he \add is\add*
the father of Jesse, the father of David.

Now these \add are\add* the generations of Pharez: Pharez
begat Hezron,
And Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminadab,

And Amminadab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmon,\f + \fr 4.20 
\ft Salmon: or, Salmah\f*
And Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed,
And Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.

verses.text:
Now there was a certain man of Ramathaim-zophim, of mount Ephraim,
and his name \add was\add* Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of
Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephrathite:

And he had two wives; the name of the one \add was\add* Hannah,
and the name of the other Peninnah: and Peninnah had children, but
Hannah had no children.

And this man went up out of his city yearly to worship and to
sacrifice unto the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts in Shiloh. And the two sons
of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the \nd LORD\nd*, \add were\add*
there.\f + \fr 1.3  \ft yearly: Heb. from year to year\f*

And when the time was that Elkanah offered, he gave to Peninnah
his wife, and to all her sons and her daughters, portions:

But unto Hannah he gave a worthy portion; for he loved Hannah:
but the \nd LORD\nd* had shut up her womb.\f + \fr 1.5  \ft worthy: or,
double\f*

And her adversary also provoked her sore, for to make her fret,
because the \nd LORD\nd* had shut up her womb.\f + \fr 1.6  \ft provoked: Heb.
angered\f*

And \add as\add* he did so year by year, when she went up to the
house of the \nd LORD\nd*, so she provoked her; therefore she wept,
and did not eat.\f + \fr 1.7  \ft when…: or, from the time that she, etc: Heb. from her going
up\f*

Then said Elkanah her husband to her, Hannah, why weepest thou? and why
eatest thou not? and why is thy heart grieved? \add am\add* not I
better to thee than ten sons?

So Hannah rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and after
they had drunk. Now Eli the priest sat upon a seat by a post of the
temple of the \nd LORD\nd*.

And she \add was\add* in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the
\nd LORD\nd*, and wept sore.\f + \fr 1.10  \ft in…: Heb. bitter of
soul\f*

And she vowed a vow, and said, O \nd LORD\nd* of hosts, if thou wilt
indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and not
forget thine handmaid, but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child,
then I will give him unto the \nd LORD\nd* all the days of his life,
and there shall no razor come upon his head.\f + \fr 1.11  \ft a man…: Heb. seed of
men\f*

And it came to pass, as she continued praying before the \nd LORD\nd*,
that Eli marked her mouth.\f + \fr 1.12  \ft continued…: Heb. multiplied to
pray\f*

Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her
voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought  she had been drunken.

And Eli said unto her, How long wilt thou be drunken? put
away thy wine from thee.

And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I \add am\add*
a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong
drink, but have poured out my soul before the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 1.15 
\ft of a sorrowful…: Heb. hard of spirit\f*

Count not thine handmaid for a daughter of Belial: for out of the
abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.\f + \fr 1.16 
\ft complaint: or, meditation\f*

Then Eli answered and said, Go in peace: and the God of Israel
grant \add thee\add* thy petition that thou hast asked of him.

And she said, Let thine handmaid find grace in thy sight.
So the woman went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more
\add sad\add*.

And they rose up in the morning early, and worshipped before
the 
d LORD
d*, and returned, and came to their house to Ramah:
and Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and the 
d LORD
d* remembered her.

Wherefore it came to pass, when the time was come about after
Hannah had conceived, that she bare a son, and called his name Samuel,
\add saying\add*, Because I have asked him of the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 1.20 
\ft when…: Heb. in revolution of days\f*\f + \fr 1.20  \ft Samuel: that is, Asked of
God\f*

And the man Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer unto the
\nd LORD\nd* the yearly sacrifice, and his vow.

But Hannah went not up; for she said unto her husband, \add I will not go
up\add* until the child be weaned, and \add then\add* I will bring
him, that he may appear before the \nd LORD\nd*, and there abide
for ever.

And Elkanah her husband said unto her, Do what seemeth thee
good; tarry until thou have weaned him; only the \nd LORD\nd* establish
his word. So the woman abode, and gave her son suck until she weaned him.

And when she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with
three bullocks, and one ephah of flour, and a bottle of wine, and
brought him unto the house of the \nd LORD\nd* in Shiloh: and the
child \add was\add* young.
And they slew a bullock, and brought the child to Eli.

And she said, Oh my lord, \add as\add* thy soul liveth, my
lord, I \add am\add* the woman that stood by thee here, praying unto the
\nd LORD\nd*.

For this child I prayed; and the \nd LORD\nd* hath given me my
petition which I asked of him:

Therefore also I have lent him to the 
d LORD
d*; as long as he
liveth he shall be lent to the 
d LORD
d*. And he worshipped the

d LORD
d* there.  +  r 1.28   t lent him: or, returned him, whom I have obtained by
petition *  +  r 1.28   t he shall…: or, he whom I have obtained by petition shall be
returned *

And Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the 
d LORD
d*,
mine horn is exalted in the 
d LORD
d*: my mouth is enlarged over mine
enemies; because I rejoice in thy salvation.

\add There is\add* none holy as the \nd LORD\nd*: for \add there
is\add* none beside thee: neither \add is there\add* any rock like our
God.

Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let \add not\add* arrogancy
come out of your mouth: for the \nd LORD\nd* \add is\add* a God of
knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.\f + \fr 2.3  \ft arrogancy: Heb.
hard\f*

The bows of the mighty men \add are\add* broken, and they that
stumbled are girded with strength.

\add They that were\add* full have hired out themselves for
bread; and \add they that were\add* hungry ceased: so that the barren
hath born seven; and she that hath many children is waxed feeble.

The \nd LORD\nd* killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down
to the grave, and bringeth up.

The \nd LORD\nd* maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth
low, and lifteth up.

He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, \add and\add* lifteth
up the beggar from the dunghill, to set \add them\add* among princes,
and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the
earth \add are\add* the \nd LORD’s\nd*, and he hath set the world upon them.

He will keep the feet of his saints, and the wicked shall be
silent in darkness; for by strength shall no man prevail.

The adversaries of the \nd LORD\nd* shall be broken to pieces;
out of heaven shall he thunder upon them: the \nd LORD\nd* shall
judge the ends of the earth; and he shall give strength unto his
king, and exalt the horn of his anointed.

And Elkanah went to Ramah to his house. And the child did
minister unto the \nd LORD\nd* before Eli the priest.

Now the sons of Eli \add were\add* sons of Belial; they knew
not the \nd LORD\nd*.

And he struck \add it\add* into the pan, or kettle, or caldron,
or pot; all that the fleshhook brought up the priest took for himself. So they
did in Shiloh unto all the Israelites that came thither.

Also before they burnt the fat, the priest’s servant came,
and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the
priest; for he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw.

And \add if\add* any man said unto him, Let them not fail to
burn the fat presently, and \add then\add* take \add as much\add*
as thy soul desireth; then he would answer him, \add Nay;\add* but thou shalt
give \add it me\add* now: and if not, I will take \add it\add* by
force.\f + \fr 2.16  \ft presently: Heb. as on the day\f*

Wherefore the sin of the young men was very great before the

d LORD
d*: for men abhorred  the offering of the 
d LORD
d*.

But Samuel ministered before the \nd LORD\nd*, \add being\add*
a child, girded with a linen ephod.

Moreover his mother made him a little coat, and brought \add it\add*
to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer
the yearly sacrifice.

And Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, and said, The \nd LORD\nd*
give thee seed of this woman for the loan which is lent to the \nd LORD\nd*.
And they went unto their own home.\f + \fr 2.20  \ft loan…: or, petition which she asked,
etc\f*

And the \nd LORD\nd* visited Hannah, so that she conceived,
and bare three sons and two daughters. And the child Samuel grew
before the \nd LORD\nd*.

Now Eli was very old, and heard all that his sons did unto all
Israel; and how they lay with the women that assembled \add at\add*
the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.\f + \fr 2.22  \ft assembled: Heb. assembled by
troops\f*

And he said unto them, Why do ye such things? for I hear of your
evil dealings by all this people.\f + \fr 2.23  \ft of your…: or, evil words of
you\f*

Nay, my sons; for \add it is\add* no good report that I hear:
ye make the \nd LORD’s\nd* people to transgress.\f + \fr 2.24  \ft transgress: or, cry
out\f*

If one man sin against another, the judge shall judge him: but if a
man sin against the \nd LORD\nd*, who shall intreat for him? Notwithstanding they
hearkened not unto the voice of their father, because the \nd LORD\nd*
would slay them.

And the child Samuel grew on, and was in favour both with the
\nd LORD\nd*, and also with men.

And there came a man of God unto Eli, and said unto him, Thus
saith the \nd LORD\nd*, Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy
father, when they were in Egypt in Pharaoh’s house?

And did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel \add to
be\add* my priest, to offer upon mine altar, to burn incense, to
wear an ephod before me? and did I give unto the house of thy father
all the offerings made by fire of the children of Israel?

Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have
commanded \add in my\add* habitation; and honourest thy sons above me, to make yourselves
fat with the chiefest of all the offerings of Israel my people?

Wherefore the \nd LORD\nd* God of Israel saith, I said indeed
\add that\add* thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk
before me for ever: but now the \nd LORD\nd* saith, Be it far from
me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise
me shall be lightly esteemed.

Behold, the days come, that I will cut off thine arm, and the
arm of thy father’s house, that there shall not be an old man in thine
house.

And thou shalt see an enemy \add in my\add* habitation, in all
\add the wealth\add* which \add God\add* shall give Israel: and there shall not be an old
man in thine house for ever.\f + \fr 2.32  \ft an enemy…: or, the affliction of the tabernacle, for all the wealth which God
would have given Israel\f*

And the man of thine, \add whom\add* I shall not cut off from mine
altar, \add shall be\add* to consume thine eyes, and to grieve thine
heart: and all the increase of thine house shall die in the flower of their
age.\f + \fr 2.33  \ft in the flower…: Heb. men\f*

And this \add shall be\add* a sign unto thee, that shall come
upon thy two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas; in one day they shall
die both of them.

And I will raise me up a faithful priest, \add that\add* shall
do according to \add that\add* which \add is\add* in mine heart and in my
mind: and I will build him a sure house; and he shall walk before
mine anointed for ever.

And it shall come to pass, \add that\add* every one that is
left in thine house shall come \add and\add* crouch to him for a
piece of silver and a morsel of bread, and shall say, Put me, I pray thee, into
one of the priests’ offices, that I may eat a piece of bread.\f + \fr 2.36 
\ft Put: Heb. Join\f*\f + \fr 2.36  \ft one of…: or, somewhat about the
priesthood\f*

And the child Samuel ministered unto the 
d LORD
d* before
Eli. And the word of the 
d LORD
d* was precious in those days;
\add there was\add* no open vision.

And ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the \nd LORD\nd*,
where the ark of God \add was\add*, and Samuel was laid down \add to
sleep;\add*

That the \nd LORD\nd* called Samuel: and he answered, Here
\add am\add* I.

And he ran unto Eli, and said, Here \add am\add* I; for thou
calledst me. And he said, I called not; lie down again. And he went
and lay down.

And the \nd LORD\nd* called yet again, Samuel. And Samuel arose
and went to Eli, and said, Here \add am\add* I; for thou didst call
me. And he answered, I called not, my son; lie down again.

Now Samuel did not yet know the \nd LORD\nd*, neither was the
word of the \nd LORD\nd* yet revealed unto him.\f + \fr 3.7  \ft Now…: or, Thus did Samuel before he knew the
\+nd LORD\+nd*, and before the word of the \+nd LORD\+nd* was revealed unto
him\f*

And the 
d LORD
d* called Samuel again the third time. And he

that he may go again to his place which thou hast appointed him, and let him not go
down with us to battle, lest in the battle he be an adversary to us: for wherewith should he
reconcile himself unto his master? \add should it\add* not \add be\add*
with the heads of these men?

\add Is\add* not this David, of whom they sang one to another in
dances, saying, Saul slew his thousands, and David his ten thousands?

Then Achish called David, and said unto him, Surely, \add as\add*
the \nd LORD\nd* liveth, thou hast been upright, and thy going out
and thy coming in with me in the host \add is\add* good in my sight:
for I have not found evil in thee since the day of thy coming unto me unto this
day: nevertheless the lords favour thee not.\f + \fr 29.6  \ft the lords…: Heb. thou art not good in the eyes of the
lords\f*

Wherefore now return, and go in peace, that thou displease
not the lords of the Philistines.\f + \fr 29.7  \ft displease…: Heb. do not evil in the eyes of the
lords\f*

And David said unto Achish, But what have I done? and what hast thou
found in thy servant so long as I have been with thee unto this day,
that I may not go fight against the enemies of my lord the king?\f + \fr 29.8 
\ft with…: Heb. before thee\f*

And Achish answered and said to David, I know that thou \add art\add*
good in my sight, as an angel of God: notwithstanding the princes
of the Philistines have said, He shall not go up with us to the battle.

Wherefore now rise up early in the morning with thy master’s
servants that are come with thee: and as soon as ye be up early in the
morning, and have light, depart.

So David and his men rose up early to depart in the morning,
to return into the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went
up to Jezreel.

And had taken the women captives, that \add were\add* therein: they
slew not any, either great or small, but carried \add them\add* away,
and went on their way.

So David and his men came to the city, and, behold, \add it
was\add* burned with fire; and their wives, and their sons, and their
daughters, were taken captives.

Then David and the people that \add were\add* with him lifted
up their voice and wept, until they had no more power to weep.

And David’s two wives were taken captives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess,
and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

And David was greatly distressed; for the people spake of stoning
him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his
sons and for his daughters: but David encouraged himself in the \nd LORD\nd*
his God.\f + \fr 30.6  \ft grieved: Heb. bitter\f*

And David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech’s son, I pray thee, bring me
hither the ephod. And Abiathar brought thither the ephod to David.

And David enquired at the \nd LORD\nd*, saying, Shall I pursue
after this troop? shall I overtake them? And he answered him, Pursue:
for thou shalt surely overtake \add them\add*, and without fail recover
\add all\add*.

So David went, he and the six hundred men that \add were\add*
with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those that were left
behind stayed.

But David pursued, he and four hundred men: for two hundred
abode behind, which were so faint that they could not go over the
brook Besor.

And they gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of
raisins: and when he had eaten, his spirit came again to him: for he had
eaten no bread, nor drunk \add any\add* water, three days and three
nights.

And David said unto him, To whom \add belongest\add* thou? and whence
\add art\add* thou? And he said, I \add am\add* a young man of Egypt,
servant to an Amalekite; and my master left me, because three days
agone I fell sick.

We made an invasion \add upon\add* the south of the Cherethites, and upon
\add the coast\add* which \add belongeth\add* to Judah, and upon the
south of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire.

And David said to him, Canst thou bring me down to this company?
And he said, Swear unto me by God, that thou wilt neither kill me,
nor deliver  me into the hands of my master, and I will bring thee
down to this company.

And when he had brought him down, behold, \add they were\add*
spread abroad upon all the earth, eating and drinking, and dancing,
because of all the great spoil that they had taken out of the land
of the Philistines, and out of the land of Judah.

And David smote them from the twilight even unto the evening
of the next day: and there escaped not a man of them, save four hundred
young men, which rode upon camels, and fled.\f + \fr 30.17  \ft the next…: Heb. their
morrow\f*

And David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away:
and David rescued his two wives.

And there was nothing lacking to them, neither small nor great,
neither sons nor daughters, neither spoil, nor any \add thing\add*
that they had taken to them: David recovered  all.

And David took all the flocks and the herds, \add which\add*
they drave before those \add other\add* cattle, and said, This \add is\add*
David’s spoil.

And David came to the two hundred men, which were so faint
that they could not follow David, whom they had made also to abide
at the brook Besor: and they went forth to meet David, and to meet
the people that \add were\add* with him: and when David came near
to the people, he saluted them.\f + \fr 30.21  \ft saluted…: or, asked them how they
did\f*

Then answered all the wicked men and \add men\add* of Belial,
of those that went with David, and said, Because they went not with us, we will not
give them \add ought\add* of the spoil that we have recovered, save to every
man his wife and his children, that they may lead \add them\add*
away, and depart.\f + \fr 30.22  \ft those: Heb. men\f*

Then said David, Ye shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the
\nd LORD\nd* hath given us, who hath preserved us, and delivered
the company that came against us into our hand.

For who will hearken unto you in this matter? but as his part
\add is\add* that goeth down to the battle, so \add shall\add* his
part \add be\add* that tarrieth by the stuff: they shall part alike.

And it was \add so\add* from that day forward, that he made
it a statute and an ordinance for Israel unto this day.\f + \fr 30.25 
\ft forward: Heb. and forward\f*

And when David came to Ziklag, he sent of the spoil unto the
elders of Judah, \add even\add* to his friends, saying, Behold a
present for you of the spoil of the enemies of the \nd LORD\nd*;\f + \fr 30.26 
\ft present: Heb. blessing\f*

To \add  them\add* which \add were\add* in Beth-el, and to
\add them\add* which \add were\add* in south Ramoth, and to \add them\add* which
\add were\add* in Jattir,

And to \add them\add* which \add were\add* in Aroer, and to
\add them\add* which \add were\add* in Siphmoth, and to \add them\add* which
\add were\add* in Eshtemoa,

And to \add them\add* which \add were\add* in Rachal, and to
\add them\add* which \add were\add* in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to
\add them\add* which \add were\add* in the cities of the Kenites,

And to \add them\add* which \add were\add* in Hormah, and to
\add them\add* which \add were\add* in Chor-ashan, and to \add them\add* which
\add were\add* in Athach,

And to \add them\add* which \add were\add* in Hebron, and to all the
places where David himself and his men were wont to haunt.

Now the Philistines fought against Israel: and the men of Israel
fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa.\f + \fr 31.1 
\ft slain: or, wounded\f*

And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit
him; and he was sore wounded of the archers.\f + \fr 31.3  \ft and the archers: Heb. and the shooters, men with
bows\f*\f + \fr 31.3  \ft hit…: Heb. found him\f*

Then said Saul unto his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me
through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through,
and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid.
Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell upon it.\f + \fr 31.4  \ft abuse…: or, mock
me\f*

And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon his
sword, and died with him.

So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armourbearer, and all his
men, that same day together.

And when the men of Israel that \add were\add* on the other
side of the valley, and \add they\add* that \add were\add* on the other
side Jordan, saw that the men of Israel fled, and that Saul and his
sons were dead, they forsook the cities, and fled; and the Philistines
came and dwelt in them.

And it came to pass on the morrow, when the Philistines came
to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his three sons fallen
in mount Gilboa.

And they cut off his head, and stripped off his armour, and
sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to publish \add it
in\add* the house of their idols, and among the people.

And they put his armour in the house of Ashtaroth: and they
fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.

And when the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard of that which the
Philistines had done to Saul;\f + \fr 31.11  \ft of that: or, concerning him
that\f*

All the valiant men arose, and went all night, and took the
body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan,
and came to Jabesh, and burnt them there.

And they took their bones, and buried \add them\add* under a
tree at Jabesh, and fasted seven days.

verses.text:
It came even to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man
came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes rent, and earth upon his
head: and \add so\add* it was, when he came to David, that he fell
to the earth, and did obeisance.

And David said unto him, From whence comest thou? And he said
unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.

And David said unto him, How went the matter? I pray thee,
tell me. And he answered, That the people are fled from the battle,
and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan
his son are dead also.\f + \fr 1.4  \ft How…: Heb. What was, etc\f*

And David said unto the young man that told him, How knowest
thou that Saul and Jonathan his son be dead?

And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance
upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear; and, lo, the
chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.

And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called unto me. And I
answered, Here \add am\add* I.\f + \fr 1.7  \ft Here…: Heb. Behold
me\f*

And he said unto me, Who \add art\add* thou? And I answered him, I
\add am\add* an Amalekite.

He said unto me again, Stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay
me: for anguish is come upon me, because my life \add is\add* yet whole in
me.\f + \fr 1.9  \ft anguish…: or, my coat of mail (or, my embroidered coat) hindereth me, that my,
etc\f*

So I stood upon him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not
live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that \add was\add*
upon his head, and the bracelet that \add was\add* on his arm, and have
brought them hither unto my lord.

Then David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the
men that \add were\add* with him:

And they mourned, and wept, and fasted until even, for Saul,
and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the \nd LORD\nd*,
and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword.

And David said unto the young man that told him, Whence \add art\add*
thou? And he answered, I \add am\add* the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.

And David said unto him, How wast thou not afraid to stretch
forth thine hand to destroy the \nd LORD’s\nd* anointed?

And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near,
\add and\add* fall upon him. And he smote him that he died.

And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over
Jonathan his son:

(Also he bade them teach the children of Judah \add the use
of\add* the bow: behold, \add it is\add* written in the book of Jasher.)\f + \fr 1.18 
\ft of Jasher: or, of the upright\f*

The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places: how are the
mighty fallen!

Tell \add it\add* not in Gath, publish \add it\add* not in the
streets of Askelon; lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice,
lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.

Ye mountains of Gilboa, \add let there be\add* no dew, neither
\add let there be\add* rain, upon you, nor fields of offerings: for there the
shield of the mighty is vilely cast away, the shield of Saul, \add as though he
had\add* not \add been\add* anointed with oil.

From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the
bow of Jonathan turned not back, and the sword of Saul returned not
empty.

Saul and Jonathan \add were\add* lovely and pleasant in their
lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter
than eagles, they were stronger than lions.\f + \fr 1.23  \ft pleasant: or,
sweet\f*

Ye daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in
scarlet, with \add other\add* delights, who put on ornaments of gold
upon your apparel.

How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan,
\add thou wast\add* slain in thine high places.

I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant
hast thou been unto me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the
love of women.
How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!

And it came to pass after this, that David enquired of the
\nd LORD\nd*, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah?
And the \nd LORD\nd* said unto him, Go up. And David said, Whither shall I go
up? And he said, Unto Hebron.

So David went up thither, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the
Jezreelitess, and Abigail Nabal’s wife the Carmelite.

And his men that \add were\add* with him did David bring up,
every man with his household: and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.

And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king
over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, \add That\add*
the men of Jabesh-gilead \add were they\add* that buried Saul.

And David sent messengers unto the men of Jabesh-gilead, and
said unto them, Blessed \add be\add* ye of the \nd LORD\nd*, that ye have
shewed this kindness unto your lord, \add even\add* unto Saul, and have
buried him.

And now the \nd LORD\nd* shew kindness and truth unto you: and I also will
requite you this kindness, because ye have done this thing.

Therefore now let your hands be strengthened, and be ye valiant:
for your master Saul is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed
me king over them.\f + \fr 2.7  \ft be ye…: Heb. be ye the sons of
valour\f*

But Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul’s host, took Ish-bosheth
the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim;\f + \fr 2.8  \ft Saul’s host: Heb. the host which was
Saul’s\f*\f + \fr 2.8  \ft Ish-bosheth: or, Esh-baal\f*

And made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over
Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.

Ish-bosheth Saul’s son \add was\add* forty years old when he began to
reign over Israel, and reigned two years. But the house of Judah
followed David.

And the time that David was king in Hebron over the house
of Judah was seven years and six months.\f + \fr 2.11  \ft time: Heb. number of
days\f*

And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ish-bosheth
the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went
out, and met together by the pool of Gibeon: and they sat down, the one on the one side of the
pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.\f + \fr 2.13 
\ft together: Heb. them together\f*

And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men now arise, and play
before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.

Then there arose and went over by number twelve of Benjamin, which
\add pertained\add* to Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the
servants of David.

And they caught every one his fellow by the head, and \add thrust\add*
his sword in his fellow’s side; so they fell down together: wherefore that
place was called Helkath-hazzurim, which \add is\add* in Gibeon.\f + \fr 2.16 
\ft Helkath-hazzurim: that is, The field of strong men\f*

And there was a very sore battle that day; and Abner was beaten,
and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.

And there were three sons of Zeruiah there, Joab, and Abishai,
and Asahel: and Asahel \add was as\add* light of foot as a wild roe.\f + \fr 2.18 
\ft of foot: Heb. of his feet\f*\f + \fr 2.18  \ft as a wild…: Heb. as one of the roes that is in the
field\f*

And Asahel pursued after Abner; and in going he turned not to the right
hand nor to the left from following Abner.\f + \fr 2.19  \ft from…: Heb. from after
Abner\f*

Then Abner looked behind him, and said, \add Art\add* thou
Asahel? And he answered, I \add am\add*.

And Abner said to him, Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy
left, and lay thee hold on one of the young men, and take thee his
armour. But Asahel would not turn aside from following of him.\f + \fr 2.21 
\ft armour: or, spoil\f*

And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn thee aside from following
me: wherefore should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold
up my face to Joab thy brother?

Howbeit he refused to turn aside: wherefore Abner with the hinder
end of the spear smote him under the fifth \add rib\add*, that the
spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same
place: and it came to pass, \add that\add* as many as came to the
place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.

Joab also and Abishai pursued after Abner: and the sun went
down when they were come to the hill of Ammah, that \add lieth\add*
before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.

And the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together
after Abner, and became one troop, and stood on the top of an hill.

Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour
for ever? knowest thou not that it will be bitterness in the latter
end? how long shall it be then, ere thou bid the people return from
following their brethren?

And Joab said, \add As\add* God liveth, unless thou hadst
spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone up every one
from following his brother.\f + \fr 2.27  \ft in the…: Heb. from the
morning\f*\f + \fr 2.27  \ft gone…: or, gone away\f*

So Joab blew a trumpet, and all the people stood still, and
pursued after Israel no more, neither fought they any more.

And Abner and his men walked all that night through the plain,
and passed over Jordan, and went through all Bithron, and they came
to Mahanaim.

And Joab returned from following Abner: and when he had gathered
all the people together, there lacked of David’s servants nineteen
men and Asahel.

But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin, and of
Abner’s men, \add so that\add* three hundred and threescore men died.

And they took up Asahel, and buried him in the sepulchre
of his father, which \add was in\add* Beth-lehem. And Joab and his
men went all night, and they came to Hebron at break of day.

Now there was long war between the house of Saul and the house
of David: but David waxed stronger and stronger, and the house of
Saul waxed weaker and weaker.

And unto David were sons born in Hebron: and his firstborn
was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;

And the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth,
Shephatiah the son of Abital;

And the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah David’s wife. These were born
to David in Hebron.

And it came to pass, while there was war between the house
of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong for the
house of Saul.

And Saul had a concubine, whose name \add was\add* Rizpah,
the daughter of Aiah: and \add Ish-bosheth\add* said to Abner, Wherefore hast thou gone
in unto my father’s concubine?

Then was Abner very wroth for the words of Ish-bosheth, and
said, \add Am\add* I a dog’s head, which against Judah do shew kindness
this day unto the house of Saul thy father, to his brethren, and to his
friends, and have not delivered thee into the hand of David, that thou
chargest me to day with a fault concerning this woman?

So do God to Abner, and more also, except, as the \nd LORD\nd*
hath sworn to David, even so I do to him;

To translate the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set
up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to
Beer-sheba.
And he could not answer Abner a word again, because he feared him.

And Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, Whose
\add is\add* the land? saying \add also\add*, Make thy league with me, and, behold, my
hand \add shall be\add* with thee, to bring about all Israel unto thee.

And he said, Well; I will make a league with thee: but one
thing I require of thee, that is, Thou shalt not see my face, except thou
first bring Michal Saul’s daughter, when thou comest to see my face.\f + \fr 3.13 
\ft that is: Heb. saying\f*

And David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth Saul’s son, saying,
Deliver \add me\add* my wife Michal, which I espoused to me for an
hundred foreskins of the Philistines.

And Ish-bosheth sent, and took her from \add her\add* husband,
\add even\add* from Phaltiel the son of Laish.\f + \fr 3.15  \ft Phaltiel: also called,
Phalti\f*

And her husband went with her along weeping behind her to
Bahurim. Then said Abner unto him, Go, return. And he returned.\f + \fr 3.16 
\ft along…: Heb. going and weeping\f*

And Abner had communication with the elders of Israel, saying,
Ye sought for David in times past \add to be\add* king over you:\f + \fr 3.17 
\ft in times…: Heb. both yesterday and the third day\f*

Now then do \add it:\add* for the \nd LORD\nd* hath spoken
of David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save my
people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the
hand of all their enemies.

And Abner also spake in the ears of Benjamin: and Abner went
also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good
to Israel, and that seemed good to the whole house of Benjamin.

So Abner came to David to Hebron, and twenty men with him. And
David made Abner and the men that \add were\add* with him a feast.

And Abner said unto David, I will arise and go, and will gather
all Israel unto my lord the king, that they may make a league with thee, and that thou mayest
reign over all that thine heart desireth. And David sent Abner away;
and he went in peace.

And, behold, the servants of David and Joab came from \add pursuing\add*
a troop, and brought in a great spoil with them: but Abner \add was\add*
not with David in Hebron; for he had sent him away, and he was gone
in peace.

When Joab and all the host that \add was\add* with him were
come, they told Joab, saying, Abner the son of Ner came to the king,
and he hath sent him away, and he is gone in peace.

Then Joab came to the king, and said, What hast thou done?
behold, Abner came unto thee; why \add is\add* it \add that\add*
thou hast sent him away, and he is quite gone?

Thou knowest Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive
thee, and to know thy going out and thy coming in, and to know all that thou
doest.

And when Joab was come out from David, he sent messengers
after Abner, which brought him again from the well of Sirah: but
David knew \add it\add* not.

And when Abner was returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside
in the gate to speak with him quietly, and smote him there under the
fifth \add rib\add*, that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.\f + \fr 3.27 
\ft quietly: or, peaceably\f*

And afterward when David heard \add it\add*, he said, I and my
kingdom \add are\add* guiltless before the \nd LORD\nd* for ever
from the blood of Abner the son of Ner:\f + \fr 3.28  \ft blood: Heb.
bloods\f*

Let it rest on the head of Joab, and on all his father’s house;
and let there not fail from the house of Joab one that hath an issue,
or that is a leper, or that leaneth on a staff, or that falleth on the
sword, or that lacketh bread.\f + \fr 3.29  \ft fail: Heb. be cut
off\f*

So Joab and Abishai his brother slew Abner, because he had
slain their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.

And David said to Joab, and to all the people that \add were\add*
with him, Rend your clothes, and gird you with sackcloth, and mourn
before Abner. And king David \add himself\add* followed the bier.\f + \fr 3.31 
\ft bier: Heb. bed\f*

And they buried Abner in Hebron: and the king lifted up his
voice, and wept at the grave of Abner; and all the people wept.

And the king lamented over Abner, and said, Died Abner as a
fool dieth?

Thy hands \add were\add* not bound, nor thy feet put into
fetters: as a man falleth before wicked men, \add so\add* fellest
thou. And all the people wept again over him.\f + \fr 3.34  \ft wicked…: Heb. children of
iniquity\f*

And when all the people came to cause David to eat meat while it was
yet day, David sware, saying, So do God to me, and more also, if I
taste bread, or ought else, till the sun be down.

And all the people took notice \add of it\add*, and it pleased
them: as whatsoever the king did pleased all the people.\f + \fr 3.36 
\ft pleased them: Heb. was good in their eyes\f*

For all the people and all Israel understood that day that it was not of the
king to slay Abner the son of Ner.

And the king said unto his servants, Know ye not that there is a
prince and a great man fallen this day in Israel?

And I \add am\add* this day weak, though anointed king; and these
men the sons of Zeruiah \add be\add* too hard for me: the \nd LORD\nd*
shall reward the doer of evil according to his wickedness.\f + \fr 3.39 
\ft weak: Heb. tender\f*

And when Saul’s son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his
hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.

And Saul’s son had two men \add that were\add* captains of
