verses.text:
And Solomon the son of David was strengthened in his kingdom,
and the \nd LORD\nd* his God \add was\add* with him, and magnified
him exceedingly.

Then Solomon spake unto all Israel, to the captains of thousands
and of hundreds, and to the judges, and to every governor in all
Israel, the chief of the fathers.

So Solomon, and all the congregation with him, went to the high
place that \add was\add* at Gibeon; for there was the tabernacle
of the congregation of God, which Moses the servant of the \nd LORD\nd*
had made in the wilderness.

But the ark of God had David brought up from Kirjath-jearim to
\add the place which\add* David had prepared for it: for he had pitched
a tent for it at Jerusalem.

Moreover the brasen altar, that Bezaleel the son of Uri, the
son of Hur, had made, he put before the tabernacle of the \nd LORD\nd*:
and Solomon and the congregation sought unto it.\f + \fr 1.5  \ft he put: or, was
there\f*

And Solomon went up thither to the brasen altar before the
\nd LORD\nd*, which \add was\add* at the tabernacle of the congregation,
and offered a thousand burnt offerings upon it.

In that night did God appear unto Solomon, and said unto him,
Ask what I shall give thee.

And Solomon said unto God, Thou hast shewed great mercy unto
David my father, and hast made me to reign in his stead.

Now, O \nd LORD\nd* God, let thy promise unto David my father
be established: for thou hast made me king over a people like the
dust of the earth in multitude.\f + \fr 1.9  \ft like…: Heb. much as the dust of the
earth\f*

Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come
in before this people: for who can judge this thy people, \add that is
so\add* great?

And God said to Solomon, Because this was in thine heart,
and thou hast not asked riches, wealth, or honour, nor the life of thine
enemies, neither yet hast asked long life; but hast asked wisdom
and knowledge for thyself, that thou mayest judge my people, over whom I have made thee
king:

Wisdom and knowledge \add is\add* granted unto thee; and I will
give thee riches, and wealth, and honour, such as none of the kings have had that
\add have been\add* before thee, neither shall there any after thee have the like.

Then Solomon came \add from his journey\add* to the high
place that \add was\add* at Gibeon to Jerusalem, from before the
tabernacle of the congregation, and reigned over Israel.

And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen: and he had a thousand
and four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, which he
placed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem.

And the king made silver and gold at Jerusalem \add as plenteous\add*
as stones, and cedar trees made he as the sycomore trees that \add are\add*
in the vale for abundance.\f + \fr 1.15  \ft made: Heb. gave\f*

And Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt, and linen yarn:
the king’s merchants received the linen yarn at a price.\f + \fr 1.16 
\ft Solomon…: Heb. the going forth of the horses which was Solomon’s\f*

And they fetched up, and brought forth out of Egypt a chariot
for six hundred \add shekels\add* of silver, and an horse for an
hundred and fifty: and so brought they out \add horses\add* for all the
kings of the Hittites, and for the kings of Syria, by their means.\f + \fr 1.17 
\ft means: Heb. hand\f*

And Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the
\nd LORD\nd*, and an house for his kingdom.

And Solomon told out threescore and ten thousand men to bear
burdens, and fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three
thousand and six hundred to oversee them.

And Solomon sent to Huram the king of Tyre, saying, As thou didst
deal with David my father, and didst send him cedars to build him an
house to dwell therein, \add even so deal with me\add*.\f + \fr 2.3 
\ft Huram: or, Hiram\f*

Behold, I build an house to the name of the \nd LORD\nd* my
God, to dedicate \add it\add* to him, \add and\add* to burn before
him sweet incense, and for the continual shewbread, and for the burnt
offerings morning and evening, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons,
and on the solemn feasts of the \nd LORD\nd* our God. This \add is an
ordinance\add* for ever to Israel.\f + \fr 2.4  \ft sweet…: Heb. incense of
spices\f*

And the house which I build \add is\add* great: for great \add is\add*
our God above all gods.

But who is able to build him an house, seeing the heaven and
heaven of heavens cannot contain him? who \add am\add* I then, that I should
build him an house, save only to burn sacrifice before him?\f + \fr 2.6 
\ft is able: Heb. hath retained, or, obtained strength\f*

Send me now therefore a man cunning to work in gold, and in
silver, and in brass, and in iron, and in purple, and crimson, and
blue, and that can skill to grave with the cunning men that \add are\add*
with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father did provide.\f + \fr 2.7 
\ft to grave: Heb. to grave gravings\f*

Send me also cedar trees, fir trees, and algum trees, out of
Lebanon: for I know that thy servants can skill to cut timber in
Lebanon; and, behold, my servants \add shall be\add* with thy servants,\f + \fr 2.8 
\ft algum: also called, almuggim\f*

Even to prepare me timber in abundance: for the house which I am about to
build \add shall be\add* wonderful great.\f + \fr 2.9  \ft wonderful…: Heb. great and
wonderful\f*

And, behold, I will give to thy servants, the hewers that
cut timber, twenty thousand measures of beaten wheat, and twenty
thousand measures of barley, and twenty thousand baths of wine, and
twenty thousand baths of oil.

Then Huram the king of Tyre answered in writing, which he
sent to Solomon, Because the \nd LORD\nd* hath loved his people,
he hath made thee king over them.

Huram said moreover, Blessed \add be\add* the \nd LORD\nd*
God of Israel, that made heaven and earth, who hath given to David
the king a wise son, endued with prudence and understanding, that might
build an house for the \nd LORD\nd*, and an house for his kingdom.\f + \fr 2.12 
\ft endued…: Heb. knowing prudence and understanding\f*

And now I have sent a cunning man, endued with understanding,
of Huram my father’s,

The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father
\add was\add* a man of Tyre, skilful to work in gold, and in silver,
in brass, in iron, in stone, and in timber, in purple, in blue, and in fine
linen, and in crimson; also to grave any manner of graving, and to find
out every device which shall be put to him, with thy cunning men,
and with the cunning men of my lord David thy father.

Now therefore the wheat, and the barley, the oil, and the
wine, which my lord hath spoken of, let him send unto his servants:

And we will cut wood out of Lebanon, as much as thou shalt
need: and we will bring it to thee in floats by sea to Joppa; and thou shalt carry it
up to Jerusalem.\f + \fr 2.16  \ft as much…: Heb according to all thy
need\f*\f + \fr 2.16  \ft Joppa: Heb. Japho\f*

And Solomon numbered all the strangers that \add were\add*
in the land of Israel, after the numbering wherewith David his father
had numbered them; and they were found an hundred and fifty thousand
and three thousand and six hundred.\f + \fr 2.17  \ft the strangers: Heb. the men the
strangers\f*

And he set threescore and ten thousand of them \add to be\add*
bearers of burdens, and fourscore thousand \add to be\add* hewers
in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred overseers to
set the people a work.

Then Solomon began to build the house of the \nd LORD\nd* at
Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where \add the \+nd Lord\+nd*\add* appeared
unto David his father, in the place that David had prepared in the
threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite.\f + \fr 3.1  \ft where…: or, which was seen of David his
father\f*\f + \fr 3.1  \ft Ornan: also called, Araunah\f*

And he began to build in the second \add day\add* of the second
month, in the fourth year of his reign.

Now these \add are the things wherein\add* Solomon was instructed
for the building of the house of God. The length by cubits after the
first measure \add was\add* threescore cubits, and the breadth twenty
cubits.\f + \fr 3.3  \ft instructed: Heb. founded\f*

And the porch that \add was\add* in the front \add of the house\add*,
the length \add of it was\add* according to the breadth of the house,
twenty cubits, and the height \add was\add* an hundred and twenty:
and he overlaid it within with pure gold.

And the greater house he cieled with fir tree, which he overlaid
with fine gold, and set thereon palm trees and chains.

And he garnished the house with precious stones for beauty:
and the gold \add was\add* gold of Parvaim.\f + \fr 3.6  \ft garnished: Heb.
covered\f*

He overlaid also the house, the beams, the posts, and the walls
thereof, and the doors thereof, with gold; and graved cherubims on the
walls.

And he made the most holy house, the length whereof \add was\add*
according to the breadth of the house, twenty cubits, and the breadth
thereof twenty cubits: and he overlaid it with fine gold, \add amounting\add*
to six hundred talents.

And the weight of the nails \add was\add* fifty shekels of
gold. And he overlaid the upper chambers with gold.

And in the most holy house he made two cherubims of image
work, and overlaid them with gold.\f + \fr 3.10  \ft image…: or, (as some think) of moveable
work\f*

And the wings of the cherubims \add were\add* twenty cubits
long: one wing \add of the one cherub was\add* five cubits, reaching
to the wall of the house: and the other wing \add was likewise\add*
five cubits, reaching to the wing of the other cherub.

And \add one\add* wing of the other cherub \add was\add* five
cubits, reaching to the wall of the house: and the other wing \add was\add*
five cubits \add also\add*, joining to the wing of the other cherub.

The wings of these cherubims spread themselves forth twenty
cubits: and they stood on their feet, and their faces \add were\add*
inward.\f + \fr 3.13  \ft inward: or, toward the house\f*

And he made the vail \add of\add* blue, and purple, and crimson,
and fine linen, and wrought cherubims thereon.\f + \fr 3.14  \ft wrought: Heb. caused to
ascend\f*

Also he made before the house two pillars of thirty and five
cubits high, and the chapiter that \add was\add* on the top of each of them
\add was\add* five cubits.\f + \fr 3.15  \ft high: Heb. long\f*

And he made chains, \add as\add* in the oracle, and put \add them\add*
on the heads of the pillars; and made an hundred pomegranates, and
put \add them\add* on the chains.

And he reared up the pillars before the temple, one on the right
hand, and the other on the left; and called the name of that on the right
hand Jachin, and the name of that on the left Boaz.\f + \fr 3.17 
\ft Jachin: that is, He shall establish\f*\f + \fr 3.17  \ft Boaz: that is, In it is
strength\f*

Moreover he made an altar of brass, twenty cubits the length
thereof, and twenty cubits the breadth thereof, and ten cubits the
height thereof.

Also he made a molten sea of ten cubits from brim to brim,
round in compass, and five cubits the height thereof; and a line
of thirty cubits did compass it round about.\f + \fr 4.2  \ft from…: Heb. from his brim to his
brim\f*

And under it \add was\add* the similitude of oxen, which did
compass it round about: ten in a cubit, compassing the sea round
about. Two rows of oxen \add were\add* cast, when it was cast.

It stood upon twelve oxen, three looking toward the north,
and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south,
and three looking toward the east: and the sea \add was set\add*
above upon them, and all their hinder parts \add were\add* inward.

And the thickness of it \add was\add* an handbreadth, and the
brim of it like the work of the brim of a cup, with flowers of lilies;
\add and\add* it received and held three thousand baths.\f + \fr 4.5 
\ft with flowers…: or, like a lilyflower\f*

He made also ten lavers, and put five on the right hand, and
five on the left, to wash in them: such things as they offered for the burnt
offering they washed in them; but the sea \add was\add* for the priests
to wash in.\f + \fr 4.6  \ft such…: Heb. the work of burnt offering\f*

And he made ten candlesticks of gold according to their form,
and set \add them\add* in the temple, five on the right hand, and
five on the left.

He made also ten tables, and placed \add them\add* in the temple,
five on the right side, and five on the left. And he made an hundred
basons of gold.\f + \fr 4.8  \ft basons: or, bowls\f*

Furthermore he made the court of the priests, and the great
court, and doors for the court, and overlaid the doors of them with
brass.

And he set the sea on the right side of the east end, over
against the south.

And Huram made the pots, and the shovels, and the basons.
And Huram finished the work that he was to make for king Solomon
for the house of God;\f + \fr 4.11  \ft basons: or, bowls\f*\f + \fr 4.11 
\ft finished: Heb. finished to make\f*

\add To wit\add*, the two pillars, and the pommels, and the
chapiters \add which were\add* on the top of the two pillars, and the
two wreaths to cover the two pommels of the chapiters which \add were\add*
on the top of the pillars;

And four hundred pomegranates on the two wreaths; two rows
of pomegranates on each wreath, to cover the two pommels of the chapiters which
\add were\add* upon the pillars.\f + \fr 4.13  \ft upon: Heb. upon the face
of\f*

He made also bases, and lavers made he upon the bases;\f + \fr 4.14 
\ft lavers: or, caldrons\f*
One sea, and twelve oxen under it.

The pots also, and the shovels, and the fleshhooks, and all their
instruments, did Huram his father make to king Solomon for the house
of the \nd LORD\nd* of bright brass.\f + \fr 4.16  \ft bright: Heb. made bright, or,
scoured\f*

In the plain of Jordan did the king cast them, in the clay
ground between Succoth and Zeredathah.\f + \fr 4.17  \ft clay…: Heb. thicknesses of the
ground\f*

Thus Solomon made all these vessels in great abundance: for the
weight of the brass could not be found out.

And Solomon made all the vessels that \add were for\add*
the house of God, the golden altar also, and the tables whereon the
shewbread \add was set;\add*

Moreover the candlesticks with their lamps, that they should
burn after the manner before the oracle, of pure gold;

And the flowers, and the lamps, and the tongs, \add made he
of\add* gold, \add and\add* that perfect gold;\f + \fr 4.21  \ft perfect…: Heb. perfections of
gold\f*

And the snuffers, and the basons, and the spoons, and the
censers, \add of\add* pure gold: and the entry of the house, the
inner doors thereof for the most holy \add place\add*, and the doors
of the house of the temple, \add were of\add* gold.\f + \fr 4.22 
\ft basons: or, bowls\f*

Thus all the work that Solomon made for the house of the \nd LORD\nd*
was finished: and Solomon brought in \add all\add* the things that
David his father had dedicated; and the silver, and the gold, and all the
instruments, put he among the treasures of the house of God.

Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads
of the tribes, the chief of the fathers of the children of Israel,
unto Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the \nd LORD\nd*
out of the city of David, which \add is\add* Zion.

Wherefore all the men of Israel assembled themselves unto the
king in the feast which \add was\add* in the seventh month.

And all the elders of Israel came; and the Levites took up
the ark.

And they brought up the ark, and the tabernacle of the congregation,
and all the holy vessels that \add were\add* in the tabernacle, these did the
priests \add and\add* the Levites bring up.

Also king Solomon, and all the congregation of Israel that were
assembled unto him before the ark, sacrificed sheep and oxen, which could not be
told nor numbered for multitude.

And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the \nd LORD\nd*
unto his place, to the oracle of the house, into the most holy \add place,
even\add* under the wings of the cherubims:

For the cherubims spread forth \add their\add* wings over the
place of the ark, and the cherubims covered the ark and the staves
thereof above.

And they drew out the staves \add of the ark\add*, that the
ends of the staves were seen from the ark before the oracle; but they were not
seen without. And there it is unto this day.\f + \fr 5.9  \ft there…: or, they are
there\f*

\add There was\add* nothing in the ark save the two tables
which Moses put \add therein\add* at Horeb, when the \nd LORD\nd*
made \add a covenant\add* with the children of Israel, when they came
out of Egypt.\f + \fr 5.10  \ft when the \+nd LORD\+nd*: or, where,
etc\f*

And it came to pass, when the priests were come out of the
holy \add place:\add* (for all the priests \add that were\add* present
were sanctified, \add and\add* did not \add then\add* wait by course:\f + \fr 5.11 
\ft present: Heb. found\f*

Also the Levites \add which were\add* the singers, all of them of
Asaph, of Heman, of Jeduthun, with their sons and their brethren,
\add being\add* arrayed in white linen, having cymbals and psalteries
and harps, stood at the east end of the altar, and with them an hundred
and twenty priests sounding with trumpets:)

It came even to pass, as the trumpeters and singers \add were\add*
as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the
\nd LORD\nd*; and when they lifted up \add their\add* voice with the
trumpets and cymbals and instruments of musick, and praised the \nd LORD\nd*,
\add saying\add*, For \add he is\add* good; for his mercy \add endureth\add*
for ever: that \add then\add* the house was filled with a cloud,
\add even\add* the house of the \nd LORD\nd*;

So that the priests could not stand to minister by reason
of the cloud: for the glory of the \nd LORD\nd* had filled the house
of God.

Then said Solomon, The \nd LORD\nd* hath said that he would
dwell in the thick darkness.

But I have built an house of habitation for thee, and a place
for thy dwelling for ever.

And the king turned his face, and blessed the whole congregation
of Israel: and all the congregation of Israel stood.

And he said, Blessed \add be\add* the \nd LORD\nd* God of Israel,
who hath with his hands fulfilled \add that\add* which he spake with his
mouth to my father David, saying,

Since the day that I brought forth my people out of the land
of Egypt I chose no city among all the tribes of Israel to build
an house in, that my name might be there; neither chose I any man
to be a ruler over my people Israel:

But I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there; and have
chosen David to be over my people Israel.

Now it was in the heart of David my father to build an house
for the name of the \nd LORD\nd* God of Israel.

But the \nd LORD\nd* said to David my father, Forasmuch as it was in thine
heart to build an house for my name, thou didst well in that it was in thine
heart:

Notwithstanding thou shalt not build the house; but thy son
which shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house
for my name.

The 
d LORD
d* therefore hath performed his word that he hath
spoken: for I am risen up in the room of David my father, and am
set on the throne of Israel, as the 
d LORD
d* promised, and have
built the house for the name of the 
d LORD
d* God of Israel.

And in it have I put the ark, wherein \add is\add* the covenant
of the \nd LORD\nd*, that he made with the children of Israel.

And he stood before the altar of the \nd LORD\nd* in the presence of all the
congregation of Israel, and spread forth his hands:

For Solomon had made a brasen scaffold, of five cubits long,
and five cubits broad, and three cubits high, and had set it in the
midst of the court: and upon it he stood, and kneeled down upon his
knees before all the congregation of Israel, and spread forth his
hands toward heaven,\f + \fr 6.13  \ft long…: Heb. the length thereof,
etc\f*

And said, O \nd LORD\nd* God of Israel, \add there is\add*
no God like thee in the heaven, nor in the earth; which keepest covenant, and
\add shewest\add* mercy unto thy servants, that walk before thee with all their
hearts:

Thou which hast kept with thy servant David my father that which thou hast
promised him; and spakest with thy mouth, and hast fulfilled \add it\add*
with thine hand, as \add it is\add* this day.

Now therefore, O \nd LORD\nd* God of Israel, keep with thy
servant David my father that which thou hast promised him, saying,
There shall not fail thee a man in my sight to sit upon the throne
of Israel; yet so that thy children take heed to their way to walk
in my law, as thou hast walked before me.\f + \fr 6.16  \ft There…: Heb. There shall not a man be cut
off\f*

Now then, O \nd LORD\nd* God of Israel, let thy word be verified,
which thou hast spoken unto thy servant David.

But will God in very deed dwell with men on the earth? behold,
heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this
house which I have built!

Have respect therefore to the prayer of thy servant, and to his
supplication, O \nd LORD\nd* my God, to hearken unto the cry and the
prayer which thy servant prayeth before thee:

That thine eyes may be open upon this house day and night,
upon the place whereof thou hast said that thou wouldest put thy
name there; to hearken unto the prayer which thy servant prayeth
toward this place.\f + \fr 6.20  \ft toward…: or, in this place\f*

Hearken therefore unto the supplications of thy servant, and of thy
people Israel, which they shall make toward this place: hear thou from thy
dwelling place, \add even\add* from heaven; and when thou hearest,
forgive.\f + \fr 6.21  \ft make: Heb. pray\f*\f + \fr 6.21  \ft toward…: or, in this
place\f*

If a man sin against his neighbour, and an oath be laid upon him to make him
swear, and the oath come before thine altar in this house;\f + \fr 6.22 
\ft and an oath…: Heb. and he require an oath of him\f*

And if thy people Israel be put to the worse before the enemy,
because they have sinned against thee; and shall return and confess
thy name, and pray and make supplication before thee in this house;\f + \fr 6.24 
\ft be put…: or, be smitten\f*\f + \fr 6.24  \ft in: or, toward\f*

Then hear thou from the heavens, and forgive the sin of thy
people Israel, and bring them again unto the land which thou gavest
to them and to their fathers.

When the heaven is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have
sinned against thee; \add yet\add* if they pray toward this place,
and confess thy name, and turn from their sin, when thou dost afflict
them;\f + \fr 6.26  \ft toward…: or, in this place\f*

Then hear thou from heaven, and forgive the sin of thy servants,
and of thy people Israel, when thou hast taught them the good way,
wherein they should walk; and send rain upon thy land, which thou hast
given unto thy people for an inheritance.

If there be dearth in the land, if there be pestilence, if there be
blasting, or mildew, locusts, or caterpillers; if their enemies besiege
them in the cities of their land; whatsoever sore or whatsoever sickness
\add there be:\add*\f + \fr 6.28  \ft in the cities…: Heb. in the land of their
gates\f*

\add Then\add* what prayer \add or\add* what supplication
soever shall be made of any man, or of all thy people Israel, when every
one shall know his own sore and his own grief, and shall spread forth
his hands in this house:\f + \fr 6.29  \ft in: or, toward\f*\f + \fr 6.29 
\ft toward…: or, in this place\f*

Then hear thou from heaven thy dwelling place, and forgive,
and render unto every man according unto all his ways, whose heart
thou knowest; (for thou only knowest the hearts of the children of
men:)

That they may fear thee, to walk in thy ways, so long as they
live in the land which thou gavest unto our fathers.\f + \fr 6.31 
\ft so long…: Heb. all the days which\f*\f + \fr 6.31  \ft in the land: Heb. upon the face of the
land\f*

Moreover concerning the stranger, which is not of thy people
Israel, but is come from a far country for thy great name’s sake, and thy
mighty hand, and thy stretched out arm; if they come and pray in this
house;\f + \fr 6.32  \ft toward…: or, in this place\f*

Then hear thou from the heavens, \add even\add* from thy dwelling
place, and do according to all that the stranger calleth to thee for; that all
people of the earth may know thy name, and fear thee, as \add doth\add*
thy people Israel, and may know that this house which I have built
is called by thy name.\f + \fr 6.33  \ft this…: Heb. thy name is called upon this
house\f*

If thy people go out to war against their enemies by the way
that thou shalt send them, and they pray unto thee toward this city
which thou hast chosen, and the house which I have built for thy
name;

of Megiddo.

And the archers shot at king Josiah; and the king said to his
servants, Have me away; for I am sore wounded.\f + \fr 35.23  \ft wounded: Heb. made
sick\f*

His servants therefore took him out of that chariot, and put
him in the second chariot that he had; and they brought him to Jerusalem,
and he died, and was buried in \add one of\add* the sepulchres of his
fathers. And all Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.\f + \fr 35.24 
\ft in one…: or, among the sepulchres\f*

And Jeremiah lamented for Josiah: and all the singing men
and the singing women spake of Josiah in their lamentations to this
day, and made them an ordinance in Israel: and, behold, they \add are\add*
written in the lamentations.

Now the rest of the acts of Josiah, and his goodness, according to
\add that which was\add* written in the law of the \nd LORD\nd*,\f + \fr 35.26 
\ft goodness: Heb. kindnesses\f*

And his deeds, first and last, behold, they \add are\add*
written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah,
and made him king in his father’s stead in Jerusalem.

Jehoahaz \add was\add* twenty and three years old when he began to
reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.

And the king of Egypt put him down at Jerusalem, and condemned
the land in an hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.\f + \fr 36.3 
\ft put…: Heb. removed him\f*

And the king of Egypt made Eliakim his brother king over Judah
and Jerusalem, and turned his name to Jehoiakim. And Necho took Jehoahaz
his brother, and carried him to Egypt.

Jehoiakim \add was\add* twenty and five years old when he began to
reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem: and he did \add that which
was\add* evil in the sight of the \nd LORD\nd* his God.

Against him came up Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and bound
him in fetters, to carry him to Babylon.\f + \fr 36.6  \ft fetters: or,
chains\f*

Nebuchadnezzar also carried of the vessels of the house of the
\nd LORD\nd* to Babylon, and put them in his temple at Babylon.

Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and his abominations
which he did, and that which was found in him, behold, they \add are\add*
written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah: and Jehoiachin
his son reigned in his stead.\f + \fr 36.8  \ft Jehoiachin: also called, Jeconiah, or,
Coniah\f*

Jehoiachin \add was\add* eight years old when he began to
reign, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem: and he
did \add that which was\add* evil in the sight of the \nd LORD\nd*.

And when the year was expired, king Nebuchadnezzar sent, and
brought him to Babylon, with the goodly vessels of the house of the
\nd LORD\nd*, and made Zedekiah his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem.\f + \fr 36.10 
\ft when…: Heb. at the return of the year\f*\f + \fr 36.10  \ft goodly…: Heb. vessels of
desire\f*\f + \fr 36.10  \ft Zedekiah…: or, Mattaniah, his father’s
brother\f*

Zedekiah \add was\add* one and twenty years old when he began to
reign, and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.

And he did \add that which was\add* evil in the sight of the

d LORD
d* his God, \add and\add* humbled not himself before Jeremiah
the prophet \add speaking\add* from the mouth of the 
d LORD
d*.

And he also rebelled against king Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him
swear by God: but he stiffened his neck, and hardened his heart from
turning unto the \nd LORD\nd* God of Israel.

Moreover all the chief of the priests, and the people, transgressed
very much after all the abominations of the heathen; and polluted
the house of the \nd LORD\nd* which he had hallowed in Jerusalem.

And the \nd LORD\nd* God of their fathers sent to them by
his messengers, rising up betimes, and sending; because he had compassion
on his people, and on his dwelling place:\f + \fr 36.15  \ft by: Heb. by the hand
of\f*\f + \fr 36.15  \ft betimes: that is, continually and carefully\f*

But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words,
and misused his prophets, until the wrath of the \nd LORD\nd* arose
against his people, till \add there was\add* no remedy.\f + \fr 36.16 
\ft remedy: Heb. healing\f*

Therefore he brought upon them the king of the Chaldees, who
slew their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary,
and had no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man, or him that stooped for
age: he gave \add them\add* all into his hand.

And all the vessels of the house of God, great and small,
and the treasures of the house of the \nd LORD\nd*, and the treasures
of the king, and of his princes; all \add these\add* he brought to
Babylon.

And they burnt the house of God, and brake down the wall of
Jerusalem, and burnt all the palaces thereof with fire, and destroyed
all the goodly vessels thereof.

And them that had escaped from the sword carried he away to
Babylon; where they were servants to him and his sons until the reign
of the kingdom of Persia:\f + \fr 36.20  \ft them…: Heb. the remainder from the
sword\f*

To fulfil the word of the \nd LORD\nd* by the mouth of Jeremiah,
until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths: \add for\add* as long as
she lay desolate she kept sabbath, to fulfil threescore and ten years.

Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word
of the \nd LORD\nd* \add spoken\add* by the mouth of Jeremiah might be
accomplished, the \nd LORD\nd* stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king
of Persia, that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and
\add put it\add* also in writing, saying,

Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia, All the kingdoms of the earth
hath the \nd LORD\nd* God of heaven given me; and he hath charged
me to build him an house in Jerusalem, which \add is\add* in Judah. Who
\add is there\add* among you of all his people? The \nd LORD\nd*
his God \add be\add* with him, and let him go up.

headers.mt1: Ezra

verses.text:
Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word
of the \nd LORD\nd* by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled,
the \nd LORD\nd* stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, that he made a
proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and \add put it\add* also in
writing, saying,\f + \fr 1.1  \ft made…: Heb. caused a voice to pass\f*

Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia, The \nd LORD\nd* God of heaven
hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged
me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which \add is\add* in Judah.

Who \add is there\add* among you of all his people? his God
be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which \add is\add* in
Judah, and build the house of the \nd LORD\nd* God of Israel, (he
\add is\add* the God,) which \add is\add* in Jerusalem.

And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the
men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods,
and with beasts, beside the freewill offering for the house of God that
\add is\add* in Jerusalem.\f + \fr 1.4  \ft help…: Heb. lift him
up\f*

Then rose up the chief of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin,
and the priests, and the Levites, with all \add them\add* whose spirit
God had raised, to go up to build the house of the \nd LORD\nd* which
\add is\add* in Jerusalem.

And all they that \add were\add* about them strengthened their
hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, and with beasts,
and with precious things, beside all \add that\add* was willingly
offered.\f + \fr 1.6  \ft strengthened…: that is, helped them\f*

Even those did Cyrus king of Persia bring forth by the hand
of Mithredath the treasurer, and numbered them unto Sheshbazzar,
the prince of Judah.

And this \add is\add* the number of them: thirty chargers of
gold, a thousand chargers of silver, nine and twenty knives,

Thirty basons of gold, silver basons of a second \add sort\add*
four hundred and ten, \add and\add* other vessels a thousand.

All the vessels of gold and of silver \add were\add* five
thousand and four hundred. All \add these\add* did Sheshbazzar bring
up with \add them of\add* the captivity that were brought up from
Babylon unto Jerusalem.\f + \fr 1.11  \ft the captivity: Heb. the
transportation\f*

Now these \add are\add* the children of the province that went
up out of the captivity, of those which had been carried away, whom
Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away unto Babylon,
and came again unto Jerusalem and Judah, every one unto his city;

Which came with Zerubbabel: Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah,
Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, Baanah. The number of the
men of the people of Israel:\f + \fr 2.2  \ft Seraiah: also called,
Azariah\f*\f + \fr 2.2  \ft Reelaiah: or, Raamiah\f*\f + \fr 2.2 
\ft Mispar: or, Mispereth\f*\f + \fr 2.2  \ft Rehum: or, Nehum\f*

The children of Parosh, two thousand an hundred seventy and
two.
The children of Shephatiah, three hundred seventy and two.
The children of Arah, seven hundred seventy and five.

The children of Pahath-moab, of the children of Jeshua \add and\add*
Joab, two thousand eight hundred and twelve.
The children of Elam, a thousand two hundred fifty and four.
The children of Zattu, nine hundred forty and five.
The children of Zaccai, seven hundred and threescore.

The children of Bani, six hundred forty and two.\f + \fr 2.10 
\ft Bani: also called, Binnui\f*
The children of Bebai, six hundred twenty and three.
The children of Azgad, a thousand two hundred twenty and two.
The children of Adonikam, six hundred sixty and six.
The children of Bigvai, two thousand fifty and six.
The children of Adin, four hundred fifty and four.
The children of Ater of Hezekiah, ninety and eight.
The children of Bezai, three hundred twenty and three.

The children of Jorah, an hundred and twelve.\f + \fr 2.18 
\ft Jorah: also called, Hariph\f*
The children of Hashum, two hundred twenty and three.

The children of Gibbar, ninety and five.\f + \fr 2.20  \ft Gibbar: also called,
Gibeon\f*
The children of Beth-lehem, an hundred twenty and three.
The men of Netophah, fifty and six.
The men of Anathoth, an hundred twenty and eight.

The children of Azmaveth, forty and two.\f + \fr 2.24  \ft Azmaveth: also called,
Beth-azmaveth\f*

The children of Kirjath-arim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven
hundred and forty and three.
The children of Ramah and Gaba, six hundred twenty and one.
The men of Michmas, an hundred twenty and two.
The men of Beth-el and Ai, two hundred twenty and three.
The children of Nebo, fifty and two.
The children of Magbish, an hundred fifty and six.

The children of the other Elam, a thousand two hundred fifty
and four.
The children of Harim, three hundred and twenty.

The children of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred twenty
and five.\f + \fr 2.33  \ft Hadid: or, Harid, as it is in some copies\f*
The children of Jericho, three hundred forty and five.

The children of Senaah, three thousand and six hundred and
thirty.

The priests: the children of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua,
nine hundred seventy and three.
The children of Immer, a thousand fifty and two.
The children of Pashur, a thousand two hundred forty and seven.
The children of Harim, a thousand and seventeen.

The Levites: the children of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the children
of Hodaviah, seventy and four.\f + \fr 2.40  \ft Hodaviah: also called, Judah or
Hodevah\f*

The singers: the children of Asaph, an hundred twenty and
eight.

The children of the porters: the children of Shallum, the
children of Ater, the children of Talmon, the children of Akkub,
the children of Hatita, the children of Shobai, \add in\add* all an
hundred thirty and nine.

The Nethinims: the children of Ziha, the children of Hasupha,
the children of Tabbaoth,

The children of Keros, the children of Siaha, the children
of Padon,\f + \fr 2.44  \ft Siaha: also called, Sia\f*

The children of Lebanah, the children of Hagabah, the children
of Akkub,

The children of Hagab, the children of Shalmai, the children
of Hanan,\f + \fr 2.46  \ft Shalmai: also called, Shamlai\f*

The children of Giddel, the children of Gahar, the children
of Reaiah,

The children of Rezin, the children of Nekoda, the children
of Gazzam,

The children of Uzza, the children of Paseah, the children
of Besai,

The children of Asnah, the children of Mehunim, the children
of Nephusim,\f + \fr 2.50  \ft Nephusim: also called, Nephishesim\f*

The children of Bakbuk, the children of Hakupha, the children
of Harhur,

The children of Bazluth, the children of Mehida, the children
of Harsha,\f + \fr 2.52  \ft Bazluth: also called, Bazlith\f*

The children of Barkos, the children of Sisera, the children
of Thamah,

The children of Solomon’s servants: the children of Sotai,
the children of Sophereth, the children of Peruda,\f + \fr 2.55 
\ft Peruda: also called, Perida\f*

The children of Jaalah, the children of Darkon, the children
of Giddel,

The children of Shephatiah, the children of Hattil, the children
of Pochereth of Zebaim, the children of Ami.\f + \fr 2.57  \ft Ami: also called,
Amon\f*

All the Nethinims, and the children of Solomon’s servants,
\add were\add* three hundred ninety and two.

And these \add were\add* they which went up from Tel-melah,
Tel-harsa, Cherub, Addan, \add and\add* Immer: but they could not
shew their father’s house, and their seed, whether they \add were\add*
of Israel:\f + \fr 2.59  \ft Addan: also called, Addon\f*\f + \fr 2.59 
\ft seed: or, pedigree\f*

The children of Delaiah, the children of Tobiah, the children
of Nekoda, six hundred fifty and two.

And of the children of the priests: the children of Habaiah,
the children of Koz, the children of Barzillai; which took a wife
of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their
name:

These sought their register \add among\add* those that were reckoned by
genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted,
put from the priesthood.\f + \fr 2.62  \ft were they…: Heb. they were polluted from the
priesthood\f*

And the Tirshatha said unto them, that they should not eat
of the most holy things, till there stood up a priest with Urim and with
Thummim.\f + \fr 2.63  \ft Tirshatha: or, governor\f*

The whole congregation together \add was\add* forty and two
thousand three hundred \add and\add* threescore,

Beside their servants and their maids, of whom \add there
were\add* seven thousand three hundred thirty and seven: and \add 
there were\add* among them two hundred singing men and singing women.

Their horses \add were\add* seven hundred thirty and six;
their mules, two hundred forty and five;

Their camels, four hundred thirty and five; \add their\add*
asses, six thousand seven hundred and twenty.

And \add some\add* of the chief of the fathers, when they
came to the house of the \nd LORD\nd* which \add is\add* at Jerusalem,
offered freely for the house of God to set it up in his place:

They gave after their ability unto the treasure of the work
threescore and one thousand drams of gold, and five thousand pound
of silver, and one hundred priests’ garments.

So the priests, and the Levites, and \add some\add* of the
people, and the singers, and the porters, and the Nethinims, dwelt
in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.

And when the seventh month was come, and the children of Israel
\add were\add* in the cities, the people gathered themselves together
as one man to Jerusalem.

Then stood up Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and his brethren the
priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and his brethren, and
builded the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings thereon, as
\add it is\add* written in the law of Moses the man of God.\f + \fr 3.2 
\ft Jeshua: also called, Joshua\f*\f + \fr 3.2  \ft Zerubbabel: Gr.
Zorobabel\f*\f + \fr 3.2  \ft Shealtiel: Gr. Salathiel\f*

And they set the altar upon his bases; for fear \add was\add*
upon them because of the people of those countries: and they offered
burnt offerings thereon unto the \nd LORD\nd*, \add even\add* burnt
offerings morning and evening.

They kept also the feast of tabernacles, as \add it is\add*
written, and \add offered\add* the daily burnt offerings by number,
according to the custom, as the duty of every day required;\f + \fr 3.4 
\ft as the duty…: Heb. the matter of the day in his day\f*

And afterward \add offered\add* the continual burnt offering,
both of the new moons, and of all the set feasts of the \nd LORD\nd*
that were consecrated, and of every one that willingly offered a freewill
offering unto the \nd LORD\nd*.

From the first day of the seventh month began they to offer
burnt offerings unto the \nd LORD\nd*. But the foundation of the
temple of the \nd LORD\nd* was not \add yet\add* laid.\f + \fr 3.6 
\ft the foundation…: Heb. the temple of the \+nd LORD\+nd* was not yet
founded\f*

They gave money also unto the masons, and to the carpenters;
and meat, and drink, and oil, unto them of Zidon, and to them of
Tyre, to bring cedar trees from Lebanon to the sea of Joppa, according to the
grant that they had of Cyrus king of Persia.\f + \fr 3.7  \ft carpenters: or,
workmen\f*

Now in the second year of their coming unto the house of God
at Jerusalem, in the second month, began Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel,
and Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and the remnant of their brethren
the priests and the Levites, and all they that were come out of the
captivity unto Jerusalem; and appointed the Levites, from twenty
years old and upward, to set forward the work of the house of the
\nd LORD\nd*.

Then stood Jeshua \add with\add* his sons and his brethren,
Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, together, to set forward
the workmen in the house of God: the sons of Henadad, \add with\add*
their sons and their brethren the Levites.\f + \fr 3.9  \ft Judah: also called,
Hodaviah\f*\f + \fr 3.9  \ft together: Heb. as one\f*

And when the builders laid the foundation of the temple of the
\nd LORD\nd*, they set the priests in their apparel with trumpets,
and the Levites the sons of Asaph with cymbals, to praise the \nd LORD\nd*,
after the ordinance of David king of Israel.

And they sang together by course in praising and giving thanks
unto the 
d LORD
d*; because \add he is\add* good, for his mercy
\add endureth\add* for ever toward Israel. And all the people shouted
with a great shout, when they praised the 
d LORD
d*, because the
foundation of the house of the 
d LORD
d* was laid.

But many of the priests and Levites and chief of the fathers,
\add who were\add* ancient men, that had seen the first house, when the
foundation of this house was laid before their eyes, wept with a
loud voice; and many shouted aloud for joy:

So that the people could not discern the noise of the shout
of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people: for the people
shouted with a loud shout, and the noise was heard afar off.

Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the
children of the captivity builded the temple unto the \nd LORD\nd*
God of Israel;\f + \fr 4.1  \ft the children…: Heb. the sons of the
transportation\f*

Then they came to Zerubbabel, and to the chief of the fathers,
and said unto them, Let us build with you: for we seek your God, as ye
\add do;\add* and we do sacrifice unto him since the days of Esar-haddon
king of Assur, which brought us up hither.

But Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, and the rest of the chief of the
fathers of Israel, said unto them, Ye have nothing to do with us to
build an house unto our God; but we ourselves together will build
unto the \nd LORD\nd* God of Israel, as king Cyrus the king of Persia
hath commanded us.

Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people
of Judah, and troubled them in building,

And hired counsellors against them, to frustrate their purpose,
all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius
king of Persia.

And in the reign of Ahasuerus, in the beginning of his reign,
wrote they \add unto him\add* an accusation against the inhabitants
of Judah and Jerusalem.\f + \fr 4.6  \ft Ahasuerus: Heb. Ahashverosh\f*

And in the days of Artaxerxes wrote Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel,
and the rest of their companions, unto Artaxerxes king of Persia;
and the writing of the letter \add was\add* written in the Syrian
tongue, and interpreted in the Syrian tongue.\f + \fr 4.7  \ft Bishlam: or, in
peace\f*\f + \fr 4.7  \ft companions: Heb. societies\f*

Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter
against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king in this sort:\f + \fr 4.8 
\ft scribe: or, secretary\f*

Then \add wrote\add* Rehum the chancellor, and Shimshai the
scribe, and the rest of their companions; the Dinaites, the Apharsathchites,
the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Archevites, the Babylonians,
the Susanchites, the Dehavites, \add and\add* the Elamites,\f + \fr 4.9 
\ft companions: Chaldee, societies\f*

And the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Asnappar
brought over, and set in the cities of Samaria, and the rest \add that
are\add* on this side the river, and at such a time.\f + \fr 4.10 
\ft at such…: Chaldee, Cheeneth\f*

This \add is\add* the copy of the letter that they sent unto
him, \add even\add* unto Artaxerxes the king; Thy servants the men
on this side the river, and at such a time.

Be it known unto the king, that the Jews which came up from
thee to us are come unto Jerusalem, building  the rebellious and the
bad city, and have set up the walls \add thereof\add*, and joined
the foundations.\f + \fr 4.12  \ft set up: or, finished\f*\f + \fr 4.12 
\ft joined: Chaldee, sewed together\f*

Be it known now unto the king, that, if this city be builded,
and the walls set up \add again, then\add* will they not pay toll,
tribute, and custom, and \add so\add* thou shalt endamage the revenue
of the kings.\f + \fr 4.13  \ft pay: Chaldee, give\f*\f + \fr 4.13 
\ft revenue: or, strength\f*

Now because we have maintenance from \add the king’s\add*
palace, and it was not meet for us to see the king’s dishonour, therefore
have we sent and certified the king;\f + \fr 4.14  \ft we have…: Chaldee, we are salted with the salt of the
palace\f*

That search may be made in the book of the records of thy
fathers: so shalt thou find in the book of the records, and know
that this city \add is\add* a rebellious city, and hurtful unto kings
and provinces, and that they have moved sedition within the same
of old time: for which cause was this city destroyed. \f + \fr 4.15 
\ft moved: Chaldee, made\f*\f + \fr 4.15  \ft within…: Chaldee, in the midst
thereof\f*

We certify the king that, if this city be builded \add again\add*,
and the walls thereof set up, by this means thou shalt have no portion
on this side the river.

\add Then\add* sent the king an answer unto Rehum the chancellor, and
\add to\add* Shimshai the scribe, and \add to\add* the rest of their
companions that dwell in Samaria, and \add unto\add* the rest beyond
the river, Peace, and at such a time.\f + \fr 4.17  \ft companions: Chaldee,
societies\f*
The letter which ye sent unto us hath been plainly read before me.

And I commanded, and search hath been made, and it is found
that this city of old time hath made insurrection against kings, and
\add that\add* rebellion and sedition have been made therein.\f + \fr 4.19 
\ft I commanded: Chaldee, by me a decree is set\f*\f + \fr 4.19 
\ft made insurrection: Chaldee, lifted up itself\f*

There have been mighty kings also over Jerusalem, which have
ruled over all \add countries\add* beyond the river; and toll, tribute,
and custom, was paid unto them.

Give ye now commandment to cause these men to cease, and that
this city be not builded, until \add another\add* commandment shall be
given from me.\f + \fr 4.21  \ft Give…: Chaldee, Make a decree\f*

Take heed now that ye fail not to do this: why should damage
grow to the hurt of the kings?

Now when the copy of king Artaxerxes’ letter \add was\add*
read before Rehum, and Shimshai the scribe, and their companions,
they went up in haste to Jerusalem unto the Jews, and made them to
cease by force and power.\f + \fr 4.23  \ft by force…: Chaldee, by arm and
power\f*

Then ceased the work of the house of God which \add is\add*
at Jerusalem. So it ceased unto the second year of the reign of Darius
king of Persia.

Then the prophets, Haggai the prophet, and Zechariah the son
of Iddo, prophesied unto the Jews that \add were\add* in Judah and
Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, \add even\add* unto them.

Then rose up Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the
son of Jozadak, and began to build the house of God which \add is\add*
at Jerusalem: and with them \add were\add* the prophets of God helping them.

At the same time came to them Tatnai, governor on this side
the river, and Shethar-boznai, and their companions, and said thus
unto them, Who hath commanded you to build this house, and to make
up this wall?

Then said we unto them after this manner, What are the names
of the men that make this building?\f + \fr 5.4  \ft make: Chaldee,
build\f*

But the eye of their God was upon the elders of the Jews, that they could
not cause them to cease, till the matter came to Darius: and then
they returned answer by letter concerning this \add matter\add*.

The copy of the letter that Tatnai, governor on this side
the river, and Shethar-boznai, and his companions the Apharsachites, which
\add were\add* on this side the river, sent unto Darius the king:

They sent a letter unto him, wherein was written thus; Unto
Darius the king, all peace.\f + \fr 5.7  \ft wherein: Chaldee, in the midst
whereof\f*

Be it known unto the king, that we went into the province of
Judea, to the house of the great God, which is builded with great
stones, and timber is laid in the walls, and this work goeth fast
on, and prospereth in their hands.\f + \fr 5.8  \ft great…: Chaldee, stones of
rolling\f*

Of the sons also of Bebai; Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, \add and\add*
Athlai.

And of the sons of Bani; Meshullam, Malluch, and Adaiah, Jashub,
and Sheal, and Ramoth.

And of the sons of Pahath-moab; Adna, and Chelal, Benaiah,
Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezaleel, and Binnui, and Manasseh.

And \add of\add* the sons of Harim; Eliezer, Ishijah, Malchiah,
Shemaiah, Shimeon,

Of the sons of Hashum; Mattenai, Mattathah, Zabad, Eliphelet,
Jeremai, Manasseh, \add and\add* Shimei.
Of the sons of Bani; Maadai, Amram, and Uel,
Benaiah, Bedeiah, Chelluh,
Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,
Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Jaasau,
And Bani, and Binnui, Shimei,
And Shelemiah, and Nathan, and Adaiah,

Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,\f + \fr 10.40  \ft Machnadebai: or, Mabnadebai, according to some
copies\f*
Azareel, and Shelemiah, Shemariah,
Shallum, Amariah, \add and\add* Joseph.

Of the sons of Nebo; Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jadau,
and Joel, Benaiah.

All these had taken strange wives: and \add some\add* of them
had wives by whom they had children.

headers.toc1: The Book of Nehemiah
headers.mt1: The Book of Nehemiah

verses.text:
The words of Nehemiah the son of Hachaliah. And it came to pass in the
month Chisleu, in the twentieth year, as I was in Shushan the palace,

That Hanani, one of my brethren, came, he and \add certain\add*
men of Judah; and I asked them concerning the Jews that had escaped,
which were left of the captivity, and concerning Jerusalem.

And they said unto me, The remnant that are left of the captivity
there in the province \add are\add* in great affliction and reproach:
the wall of Jerusalem also \add is\add* broken down, and the gates
thereof are burned with fire.

And it came to pass, when I heard these words, that I sat
down and wept, and mourned \add certain\add* days, and fasted, and
prayed before the God of heaven,

And said, I beseech thee, O \nd LORD\nd* God of heaven, the
great and terrible God, that keepeth covenant and mercy for them that
love him and observe his commandments:

Let thine ear now be attentive, and thine eyes open, that thou mayest
hear the prayer of thy servant, which I pray before thee now, day
and night, for the children of Israel thy servants, and confess the
sins of the children of Israel, which we have sinned against thee: both I and my
father’s house have sinned.

We have dealt very corruptly against thee, and have not kept
the commandments, nor the statutes, nor the judgments, which thou
commandedst thy servant Moses.

Remember, I beseech thee, the word that thou commandedst thy
servant Moses, saying, \add If\add* ye transgress, I will scatter you
abroad among the nations:

But \add if\add* ye turn unto me, and keep my commandments,
and do them; though there were of you cast out unto the uttermost
part of the heaven, \add yet\add* will I gather them from thence, and will
bring them unto the place that I have chosen to set my name there.

Now these \add are\add* thy servants and thy people, whom thou hast
redeemed by thy great power, and by thy strong hand.

O Lord, I beseech thee, let now thine ear be attentive to the
prayer of thy servant, and to the prayer of thy servants, who desire
to fear thy name: and prosper, I pray thee, thy servant this day,
and grant him mercy in the sight of this man. For I was the king’s
cupbearer.

And it came to pass in the month Nisan, in the twentieth year
of Artaxerxes the king, \add that\add* wine \add was\add* before
him: and I took up the wine, and gave \add it\add* unto the king. Now I had not been
\add beforetime\add* sad in his presence.

Wherefore the king said unto me, Why \add is\add* thy countenance
sad, seeing thou \add art\add* not sick? this \add is\add* nothing
\add else\add* but sorrow of heart. Then I was very sore afraid,

And said unto the king, Let the king live for ever: why should not my
countenance be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers’ sepulchres,
\add lieth\add* waste, and the gates thereof are consumed with fire?

Then the king said unto me, For what dost thou make request?
So I prayed to the God of heaven.

And I said unto the king, If it please the king, and if thy
servant have found favour in thy sight, that thou wouldest send me unto
Judah, unto the city of my fathers’ sepulchres, that I may build it.

And the king said unto me, (the queen also sitting by him,)
For how long shall thy journey be? and when wilt thou return? So it
pleased the king to send me; and I set him a time.\f + \fr 2.6  \ft queen: Heb.
wife\f*

And a letter unto Asaph the keeper of the king’s forest, that he may
give me timber to make beams for the gates of the palace which \add appertained\add*
to the house, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I shall enter
into. And the king granted  me, according to the good hand of my
God upon me.

Then I came to the governors beyond the river, and gave them the
king’s letters. Now the king had sent captains of the army and horsemen with me.

When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite,
heard \add of it\add*, it grieved them exceedingly that there was
come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.
So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days.

And I arose in the night, I and some few men with me; neither
told I \add any\add* man what my God had put in my heart to do at
Jerusalem: neither \add was there any\add* beast with me, save the
beast that I rode upon.

And I went out by night by the gate of the valley, even before
the dragon well, and to the dung port, and viewed the walls of Jerusalem,
which were broken down, and the gates thereof were consumed with
fire.

Then I went on to the gate of the fountain, and to the king’s
pool: but \add there was\add* no place for the beast \add that was\add*
under me to pass.

Then went I up in the night by the brook, and viewed the wall,
and turned back, and entered by the gate of the valley, and \add so\add*
returned.

And the rulers knew not whither I went, or what I did; neither had I as
yet told \add it\add* to the Jews, nor to the priests, nor to the
nobles, nor to the rulers, nor to the rest that did the work.

Then said I unto them, Ye see the distress that we \add are\add*
in, how Jerusalem \add lieth\add* waste, and the gates thereof are
burned with fire: come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem,
that we be no more a reproach.

Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the
king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise
up and build. So they strengthened their hands for \add this\add*
good \add work\add*.

But when Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the
Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian, heard \add it\add*, they laughed us to
scorn, and despised us, and said, What \add is\add* this thing that ye
do? will ye rebel against the king?

Then answered I them, and said unto them, The God of heaven,
he will prosper us; therefore we his servants will arise and build:
but ye have no portion, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.

Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brethren the
priests, and they builded the sheep gate; they sanctified it, and set
up the doors of it; even unto the tower of Meah they sanctified it, unto the
tower of Hananeel.

And next unto him builded the men of Jericho. And next to them
builded Zaccur the son of Imri.\f + \fr 3.2  \ft next unto…: Heb. at his
hand\f*

But the fish gate did the sons of Hassenaah build, who \add also\add*
laid the beams thereof, and set up the doors thereof, the locks thereof, and the
bars thereof.

And next unto them repaired Meremoth the son of Urijah, the
son of Koz. And next unto them repaired Meshullam the son of Berechiah,
the son of Meshezabeel. And next unto them repaired Zadok the son
of Baana.

And next unto them the Tekoites repaired; but their nobles
put not their necks to the work of their Lord.

Moreover the old gate repaired Jehoiada the son of Paseah,
and Meshullam the son of Besodeiah; they laid the beams thereof, and set
up the doors thereof, and the locks thereof, and the bars thereof.

And next unto them repaired Melatiah the Gibeonite, and Jadon
the Meronothite, the men of Gibeon, and of Mizpah, unto the throne
of the governor on this side the river.

Next unto him repaired Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths.
Next unto him also repaired Hananiah the son of \add one of\add*
the apothecaries, and they fortified Jerusalem unto the broad wall.\f + \fr 3.8 
\ft fortified…: or, left Jerusalem unto the broad wall\f*

And next unto them repaired Rephaiah the son of Hur, the ruler
of the half part of Jerusalem.

And next unto them repaired Jedaiah the son of Harumaph, even over against his
house. And next unto him repaired Hattush the son of Hashabniah.

Malchijah the son of Harim, and Hashub the son of Pahath-moab,
repaired the other piece, and the tower of the furnaces.\f + \fr 3.11 
\ft other…: Heb. second measure\f*

And next unto him repaired Shallum the son of Halohesh, the
ruler of the half part of Jerusalem, he and his daughters.

But the dung gate repaired Malchiah the son of Rechab, the
ruler of part of Beth-haccerem; he built it, and set up the doors
thereof, the locks thereof, and the bars thereof.

But the gate of the fountain repaired Shallun the son of Col-hozeh,
the ruler of part of Mizpah; he built it, and covered it, and set
up the doors thereof, the locks thereof, and the bars thereof, and the
wall of the pool of Siloah by the king’s garden, and unto the stairs
that go down from the city of David.

After him repaired Nehemiah the son of Azbuk, the ruler of the
half part of Beth-zur, unto \add the place\add* over against the
sepulchres of David, and to the pool that was made, and unto the
house of the mighty.

After him repaired the Levites, Rehum the son of Bani. Next unto
him repaired Hashabiah, the ruler of the half part of Keilah, in his
part.

After him repaired their brethren, Bavai the son of Henadad,
the ruler of the half part of Keilah.

And next to him repaired Ezer the son of Jeshua, the ruler
of Mizpah, another piece over against the going up to the armoury
at the turning \add of the wall\add*.

After him Baruch the son of Zabbai earnestly repaired the
other piece, from the turning \add of the wall\add* unto the door
of the house of Eliashib the high priest.\f + \fr 3.20  \ft Zabbai: also called,
Zaccai\f*

After him repaired Meremoth the son of Urijah the son of Koz
another piece, from the door of the house of Eliashib even to the
end of the house of Eliashib.
And after him repaired the priests, the men of the plain.

After him repaired Benjamin and Hashub over against their
house. After him repaired Azariah the son of Maaseiah the son of
Ananiah by his house.

Palal the son of Uzai, over against the turning \add of the
wall\add*, and the tower which lieth out from the king’s high house, that
\add was\add* by the court of the prison. After him Pedaiah the son
of Parosh.

Moreover the Nethinims dwelt  in Ophel, unto \add the place\add*
over against the water gate toward the east, and the tower that lieth
out.\f + \fr 3.26  \ft dwelt…: or, which dwelt in Ophel, repaired
unto\f*\f + \fr 3.26  \ft Ophel: or, tower\f*

After them the Tekoites repaired another piece, over against the
great tower that lieth out, even unto the wall of Ophel.

From above the horse gate repaired the priests, every one
over against his house.

After them repaired Zadok the son of Immer over against his
house. After him repaired also Shemaiah the son of Shechaniah, the
keeper of the east gate.

After him repaired Hananiah the son of Shelemiah, and Hanun
the sixth son of Zalaph, another piece. After him repaired Meshullam
the son of Berechiah over against his chamber.

After him repaired Malchiah the goldsmith’s son unto the place
of the Nethinims, and of the merchants, over against the gate Miphkad,
and to the going up of the corner.\f + \fr 3.31  \ft going…: or, corner
chamber\f*

And between the going up of the corner unto the sheep gate
repaired the goldsmiths and the merchants.\f + \fr 3.32  \ft going…: or, corner
chamber\f*

But it came to pass, that when Sanballat heard that we builded
the wall, he was wroth, and took great indignation, and mocked the
Jews.

And he spake before his brethren and the army of Samaria, and
said, What do these feeble Jews? will they fortify themselves? will they
sacrifice? will they make an end in a day? will they revive the stones
out of the heaps of the rubbish which are burned?\f + \fr 4.2  \ft fortify…: Heb. leave to
themselves\f*

Now Tobiah the Ammonite \add was\add* by him, and he said,
Even that which they build, if a fox go up, he shall even break down
their stone wall.

Hear, O our God; for we are despised: and turn their reproach
upon their own head, and give them for a prey in the land of captivity:\f + \fr 4.4 
\ft despised: Heb. despite\f*

And cover not their iniquity, and let not their sin be blotted
out from before thee: for they have provoked \add thee\add* to anger
before the builders.

So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together
unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.

But it came to pass, \add that\add* when Sanballat, and Tobiah,
and the Arabians, and the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites, heard that the
walls of Jerusalem were made up, \add and\add* that the breaches
began to be stopped, then they were very wroth, \f + \fr 4.7  \ft were made up: Heb.
ascended\f*

And conspired all of them together to come \add and\add* to
fight against Jerusalem, and to hinder it.\f + \fr 4.8  \ft to hinder…: Heb. to make an error to
it\f*

Nevertheless we made our prayer unto our God, and set a watch
against them day and night, because of them.

And Judah said, The strength of the bearers of burdens is
decayed, and \add there is\add* much rubbish; so that we are not
able to build the wall.

And our adversaries said, They shall not know, neither see,
till we come in the midst among them, and slay them, and cause the
work to cease.

And it came to pass, that when the Jews which dwelt by them
came, they said unto us ten times, From all places whence ye shall
return unto us \add they will be upon you\add*.\f + \fr 4.12  \ft From all…: or, That from all places ye must return to
us\f*

Therefore set I in the lower places behind the wall, \add and\add*
on the higher places, I even set the people after their families
with their swords, their spears, and their bows.\f + \fr 4.13  \ft in the…: Heb. from the lower parts of the place,
etc\f*

And I looked, and rose up, and said unto the nobles, and to the
rulers, and to the rest of the people, Be not ye afraid of them:
remember  the Lord, \add which is\add* great and terrible, and fight
for your brethren, your sons, and your daughters, your wives, and your
houses.

And it came to pass, when our enemies heard that it was known
unto us, and God had brought their counsel to nought, that we returned
all of us to the wall, every one unto his work.

And it came to pass from that time forth, \add that\add* the
half of my servants wrought in the work, and the other half of them
held both the spears, the shields, and the bows, and the habergeons;
and the rulers \add were\add* behind all the house of Judah.

They which builded on the wall, and they that bare burdens,
with those that laded, \add every one\add* with one of his hands
wrought in the work, and with the other \add hand\add* held a weapon.

For the builders, every one had his sword girded by his side, and
\add so\add* builded. And he that sounded the trumpet \add was\add*
by me.\f + \fr 4.18  \ft by his side: Heb. on his loins\f*

And I said unto the nobles, and to the rulers, and to the
rest of the people, The work \add is\add* great and large, and we are
separated upon the wall, one far from another.

In what place \add therefore\add* ye hear the sound of the
trumpet, resort ye thither unto us: our God shall fight for us.

So we laboured in the work: and half of them held the spears
from the rising of the morning till the stars appeared.

Likewise at the same time said I unto the people, Let every
one with his servant lodge  within Jerusalem, that in the night they may be a
guard to us, and labour on the day.

So neither I, nor my brethren, nor my servants, nor the men
of the guard which followed me, none of us put off our clothes, \add saving
that\add* every one put them off for washing.\f + \fr 4.23  \ft saving…: or, every one went with his weapon for
water\f*

And there was a great cry of the people and of their wives
against their brethren the Jews.

For there were that said, We, our sons, and our daughters,
\add are\add* many: therefore we take up corn \add for them\add*,
that we may eat, and live.

\add Some\add* also there were that said, We have mortgaged
our lands, vineyards, and houses, that we might buy corn, because of the
dearth.

There were also that said, We have borrowed money for the king’s
tribute, \add and that upon\add* our lands and vineyards.

Yet now our flesh \add is\add* as the flesh of our brethren,
our children as their children: and, lo, we bring into bondage our
sons and our daughters to be servants, and \add some\add* of our
daughters are brought unto bondage \add already:\add* neither \add is
it\add* in our power \add to redeem them;\add* for other men have our
lands and vineyards.
And I was very angry when I heard their cry and these words.

Then I consulted with myself, and I rebuked the nobles, and the
rulers, and said unto them, Ye exact usury, every one of his brother.
And I set a great assembly against them.\f + \fr 5.7  \ft I consulted…: Heb. my heart consulted in
me\f*

And I said unto them, We after our ability have redeemed our
brethren the Jews, which were sold unto the heathen; and will ye even
sell your brethren? or shall they be sold unto us? Then held they their
peace, and found nothing \add to answer\add*.

Also I said, It \add is\add* not good that ye do: ought ye not to
walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the heathen
our enemies?

I likewise, \add and\add* my brethren, and my servants, might
exact of them money and corn: I pray you, let us leave off this usury.

Restore, I pray you, to them, even this day, their lands,
their vineyards, their oliveyards, and their houses, also the hundredth
\add part\add* of the money, and of the corn, the wine, and the oil,
that ye exact of them.

Then said they, We will restore \add them\add*, and will require
nothing of them; so will we do as thou sayest. Then I called the
priests, and took an oath of them, that they should do according to this
promise.

Also I shook my lap, and said, So God shake out every man
from his house, and from his labour, that performeth not this promise,
even thus be he shaken out, and emptied. And all the congregation
said, Amen, and praised the \nd LORD\nd*. And the people did according to this
promise.\f + \fr 5.13  \ft emptied: Heb. empty, or, void\f*

Moreover from the time that I was appointed to be their governor
in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year even unto the two and
thirtieth year of Artaxerxes the king, \add that is\add*, twelve
years, I and my brethren have not eaten the bread of the governor.

But the former governors that \add had been\add* before me were
chargeable unto the people, and had taken of them bread and wine,
beside forty shekels of silver; yea, even their servants bare rule
over the people: but so did not I, because of the fear of God.

Yea, also I continued in the work of this wall, neither bought
we any land: and all my servants \add were\add* gathered thither unto the
work.

Moreover \add there were\add* at my table an hundred and fifty
of the Jews and rulers, beside those that came unto us from among the
heathen that \add are\add* about us.

Now \add that\add* which was prepared \add for me\add* daily
\add was\add* one ox \add and\add* six choice sheep; also fowls were
prepared for me, and once in ten days store of all sorts of wine:
yet for all this required not I the bread of the governor, because the
bondage was heavy upon this people.

Think upon me, my God, for good, \add according\add* to all that I have
done for this people.

Now it came to pass, when Sanballat, and Tobiah, and Geshem
the Arabian, and the rest of our enemies, heard that I had builded
the wall, and \add that\add* there was no breach left therein; (though
at that time I had not set up the doors upon the gates;)

That Sanballat and Geshem sent unto me, saying, Come, let us
meet together in \add some one of\add* the villages in the plain
of Ono. But they thought to do me mischief.

And I sent messengers unto them, saying, I \add am\add* doing
a great work, so that I cannot come down: why should the work cease,
whilst I leave it, and come down to you?

Yet they sent unto me four times after this sort; and I answered
them after the same manner.

Then sent Sanballat his servant unto me in like manner the
fifth time with an open letter in his hand;

Wherein \add was\add* written, It is reported among the heathen,
and Gashmu saith \add it, that\add* thou and the Jews think to rebel:
for which cause thou buildest the wall, that thou mayest be their
king, according to these words.\f + \fr 6.6  \ft Gashmu: also called,
Geshem\f*

And thou hast also appointed prophets to preach of thee at
Jerusalem, saying, \add There is\add* a king in Judah: and now shall it be
reported to the king according to these words. Come now therefore, and let us take
counsel together.

Then I sent unto him, saying, There are no such things done
as thou sayest, but thou feignest them out of thine own heart.

Afterward I came unto the house of Shemaiah the son of Delaiah
the son of Mehetabeel, who \add was\add* shut up; and he said, Let us meet
together in the house of God, within the temple, and let us shut
the doors of the temple: for they will come to slay thee; yea, in the
night will they come to slay thee.

And I said, Should such a man as I flee? and who \add is there\add*, that,
\add being\add* as I \add am\add*, would go into the temple to save his
life? I will not go in.

And, lo, I perceived that God had not sent him; but that he
pronounced this prophecy against me: for Tobiah and Sanballat had
hired him.

Therefore \add was\add* he hired, that I should be afraid,
and do so, and sin, and \add that\add* they might have \add matter\add*
for an evil report, that they might reproach me.

My God, think thou upon Tobiah and Sanballat according to these their
works, and on the prophetess Noadiah, and the rest of the prophets,
that would have put me in fear.

So the wall was finished in the twenty and fifth \add day\add* of
\add the month\add* Elul, in fifty and two days.

And it came to pass, that when all our enemies heard \add thereof\add*,
and all the heathen that \add were\add* about us saw \add these things\add*,
they were much cast down in their own eyes: for they perceived that this
work was wrought of our God.

Moreover in those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters
unto Tobiah, and \add the letters\add* of Tobiah came unto them.\f + \fr 6.17 
\ft sent…: Heb. multiplied their letters passing to Tobiah\f*

For \add there were\add* many in Judah sworn unto him, because he
\add was\add* the son in law of Shechaniah the son of Arah; and his
son Johanan had taken the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah.

Also they reported his good deeds before me, and uttered my
words to him. \add And\add* Tobiah sent letters to put me in fear.\f + \fr 6.19 
\ft words: or, matters\f*

Now it came to pass, when the wall was built, and I had set
up the doors, and the porters and the singers and the Levites were
appointed,

That I gave my brother Hanani, and Hananiah the ruler of the
palace, charge  over Jerusalem: for he \add was\add* a faithful man,
and feared God above many.

And I said unto them, Let not the gates of Jerusalem be opened
until the sun be hot; and while they stand by, let them shut the
doors, and bar \add them:\add* and appoint watches of the inhabitants
of Jerusalem, every one in his watch, and every one \add to be\add*
over against his house.

Now the city \add was\add* large and great: but the people
\add were\add* few therein, and the houses \add were\add* not builded.\f + \fr 7.4 
\ft large: Heb. broad in spaces\f*

And my God put into mine heart to gather together the nobles,
and the rulers, and the people, that they might be reckoned by genealogy.
And I found a register of the genealogy of them which came up at the
first, and found written therein,

These \add are\add* the children of the province, that went
up out of the captivity, of those that had been carried away, whom
Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away, and came again
to Jerusalem and to Judah, every one unto his city;

Who came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah,
Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, Baanah. The
number, \add I say\add*, of the men of the people of Israel \add was
this;\add*\f + \fr 7.7  \ft Azariah: also called, Seraiah\f*

The children of Parosh, two thousand an hundred seventy and
two.
The children of Shephatiah, three hundred seventy and two.
The children of Arah, six hundred fifty and two.

The children of Pahath-moab, of the children of Jeshua and
Joab, two thousand and eight hundred \add and\add* eighteen.
The children of Elam, a thousand two hundred fifty and four.
The children of Zattu, eight hundred forty and five.
The children of Zaccai, seven hundred and threescore.

The children of Binnui, six hundred forty and eight.\f + \fr 7.15 
\ft Binnui: also called, Bani\f*
The children of Bebai, six hundred twenty and eight.

The children of Azgad, two thousand three hundred twenty and
two.
The children of Adonikam, six hundred threescore and seven.
The children of Bigvai, two thousand threescore and seven.
The children of Adin, six hundred fifty and five.
The children of Ater of Hezekiah, ninety and eight.
The children of Hashum, three hundred twenty and eight.
The children of Bezai, three hundred twenty and four.

The children of Hariph, an hundred and twelve.\f + \fr 7.24 
\ft Hariph: also called, Jora\f*

The children of Gibeon, ninety and five.\f + \fr 7.25  \ft Gibeon: also called,
Gibbar\f*

The men of Beth-lehem and Netophah, an hundred fourscore and
eight.
The men of Anathoth, an hundred twenty and eight.

The men of Beth-azmaveth, forty and two.\f + \fr 7.28  \ft Beth-azmaveth: also called,
Azmaveth\f*

The men of Kirjath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred
