And at Ziklag, and at Mekonah, and in the villages thereof,
And at En-rimmon, and at Zareah, and at Jarmuth,

Zanoah, Adullam, and \add in\add* their villages, at Lachish,
and the fields thereof, at Azekah, and \add in\add* the villages
thereof. And they dwelt from Beer-sheba unto the valley of Hinnom.

The children also of Benjamin from Geba \add dwelt\add* at
Michmash, and Aija, and Beth-el, and \add in\add* their villages,\f + \fr 11.31 
\ft from: or, of\f*\f + \fr 11.31  \ft at: or, to\f*
\add And\add* at Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
Lod, and Ono, the valley of craftsmen.

And of the Levites \add were\add* divisions \add in\add* Judah,
\add and\add* in Benjamin.

Now these \add are\add* the priests and the Levites that went
up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah,
Ezra,

Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,\f + \fr 12.2  \ft Malluch: also called,
Melicu\f*

Shechaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,\f + \fr 12.3  \ft Shechaniah: also called,
Shebaniah\f*\f + \fr 12.3  \ft Rehum: also called, Harim\f*\f + \fr 12.3 
\ft Meremoth: also called, Meraioth\f*

Iddo, Ginnetho, Abijah,\f + \fr 12.4  \ft Ginnetho: also called,
Ginnethon\f*

Miamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,\f + \fr 12.5  \ft Miamin: also called,
Miniamin\f*\f + \fr 12.5  \ft Maadiah: also called, Moadiah\f*
Shemaiah, and Joiarib, Jedaiah,

Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These \add were\add* the chief
of the priests and of their brethren in the days of Jeshua.\f + \fr 12.7 
\ft Sallu: also called, Sallai\f*

Moreover the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah,
\add and\add* Mattaniah, \add which was\add* over the thanksgiving,
he and his brethren.\f + \fr 12.8  \ft the thanksgiving: that is, the psalms of
thanksgiving\f*

Also Bakbukiah and Unni, their brethren, \add were\add* over against them in the
watches.

And Jeshua begat Joiakim, Joiakim also begat Eliashib, and
Eliashib begat Joiada,
And Joiada begat Jonathan, and Jonathan begat Jaddua.

And in the days of Joiakim were priests, the chief of the
fathers: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;
Of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;
Of Melicu, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;
Of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;
Of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;
Of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai;
Of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan;
And of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;
Of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;
Of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethaneel.

The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, and Johanan,
and Jaddua, \add were\add* recorded chief of the fathers: also the
priests, to the reign of Darius the Persian.

The sons of Levi, the chief of the fathers, \add were\add*
written in the book of the chronicles, even until the days of Johanan
the son of Eliashib.

And the chief of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua
the son of Kadmiel, with their brethren over against them, to praise
\add and\add* to give thanks, according to the commandment of David
the man of God, ward over against ward.

Mattaniah, and Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, Akkub,
\add were\add* porters keeping the ward at the thresholds of the
gates.\f + \fr 12.25  \ft thresholds: or, treasuries, or, assemblies\f*

These \add were\add* in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua,
the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and of
Ezra the priest, the scribe.

And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought
the Levites out of all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem,
to keep the dedication with gladness, both with thanksgivings, and with
singing, \add with\add* cymbals, psalteries, and with harps.

Also from the house of Gilgal, and out of the fields of Geba
and Azmaveth: for the singers had builded them villages round about
Jerusalem.

And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and purified
the people, and the gates, and the wall.

Then I brought up the princes of Judah upon the wall, and
appointed two great \add companies of them that gave\add* thanks,
\add whereof one\add* went on the right hand upon the wall toward the
dung gate:
And after them went Hoshaiah, and half of the princes of Judah,
Judah, and Benjamin, and Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,

And \add certain\add* of the priests’ sons with trumpets; \add namely\add*,
Zechariah the son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah,
the son of Michaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph:

And his brethren, Shemaiah, and Azarael, Milalai, Gilalai,
Maai, Nethaneel, and Judah, Hanani, with the musical instruments
of David the man of God, and Ezra the scribe before them.

And at the fountain gate, which was over against them, they went
up by the stairs of the city of David, at the going up of the wall,
above the house of David, even unto the water gate eastward.

And the other \add company of them that gave\add* thanks went
over against \add them\add*, and I after them, and the half of the
people upon the wall, from beyond the tower of the furnaces even unto the
broad wall;

And from above the gate of Ephraim, and above the old gate,
and above the fish gate, and the tower of Hananeel, and the tower
of Meah, even unto the sheep gate: and they stood still in the prison
gate.

So stood the two \add companies of them that gave\add* thanks
in the house of God, and I, and the half of the rulers with me:

And the priests; Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Michaiah, Elioenai,
Zechariah, \add and\add* Hananiah, with trumpets;

And Maaseiah, and Shemaiah, and Eleazar, and Uzzi, and Jehohanan,
and Malchijah, and Elam, and Ezer. And the singers sang loud, with
Jezrahiah \add their\add* overseer.\f + \fr 12.42  \ft sang…: Heb. made their voice to be
heard\f*

Also that day they offered great sacrifices, and rejoiced:
for God had made them rejoice with great joy: the wives also and the
children rejoiced: so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard even afar
off.

And at that time were some appointed over the chambers for the
treasures, for the offerings, for the firstfruits, and for the tithes,
to gather into them out of the fields of the cities the portions
of the law for the priests and Levites: for Judah rejoiced for the
priests and for the Levites that waited.\f + \fr 12.44  \ft of the law: that is, appointed by the
law\f*\f + \fr 12.44  \ft for Judah…: Heb. for the joy of Judah\f*\f + \fr 12.44 
\ft waited: Heb. stood\f*

And both the singers and the porters kept the ward of their
God, and the ward of the purification, according to the commandment
of David, \add and\add* of Solomon his son.

For in the days of David and Asaph of old \add there were\add*
chief of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgiving unto God.

And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel, and in the days
of Nehemiah, gave the portions of the singers and the porters, every
day his portion: and they sanctified \add holy things\add* unto the
Levites; and the Levites sanctified \add them\add* unto the children
of Aaron.\f + \fr 12.47  \ft sanctified: that is, set apart\f*

On that day they read in the book of Moses in the audience
of the people; and therein was found written, that the Ammonite and the
Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever;\f + \fr 13.1 
\ft they…: Heb. there was read\f*\f + \fr 13.1  \ft audience: Heb.
ears\f*

Because they met not the children of Israel with bread and with
water, but hired Balaam against them, that he should curse them: howbeit our
God turned the curse into a blessing.

Now it came to pass, when they had heard the law, that they
separated from Israel all the mixed multitude.

And before this, Eliashib the priest, having the oversight
of the chamber of the house of our God, \add was\add* allied unto
Tobiah:\f + \fr 13.4  \ft having…: Heb. being set over\f*

And he had prepared for him a great chamber, where aforetime
they laid the meat offerings, the frankincense, and the vessels,
and the tithes of the corn, the new wine, and the oil, which was
commanded \add to be given\add* to the Levites, and the singers,
and the porters; and the offerings of the priests.\f + \fr 13.5 
\ft which…: Heb. the commandment of the Levites\f*

But in all this \add time\add* was not I at Jerusalem: for in the
two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon came I unto the
king, and after certain days obtained I leave of the king:\f + \fr 13.6 
\ft after…: Heb. at the end of days\f*\f + \fr 13.6  \ft obtained…: or, I earnestly
requested\f*

And I came to Jerusalem, and understood of the evil that Eliashib
did for Tobiah, in preparing him a chamber in the courts of the house
of God.

And it grieved me sore: therefore I cast forth all the household
stuff of Tobiah out of the chamber.

Then I commanded, and they cleansed the chambers: and thither brought I
again the vessels of the house of God, with the meat offering and the
frankincense.

And I perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been
given \add them:\add* for the Levites and the singers, that did the
work, were fled every one to his field.

Then contended I with the rulers, and said, Why is the house
of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their
place.\f + \fr 13.11  \ft place: Heb. standing\f*

Then brought all Judah the tithe of the corn and the new wine
and the oil unto the treasuries.\f + \fr 13.12  \ft treasuries: or,
storehouses\f*

And I made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest,
and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah: and next to them
\add was\add* Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah: for they were
counted faithful, and their office \add was\add* to distribute unto their
brethren.\f + \fr 13.13  \ft treasuries: or, storehouses\f*\f + \fr 13.13 
\ft next…: Heb. at their hand\f*\f + \fr 13.13  \ft their office…: Heb. it was upon
them\f*

Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my
good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for the
offices thereof.\f + \fr 13.14  \ft good…: Heb. kindnesses\f*\f + \fr 13.14 
\ft offices: or, observations\f*

In those days saw I in Judah \add some\add* treading  wine
presses on the sabbath, and bringing in sheaves, and lading asses;
as also wine, grapes, and figs, and all \add manner of\add* burdens,
which they brought into Jerusalem on the sabbath day: and I testified
\add against them\add* in the day wherein they sold victuals.

There dwelt men of Tyre also therein, which brought fish,
and all manner of ware, and sold on the sabbath unto the children
of Judah, and in Jerusalem.

Then I contended with the nobles of Judah, and said unto them, What
evil thing \add is\add* this that ye do, and profane the sabbath
day?

Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this
evil upon us, and upon this city? yet ye bring more wrath upon Israel
by profaning the sabbath.

And it came to pass, that when the gates of Jerusalem began to be
dark before the sabbath, I commanded that the gates should be shut,
and charged that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and
\add some\add* of my servants set I at the gates, \add that\add*
there should no burden be brought in on the sabbath day.

So the merchants and sellers of all kind of ware lodged without
Jerusalem once or twice.

Then I testified against them, and said unto them, Why lodge
ye about the wall? if ye do \add so\add* again, I will lay hands
on you. From that time forth came they no \add more\add* on the sabbath.\f + \fr 13.21 
\ft about: Heb. before\f*

And I commanded the Levites that they should cleanse themselves, and
\add that\add* they should come \add and\add* keep the gates, to
sanctify the sabbath day. Remember me, O my God, \add concerning\add*
this also, and spare me according to the greatness of thy mercy.\f + \fr 13.22 
\ft greatness: or, multitude\f*

In those days also saw I Jews \add that\add* had married
wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, \add and\add* of Moab:\f + \fr 13.23 
\ft had…: Heb. had made to dwell with them\f*

And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and
could not speak in the Jews’ language, but according to the language
of each people.\f + \fr 13.24  \ft could…: Heb. they discerned not to
speak\f*\f + \fr 13.24  \ft of each…: Heb. of people and people\f*

And I contended with them, and cursed them, and smote certain
of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God,
\add saying\add*, Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons,
nor take their daughters unto your sons, or for yourselves.\f + \fr 13.25 
\ft cursed: or, reviled\f*

Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? yet among
many nations was there no king like him, who was beloved of his God,
and God made him king over all Israel: nevertheless even him did
outlandish women cause to sin.

Shall we then hearken unto you to do all this great evil,
to transgress against our God in marrying strange wives?

And \add one\add* of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib
the high priest, \add was\add* son in law to Sanballat the Horonite:
therefore I chased him from me.

Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood,
and the covenant of the priesthood, and of the Levites.\f + \fr 13.29 
\ft because…: Heb. for the defilings\f*

Thus cleansed I them from all strangers, and appointed the
wards of the priests and the Levites, every one in his business;

And for the wood offering, at times appointed, and for the
firstfruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.

headers.toc1: The Book of Esther
headers.mt1: The Book of Esther

verses.text:
Now it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus, (this \add is\add*
Ahasuerus which reigned, from India even unto Ethiopia, \add over\add*
an hundred and seven and twenty provinces:)

\add That\add* in those days, when the king Ahasuerus sat on the
throne of his kingdom, which \add was\add* in Shushan the palace,

In the third year of his reign, he made a feast unto all his
princes and his servants; the power of Persia and Media, the nobles
and princes of the provinces, \add being\add* before him:

When he shewed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the honour
of his excellent majesty many days, \add even\add* an hundred and
fourscore days.

And when these days were expired, the king made a feast unto all the
people that were present in Shushan the palace, both unto great and
small, seven days, in the court of the garden of the king’s palace;\f + \fr 1.5 
\ft present: Heb. found\f*

\add Where were\add* white, green, and blue, \add hangings\add*,
fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings and
pillars of marble: the beds \add were of\add* gold and silver, upon a
pavement of red, and blue, and white, and black, marble.\f + \fr 1.6 
\ft blue, hangings: or, violet, etc\f*\f + \fr 1.6  \ft of red…: or, of porphyre, and marble and alabaster, and stone of blue
colour\f*

And they gave \add them\add* drink in vessels of gold, (the
vessels being diverse one from another,) and royal wine in abundance,
according to the state of the king.\f + \fr 1.7  \ft royal…: Heb. wine of the
kingdom\f*\f + \fr 1.7  \ft state: Heb. hand\f*

And the drinking \add was\add* according to the law; none did
compel: for so the king had appointed to all the officers of his
house, that they should do according to every man’s pleasure.

Also Vashti the queen made a feast for the women \add in\add*
the royal house which \add belonged\add* to king Ahasuerus.

On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was merry
with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, and Abagtha,
Zethar, and Carcas, the seven chamberlains that served in the presence
of Ahasuerus the king,\f + \fr 1.10  \ft chamberlains: or, eunuchs\f*

To bring Vashti the queen before the king with the crown royal,
to shew the people and the princes her beauty: for she \add was\add*
fair to look on.\f + \fr 1.11  \ft fair…: Heb. good of countenance\f*

But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s commandment
by \add his\add* chamberlains: therefore was the king very wroth,
and his anger burned in him.\f + \fr 1.12  \ft by his…: Heb. which was by the hand of his
eunuchs\f*

Then the king said to the wise men, which knew the times, (for so
\add was\add* the king’s manner toward all that knew law and judgment:

And the next unto him \add was\add* Carshena, Shethar, Admatha,
Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, \add and\add* Memucan, the seven princes
of Persia and Media, which saw the king’s face, \add and\add* which
sat the first in the kingdom;)

What shall we do unto the queen Vashti according to law, because she hath not
performed the commandment of the king Ahasuerus by the chamberlains?\f + \fr 1.15 
\ft What…: Heb. What to do\f*

And Memucan answered before the king and the princes, Vashti
the queen hath not done wrong to the king only, but also to all the
princes, and to all the people that \add are\add* in all the provinces
of the king Ahasuerus.

For \add this\add* deed of the queen shall come abroad unto all
women, so that they shall despise their husbands in their eyes, when it shall be
reported, The king Ahasuerus commanded Vashti the queen to be brought
in before him, but she came not.

\add Likewise\add* shall the ladies of Persia and Media say
this day unto all the king’s princes, which have heard of the deed
of the queen. Thus \add shall there arise\add* too much contempt
and wrath.

If it please the king, let there go a royal commandment from
him, and let it be written among the laws of the Persians and the
Medes, that it be not altered, That Vashti come no more before king
Ahasuerus; and let the king give her royal estate unto another that is
better than she.\f + \fr 1.19  \ft If it…: Heb. If it be good with the
king\f*\f + \fr 1.19  \ft unto…: Heb. unto her companion\f*\f + \fr 1.19 
\ft from him: Heb. from before him\f*\f + \fr 1.19  \ft be not…: Heb. pass not
away\f*

And when the king’s decree which he shall make shall be published
throughout all his empire, (for it is great,) all the wives shall
give to their husbands honour, both to great and small.

And the saying pleased  the king and the princes; and the
king did according to the word of Memucan:\f + \fr 1.21  \ft pleased…: Heb. was good in the eyes of the
king\f*

For he sent letters into all the king’s provinces, into every
province according to the writing thereof, and to every people after their
language, that every man should bear rule in his own house, and that
\add it\add* should be published according to the language of every
people.\f + \fr 1.22  \ft that it…: Heb. that one should publish it according to the language of his
people\f*

After these things, when the wrath of king Ahasuerus was appeased,
he remembered Vashti, and what she had done, and what was decreed against her.

Then said the king’s servants that ministered unto him, Let there be
fair young virgins sought for the king:

And let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his
kingdom, that they may gather together all the fair young virgins
unto Shushan the palace, to the house of the women, unto the custody
of Hege the king’s chamberlain, keeper  of the women; and let their things for
purification be given \add them:\add*\f + \fr 2.3  \ft unto the…: Heb. unto the
hand\f*\f + \fr 2.3  \ft Hege: also called, Hegai\f*

And let the maiden which pleaseth the king be queen instead of
Vashti. And the thing pleased the king; and he did so.

Who had been carried away from Jerusalem with the captivity
which had been carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar
the king of Babylon had carried away.\f + \fr 2.6  \ft Jeconiah: also called,
Jehoiachin\f*

And he brought up Hadassah, that \add is\add*, Esther, his
uncle’s daughter: for she had neither father nor mother, and the
maid \add was\add* fair and beautiful; whom Mordecai, when her father
and mother were dead, took for his own daughter.\f + \fr 2.7  \ft brought…: Heb.
nourished\f*\f + \fr 2.7  \ft fair…: Heb. fair of form, and good of
countenance\f*

So it came to pass, when the king’s commandment and his decree
was heard, and when many maidens were gathered together unto Shushan
the palace, to the custody of Hegai, that Esther was brought also unto the
king’s house, to the custody of Hegai, keeper of the women.

And the maiden pleased  him, and she obtained kindness of him;
and he speedily gave her her things for purification, with such things as
belonged to her, and seven maidens, \add which were\add* meet to be
given her, out of the king’s house: and he preferred her and her
maids unto the best \add place\add* of the house of the women.\f + \fr 2.9 
\ft such…: Heb. her portions\f*\f + \fr 2.9  \ft preferred: Heb.
changed\f*

Esther had not shewed her people nor her kindred: for Mordecai
had charged her that she should not shew \add it\add*.

And Mordecai walked every day before the court of the women’s
house, to know how Esther did, and what should become of her.\f + \fr 2.11 
\ft to know…: Heb. to know the peace\f*

Now when every maid’s turn was come to go in to king Ahasuerus,
after that she had been twelve months, according to the manner of the
women, (for so were the days of their purifications accomplished,
\add to wit\add*, six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with sweet
odours, and with \add other\add* things for the purifying of the
women;)

Then thus came \add every\add* maiden unto the king; whatsoever she
desired was given her to go with her out of the house of the women
unto the king’s house.

In the evening she went, and on the morrow she returned into the
second house of the women, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the king’s
chamberlain, which kept the concubines: she came in unto the king
no more, except the king delighted in her, and that she were called
by name.

Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the
uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter, was come to go
in unto the king, she required nothing but what Hegai the king’s
chamberlain, the keeper of the women, appointed. And Esther obtained
favour in the sight of all them that looked upon her.

So Esther was taken unto king Ahasuerus into his house royal
in the tenth month, which \add is\add* the month Tebeth, in the seventh
year of his reign.

And the king loved Esther above all the women, and she obtained
grace and favour in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he
set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen instead of
Vashti.\f + \fr 2.17  \ft favour: or, kindness\f*\f + \fr 2.17  \ft in his…: Heb. before
him\f*

Then the king made a great feast unto all his princes and his
servants, \add even\add* Esther’s feast; and he made a release to the
provinces, and gave gifts, according to the state of the king.\f + \fr 2.18 
\ft release: Heb. rest\f*

And when the virgins were gathered together the second time,
then Mordecai sat in the king’s gate.

In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king’s gate, two
of the king’s chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept
the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.\f + \fr 2.21 
\ft Bigthan: also called, Bigthana\f*\f + \fr 2.21  \ft the door: Heb. the
threshold\f*

And the thing was known to Mordecai, who told \add it\add*
unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king \add thereof\add*
in Mordecai’s name.

And when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found
out; therefore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written
in the book of the chronicles before the king.

After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son
of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the
princes that \add were\add* with him.

And all the king’s servants, that \add were\add* in the king’s
gate, bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded
concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did \add him\add* reverence.

Then the king’s servants, which \add were\add* in the king’s
gate, said unto Mordecai, Why transgressest thou the king’s commandment?

Now it came to pass, when they spake daily unto him, and he
hearkened not unto them, that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai’s
matters would stand: for he had told them that he \add was\add* a
Jew.

And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence,
then was Haman full of wrath.

And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had
shewed him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy
all the Jews that \add were\add* throughout the whole kingdom of
Ahasuerus, \add even\add* the people of Mordecai.

In the first month, that \add is\add*, the month Nisan, in the
twelfth year of king Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, that \add is\add*,
the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month, \add to\add*
the twelfth \add month\add*, that \add is\add*, the month Adar.

And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people
scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces
of thy kingdom; and their laws \add are\add* diverse from all people;
neither keep they the king’s laws: therefore it \add is\add* not for the
king’s profit to suffer them.\f + \fr 3.8  \ft for the…: Heb. meet or, equal,
etc\f*

If it please the king, let it be written that they may be destroyed:
and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver to the hands of those that have the
charge of the business, to bring \add it\add* into the king’s treasuries.\f + \fr 3.9 
\ft that they…: Heb. to destroy them\f*\f + \fr 3.9  \ft pay: Heb.
weigh\f*

And the king took his ring from his hand, and gave it unto
Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews’ enemy.\f + \fr 3.10 
\ft enemy: or, oppressor\f*

And the king said unto Haman, The silver \add is\add* given
to thee, the people also, to do with them as it seemeth good to thee.

Then were the king’s scribes  called on the thirteenth day
of the first month, and there was written according to all that Haman
had commanded unto the king’s lieutenants, and to the governors that
\add were\add* over every province, and to the rulers of every people
of every province according to the writing thereof, and \add to\add*
every people after their language; in the name of king Ahasuerus
was it written, and sealed with the king’s ring.\f + \fr 3.12  \ft scribes: or,
secretaries\f*

And the letters were sent by posts into all the king’s provinces,
to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Jews, both young
and old, little children and women, in one day, \add even\add* upon the
thirteenth \add day\add* of the twelfth month, which is the month
Adar, and \add to take\add* the spoil of them for a prey.

The copy of the writing for a commandment to be given in every
province was published unto all people, that they should be ready
against that day.

The posts went out, being hastened by the king’s commandment,
and the decree was given in Shushan the palace. And the king and
Haman sat down to drink; but the city Shushan was perplexed.

And came even before the king’s gate: for none \add might\add*
enter into the king’s gate clothed with sackcloth.

And in every province, whithersoever the king’s commandment
and his decree came, \add there was\add* great mourning among the
Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth
and ashes.\f + \fr 4.3  \ft many…: Heb. sackcloth and ashes were laid under
many\f*

So Esther’s maids and her chamberlains came and told \add it\add*
her. Then was the queen exceedingly grieved; and she sent raiment
to clothe Mordecai, and to take away his sackcloth from him: but he
received \add it\add* not.\f + \fr 4.4  \ft chamberlains: Heb. eunuchs\f*

Then called Esther for Hatach, \add one\add* of the king’s
chamberlains, whom he had appointed to attend upon her, and gave him a
commandment to Mordecai, to know what it \add was\add*, and why it
\add was\add*.\f + \fr 4.5  \ft appointed…: Heb. set before her\f*

So Hatach went forth to Mordecai unto the street of the city, which
\add was\add* before the king’s gate.

And Mordecai told him of all that had happened unto him, and of the
sum of the money that Haman had promised to pay to the king’s treasuries
for the Jews, to destroy them.

Also he gave him the copy of the writing of the decree that was
given at Shushan to destroy them, to shew \add it\add* unto Esther,
and to declare \add it\add* unto her, and to charge her that she should go
in unto the king, to make supplication unto him, and to make request
before him for her people.
And Hatach came and told Esther the words of Mordecai.

Again Esther spake unto Hatach, and gave him commandment
unto Mordecai;

All the king’s servants, and the people of the king’s provinces,
do know, that whosoever, whether man or woman, shall come unto the
king into the inner court, who is not called, \add there is\add*
one law of his to put \add him\add* to death, except such to whom the
king shall hold out the golden sceptre, that he may live: but I have not been
called to come in unto the king these thirty days.
And they told to Mordecai Esther’s words.

Then Mordecai commanded to answer Esther, Think not with thyself
that thou shalt escape in the king’s house, more than all the Jews.

For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, \add then\add*
shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another
place; but thou and thy father’s house shall be destroyed: and who
knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for \add such\add* a
time as this?\f + \fr 4.14  \ft enlargement: Heb. respiration\f*

Then Esther bade \add them\add* return Mordecai \add this
answer\add*,

Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan,
and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or
day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the
king, which \add is\add* not according to the law: and if I perish,
I perish.\f + \fr 4.16  \ft present: Heb. found\f*

So Mordecai went his way, and did according to all that Esther
had commanded him.\f + \fr 4.17  \ft went…: Heb. passed\f*

Now it came to pass on the third day, that Esther put on \add her\add*
royal \add apparel\add*, and stood in the inner court of the king’s
house, over against the king’s house: and the king sat upon his royal
throne in the royal house, over against the gate of the house.

And it was so, when the king saw Esther the queen standing
in the court, \add that\add* she obtained favour in his sight: and the
king held out to Esther the golden sceptre that \add was\add* in his
hand. So Esther drew near, and touched the top of the sceptre.

Then said the king unto her, What wilt thou, queen Esther? and what
\add is\add* thy request? it shall be even given thee to the half
of the kingdom.

And Esther answered, If \add it seem\add* good unto the king,
let the king and Haman come this day unto the banquet that I have
prepared for him.

Then the king said, Cause Haman to make haste, that he may
do as Esther hath said. So the king and Haman came to the banquet
that Esther had prepared.

And the king said unto Esther at the banquet of wine, What
\add is\add* thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: and what
\add is\add* thy request? even to the half of the kingdom it shall be
performed.

Then answered Esther, and said, My petition and my request
\add is;\add*

If I have found favour in the sight of the king, and if it
please the king to grant my petition, and to perform my request,
let the king and Haman come to the banquet that I shall prepare for them, and I will
do to morrow as the king hath said.\f + \fr 5.8  \ft perform: Heb.
do\f*

Then went Haman forth that day joyful and with a glad heart:
but when Haman saw Mordecai in the king’s gate, that he stood not
up, nor moved for him, he was full of indignation against Mordecai.

Nevertheless Haman refrained himself: and when he came home,
he sent and called for his friends, and Zeresh his wife.\f + \fr 5.10 
\ft called…: Heb. caused to come\f*

And Haman told them of the glory of his riches, and the multitude
of his children, and all \add the things\add* wherein the king had
promoted him, and how he had advanced him above the princes and servants
of the king.

Haman said moreover, Yea, Esther the queen did let no man come
in with the king unto the banquet that she had prepared but myself; and to
morrow am I invited unto her also with the king.

Yet all this availeth me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai
the Jew sitting at the king’s gate.

Then said Zeresh his wife and all his friends unto him, Let a
gallows be made of fifty cubits high, and to morrow speak thou unto the
king that Mordecai may be hanged thereon: then go thou in merrily
with the king unto the banquet. And the thing pleased Haman; and he
caused the gallows to be made.\f + \fr 5.14  \ft gallows: Heb. tree\f*

On that night could not the king sleep, and he commanded to
bring the book of records of the chronicles; and they were read before
the king.\f + \fr 6.1  \ft could…: Heb. the king’s sleep fled away\f*

And it was found written, that Mordecai had told of Bigthana
and Teresh, two of the king’s chamberlains, the keepers of the door,
who sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.\f + \fr 6.2  \ft Bigthana: also called,
Bigthan\f*\f + \fr 6.2  \ft door: Heb. threshold\f*

And the king said, What honour and dignity hath been done to
Mordecai for this? Then said the king’s servants that ministered
unto him, There is nothing done for him.

And the king said, Who \add is\add* in the court? Now Haman
was come into the outward court of the king’s house, to speak unto the
king to hang Mordecai on the gallows that he had prepared for him.

And the king’s servants said unto him, Behold, Haman standeth
in the court. And the king said, Let him come in.

So Haman came in. And the king said unto him, What shall be
done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour? Now Haman thought
in his heart, To whom would the king delight to do honour more than to
myself?\f + \fr 6.6  \ft whom the king…: Heb. in whose honour the king
delighteth\f*

And Haman answered the king, For the man whom the king delighteth
 to honour,\f + \fr 6.7  \ft whom the king…: Heb. in whose honour the king
delighteth\f*

Let the royal apparel be brought which the king \add useth\add*
to wear, and the horse that the king rideth upon, and the crown royal
which is set upon his head:\f + \fr 6.8  \ft Let…: Heb. Let them bring the royal
apparel\f*\f + \fr 6.8  \ft which the king…: Heb. wherewith the king clotheth
himself\f*

And let this apparel and horse be delivered to the hand of
one of the king’s most noble princes, that they may array the man
\add withal\add* whom the king delighteth to honour, and bring him on
horseback through the street of the city, and proclaim before him, Thus shall it be
done to the man whom the king delighteth to honour.\f + \fr 6.9 
\ft bring…: Heb. cause him to ride\f*

Then the king said to Haman, Make haste, \add and\add* take
the apparel and the horse, as thou hast said, and do even so to Mordecai
the Jew, that sitteth at the king’s gate: let nothing fail of all that thou hast
spoken.\f + \fr 6.10  \ft let…: Heb. suffer not a whit to fall\f*

Then took Haman the apparel and the horse, and arrayed Mordecai,
and brought him on horseback through the street of the city, and
proclaimed before him, Thus shall it be done unto the man whom the
king delighteth  to honour.

And Mordecai came again to the king’s gate. But Haman hasted
to his house mourning, and having his head covered.

And Haman told Zeresh his wife and all his friends every \add thing\add*
that had befallen him. Then said his wise men and Zeresh his wife
unto him, If Mordecai \add be\add* of the seed of the Jews, before
whom thou hast begun to fall, thou shalt not prevail against him, but shalt
surely fall before him.

And while they \add were\add* yet talking with him, came the
king’s chamberlains, and hasted to bring Haman unto the banquet that
Esther had prepared.

So the king and Haman came to banquet with Esther the queen.\f + \fr 7.1 
\ft to banquet: Heb. to drink\f*

And the king said again unto Esther on the second day at the
banquet of wine, What \add is\add* thy petition, queen Esther? and it shall be
granted thee: and what \add is\add* thy request? and it shall be
performed, \add even\add* to the half of the kingdom.

Then Esther the queen answered and said, If I have found favour
in thy sight, O king, and if it please the king, let my life be given
me at my petition, and my people at my request:

For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain,
and to perish. But if we had been sold for bondmen and bondwomen,
I had held my tongue, although the enemy could not countervail the
king’s damage.\f + \fr 7.4  \ft to be destroyed…: Heb. that they should destroy, and kill, and cause to
perish\f*

Then the king Ahasuerus answered and said unto Esther the
queen, Who is he, and where is he, that durst presume in his heart
to do so?\f + \fr 7.5  \ft that…: Heb. whose heart hath filled him\f*

And Esther said, The adversary and enemy \add is\add* this
wicked Haman. Then Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.\f + \fr 7.6 
\ft The adversary: Heb. The man adversary\f*\f + \fr 7.6  \ft before: or, at the presence
of\f*

And the king arising from the banquet of wine in his wrath
\add went\add* into the palace garden: and Haman stood up to make
request for his life to Esther the queen; for he saw that there was
evil determined against him by the king.

Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place
of the banquet of wine; and Haman was fallen upon the bed whereon
Esther \add was\add*. Then said the king, Will he force the queen
also before me in the house? As the word went out of the king’s mouth,
they covered Haman’s face.\f + \fr 7.8  \ft before me: Heb. with
me\f*

And Harbonah, one of the chamberlains, said before the king,
Behold also, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman had made
for Mordecai, who had spoken good for the king, standeth in the house
of Haman. Then the king said, Hang him thereon.\f + \fr 7.9  \ft gallows: Heb.
tree\f*

So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for
Mordecai. Then was the king’s wrath pacified.

On that day did the king Ahasuerus give the house of Haman
the Jews’ enemy unto Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the
king; for Esther had told what he \add was\add* unto her.

And the king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman,
and gave it unto Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house
of Haman.

And Esther spake yet again before the king, and fell down
at his feet, and besought him with tears to put away the mischief
of Haman the Agagite, and his device that he had devised against the
Jews.\f + \fr 8.3  \ft and besought…: Heb. and she wept, and besought
him\f*

Then the king held out the golden sceptre toward Esther. So
Esther arose, and stood before the king,

And said, If it please the king, and if I have found favour
in his sight, and the thing \add seem\add* right before the king, and I
\add be\add* pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the
letters devised by Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he
wrote to destroy the Jews which \add are\add* in all the king’s provinces:\f + \fr 8.5 
\ft devised: Heb. the device\f*\f + \fr 8.5  \ft which he…: or, who
wrote\f*

For how can I endure to see the evil that shall come unto my
people? or how can I endure to see the destruction of my kindred?\f + \fr 8.6 
\ft endure…: Heb. be able that I may see\f*

Then the king Ahasuerus said unto Esther the queen and to
Mordecai the Jew, Behold, I have given Esther the house of Haman,
and him they have hanged upon the gallows, because he laid his hand
upon the Jews.

Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the king’s
name, and seal \add it\add* with the king’s ring: for the writing
which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring,
may no man reverse.

Then were the king’s scribes called at that time in the third
month, that \add is\add*, the month Sivan, on the three and twentieth
\add day\add* thereof; and it was written according to all that Mordecai
commanded unto the Jews, and to the lieutenants, and the deputies
and rulers of the provinces which \add are\add* from India unto Ethiopia,
an hundred twenty and seven provinces, unto every province according to the
writing thereof, and unto every people after their language, and to the
Jews according to their writing, and according to their language.

And he wrote in the king Ahasuerus’ name, and sealed \add it\add*
with the king’s ring, and sent letters by posts on horseback, \add and\add*
riders  on mules, camels, \add and\add* young dromedaries:

Wherein the king granted the Jews which \add were\add* in every
city to gather themselves together, and to stand for their life,
to destroy, to slay, and to cause to perish, all the power of the
people and province that would assault them, \add both\add* little
ones and women, and \add to take\add* the spoil of them for a prey,

Upon one day in all the provinces of king Ahasuerus, \add namely\add*,
upon the thirteenth \add day\add* of the twelfth month, which \add is\add*
the month Adar.

The copy of the writing for a commandment to be given in every
province \add was\add* published unto all people, and that the Jews
should be ready against that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.\f + \fr 8.13 
\ft published: Heb. revealed\f*

\add So\add* the posts that rode upon mules \add and\add*
camels went out, being hastened and pressed on by the king’s commandment.
And the decree was given at Shushan the palace.

And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal
apparel of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a
garment of fine linen and purple: and the city of Shushan rejoiced
and was glad.\f + \fr 8.15  \ft blue: or, violet\f*
The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour.

And in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the
king’s commandment and his decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness,
a feast and a good day. And many of the people of the land became
Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell upon them.

Now in the twelfth month, that \add is\add*, the month Adar,
on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king’s commandment and his
decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies
of the Jews hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned
to the contrary, that the Jews had rule over them that hated them;)

The Jews gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the
provinces of the king Ahasuerus, to lay hand on such as sought their
hurt: and no man could withstand them; for the fear of them fell
upon all people.

And all the rulers of the provinces, and the lieutenants, and the
deputies, and officers of the king, helped the Jews; because the
fear of Mordecai fell upon them.\f + \fr 9.3  \ft officers…: Heb. those which did the business that belonged to the
king\f*

For Mordecai \add was\add* great in the king’s house, and his
fame went out throughout all the provinces: for this man Mordecai
waxed greater and greater.

Thus the Jews smote all their enemies with the stroke of the
sword, and slaughter, and destruction, and did what they would unto those that
hated them.\f + \fr 9.5  \ft what…: Heb. according to their will\f*

And in Shushan the palace the Jews slew and destroyed five
hundred men.
And Parshandatha, and Dalphon, and Aspatha,
And Poratha, and Adalia, and Aridatha,
And Parmashta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Vajezatha,

The ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the
Jews, slew they; but on the spoil laid they not their hand.

On that day the number of those that were slain in Shushan
the palace was brought before the king.\f + \fr 9.11  \ft was…: Heb.
came\f*

And the king said unto Esther the queen, The Jews have slain
and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten
sons of Haman; what have they done in the rest of the king’s provinces? now what
\add is\add* thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: or what
\add is\add* thy request further? and it shall be done.

Then said Esther, If it please the king, let it be granted
to the Jews which \add are\add* in Shushan to do to morrow also according unto this
day’s decree, and let Haman’s ten sons be hanged upon the gallows.\f + \fr 9.13 
\ft let Haman’s…: Heb. let men hang, etc\f*

And the king commanded it so to be done: and the decree was
given at Shushan; and they hanged Haman’s ten sons.

For the Jews that \add were\add* in Shushan gathered themselves
together on the fourteenth day also of the month Adar, and slew three
hundred men at Shushan; but on the prey they laid not their hand.

But the other Jews that \add were\add* in the king’s provinces
gathered themselves together, and stood for their lives, and had
rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five
thousand, but they laid not their hands on the prey,

On the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and on the fourteenth
day of the same rested they, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.\f + \fr 9.17 
\ft of the same: Heb. in it\f*

But the Jews that \add were\add* at Shushan assembled together
on the thirteenth \add day\add* thereof, and on the fourteenth thereof; and on the
fifteenth \add day\add* of the same they rested, and made it a day
of feasting and gladness.

Therefore the Jews of the villages, that dwelt in the unwalled
towns, made the fourteenth day of the month Adar \add a day of\add*
gladness and feasting, and a good day, and of sending portions one
to another.

And Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters unto all the
Jews that \add were\add* in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus,
\add both\add* nigh and far,

To stablish \add this\add* among them, that they should keep
the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same,
yearly,

As the days wherein the Jews rested from their enemies, and the
month which was turned unto them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning
into a good day: that they should make them days of feasting and
joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.

And the Jews undertook to do as they had begun, and as Mordecai
had written unto them;

Because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy
of all the Jews, had devised against the Jews to destroy them, and had
cast Pur, that \add is\add*, the lot, to consume them, and to destroy
them;\f + \fr 9.24  \ft consume: Heb. crush\f*

But when \add Esther\add* came before the king, he commanded
by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Jews,
should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be
hanged on the gallows.\f + \fr 9.25  \ft when…: Heb. when she came\f*

Wherefore they called these days Purim after the name of Pur.
Therefore for all the words of this letter, and \add of that\add*
which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come unto
them,\f + \fr 9.26  \ft Pur: that is, Lot\f*

The Jews ordained, and took upon them, and upon their seed,
and upon all such as joined themselves unto them, so as it should not
fail, that they would keep these two days according to their writing, and according to their
\add appointed\add* time every year;\f + \fr 9.27  \ft fail: Heb.
pass\f*

And \add that\add* these days \add should be\add* remembered
and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province,
and every city; and \add that\add* these days of Purim should not
fail from among the Jews, nor the memorial of them perish from their
seed.\f + \fr 9.28  \ft fail: Heb. pass\f*\f + \fr 9.28  \ft perish: Heb. be
ended\f*

Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai
the Jew, wrote with all authority, to confirm this second letter
of Purim.\f + \fr 9.29  \ft authority: Heb. strength\f*

And he sent the letters unto all the Jews, to the hundred
twenty and seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, \add with\add*
words of peace and truth,

To confirm these days of Purim in their times \add appointed\add*,
according as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had enjoined them, and as they had
decreed for themselves and for their seed, the matters of the fastings
and their cry.\f + \fr 9.31  \ft themselves: Heb. their souls\f*

And the decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim;
and it was written in the book.

And the king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land, and \add upon\add*
the isles of the sea.

And all the acts of his power and of his might, and the declaration
of the greatness of Mordecai, whereunto the king advanced him, \add are\add*
they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media
and Persia?\f + \fr 10.2  \ft advanced…: Heb. made him great\f*

For Mordecai the Jew \add was\add* next unto king Ahasuerus,
and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren,
seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.

headers.toc1: The Book of Job
headers.mt1: The Book of Job

verses.text:
There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name \add was\add*
Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God,
and eschewed evil.
And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters.

His substance also was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand
camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses,
and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the
men of the east.\f + \fr 1.3  \ft substance: or, cattle\f*\f + \fr 1.3 
\ft household: or, husbandry\f*\f + \fr 1.3  \ft men: Heb. sons\f*

And his sons went and feasted \add in their\add* houses, every
one his day; and sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to
drink with them.

And it was so, when the days of \add their\add* feasting were gone
about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the
morning, and offered burnt offerings \add according\add* to the number
of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and
cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.\f + \fr 1.5 
\ft continually: Heb. all the days\f*

Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the
\nd LORD\nd*, and Satan came also among them.\f + \fr 1.6  \ft Satan: Heb. the
adversary\f*\f + \fr 1.6  \ft among: Heb. in the midst of\f*

And the 
d LORD
d* said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then
Satan answered the 
d LORD
d*, and said, From going to and fro
in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

And the \nd LORD\nd* said unto Satan, Hast thou considered
my servant Job, that \add there is\add* none like him in the earth,
a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth
evil?\f + \fr 1.8  \ft considered: Heb. set thy heart on\f*

Then Satan answered the \nd LORD\nd*, and said, Doth Job fear
God for nought?

Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house,
and about all that he hath on every side? thou hast blessed the work
of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.\f + \fr 1.10 
\ft substance: or, cattle\f*

But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will
curse thee to thy face.\f + \fr 1.11  \ft and he…: Heb. if he curse thee not to thy
face\f*

And the \nd LORD\nd* said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath
\add is\add* in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine
hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 1.12 
\ft power: Heb. hand\f*

And there was a day when his sons and his daughters \add were\add*
eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house:

And there came a messenger unto Job, and said, The oxen were
plowing, and the asses feeding beside them:

While he \add was\add* yet speaking, there came also another, and
said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the
sheep, and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped
alone to tell thee.\f + \fr 1.16  \ft The fire…: or, A great fire\f*

While he \add was\add* yet speaking, there came also another, and
said, The Chaldeans made out three bands, and fell upon the camels,

\ft that…: Heb. the rest of thy table\f*

But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment
and justice take hold \add on thee\add*.\f + \fr 36.17  \ft take…: or, should uphold
thee\f*

Because \add there is\add* wrath, \add beware\add* lest he take thee
away with \add his\add* stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver
thee.\f + \fr 36.18  \ft deliver…: Heb. turn thee aside\f*

Will he esteem thy riches? \add no\add*, not gold, nor all the
forces of strength.
Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place.

Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this hast thou chosen
rather than affliction.
Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him?

Who hath enjoined him his way? or who can say, Thou hast wrought
iniquity?
Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold.
Every man may see it; man may behold \add it\add* afar off.

Behold, God \add is\add* great, and we know \add him\add*
not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.

For he maketh small the drops of water: they pour down rain
according to the vapour thereof:
Which the clouds do drop \add and\add* distil upon man abundantly.

Also can \add any\add* understand the spreadings of the clouds,
\add or\add* the noise of his tabernacle?

Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom
of the sea.\f + \fr 36.30  \ft bottom: Heb. roots\f*
For by them judgeth he the people; he giveth meat in abundance.

With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it \add not to
shine\add* by \add the cloud\add* that cometh betwixt.

The noise thereof sheweth concerning it, the cattle also concerning the
vapour.\f + \fr 36.33  \ft the vapour: Heb. that which goeth up\f*
At this also my heart trembleth, and is moved out of his place.

Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound \add that\add*
goeth out of his mouth.\f + \fr 37.2  \ft Hear…: Heb. Hear in hearing\f*

He directeth it under the whole heaven, and his lightning unto the
ends of the earth.\f + \fr 37.3  \ft lightning: Heb. light\f*\f + \fr 37.3 
\ft ends: Heb. wings\f*

After it a voice roareth: he thundereth with the voice of his
excellency; and he will not stay them when his voice is heard.

God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth
he, which we cannot comprehend.

For he saith to the snow, Be thou \add on\add* the earth; likewise to the
small rain, and to the great rain of his strength.\f + \fr 37.6 
\ft likewise…: Heb. and to the shower of rain, and to the showers of rain of his
strength\f*

He sealeth up the hand of every man; that all men may know
his work.
Then the beasts go into dens, and remain in their places.

Out of the south cometh the whirlwind: and cold out of the
north.\f + \fr 37.9  \ft south: Heb. chamber\f*\f + \fr 37.9  \ft north: Heb. scattering
winds\f*

By the breath of God frost is given: and the breadth of the
waters is straitened.

Also by watering he wearieth the thick cloud: he scattereth
his bright cloud:\f + \fr 37.11  \ft his…: Heb. the cloud of his
light\f*

And it is turned round about by his counsels: that they may
do whatsoever he commandeth them upon the face of the world in the
earth.

He causeth it to come, whether for correction, or for his
land, or for mercy.\f + \fr 37.13  \ft correction: Heb. a rod\f*

Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous
works of God.

Dost thou know when God disposed them, and caused the light
of his cloud to shine?

Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous
works of him which is perfect in knowledge?

How thy garments \add are\add* warm, when he quieteth the
earth by the south \add wind\add*?

Hast thou with him spread out the sky, \add which is\add*
strong, \add and\add* as a molten looking glass?

Teach us what we shall say unto him; \add for\add* we cannot
order \add our speech\add* by reason of darkness.

Shall it be told him that I speak? if a man speak, surely he shall be swallowed
up.

And now \add men\add* see not the bright light which \add is\add*
in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth them.

Fair weather cometh out of the north: with God \add is\add*
terrible majesty.\f + \fr 37.22  \ft Fair…: Heb. Gold\f*

\add Touching\add* the Almighty, we cannot find him out: \add he
is\add* excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice:
he will not afflict.

Men do therefore fear him: he respecteth not any \add that
are\add* wise of heart.

Then the \nd LORD\nd* answered  Job out of the whirlwind, and
said,

Who \add is\add* this that darkeneth counsel by words without
knowledge?

Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and
answer thou me.\f + \fr 38.3  \ft answer…: Heb. make me know\f*

Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare,
if thou hast understanding.\f + \fr 38.4  \ft hast…: Heb. knowest
understanding\f*

Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath
stretched the line upon it?

Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid
the corner stone thereof;\f + \fr 38.6  \ft foundations: Heb. sockets\f*\f + \fr 38.6 
\ft fastened: Heb. made to sink?\f*

When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God
shouted for joy?

Or \add who\add* shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth,
\add as if\add* it had issued out of the womb?

When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and thick darkness
a swaddlingband for it,

And brake up for it my decreed \add place\add*, and set bars
and doors,\f + \fr 38.10  \ft brake…: or, established my decree upon
it\f*

And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy
proud waves be stayed?\f + \fr 38.11  \ft thy…: Heb. the pride of thy
waves\f*

Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; \add and\add*
caused the dayspring to know his place;

That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, that the
wicked might be shaken out of it?\f + \fr 38.13  \ft ends: Heb. wings\f*

It is turned as clay \add to\add* the seal; and they stand
as a garment.

And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the high
arm shall be broken.

Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou
walked in the search of the depth?

Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou
seen the doors of the shadow of death?

Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? declare if thou
knowest it all.

Where \add is\add* the way \add where\add* light dwelleth? and
\add as for\add* darkness, where \add is\add* the place thereof,

That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest
know the paths \add to\add* the house thereof?\f + \fr 38.20  \ft to the bound: or, at,
etc\f*

Knowest thou \add it\add*, because thou wast then born? or
\add because\add* the number of thy days \add is\add* great?

Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou
seen the treasures of the hail,

Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the
day of battle and war?

By what way is the light parted, \add which\add* scattereth
the east wind upon the earth?

Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters,
or a way for the lightning of thunder;

To cause it to rain on the earth, \add where\add* no man \add is;
on\add* the wilderness, wherein \add there is\add* no man;

To satisfy the desolate and waste \add ground;\add* and to cause the
bud of the tender herb to spring forth?

Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of
dew?

Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven,
who hath gendered it?

The waters are hid as \add with\add* a stone, and the face
of the deep is frozen.\f + \fr 38.30  \ft is…: Heb. is taken\f*

Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose
the bands of Orion?\f + \fr 38.31  \ft Pleiades: or, the seven stars: Heb.
Cimah\f*\f + \fr 38.31  \ft Orion: Heb. Cesil?\f*

Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in his season? or canst thou
guide Arcturus with his sons?\f + \fr 38.32  \ft Mazzaroth: or, the twelve
signs\f*\f + \fr 38.32  \ft guide: Heb. guide them\f*

Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set the
dominion thereof in the earth?

Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that abundance
of waters may cover thee?

Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we
\add are\add*?\f + \fr 38.35  \ft Here…: Heb. Behold us?\f*

Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given
understanding to the heart?

Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can stay the bottles
of heaven,\f + \fr 38.37  \ft stay: Heb. cause to lie down\f*

When the dust groweth into hardness, and the clods cleave fast
together?\f + \fr 38.38  \ft groweth…: or, is turned into mire: Heb. is
poured\f*

Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lion? or fill the appetite
of the young lions,\f + \fr 38.39  \ft the appetite: Heb. the life\f*

When they couch in \add their\add* dens, \add and\add* abide
in the covert to lie in wait?

Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones
cry unto God, they wander for lack of meat.

Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring
forth? \add or\add* canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?

Canst thou number the months \add that\add* they fulfil? or
knowest thou the time when they bring forth?

They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast
out their sorrows.

Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn;
they go forth, and return not unto them.

Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the
bands of the wild ass?

Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his
dwellings.\f + \fr 39.6  \ft barren…: Heb. salt places\f*

He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the
crying of the driver.\f + \fr 39.7  \ft of the driver: Heb. of the
exactor\f*

The range of the mountains \add is\add* his pasture, and he
searcheth after every green thing.

Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy
crib?

Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he
harrow the valleys after thee?

Wilt thou trust him, because his strength \add is\add* great?
or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?

Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and
gather \add it into\add* thy barn?

\add Gavest thou\add* the goodly wings unto the peacocks?
or wings and feathers unto the ostrich?\f + \fr 39.13  \ft wings and…: or, the feathers of the stork and
ostrich\f*
Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust,

And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild
beast may break them.

She is hardened against her young ones, as though \add they
were\add* not hers: her labour is in vain without fear;

Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted
to her understanding.

What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the
horse and his rider.

Hast thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his
neck with thunder?

Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his
nostrils \add is\add* terrible.\f + \fr 39.20  \ft terrible: Heb.
terror\f*

He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in \add his\add* strength:
he goeth on to meet the armed men.\f + \fr 39.21  \ft He paweth: or, His feet
dig\f*\f + \fr 39.21  \ft the armed…: Heb. the armour\f*

He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he
back from the sword.

The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the
shield.

He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither
believeth he that \add it is\add* the sound of the trumpet.

He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle
afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, \add and\add* stretch  her
wings toward the south?

Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest
on high?\f + \fr 39.27  \ft at…: Heb. by thy mouth\f*

She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the
rock, and the strong place.

From thence she seeketh the prey, \add and\add* her eyes behold
afar off.

Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain \add are\add*, there
\add is\add* she.
Moreover the \nd LORD\nd* answered Job, and said,

Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct \add him\add*?
he that reproveth God, let him answer it.
Then Job answered the \nd LORD\nd*, and said,

Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine
hand upon my mouth.

Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yea, twice; but I will proceed no
further.

Then answered the \nd LORD\nd* unto Job out of the whirlwind,
and said,

Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and
declare thou unto me.

Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be
righteous?
Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?

Deck thyself now \add with\add* majesty and excellency; and
array thyself with glory and beauty.

Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one \add that
is\add* proud, and abase him.

Look on every one \add that is\add* proud, \add and\add* bring him
low; and tread down the wicked in their place.

Hide them in the dust together; \add and\add* bind their faces
in secret.

Then will I also confess unto thee that thine own right hand
can save thee.

Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass
as an ox.\f + \fr 40.15  \ft behemoth: probably an extinct animal of some
kind\f*

Lo now, his strength \add is\add* in his loins, and his force
\add is\add* in the navel of his belly.

He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his stones
are wrapped together.\f + \fr 40.17  \ft He…: or, He setteth up\f*

His bones \add are as\add* strong pieces of brass; his bones
\add are\add* like bars of iron.

He \add is\add* the chief of the ways of God: he that made
him can make his sword to approach \add unto him\add*.

Surely the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts
of the field play.

He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed,
and fens.

The shady trees cover him \add with\add* their shadow; the
willows of the brook compass him about.

Behold, he drinketh up a river, \add and\add* hasteth not: he
trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth.\f + \fr 40.23 
\ft he drinketh up: Heb. he oppresseth\f*

He taketh it with his eyes: \add his\add* nose pierceth through
snares.\f + \fr 40.24  \ft He…: or, Will any take him in his sight, or, bore his nose with a
gin?\f*

Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a
cord \add which\add* thou lettest down?\f + \fr 41.1  \ft leviathan: probably an extinct animal of some
kind\f*\f + \fr 41.1  \ft which…: Heb. which thou drownest?\f*

Canst thou put an hook into his nose? or bore his jaw through with a
thorn?

Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft
\add words\add* unto thee?

Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a
servant for ever?

Wilt thou play with him as \add with\add* a bird? or wilt thou
bind him for thy maidens?

Shall the companions make a banquet of him? shall they part
him among the merchants?

Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with
fish spears?
Lay thine hand upon him, remember the battle, do no more.

Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not \add one\add*
be cast down even at the sight of him?

None \add is so\add* fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to
stand before me?

Who hath prevented me, that I should repay \add him? whatsoever
is\add* under the whole heaven is mine.

I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely
proportion.

Who can discover the face of his garment? \add or\add* who can
come \add to him\add* with his double bridle?\f + \fr 41.13  \ft with: or,
within\f*

Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth \add are\add*
terrible round about.

\add His\add* scales \add are his\add* pride, shut up together
\add as with\add* a close seal.\f + \fr 41.15  \ft scales: Heb. strong pieces of
shields\f*
One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.

They are joined one to another, they stick together, that they cannot be
sundered.

By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes \add are\add*
like the eyelids of the morning.

Out of his mouth go burning lamps, \add and\add* sparks of
fire leap out.

Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as \add out\add* of a seething
pot or caldron.
His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth.

In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into
joy before him.\f + \fr 41.22  \ft is turned into joy: Heb. rejoiceth\f*

The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm
in themselves; they cannot be moved.\f + \fr 41.23  \ft flakes: Heb.
fallings\f*

His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the
nether \add millstone\add*.

When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of
breakings they purify themselves.

The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear,
the dart, nor the habergeon.\f + \fr 41.26  \ft habergeon: or, breastplate\f*

He esteemeth iron as straw, \add and\add* brass as rotten
wood.

The arrow cannot make him flee: slingstones are turned with him into
stubble.

Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a
spear.

Sharp stones \add are\add* under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed
things upon the mire.\f + \fr 41.30  \ft Sharp stones: Heb. Sharp pieces of
potsherd\f*

He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of
ointment.

He maketh a path to shine after him; \add one\add* would think
the deep \add to be\add* hoary.

Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear.\f + \fr 41.33 
\ft is made without fear: or, behave themselves without fear\f*

He beholdeth all high \add things:\add* he \add is\add* a
king over all the children of pride.
Then Job answered the \nd LORD\nd*, and said,

I know that thou canst do every \add thing\add*, and \add that\add*
no thought can be withholden from thee.\f + \fr 42.2  \ft no thought can be…: or, no thought of thine can be
hindered\f*

Who \add is\add* he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I
uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I
knew not.

Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and
declare thou unto me.

I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine
eye seeth thee.

Wherefore I abhor \add myself\add*, and repent in dust and
ashes.

And it was \add so\add*, that after the \nd LORD\nd* had spoken
these words unto Job, the \nd LORD\nd* said to Eliphaz the Temanite,
My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not
spoken of me \add the thing that is\add* right, as my servant Job
\add hath\add*.

Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams,
and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering;
and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I
deal with you \add after your\add* folly, in that ye have not spoken of me
\add the thing which is\add* right, like my servant Job.\f + \fr 42.8 
\ft him: Heb. his face, or, person\f*

So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite \add and\add*
Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the \nd LORD\nd*
commanded them: the \nd LORD\nd* also accepted Job.\f + \fr 42.9 
\ft Job: Heb. the face of Job\f*

And the \nd LORD\nd* turned the captivity of Job, when he
prayed for his friends: also the \nd LORD\nd* gave Job twice as much as he had
before.\f + \fr 42.10  \ft gave…: Heb. added all that had been to Job unto the
double\f*

Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters,
and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat
bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted
him over all the evil that the \nd LORD\nd* had brought upon him: every
man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold.

So the \nd LORD\nd* blessed the latter end of Job more than his
beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels,
and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.
He had also seven sons and three daughters.

And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name
of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Keren-happuch.

And in all the land were no women found \add so\add* fair
as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among
their brethren.

After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his
sons, and his sons’ sons, \add even\add* four generations.
So Job died, \add being\add* old and full of days.

verses.text:
Blessed \add is\add* the man that walketh not in the counsel
of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the
seat of the scornful.\f + \fr 1.1  \ft ungodly: or, wicked\f* 
\q1

And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water,
that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not
wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.\f + \fr 1.3  \ft wither: Heb.
fade\f* 
\b
\q1

The ungodly \add are\add* not so: but \add are\add* like the
chaff which the wind driveth away. 
\q1

Therefore the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment, nor
sinners in the congregation of the righteous. 
\q1

For the \nd LORD\nd* knoweth the way of the righteous: but the
way of the ungodly shall perish.

Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?\f + \fr 2.1 
\ft rage: or, tumultuously assemble\f*\f + \fr 2.1  \ft imagine: Heb.
meditate\f* 
\q1

The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take
counsel together, against the \nd LORD\nd*, and against his anointed,
\add saying\add*, 
\q1

Let us break their bands asunder, and cast away their cords from us.
\q1

He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: the Lord shall have them in
derision. 
\q1

Then shall he speak unto them in his wrath, and vex them in his sore
displeasure.\f + \fr 2.5  \ft vex: or, trouble\f* 
\q1

Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion.\f + \fr 2.6 
\ft set: Heb. anointed\f*\f + \fr 2.6  \ft upon…: Heb. upon Zion, the hill of my
holiness\f* 
\b
\q1

I will declare the decree: the \nd LORD\nd* hath said unto me, Thou
\add art\add* my Son; this day have I begotten thee.\f + \fr 2.7 
\ft the decree: or, for a decree\f* 
\q1

Ask of me, and I shall give \add thee\add* the heathen \add for\add*
thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth \add for\add*
thy possession. 
\q1

Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in
pieces like a potter’s vessel. 
\b
\q1

Be wise now therefore, O ye kings: be instructed, ye judges
of the earth. 
\q1

Serve the \nd LORD\nd* with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
\q1

Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish \add from\add*
the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed \add are\add*
all they that put their trust in him.

\d A Psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son. 
\q1

\nd LORD\nd*, how are they increased that trouble me! many
\add are\add* they that rise up against me. 
\q1

Many \add there be\add* which say of my soul, \add There is\add*
no help for him in God. Selah. 
\q1

But thou, O \nd LORD\nd*, \add art\add* a shield for me; my
glory, and the lifter up of mine head.\f + \fr 3.3  \ft for: or,
about\f* 
\b
\q1

I cried unto the \nd LORD\nd* with my voice, and he heard me out of his
holy hill. Selah. 
\q1

I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the \nd LORD\nd* sustained me.
\q1

I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people, that have
set \add themselves\add* against me round about. 
\q1

Arise, O \nd LORD\nd*; save me, O my God: for thou hast smitten
all mine enemies \add upon\add* the cheek bone; thou hast broken
the teeth of the ungodly. 
\q1

Salvation \add belongeth\add* unto the \nd LORD\nd*: thy blessing
\add is\add* upon thy people. Selah.

\d To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm of David. 
\q1

Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousness: thou hast enlarged me
\add when I was\add* in distress; have mercy upon me, and hear my
prayer.\f + \fr 4.1  \ft chief…: or, overseer\f*\f + \fr 4.1  \ft have…: or, be gracious unto
me\f* 
\q1

O ye sons of men, how long \add will ye turn\add* my glory
into shame? \add how long\add* will ye love vanity, \add and\add*
seek after leasing? Selah. 
\q1

But know that the 
d LORD
d* hath set apart him that is godly
for himself: the 
d LORD
d* will hear when I call unto him. 
\q1

Stand in awe, and sin not: commune with your own heart upon your
bed, and be still. Selah. 
\q1

Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the
\nd LORD\nd*. 
\b
\q1
