The way of an eagle in the air; the way of a serpent upon a
rock; the way of a ship in the midst of the sea; and the way of a
man with a maid.\f + \fr 30.19  \ft midst: Heb. heart\f*

Such \add is\add* the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth,
and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.

For three \add things\add* the earth is disquieted, and for
four \add which\add* it cannot bear:

For a servant when he reigneth; and a fool when he is filled
with meat;

For an odious \add woman\add* when she is married; and an
handmaid that is heir to her mistress.

There be four \add things which are\add* little upon the earth, but they
\add are\add* exceeding wise:\f + \fr 30.24  \ft exceeding…: Heb. wise, made
wise\f*

The ants \add are\add* a people not strong, yet they prepare
their meat in the summer;

The conies \add are but\add* a feeble folk, yet make they their
houses in the rocks;

The locusts have no king, yet go they forth all of them by
bands;\f + \fr 30.27  \ft by…: Heb. gathered together\f*
The spider taketh hold with her hands, and is in kings’ palaces.

There be three \add things\add* which go well, yea, four are
comely in going:

A lion \add which is\add* strongest among beasts, and turneth not
away for any;

A greyhound; an he goat also; and a king, against whom \add there
is\add* no rising up.\f + \fr 30.31  \ft greyhound: or, horse: Heb. girt in the
loins\f*

If thou hast done foolishly in lifting up thyself, or if thou hast thought
evil, \add lay\add* thine hand upon thy mouth.

Surely the churning of milk bringeth forth butter, and the
wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood: so the forcing of wrath
bringeth forth strife.
The words of king Lemuel, the prophecy that his mother taught him.

What, my son? and what, the son of my womb? and what, the son
of my vows?

Give not thy strength unto women, nor thy ways to that which
destroyeth kings.

\add It is\add* not for kings, O Lemuel, \add it is\add* not for
kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink:

Lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment
of any of the afflicted.\f + \fr 31.5  \ft pervert: Heb. alter\f*\f + \fr 31.5 
\ft of any…: Heb. of all the sons of affliction\f*

Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, and wine
unto those that be of heavy hearts.\f + \fr 31.6  \ft of…: Heb. bitter of
soul\f*
Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.

Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are
appointed to destruction.\f + \fr 31.8  \ft such…: Heb. the sons of
destruction\f*

Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the
poor and needy.

Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price \add is\add*
far above rubies.

The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no
need of spoil.
She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.

She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her
hands.

She is like the merchants’ ships; she bringeth her food from
afar.

She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her
household, and a portion to her maidens.

She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her
hands she planteth a vineyard.\f + \fr 31.16  \ft buyeth: Heb. taketh\f*

She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her
arms.

She perceiveth that her merchandise \add is\add* good: her
candle goeth not out by night.\f + \fr 31.18  \ft She…: Heb. She
tasteth\f*

She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the
distaff.

She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yea, she reacheth
forth her hands to the needy.\f + \fr 31.20  \ft She…: Heb. She spreadeth\f*

She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her
household \add are\add* clothed with scarlet.\f + \fr 31.21  \ft scarlet: or, double
garments\f*

She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing \add is\add*
silk and purple.

Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the
elders of the land.

She maketh fine linen, and selleth \add it;\add* and delivereth
girdles unto the merchant.

Strength and honour \add are\add* her clothing; and she shall
rejoice in time to come.

She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue \add is\add*
the law of kindness.

She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth
not the bread of idleness.

Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband \add also\add*,
and he praiseth her.

Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them
all.\f + \fr 31.29  \ft have…: or, have gotten riches\f*

Favour \add is\add* deceitful, and beauty \add is\add* vain:
\add but\add* a woman \add that\add* feareth the \nd LORD\nd*, she shall be
praised.

Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works
praise her in the gates.

headers.toc1: Ecclesiastes or, the Preacher
headers.mt1: Ecclesiastes or, the Preacher

verses.text: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all
\add is\add* vanity.

What profit hath a man of all his labour which he taketh under the
sun?

\add One\add* generation passeth away, and \add another\add*
generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.

The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his
place where he arose.\f + \fr 1.5  \ft hasteth: Heb. panteth\f*

The wind goeth toward the south, and turneth about unto the
north; it whirleth about continually, and the wind returneth again
according to his circuits.

All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea \add is\add* not
full; unto the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return
again.\f + \fr 1.7  \ft return…: Heb. return to go\f*

All things \add are\add* full of labour; man cannot utter \add it:\add*
the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.

The thing that hath been, it \add is that\add* which shall be; and that which is
done \add is\add* that which shall be done: and \add there is\add*
no new \add thing\add* under the sun.

Is there \add any\add* thing whereof it may be said, See, this
\add is\add* new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.

\add There is\add* no remembrance of former \add things;\add* neither shall there be
\add any\add* remembrance of \add things\add* that are to come with
\add those\add* that shall come after.
I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all
\add things\add* that are done under heaven: this sore travail hath
God given to the sons of man to be exercised therewith.\f + \fr 1.13 
\ft to be…: or, to afflict them\f*

I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all
\add is\add* vanity and vexation of spirit.

\add That which is\add* crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is
wanting cannot be numbered.\f + \fr 1.15  \ft that which is wanting: Heb.
defect\f*

I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I am come to great
estate, and have gotten more wisdom than all \add they\add* that have been
before me in Jerusalem: yea, my heart had great experience of wisdom
and knowledge.\f + \fr 1.16  \ft had…: Heb. had seen much\f*

And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and
folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.

For in much wisdom \add is\add* much grief: and he that increaseth
knowledge increaseth  sorrow.

I said in mine heart, Go to now, I will prove thee with mirth,
therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also \add is\add* vanity.

I said of laughter, \add It is\add* mad: and of mirth, What
doeth it?

I sought in mine heart to give myself unto wine, yet acquainting
mine heart with wisdom; and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what
\add was\add* that good for the sons of men, which they should do
under the heaven all the days of their life.\f + \fr 2.3  \ft to give…: Heb. to draw my flesh with
wine\f*\f + \fr 2.3  \ft all…: Heb. the number of the days of their
life\f*
I made me great works; I builded me houses; I planted me vineyards:

I made me gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them of all
\add kind of\add* fruits:

I made me pools of water, to water therewith the wood that bringeth
forth trees:

I got \add me\add* servants and maidens, and had servants born
in my house; also I had great possessions of great and small cattle
above all that were in Jerusalem before me:\f + \fr 2.7  \ft servants born…: Heb. sons of my
house\f*

I gathered me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure
of kings and of the provinces: I gat me men singers and women singers,
and the delights of the sons of men, \add as\add* musical instruments, and that of all
sorts.\f + \fr 2.8  \ft musical…: Heb. musical instrument and instruments\f*

So I was great, and increased more than all that were before
me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.

And whatsoever mine eyes desired I kept not from them, I withheld
not my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labour:
and this was my portion of all my labour.

Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought,
and on the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all \add was\add*
vanity and vexation of spirit, and \add there was\add* no profit
under the sun.

And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what
\add can\add* the man \add do\add* that cometh after the king? \add even\add*
that which hath been already done.\f + \fr 2.12  \ft even…: or, in those things which have been already
done\f*

Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth
darkness.\f + \fr 2.13  \ft that…: Heb. that there is an excellency in wisdom more than in folly,
etc\f*

The wise man’s eyes \add are\add* in his head; but the fool
walketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.

Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it
happeneth even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my
heart, that this also \add is\add* vanity.\f + \fr 2.15  \ft happeneth even…: Heb. happeneth to me, even to
me\f*

For \add there is\add* no remembrance of the wise more than
of the fool for ever; seeing that which now \add is\add* in the days
to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise \add man\add*?
as the fool.

Therefore I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the
sun \add is\add* grievous unto me: for all \add is\add* vanity and
vexation of spirit.

Yea, I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun:
because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me.\f + \fr 2.18 
\ft taken: Heb. laboured\f*

And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise \add man\add* or a
fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured,
and wherein I have shewed myself wise under the sun. This \add is\add*
also vanity.

Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the
labour which I took under the sun.

For there is a man whose labour \add is\add* in wisdom, and in
knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that hath not laboured therein shall he
leave it \add for\add* his portion. This also \add is\add* vanity
and a great evil.\f + \fr 2.21  \ft leave: Heb. give\f*

For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his
heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun?

For all his days \add are\add* sorrows, and his travail grief;
yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.

\add There is\add* nothing better for a man, \add than\add*
that he should eat and drink, and \add that\add* he should make his
soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it \add was\add*
from the hand of God.\f + \fr 2.24  \ft should make…: or, delight his
senses\f*

For who can eat, or who else can hasten \add hereunto\add*,
more than I?

For \add God\add* giveth to a man that \add is\add* good in his
sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth
travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to \add him that
is\add* good before God. This also \add is\add* vanity and vexation
of spirit.\f + \fr 2.26  \ft in his…: Heb. before him\f*

To every \add thing there is\add* a season, and a time to every
purpose under the heaven:

A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a
time to pluck up \add that which is\add* planted;\f + \fr 3.2  \ft to be…: Heb. to
bear\f*

A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a
time to build up;

A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a
time to dance;

A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time
to cast away;\f + \fr 3.6  \ft get: or, seek\f*

A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence,
and a time to speak;

A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time
of peace.
What profit hath he that worketh in that wherein he laboureth?

I have seen the travail, which God hath given to the sons
of men to be exercised in it.

He hath made every \add thing\add* beautiful in his time:
also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find
out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end.

I know that \add there is\add* no good in them, but for \add a
man\add* to rejoice, and to do good in his life.

And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the
good of all his labour, it \add is\add* the gift of God.

I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing
can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth \add it\add*, that
\add men\add* should fear before him.

That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath
already been; and God requireth that which is past.\f + \fr 3.15 
\ft that which is past: Heb. that which is driven away\f*

And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, \add that\add*
wickedness \add was\add* there; and the place of righteousness, \add that\add*
iniquity \add was\add* there.

I said in mine heart, God shall judge the righteous and the
wicked: for \add there is\add* a time there for every purpose and for every
work.

I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of
men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they
themselves are beasts.\f + \fr 3.18  \ft that God…: or, that they might clear God, and see,
etc\f*

All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to
dust again.

Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth upward, and the spirit
of the beast that goeth downward to the earth?\f + \fr 3.21  \ft of man: Heb. of the sons of
man\f*\f + \fr 3.21  \ft goeth upward: Heb. is ascending, etc\f*

Wherefore I perceive that \add there is\add* nothing better,
than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that \add is\add*
his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?

So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are
done under the sun: and behold the tears of \add such as were\add*
oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors
\add there was\add* power; but they had no comforter.\f + \fr 4.1 
\ft side: Heb. hand\f*

Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the
living which are yet alive.

Yea, better \add is he\add* than both they, which hath not
yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the
sun.

Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a
man is envied of his neighbour. This \add is\add* also vanity and
vexation of spirit.\f + \fr 4.4  \ft every…: Heb. all the rightness of
work\f*\f + \fr 4.4  \ft for this…: Heb. this is the envy of a man from his
neighbour\f*
The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.

Better \add is\add* an handful \add with\add* quietness, than both the
hands full \add with\add* travail and vexation of spirit.
Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.

There is one \add alone\add*, and \add there is\add* not a
second; yea, he hath neither child nor brother: yet \add is there\add*
no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither
\add saith he\add*, For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of
good? This \add is\add* also vanity, yea, it \add is\add* a sore
travail.

Two \add are\add* better than one; because they have a good
reward for their labour.

For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him
\add that is\add* alone when he falleth; for \add he hath\add* not
another to help him up.

Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can
one be warm \add alone\add*?

And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a
threefold cord is not quickly broken.

Better \add is\add* a poor and a wise child than an old and
foolish king, who will no more be admonished.\f + \fr 4.13  \ft who…: Heb. who knoweth not to be
admonished\f*

For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also \add he that
is\add* born in his kingdom becometh poor.

I considered all the living which walk under the sun, with the
second child that shall stand up in his stead.

\add There is\add* no end of all the people, \add even\add*
of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not
rejoice in him. Surely this also \add is\add* vanity and vexation
of spirit.

Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more
ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider
not that they do evil.

Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty
to utter \add any\add* thing before God: for God \add is\add* in
heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.\f + \fr 5.2 
\ft thing: or, word\f*

For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a
fool’s voice \add is known\add* by multitude of words.

When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for \add he
hath\add* no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.

Better \add is it\add* that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest
vow and not pay.

Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say
thou before the angel, that it \add was\add* an error: wherefore should
God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?

For in the multitude of dreams and many words \add there are\add* also
\add divers\add* vanities: but fear thou God.

If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of
judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for
\add he that is\add* higher than the highest regardeth; and \add there
be\add* higher than they.\f + \fr 5.8  \ft at the…: Heb. at the will, or,
purpose\f*

Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king \add himself\add*
is served by the field.

When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what
good \add is there\add* to the owners thereof, saving the beholding
\add of them\add* with their eyes?

The sleep of a labouring man \add is\add* sweet, whether he
eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer
him to sleep.

There is a sore evil \add which\add* I have seen under the
sun, \add namely\add*, riches kept for the owners thereof to their
hurt.

But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begetteth
a son, and \add there is\add* nothing in his hand.

As he came forth of his mother’s womb, naked shall he return
to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry
away in his hand.

And this also \add is\add* a sore evil, \add that\add* in all
points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that hath
laboured for the wind?

All his days also he eateth in darkness, and \add he hath\add*
much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.

Behold \add that\add* which I have seen: \add it is\add*
good and comely \add for one\add* to eat and to drink, and to enjoy
the good of all his labour that he taketh under the sun all the days
of his life, which God giveth him: for it \add is\add* his portion.\f + \fr 5.18 
\ft it is good…: Heb. there is a good which is comely, etc\f*\f + \fr 5.18 
\ft all the days: Heb. the number of the days\f*

Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him
power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his
labour; this \add is\add* the gift of God.

For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because
God answereth  \add him\add* in the joy of his heart.\f + \fr 5.20 
\ft For…: or, Though he give not much, yet he remembereth, etc\f*

There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it \add is\add*
common among men:

A man to whom God hath given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he
wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not
power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it: this \add is\add*
vanity, and it \add is\add* an evil disease.

If a man beget an hundred \add children\add*, and live many
years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not
filled with good, and also \add that\add* he have no burial; I say,
\add that\add* an untimely birth \add is\add* better than he.

For he cometh in with vanity, and departeth in darkness, and his
name shall be covered with darkness.

Moreover he hath not seen the sun, nor known \add any thing:\add*
this hath more rest than the other.

Yea, though he live a thousand years twice \add told\add*,
yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?

All the labour of man \add is\add* for his mouth, and yet the
appetite is not filled.\f + \fr 6.7  \ft appetite: Heb. soul\f*

For what hath the wise more than the fool? what hath the poor,
that knoweth to walk before the living?

Better \add is\add* the sight of the eyes than the wandering
of the desire: this \add is\add* also vanity and vexation of spirit.\f + \fr 6.9 
\ft than…: Heb. than the walking of the soul\f*

That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it
\add is\add* man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.

Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what \add is\add*
man the better?

For who knoweth what \add is\add* good for man in \add this\add*
life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow?
for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?\f + \fr 6.12 
\ft all…: Heb. the number of the days of the life of his vanity\f*

A good name \add is\add* better than precious ointment; and the
day of death than the day of one’s birth.

\add It is\add* better to go to the house of mourning, than to
go to the house of feasting: for that \add is\add* the end of all
men; and the living will lay \add it\add* to his heart.

Sorrow \add is\add* better than laughter: for by the sadness
of the countenance the heart is made better.\f + \fr 7.3  \ft Sorrow: or,
Anger\f*

The heart of the wise \add is\add* in the house of mourning;
but the heart of fools \add is\add* in the house of mirth.

\add It is\add* better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a
man to hear the song of fools.

For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so \add is\add*
the laughter of the fool: this also \add is\add* vanity.\f + \fr 7.6 
\ft crackling: Heb. sound\f*

Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth
the heart.

Better \add is\add* the end of a thing than the beginning thereof:
\add and\add* the patient in spirit \add is\add* better than the
proud in spirit.

Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the
bosom of fools.

Say not thou, What is \add the cause\add* that the former
days were better than these? for thou dost not enquire wisely concerning
this.\f + \fr 7.10  \ft wisely: Heb. out of wisdom\f*

Wisdom \add is\add* good with an inheritance: and \add by it there
is\add* profit to them that see the sun.\f + \fr 7.11  \ft good…: or, as good as an inheritance, yea, better
too\f*

For wisdom \add is\add* a defence, \add and\add* money \add is\add*
a defence: but the excellency of knowledge \add is, that\add* wisdom
giveth life to them that have it.\f + \fr 7.12  \ft defence: Heb.
shadow\f*

Consider the work of God: for who can make \add that\add*
straight, which he hath made crooked?

In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity
consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the
end that man should find nothing after him.\f + \fr 7.14  \ft set: Heb.
made\f*

All \add things\add* have I seen in the days of my vanity:
there is a just \add man\add* that perisheth in his righteousness,
and there is a wicked \add man\add* that prolongeth \add his life\add*
in his wickedness.

Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise:
why shouldest thou destroy thyself?\f + \fr 7.16  \ft destroy…: Heb. be
desolate?\f*

Be not over much wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldest thou
die before thy time?\f + \fr 7.17  \ft before…: Heb. not in thy time?\f*

\add It is\add* good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from
this withdraw not thine hand: for he that feareth God shall come
forth of them all.

Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty \add men\add*
which are in the city.

For \add there is\add* not a just man upon earth, that doeth
good, and sinneth not.

Also take no heed unto all words that are spoken; lest thou
hear thy servant curse thee:\f + \fr 7.21  \ft take…: Heb. give not thine
heart\f*

For oftentimes also thine own heart knoweth that thou thyself likewise hast
cursed others.

All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it
\add was\add* far from me.

That which is far off, and exceeding deep, who can find it
out?

I applied mine heart to know, and to search, and to seek out
wisdom, and the reason \add of things\add*, and to know the wickedness
of folly, even of foolishness \add and\add* madness:\f + \fr 7.25 
\ft I applied…: Heb. I and mine heart compassed\f*

And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart \add is\add*
snares and nets, \add and\add* her hands \add as\add* bands: whoso
pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by
her.\f + \fr 7.26  \ft whoso…: Heb. he that is good before God\f*

Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher, \add counting\add*
one by one, to find out the account:\f + \fr 7.27  \ft counting…: or, weighing one thing after another, to find out the
reason\f*

Which yet my soul seeketh, but I find not: one man among a
thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.

Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright;
but they have sought out many inventions.

Who \add is\add* as the wise \add man\add*? and who knoweth
the interpretation of a thing? a man’s wisdom maketh his face to
shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.\f + \fr 8.1 
\ft the boldness: Heb. the strength\f*

I \add counsel thee\add* to keep the king’s commandment, and
\add that\add* in regard of the oath of God.

Be not hasty to go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing;
for he doeth whatsoever pleaseth him.

Where the word of a king \add is, there is\add* power: and who may
say unto him, What doest thou?

Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise
man’s heart discerneth both time and judgment.\f + \fr 8.5  \ft shall…: Heb. shall
know\f*

Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the
misery of man \add is\add* great upon him.

For he knoweth not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall
be?\f + \fr 8.7  \ft when…: or, how it shall be?\f*

\add There is\add* no man that hath power over the spirit to
retain the spirit; neither \add hath he\add* power in the day of
death: and \add there is\add* no discharge in \add that\add* war;
neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.\f + \fr 8.8 
\ft discharge: or, casting off weapons\f*

All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work
that is done under the sun: \add there is\add* a time wherein one
man ruleth over another to his own hurt.

And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the
place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so
done: this \add is\add* also vanity.

Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily,
therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do
evil.

Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his \add days\add*
be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that
fear God, which fear before him:

But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he
prolong \add his\add* days, \add which are\add* as a shadow; because he
feareth not before God.

There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there be
just \add men\add*, unto whom it happeneth according to the work
of the wicked; again, there be wicked \add men\add*, to whom it happeneth
according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also \add is\add*
vanity.

Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing
under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall
abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which God giveth
him under the sun.

When I applied mine heart to know wisdom, and to see the
business that is done upon the earth: (for also \add there is that\add*
neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes:)

Then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find
out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek
\add it\add* out, yet he shall not find \add it;\add* yea further; though a
wise \add man\add* think to know \add it\add*, yet shall he not be
able to find \add it\add*.

For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the
righteous, and the wise, and their works, \add are\add* in the hand
of God: no man knoweth either love or hatred \add by\add* all \add that
is\add* before them.\f + \fr 9.1  \ft I considered…: Heb. I gave, or, set to my
heart\f*

All \add things come\add* alike to all: \add there is\add* one
event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the
clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that
sacrificeth not: as \add is\add* the good, so \add is\add* the sinner;
\add and\add* he that sweareth, as \add he\add* that feareth an oath.

This \add is\add* an evil among all \add things\add* that are
done under the sun, that \add there is\add* one event unto all: yea, also the
heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness \add is\add*
in their heart while they live, and after that \add they go\add*
to the dead.

For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope:
for a living dog is better than a dead lion.

For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know
not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory
of them is forgotten.

Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a
merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works.

Let thy garments be always white; and let thy head lack no
ointment.

Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the
life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the
days of thy vanity: for that \add is\add* thy portion in \add this\add*
life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.\f + \fr 9.9 
\ft Live…: Heb. See, or, Enjoy life\f*

Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do \add it\add* with thy
might; for \add there is\add* no work, nor device, nor knowledge,
nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.

I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race \add is\add*
not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread
to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour
to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are
taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare;
so \add are\add* the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it
falleth suddenly upon them.

This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it \add seemed\add*
great unto me:

\add There was\add* a little city, and few men within it; and there
came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:

Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom
delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.

Then said I, Wisdom \add is\add* better than strength: nevertheless the poor
man’s wisdom \add is\add* despised, and his words are not heard.

The words of wise \add men are\add* heard in quiet more than the
cry of him that ruleth among fools.

Wisdom \add is\add* better than weapons of war: but one sinner
destroyeth much good.

Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth
a stinking savour: \add so doth\add* a little folly him that is in
reputation for wisdom \add and\add* honour.\f + \fr 10.1  \ft Dead…: Heb. Flies of
death\f*

A wise man’s heart \add is\add* at his right hand; but a fool’s
heart at his left.

Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his wisdom
faileth \add him\add*, and he saith to every one \add that\add* he
\add is\add* a fool.\f + \fr 10.3  \ft his…: Heb. his heart\f*

If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy
place; for yielding pacifieth great offences.

There is an evil \add which\add* I have seen under the sun,
as an error \add which\add* proceedeth from the ruler:\f + \fr 10.5 
\ft from: Heb. from before\f*

Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.\f + \fr 10.6 
\ft in great…: Heb. in great heights\f*

I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking  as servants
upon the earth.

He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaketh
an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.

Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith; \add and\add*
he that cleaveth wood shall be endangered thereby.

If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he
put to more strength: but wisdom \add is\add* profitable to direct.

Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler
is no better.\f + \fr 10.11  \ft a babbler: Heb. the master of the
tongue\f*

The words of a wise man’s mouth \add are\add* gracious; but the
lips of a fool will swallow up himself.\f + \fr 10.12  \ft gracious: Heb.
grace\f*

The beginning of the words of his mouth \add is\add* foolishness:
and the end of his talk \add is\add* mischievous madness.\f + \fr 10.13 
\ft his talk: Heb. his mouth\f*

A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be
after him, who can tell him?\f + \fr 10.14  \ft is full…: Heb. multiplieth
words\f*

The labour of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he
knoweth not how to go to the city.

Woe to thee, O land, when thy king \add is\add* a child,
and thy princes eat in the morning!

Blessed \add art\add* thou, O land, when thy king \add is\add*
the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength,
and not for drunkenness!

By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness
of the hands the house droppeth through.

A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but
money answereth  all \add things\add*.\f + \fr 10.19  \ft maketh…: Heb. maketh glad the
life\f*

Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the
rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice,
and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.\f + \fr 10.20  \ft thought: or,
conscience\f*

Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after
many days.\f + \fr 11.1  \ft upon…: Heb. upon the face of the waters\f*

Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for thou knowest
not what evil shall be upon the earth.

If the clouds be full of rain, they empty \add themselves\add*
upon the earth: and if the tree fall toward the south, or toward the
north, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.

He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth
the clouds shall not reap.

As thou knowest not what \add is\add* the way of the spirit,
\add nor\add* how the bones \add do grow\add* in the womb of her that is with
child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.

In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine
hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they
both \add shall be\add* alike good.\f + \fr 11.6  \ft shall prosper: Heb. shall be
right\f*

Truly the light \add is\add* sweet, and a pleasant \add thing it
is\add* for the eyes to behold the sun:

But if a man live many years, \add and\add* rejoice in them all; yet let him
remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh
\add is\add* vanity.

Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer
thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thine heart,
and in the sight of thine eyes: but know thou, that for all these
\add things\add* God will bring thee into judgment.

Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil
from thy flesh: for childhood and youth \add are\add* vanity.\f + \fr 11.10 
\ft sorrow: or, anger\f*

While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not
darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:

In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the
strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are
few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened,\f + \fr 12.3 
\ft the grinders…: or, the grinders fail, because they grind little\f*

Also \add when\add* they shall be afraid of \add that which
is\add* high, and fears \add shall be\add* in the way, and the almond
tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire
shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners
go about the streets:

Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken,
or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the
cistern.

Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the
spirit shall return unto God who gave it.
Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all \add is\add* vanity.

And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught
the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, \add and\add*
set in order many proverbs.\f + \fr 12.9  \ft moreover…: or, the more wise the preacher was,
etc\f*

The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and \add that which
was\add* written \add was\add* upright, \add even\add* words of truth.\f + \fr 12.10 
\ft acceptable…: Heb. words of delight\f*

The words of the wise \add are\add* as goads, and as nails
fastened \add by\add* the masters of assemblies, \add which\add*
are given from one shepherd.

And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many
books \add there is\add* no end; and much study \add is\add* a weariness
of the flesh.\f + \fr 12.12  \ft study: or, reading\f*

Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God,
and keep his commandments: for this \add is\add* the whole \add duty\add*
of man.\f + \fr 12.13  \ft Let…: or, The end of the matter, even all that hath been heard,
is\f*

For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret
thing, whether \add it be\add* good, or whether \add it be\add* evil.

headers.toc1: The Song of Solomon
headers.mt1: The Song of Solomon

verses.text: The song of songs, which \add is\add* Solomon’s.

Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love
\add is\add* better than wine.\f + \fr 1.2  \ft thy…: Heb. thy loves\f*

Because of the savour of thy good ointments thy name \add is
as\add* ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.

Draw me, we will run after thee: the king hath brought me into his
chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, we will remember thy
love more than wine: the upright love thee.\f + \fr 1.4  \ft the upright…: or, they love thee
uprightly\f*

I \add am\add* black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem,
as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.

Look not upon me, because I \add am\add* black, because the
sun hath looked upon me: my mother’s children were angry with me; they
made me the keeper of the vineyards; \add but\add* mine own vineyard
have I not kept.

Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou makest
\add thy flock\add* to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turneth
aside by the flocks of thy companions?\f + \fr 1.7  \ft as one…: or, as one that is
veiled\f*

If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth
by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds’
tents.

I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in
Pharaoh’s chariots.

Thy cheeks are comely with rows \add of jewels\add*, thy neck
with chains \add of gold\add*.
We will make thee borders of gold with studs of silver.

While the king \add sitteth\add* at his table, my spikenard
sendeth forth the smell thereof.

A bundle of myrrh \add is\add* my wellbeloved unto me; he shall
lie all night betwixt my breasts.

My beloved \add is\add* unto me \add as\add* a cluster of
camphire in the vineyards of En-gedi.\f + \fr 1.14  \ft camphire: or,
cypress\f*

Behold, thou \add art\add* fair, my love; behold, thou \add art\add*
fair; thou \add hast\add* doves’ eyes.\f + \fr 1.15  \ft my love: or, my
companion\f*

Behold, thou \add art\add* fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant:
also our bed \add is\add* green.

The beams of our house \add are\add* cedar, \add and\add*
our rafters of fir.\f + \fr 1.17  \ft rafters: or, galleries\f*

I \add am\add* the rose of Sharon, \add and\add* the lily of the
valleys.

As the lily among thorns, so \add is\add* my love among the
daughters.

As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so \add is\add*
my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great
delight, and his fruit \add was\add* sweet to my taste.\f + \fr 2.3 
\ft I sat…: Heb. I delighted and sat down, etc\f*\f + \fr 2.3  \ft taste: Heb.
palate\f*

He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me
\add was\add* love.\f + \fr 2.4  \ft banqueting…: Heb. house of wine\f*

Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I \add am\add*
sick of love.\f + \fr 2.5  \ft comfort…: Heb. straw me with apples\f*

His left hand \add is\add* under my head, and his right hand
doth embrace me.

I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and
by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake \add my\add*
love, till he please.\f + \fr 2.7  \ft I charge…: Heb. I adjure you\f*

The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh leaping upon the
mountains, skipping upon the hills.

My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: behold, he standeth
behind our wall, he looketh forth at the windows, shewing himself through the
lattice.\f + \fr 2.9  \ft shewing…: Heb. flourishing\f*

My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair
one, and come away.

For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over \add and\add*
gone;

The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing \add of
birds\add* is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;

The fig tree putteth forth her green figs, and the vines \add with\add*
the tender grape give a \add good\add* smell. Arise, my love, my fair
one, and come away.

O my dove, \add that art\add* in the clefts of the rock,
in the secret \add places\add* of the stairs, let me see thy countenance,
let me hear thy voice; for sweet \add is\add* thy voice, and thy
countenance \add is\add* comely.

Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines:
for our vines \add have\add* tender grapes.

My beloved \add is\add* mine, and I \add am\add* his: he
feedeth among the lilies.

Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved,
and be thou like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.\f + \fr 2.17 
\ft of Bether: or, of division\f*

By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought
him, but I found him not.

I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad
ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

The watchmen that go about the city found me: \add to whom I
said\add*, Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?

\add It was\add* but a little that I passed from them, but I
found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him
go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, and into the
chamber of her that conceived me.

I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and
by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake \add my\add*
love, till he please.

Who \add is\add* this that cometh out of the wilderness like
pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all
powders of the merchant?

Behold his bed, which \add is\add* Solomon’s; threescore valiant men
\add are\add* about it, of the valiant of Israel.

They all hold swords, \add being\add* expert in war: every
man \add hath\add* his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the
night.

King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.\f + \fr 3.9 
\ft a chariot: or, a bed\f*

He made the pillars thereof \add of\add* silver, the bottom thereof
\add of\add* gold, the covering of it \add of\add* purple, the midst
thereof being paved \add with\add* love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.

Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon
with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his
espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.

Behold, thou \add art\add* fair, my love; behold, thou \add art\add*
fair; thou \add hast\add* doves’ eyes within thy locks: thy hair
\add is\add* as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.\f + \fr 4.1 
\ft that…: or, that eat of, etc\f*

Thy teeth \add are\add* like a flock \add of sheep that are
even\add* shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear
twins, and none \add is\add* barren among them.

Thy lips \add are\add* like a thread of scarlet, and thy speech
\add is\add* comely: thy temples \add are\add* like a piece of a
pomegranate within thy locks.

Thy neck \add is\add* like the tower of David builded for an
armoury, whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty
men.

Thy two breasts \add are\add* like two young roes that are
twins, which feed among the lilies.

Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, I will get
me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.\f + \fr 4.6 
\ft break: Heb. breathe\f*

Thou \add art\add* all fair, my love; \add there is\add* no
spot in thee.

Come with me from Lebanon, \add my\add* spouse, with me from
Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon,
from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.

How fair is thy love, my sister, \add my\add* spouse! how much
better is thy love than wine! and the smell of thine ointments than all
spices!

Thy lips, O \add my\add* spouse, drop \add as\add* the honeycomb:
honey and milk \add are\add* under thy tongue; and the smell of thy
garments \add is\add* like the smell of Lebanon.

Thy plants \add are\add* an orchard of pomegranates, with
pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,\f + \fr 4.13  \ft camphire: or,
cypress\f*

Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees
of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:

A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams
from Lebanon.

Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden,
\add that\add* the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come
into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.

I am come into my garden, my sister, \add my\add* spouse: I have
gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my
honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink,
yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.\f + \fr 5.1  \ft yea…: or, and be drunken with
loves\f*

I sleep, but my heart waketh: \add it is\add* the voice of my
beloved that knocketh, \add saying\add*, Open to me, my sister, my
love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, \add and\add*
my locks with the drops of the night.

I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed
my feet; how shall I defile them?

My beloved put in his hand by the hole \add of the door\add*,
and my bowels were moved for him.\f + \fr 5.4  \ft for him: or, (as some read) in
me\f*

I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped \add with\add*
myrrh, and my fingers \add with\add* sweet smelling myrrh, upon the
handles of the lock.\f + \fr 5.5  \ft sweet…: Heb. passing, or, running
about\f*

I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself,
\add and\add* was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not
find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote
me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.

I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved,
that ye tell him, that I \add am\add* sick of love.\f + \fr 5.8 
\ft that ye: Heb. what, etc\f*

What \add is\add* thy beloved more than \add another\add*
beloved, O thou fairest among women? what \add is\add* thy beloved more than
\add another\add* beloved, that thou dost so charge us?

My beloved \add is\add* white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten
thousand.\f + \fr 5.10  \ft the chiefest: Heb. a standard-bearer\f*

His head \add is as\add* the most fine gold, his locks \add are\add*
bushy, \add and\add* black as a raven.\f + \fr 5.11  \ft bushy: or,
curled\f*

His eyes \add are\add* as \add the eyes\add* of doves by the
rivers of waters, washed with milk, \add and\add* fitly set.\f + \fr 5.12 
\ft fitly…: Heb. sitting in fulness, that is, fitly placed, and set as a precious stone in the foil of a
ring\f*

His cheeks \add are\add* as a bed of spices, \add as\add*
sweet flowers: his lips \add like\add* lilies, dropping sweet smelling
myrrh.\f + \fr 5.13  \ft sweet flowers: or, towers of perfumes\f*

His hands \add are as\add* gold rings set with the beryl:
his belly \add is as\add* bright ivory overlaid \add with\add* sapphires.

His legs \add are as\add* pillars of marble, set upon sockets
of fine gold: his countenance \add is\add* as Lebanon, excellent
as the cedars.

His mouth \add is\add* most sweet: yea, he \add is\add* altogether
lovely. This \add is\add* my beloved, and this \add is\add* my friend,
O daughters of Jerusalem.\f + \fr 5.16  \ft mouth: Heb. palate\f*

Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? whither is thy
beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.

My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices,
to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

I \add am\add* my beloved’s, and my beloved \add is\add* mine: he
feedeth among the lilies.

Thou \add art\add* beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely
as Jerusalem, terrible as \add an army\add* with banners.

Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me: thy
hair \add is\add* as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.\f + \fr 6.5 
\ft overcome…: or, puffed me up\f*

Thy teeth \add are\add* as a flock of sheep which go up from the
washing, whereof every one beareth twins, and \add there is\add*
not one barren among them.

As a piece of a pomegranate \add are\add* thy temples within
thy locks.

There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and
virgins without number.

My dove, my undefiled is \add but\add* one; she \add is\add* the
\add only\add* one of her mother, she \add is\add* the choice \add one\add*
of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her; \add yea\add*,
the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.

Who \add is\add* she \add that\add* looketh forth as the
morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, \add and\add* terrible as
\add an army\add* with banners?

I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the
valley, \add and\add* to see whether the vine flourished, \add and\add*
the pomegranates budded.

Or ever I was aware, my soul made me \add like\add* the chariots
of Amminadib.\f + \fr 6.12  \ft Or ever…: Heb. I knew not\f*\f + \fr 6.12 
\ft made…: or, set me on the chariots of my willing people\f*

Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look
upon thee. What will ye see in the Shulamite? As it were the company
of two armies.\f + \fr 6.13  \ft of…: or, of Mahanaim\f*

How beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince’s daughter!
the joints of thy thighs \add are\add* like jewels, the work of the
hands of a cunning workman.

Thy navel \add is like\add* a round goblet, \add which\add*
wanteth not liquor: thy belly \add is like\add* an heap of wheat
set about with lilies.\f + \fr 7.2  \ft liquor: Heb. mixture\f*

Thy two breasts \add are\add* like two young roes \add that
are\add* twins.

Thy neck \add is\add* as a tower of ivory; thine eyes \add like\add*
the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim: thy nose \add is\add*
as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.

Thine head upon thee \add is\add* like Carmel, and the hair
of thine head like purple; the king \add is\add* held in the galleries.\f + \fr 7.5 
\ft Carmel: or, crimson\f*\f + \fr 7.5  \ft held: Heb. bound\f*
How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!

This thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to
clusters \add of grapes\add*.

And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine for my beloved,
that goeth \add down\add* sweetly, causing the lips of those that are
asleep to speak.\f + \fr 7.9  \ft sweetly: Heb. straightly\f*\f + \fr 7.9 
\ft of those…: or, of the ancient\f*
I \add am\add* my beloved’s, and his desire \add is\add* toward me.

Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge
in the villages.

Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine
flourish, \add whether\add* the tender grape appear, \add and\add*
the pomegranates bud forth: there will I give thee my loves.\f + \fr 7.12 
\ft appear: Heb. open\f*

The mandrakes give a smell, and at our gates \add are\add*
all manner of pleasant \add fruits\add*, new and old, \add which\add*
I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.

O that thou \add wert\add* as my brother, that sucked the breasts
of my mother! \add when\add* I should find thee without, I would
kiss thee; yea, I should not be despised.\f + \fr 8.1  \ft I should not…: Heb. they should not despise
me\f*

I would lead thee, \add and\add* bring thee into my mother’s
house, \add who\add* would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink
of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.

His left hand \add should be\add* under my head, and his right
hand should embrace me.

I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not up,
nor awake \add my\add* love, until he please.\f + \fr 8.4  \ft that…: Heb. why should ye stir up, or, why,
etc\f*

Who \add is\add* this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning
upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy
mother brought thee forth: there she brought thee forth \add that\add*
bare thee.

Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm:
for love \add is\add* strong as death; jealousy \add is\add* cruel
as the grave: the coals thereof \add are\add* coals of fire, \add which hath
a\add* most vehement flame.\f + \fr 8.6  \ft cruel: Heb. hard\f*

Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if
\add a\add* man would give all the substance of his house for love,
it would utterly be contemned.

We have a little sister, and she hath no breasts: what shall we
do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?

If she \add be\add* a wall, we will build upon her a palace
of silver: and if she \add be\add* a door, we will inclose her with
boards of cedar.

I \add am\add* a wall, and my breasts like towers: then was I in his
eyes as one that found favour.\f + \fr 8.10  \ft favour: Heb. peace\f*

Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; he let out the vineyard
unto keepers; every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand
\add pieces\add* of silver.

My vineyard, which \add is\add* mine, \add is\add* before
me: thou, O Solomon, \add must have\add* a thousand, and those that
keep the fruit thereof two hundred.

Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the companions hearken
to thy voice: cause me to hear \add it\add*.

Make haste, my beloved, and be thou like to a roe or to a
young hart upon the mountains of spices.\f + \fr 8.14  \ft Make…: Heb. Flee
away\f*

headers.toc1: The Book of the Prophet Isaiah
headers.mt1: The Book of the Prophet Isaiah

verses.text:
The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning
Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, \add and\add*
Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth: for the \nd LORD\nd*
hath spoken, I have nourished and brought up children, and they have
rebelled against me.

The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: \add but\add*
Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.

Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers,
children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the \nd LORD\nd*,
they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone
away backward.\f + \fr 1.4  \ft laden: Heb. of heaviness\f*\f + \fr 1.4 
\ft gone…: Heb. alienated, or, separated\f*

Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and
more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.\f + \fr 1.5 
\ft revolt…: Heb. increase revolt\f*

From the sole of the foot even unto the head \add there is\add*
no soundness in it; \add but\add* wounds, and bruises, and putrifying
sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified
with ointment.\f + \fr 1.6  \ft ointment: or, oil\f*

Your country \add is\add* desolate, your cities \add are\add*
burned with fire: your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and
\add it is\add* desolate, as overthrown by strangers.\f + \fr 1.7 
\ft overthrown…: Heb. the overthrow of\f*

And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard,
as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city.

Except the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts had left unto us a very small
remnant, we should have been as Sodom, \add and\add* we should have been
like unto Gomorrah.

Hear the word of the \nd LORD\nd*, ye rulers of Sodom; give
ear unto the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrah.

To what purpose \add is\add* the multitude of your sacrifices
unto me? saith the \nd LORD\nd*: I am full of the burnt offerings
of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood
of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.\f + \fr 1.11  \ft he goats: Heb. great he
goats\f*

When ye come to appear before me, who hath required this at your
hand, to tread my courts?\f + \fr 1.12  \ft to appear: Heb. to be
seen\f*

Bring no more vain oblations; incense is an abomination unto me; the new
moons and sabbaths, the calling of assemblies, I cannot away with;
\add it is\add* iniquity, even the solemn meeting.\f + \fr 1.13 
\ft iniquity: or, grief\f*

Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hateth: they are a
trouble unto me; I am weary to bear \add them\add*.

And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes
from you: yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands
are full of blood.\f + \fr 1.15  \ft make…: Heb. multiply prayer\f*\f + \fr 1.15 
\ft blood: Heb. bloods\f*

Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings
from before mine eyes; cease to do evil;

Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge
the fatherless, plead for the widow.\f + \fr 1.17  \ft relieve: or,
righten\f*

Come now, and let us reason together, saith the \nd LORD\nd*:
though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be
red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the
land:

But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the
sword: for the mouth of the \nd LORD\nd* hath spoken \add it\add*.

How is the faithful city become an harlot! it was full of
judgment; righteousness lodged in it; but now murderers.
Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water:

Thy princes \add are\add* rebellious, and companions of thieves:
every one loveth gifts, and followeth after rewards: they judge not the
fatherless, neither doth the cause of the widow come unto them.

Therefore saith the Lord, the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts, the mighty
One of Israel, Ah, I will ease me of mine adversaries, and avenge
me of mine enemies:

And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away
thy dross, and take away all thy tin:\f + \fr 1.25  \ft purely: Heb. according to
pureness\f*

And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors
as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of
righteousness, the faithful city.

Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with
righteousness.\f + \fr 1.27  \ft her…: or, they that return of her\f*

And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners
\add shall be\add* together, and they that forsake the \nd LORD\nd*
shall be consumed.\f + \fr 1.28  \ft destruction: Heb. breaking\f*

For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired,
and ye shall be confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen.

For ye shall be as an oak whose leaf fadeth, and as a garden
that hath no water.

And the strong shall be as tow, and the maker of it as a spark,
and they shall both burn together, and none shall quench \add them\add*.\f + \fr 1.31 
\ft maker…: or, and his work\f*

The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and
Jerusalem.

And it shall come to pass in the last days, \add that\add*
the mountain of the \nd LORD’s\nd* house shall be established in the
top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all
nations shall flow unto it.\f + \fr 2.2  \ft established: or, prepared\f*

And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up
to the mountain of the \nd LORD\nd*, to the house of the God of Jacob;
and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths:
for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the \nd LORD\nd*
from Jerusalem.

And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many
people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their
spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against
nation, neither shall they learn war any more.\f + \fr 2.4  \ft pruninghooks: or,
scythes\f*

O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of the
\nd LORD\nd*.

Therefore thou hast forsaken thy people the house of Jacob,
because they be replenished from the east, and \add are\add* soothsayers
like the Philistines, and they please themselves in the children
of strangers.\f + \fr 2.6  \ft from…: or, more than the\f*\f + \fr 2.6 
\ft please…: or, abound with the\f*

Their land also is full of silver and gold, neither \add is there
any\add* end of their treasures; their land is also full of horses, neither
\add is there any\add* end of their chariots:

Their land also is full of idols; they worship the work of their own
hands, that which their own fingers have made:

And the mean man boweth down, and the great man humbleth himself: therefore
forgive them not.

Enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust, for fear
of the \nd LORD\nd*, and for the glory of his majesty.

The lofty looks of man shall be humbled, and the haughtiness
of men shall be bowed down, and the \nd LORD\nd* alone shall be exalted
in that day.

For the day of the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts \add shall be\add* upon every
\add one that is\add* proud and lofty, and upon every \add one that
is\add* lifted up; and he shall be brought low:

And upon all the cedars of Lebanon, \add that are\add* high
and lifted up, and upon all the oaks of Bashan,

And upon all the high mountains, and upon all the hills \add that
are\add* lifted up,
And upon every high tower, and upon every fenced wall,

And upon all the ships of Tarshish, and upon all pleasant
pictures.\f + \fr 2.16  \ft pleasant…: Heb. pictures of desire\f*

And the loftiness of man shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness
of men shall be made low: and the \nd LORD\nd* alone shall be exalted
in that day.

And the idols he shall utterly abolish.\f + \fr 2.18  \ft he…: or, shall utterly pass
away\f*

And they shall go into the holes of the rocks, and into the
caves of the earth, for fear of the \nd LORD\nd*, and for the glory
of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.\f + \fr 2.19 
\ft of the earth: Heb. of the dust\f*

In that day a man shall cast his idols of silver, and his
idols of gold, which they made \add each one\add* for himself to
worship, to the moles and to the bats;\f + \fr 2.20  \ft his idols of silver…: Heb. the idols of his silver,
etc\f*\f + \fr 2.20  \ft each…: or, for him\f*

To go into the clefts of the rocks, and into the tops of the ragged
rocks, for fear of the \nd LORD\nd*, and for the glory of his majesty,
when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.

Cease ye from man, whose breath \add is\add* in his nostrils:
for wherein is he to be accounted of?

For, behold, the Lord, the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts, doth take
away from Jerusalem and from Judah the stay and the staff, the whole
stay of bread, and the whole stay of water,

The mighty man, and the man of war, the judge, and the prophet,
and the prudent, and the ancient,

The captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor,
and the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator.\f + \fr 3.3 
\ft the honourable…: Heb. a man eminent in countenance\f*\f + \fr 3.3 
\ft eloquent…: or, skilful of speech\f*

And I will give children \add to be\add* their princes, and
babes shall rule over them.

And the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every
one by his neighbour: the child shall behave himself proudly against the
ancient, and the base against the honourable.

When a man shall take hold of his brother of the house of his
father, \add saying\add*, Thou hast clothing, be thou our ruler, and
\add let\add* this ruin \add be\add* under thy hand:

In that day shall he swear, saying, I will not be an healer;
for in my house \add is\add* neither bread nor clothing: make me not a
ruler of the people.\f + \fr 3.7  \ft swear: Heb. lift up the hand\f*\f + \fr 3.7 
\ft healer: Heb. binder up\f*

For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen: because their
tongue and their doings \add are\add* against the \nd LORD\nd*, to
provoke the eyes of his glory.

The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they
declare their sin as Sodom, they hide \add it\add* not. Woe unto their
soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves.

Say ye to the righteous, that \add it shall be\add* well \add with
him:\add* for they shall eat the fruit of their doings.

Woe unto the wicked! \add it shall be\add* ill \add with him:\add*
for the reward of his hands shall be given him.\f + \fr 3.11  \ft given…: Heb. done to
him\f*

\add As for\add* my people, children \add are\add* their
oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they which lead thee cause
\add thee\add* to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.\f + \fr 3.12 
\ft lead…: or, call thee blessed\f*\f + \fr 3.12  \ft destroy: Heb. swallow
up\f*

The \nd LORD\nd* standeth up to plead, and standeth to judge
the people.

The \nd LORD\nd* will enter into judgment with the ancients
of his people, and the princes thereof: for ye have eaten up the
vineyard; the spoil of the poor \add is\add* in your houses.\f + \fr 3.14 
\ft eaten: or, burnt\f*

What mean ye \add that\add* ye beat my people to pieces, and
grind the faces of the poor? saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd* of hosts.

Moreover the \nd LORD\nd* saith, Because the daughters of
Zion are haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton
eyes, walking and mincing \add as\add* they go, and making a tinkling
with their feet:\f + \fr 3.16  \ft wanton…: Heb. deceiving with their
eyes\f*\f + \fr 3.16  \ft mincing: or, tripping nicely\f*

Therefore the Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the
head of the daughters of Zion, and the \nd LORD\nd* will discover
their secret parts.\f + \fr 3.17  \ft discover: Heb. make naked\f*

In that day the Lord will take away the bravery of \add their\add*
tinkling ornaments \add about their feet\add*, and \add their\add*
cauls, and \add their\add* round tires like the moon,\f + \fr 3.18 
\ft cauls: or, networks\f*

The chains, and the bracelets, and the mufflers,\f + \fr 3.19 
\ft chains: or, sweet balls\f*\f + \fr 3.19  \ft mufflers: or, spangled
ornaments\f*

The bonnets, and the ornaments of the legs, and the headbands,
and the tablets, and the earrings,\f + \fr 3.20  \ft tablets: Heb. houses of the
soul\f*

The changeable suits of apparel, and the mantles, and the
wimples, and the crisping pins,
The glasses, and the fine linen, and the hoods, and the vails.

And it shall come to pass, \add that\add* instead of sweet
smell there shall be stink; and instead of a girdle a rent; and instead of well
set hair baldness; and instead of a stomacher a girding of sackcloth;
\add and\add* burning instead of beauty.

Thy men shall fall by the sword, and thy mighty in the war.\f + \fr 3.25 
\ft mighty: Heb. might\f*

And her gates shall lament and mourn; and she \add being\add*
desolate shall sit upon the ground.\f + \fr 3.26  \ft desolate: or, emptied: Heb.
cleansed\f*

And in that day seven women shall take hold of one man, saying,
We will eat our own bread, and wear our own apparel: only let us be
called by thy name, to take away our reproach.\f + \fr 4.1  \ft let…: Heb. let thy name be called upon
us\f*\f + \fr 4.1  \ft to take…: or, take thou away\f*

In that day shall the branch of the \nd LORD\nd* be beautiful
and glorious, and the fruit of the earth \add shall be\add* excellent
and comely for them that are escaped of Israel.\f + \fr 4.2  \ft beautiful…: Heb. beauty and
glory\f*\f + \fr 4.2  \ft them…: Heb. the escaping\f*

And it shall come to pass, \add that he that is\add* left in
Zion, and \add he that\add* remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called
holy, \add even\add* every one that is written among the living in
Jerusalem:\f + \fr 4.3  \ft among…: or, to life\f*

When the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters
of Zion, and shall have purged the blood of Jerusalem from the midst
thereof by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning.

And the \nd LORD\nd* will create upon every dwelling place
of mount Zion, and upon her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day,
and the shining of a flaming fire by night: for upon all the glory
\add shall be\add* a defence.\f + \fr 4.5  \ft upon all: or, above
all\f*\f + \fr 4.5  \ft defence: Heb. covering\f*

And there shall be a tabernacle for a shadow in the daytime
from the heat, and for a place of refuge, and for a covert from storm
and from rain.

Now will I sing to my wellbeloved a song of my beloved touching his
vineyard. My wellbeloved hath a vineyard in a very fruitful hill:\f + \fr 5.1 
\ft a very…: Heb. the horn of the son of oil\f*

And he fenced it, and gathered out the stones thereof, and
planted it with the choicest vine, and built a tower in the midst
of it, and also made a winepress therein: and he looked that it should bring
forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes.\f + \fr 5.2  \ft fenced: or, made a wall
about\f*\f + \fr 5.2  \ft made: Heb. hewed\f*

And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem, and men of Judah, judge,
I pray you, betwixt me and my vineyard.

What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not
done in it? wherefore, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes,
brought it forth wild grapes?

And now go to; I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard:
I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; \add and\add*
break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down:\f + \fr 5.5 
\ft trodden…: Heb. for a treading\f*

For the vineyard of the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts \add is\add*
the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he
looked for judgment, but behold oppression; for righteousness, but behold a
cry.\f + \fr 5.7  \ft his…: Heb. plant of his pleasures\f*\f + \fr 5.7 
\ft oppression: Heb. a scab\f*

Woe unto them that join house to house, \add that\add* lay
field to field, till \add there be\add* no place, that they may be
placed alone in the midst of the earth!\f + \fr 5.8  \ft they: Heb.
ye\f*

In mine ears \add said\add* the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts, Of a
truth many houses shall be desolate, \add even\add* great and fair,
without inhabitant.\f + \fr 5.9  \ft In…: or, This is in mine ears, saith the
\+nd LORD\+nd*, etc\f*\f + \fr 5.9  \ft Of a…: Heb. If not, etc\f*

Yea, ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and the seed
of an homer shall yield an ephah.

Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, \add that\add*
they may follow strong drink; that continue until night, \add till\add*
wine inflame them!\f + \fr 5.11  \ft inflame: of, pursue\f*

And the harp, and the viol, the tabret, and pipe, and wine,
are in their feasts: but they regard not the work of the \nd LORD\nd*,
neither consider the operation of his hands.

Therefore my people are gone into captivity, because \add they
have\add* no knowledge: and their honourable men \add are\add* famished,
and their multitude dried up with thirst.\f + \fr 5.13  \ft honourable…: Heb. glory are men of
famine\f*

Therefore hell hath enlarged herself, and opened her mouth
without measure: and their glory, and their multitude, and their
pomp, and he that rejoiceth, shall descend into it.

And the mean man shall be brought down, and the mighty man
shall be humbled, and the eyes of the lofty shall be humbled:

But the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts shall be exalted in judgment,
and God that is holy shall be sanctified in righteousness.\f + \fr 5.16 
\ft God…: or, the holy God: Heb. the God the holy\f*

Then shall the lambs feed after their manner, and the waste
places of the fat ones shall strangers eat.

Woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and
sin as it were with a cart rope:

That say, Let him make speed, \add and\add* hasten his work,
that we may see \add it:\add* and let the counsel of the Holy One
of Israel draw nigh and come, that we may know \add it\add*!

Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put
darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet,
and sweet for bitter!\f + \fr 5.20  \ft call…: Heb. say concerning evil, It is good,
etc\f*

Woe unto \add them that are\add* wise in their own eyes, and
prudent in their own sight!\f + \fr 5.21  \ft in their own sight: Heb. before their
face\f*

Woe unto \add them that are\add* mighty to drink wine, and
men of strength to mingle strong drink:

Which justify the wicked for reward, and take away the righteousness
of the righteous from him!

Therefore as the fire devoureth  the stubble, and the flame
consumeth the chaff, \add so\add* their root shall be as rottenness,
and their blossom shall go up as dust: because they have cast away
the law of the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts, and despised the word of the Holy
One of Israel.\f + \fr 5.24  \ft fire: Heb. tongue of fire\f*

Therefore is the anger of the \nd LORD\nd* kindled against his
people, and he hath stretched forth his hand against them, and hath
smitten them: and the hills did tremble, and their carcases \add were\add*
torn in the midst of the streets. For all this his anger is not turned
away, but his hand \add is\add* stretched out still.\f + \fr 5.25 
\ft torn: or, as dung\f*

And he will lift up an ensign to the nations from far, and will
hiss unto them from the end of the earth: and, behold, they shall
