which eat swine’s flesh, and broth of abominable \add things is in\add*
their vessels;\f + \fr 65.4  \ft broth: or, pieces\f*

Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am
holier than thou. These \add are\add* a smoke in my nose, a fire
that burneth all the day.\f + \fr 65.5  \ft nose: or, anger\f*

Behold, \add it is\add* written before me: I will not keep silence,
but will recompense, even recompense into their bosom,

Your iniquities, and the iniquities of your fathers together,
saith the \nd LORD\nd*, which have burned incense upon the mountains,
and blasphemed me upon the hills: therefore will I measure their
former work into their bosom.

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd*, As the new wine is found in the
cluster, and \add one\add* saith, Destroy it not; for a blessing
\add is\add* in it: so will I do for my servants’ sakes, that I may not
destroy them all.

And I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob, and out of Judah
an inheritor of my mountains: and mine elect shall inherit it, and my
servants shall dwell there.

And Sharon shall be a fold of flocks, and the valley of Achor
a place for the herds to lie down in, for my people that have sought me.

But ye \add are\add* they that forsake the \nd LORD\nd*,
that forget my holy mountain, that prepare a table for that troop,
and that furnish the drink offering unto that number.\f + \fr 65.11 
\ft troop: or, Gad\f*\f + \fr 65.11  \ft number: or, Meni, a pagan
god\f*

Therefore will I number you to the sword, and ye shall all bow
down to the slaughter: because when I called, ye did not answer;
when I spake, ye did not hear; but did evil before mine eyes, and did
choose \add that\add* wherein I delighted not.

Therefore thus saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*, Behold, my servants
shall eat, but ye shall be hungry: behold, my servants shall drink,
but ye shall be thirsty: behold, my servants shall rejoice, but ye shall be
ashamed:

Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart, but ye shall
cry for sorrow of heart, and shall howl for vexation of spirit.\f + \fr 65.14 
\ft vexation: Heb. breaking\f*

And ye shall leave your name for a curse unto my chosen: for the
Lord \nd GOD\nd* shall slay thee, and call his servants by another
name:

That he who blesseth himself in the earth shall bless himself in the
God of truth; and he that sweareth in the earth shall swear by the
God of truth; because the former troubles are forgotten, and because they are
hid from mine eyes.

For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the
former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.\f + \fr 65.17 
\ft come…: Heb. come upon the heart\f*

But be ye glad and rejoice for ever \add in that\add* which I
create: for, behold, I create Jerusalem a rejoicing, and her people
a joy.

And I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and joy in my people: and the
voice of weeping shall be no more heard in her, nor the voice of
crying.

There shall be no more thence an infant of days, nor an old
man that hath not filled his days: for the child shall die an hundred
years old; but the sinner \add being\add* an hundred years old shall be
accursed.

And they shall build houses, and inhabit \add them;\add* and they shall
plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them.

They shall not build, and another inhabit; they shall not
plant, and another eat: for as the days of a tree \add are\add* the
days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their
hands.\f + \fr 65.22  \ft shall long…: Heb. shall make them continue long, or, shall wear
out\f*

They shall not labour in vain, nor bring forth for trouble; for they
\add are\add* the seed of the blessed of the \nd LORD\nd*, and their
offspring with them.

And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will answer;
and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.

The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall
eat straw like the bullock: and dust \add shall be\add* the serpent’s
meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith
the \nd LORD\nd*.

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd*, The heaven \add is\add* my throne,
and the earth \add is\add* my footstool: where \add is\add* the house
that ye build unto me? and where \add is\add* the place of my rest?

For all those \add things\add* hath mine hand made, and all those
\add things\add* have been, saith the \nd LORD\nd*: but to this \add man\add*
will I look, \add even\add* to \add him that is\add* poor and of a
contrite spirit, and trembleth at my word.

He that killeth an ox \add is as if\add* he slew a man; he that
sacrificeth a lamb, \add as if\add* he cut off a dog’s neck; he that
offereth an oblation, \add as if he offered\add* swine’s blood; he that
burneth incense, \add as if\add* he blessed an idol. Yea, they have
chosen their own ways, and their soul delighteth in their abominations.\f + \fr 66.3 
\ft lamb: or, kid\f*\f + \fr 66.3  \ft burneth: Heb. maketh a memorial
of\f*

I also will choose their delusions, and will bring their fears
upon them; because when I called, none did answer; when I spake,
they did not hear: but they did evil before mine eyes, and chose
\add that\add* in which I delighted not.\f + \fr 66.4  \ft delusions: or,
devices\f*

Hear the word of the \nd LORD\nd*, ye that tremble at his
word; Your brethren that hated you, that cast you out for my name’s
sake, said, Let the \nd LORD\nd* be glorified: but he shall appear
to your joy, and they shall be ashamed.

A voice of noise from the city, a voice from the temple, a
voice of the \nd LORD\nd* that rendereth recompence to his enemies.

Before she travailed, she brought forth; before her pain came,
she was delivered of a man child.

Who hath heard such a thing? who hath seen such things? Shall the
earth be made to bring forth in one day? \add or\add* shall a nation
be born at once? for as soon as Zion travailed, she brought forth
her children.

Shall I bring to the birth, and not cause to bring forth? saith
the \nd LORD\nd*: shall I cause to bring forth, and shut \add the
womb\add*? saith thy God.\f + \fr 66.9  \ft not…: or, not beget?\f*

Rejoice ye with Jerusalem, and be glad with her, all ye that
love her: rejoice for joy with her, all ye that mourn for her:

That ye may suck, and be satisfied with the breasts of her
consolations; that ye may milk out, and be delighted with the abundance
of her glory.\f + \fr 66.11  \ft abundance: or, brightness\f*

For thus saith the \nd LORD\nd*, Behold, I will extend peace
to her like a river, and the glory of the Gentiles like a flowing
stream: then shall ye suck, ye shall be borne upon \add her\add*
sides, and be dandled upon \add her\add* knees.

As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you; and ye shall be
comforted in Jerusalem.

And when ye see \add this\add*, your heart shall rejoice,
and your bones shall flourish like an herb: and the hand of the \nd LORD\nd*
shall be known toward his servants, and \add his\add* indignation
toward his enemies.

For, behold, the \nd LORD\nd* will come with fire, and with his
chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his
rebuke with flames of fire.

For by fire and by his sword will the 
d LORD
d* plead with all
flesh: and the slain of the 
d LORD
d* shall be many.

They that sanctify themselves, and purify themselves in the
gardens behind one \add tree\add* in the midst, eating  swine’s flesh,
and the abomination, and the mouse, shall be consumed together, saith
the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 66.17  \ft behind…: or, one after another\f*

For I \add know\add* their works and their thoughts: it shall
come, that I will gather all nations and tongues; and they shall
come, and see my glory.

And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those that
escape of them unto the nations, \add to\add* Tarshish, Pul, and
Lud, that draw the bow, \add to\add* Tubal, and Javan, \add to\add*
the isles afar off, that have not heard my fame, neither have seen
my glory; and they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles.

And they shall bring all your brethren \add for\add* an offering
unto the \nd LORD\nd* out of all nations upon horses, and in chariots,
and in litters, and upon mules, and upon swift beasts, to my holy
mountain Jerusalem, saith the \nd LORD\nd*, as the children of Israel
bring an offering in a clean vessel into the house of the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 66.20 
\ft litters: or, coaches\f*

And I will also take of them for priests \add and\add* for
Levites, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make,
shall remain before me, saith the \nd LORD\nd*, so shall your seed
and your name remain.

And it shall come to pass, \add that\add* from one new moon
to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come
to worship before me, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 66.23  \ft from one new…: Heb. from new moon to his new moon, and from
sabbath to his sabbath\f*

And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the
men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die,
neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring
unto all flesh.

headers.toc1: The Book of the Prophet Jeremiah
headers.mt1: The Book of the Prophet Jeremiah

verses.text:
The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests that
\add were\add* in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin:

To whom the word of the \nd LORD\nd* came in the days of Josiah
the son of Amon king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.

It came also in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king
of Judah, unto the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah the son of
Josiah king of Judah, unto the carrying away of Jerusalem captive
in the fifth month.
Then the word of the \nd LORD\nd* came unto me, saying,

Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest
forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, \add and\add* I ordained
thee a prophet unto the nations.\f + \fr 1.5  \ft ordained: Heb.
gave\f*

Then said I, Ah, Lord \nd GOD\nd*! behold, I cannot speak: for I
\add am\add* a child.

But the \nd LORD\nd* said unto me, Say not, I \add am\add*
a child: for thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I
command thee thou shalt speak.

Be not afraid of their faces: for I \add am\add* with thee to
deliver thee, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

Then the 
d LORD
d* put forth his hand, and touched my mouth.
And the 
d LORD
d* said unto me, Behold, I have put my words in thy
mouth.

See, I have this day set thee over the nations and over the
kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw
down, to build, and to plant.

Moreover the word of the \nd LORD\nd* came unto me, saying,
Jeremiah, what seest thou? And I said, I see a rod of an almond tree.

Then said the \nd LORD\nd* unto me, Thou hast well seen: for I will
hasten my word to perform it.

And the word of the \nd LORD\nd* came unto me the second time,
saying, What seest thou? And I said, I see a seething pot; and the
face thereof \add is\add* toward the north.\f + \fr 1.13  \ft toward…: Heb. from the face of the
north\f*

Then the \nd LORD\nd* said unto me, Out of the north an evil
shall break forth upon all the inhabitants of the land.\f + \fr 1.14 
\ft shall…: Heb. shall be opened\f*

For, lo, I will call all the families of the kingdoms of the
north, saith the \nd LORD\nd*; and they shall come, and they shall
set every one his throne at the entering of the gates of Jerusalem,
and against all the walls thereof round about, and against all the
cities of Judah.

And I will utter my judgments against them touching all their
wickedness, who have forsaken me, and have burned incense unto other
gods, and worshipped the works of their own hands.

Thou therefore gird up thy loins, and arise, and speak unto them all that I
command thee: be not dismayed at their faces, lest I confound thee
before them.\f + \fr 1.17  \ft confound: or, break to pieces\f*

For, behold, I have made thee this day a defenced city, and an
iron pillar, and brasen walls against the whole land, against the
kings of Judah, against the princes thereof, against the priests
thereof, and against the people of the land.

And they shall fight against thee; but they shall not prevail against thee; for I
\add am\add* with thee, saith the \nd LORD\nd*, to deliver thee.
Moreover the word of the \nd LORD\nd* came to me, saying,

Go and cry in the ears of Jerusalem, saying, Thus saith the
\nd LORD\nd*; I remember thee, the kindness of thy youth, the love
of thine espousals, when thou wentest after me in the wilderness,
in a land \add that was\add* not sown.\f + \fr 2.2  \ft thee: or, for thy
sake\f*

Israel \add was\add* holiness unto the 
d LORD
d*, \add and\add*
the firstfruits of his increase: all that devour him shall offend;
evil shall come upon them, saith the 
d LORD
d*.

Hear ye the word of the \nd LORD\nd*, O house of Jacob, and all the
families of the house of Israel:

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd*, What iniquity have your fathers
found in me, that they are gone far from me, and have walked after
vanity, and are become vain?

Neither said they, Where \add is\add* the \nd LORD\nd* that brought us
up out of the land of Egypt, that led us through the wilderness,
through a land of deserts and of pits, through a land of drought,
and of the shadow of death, through a land that no man passed through,
and where no man dwelt?

And I brought you into a plentiful country, to eat the fruit
thereof and the goodness thereof; but when ye entered, ye defiled
my land, and made mine heritage an abomination.\f + \fr 2.7  \ft a plentiful…: or, the land of
Carmel\f*

The priests said not, Where \add is\add* the \nd LORD\nd*?
and they that handle the law knew me not: the pastors also transgressed
against me, and the prophets prophesied by Baal, and walked after
\add things that\add* do not profit.

Wherefore I will yet plead with you, saith the \nd LORD\nd*,
and with your children’s children will I plead.

For pass over the isles of Chittim, and see; and send unto
Kedar, and consider diligently, and see if there be such a thing.\f + \fr 2.10 
\ft over: or, over to\f*

Hath a nation changed \add their\add* gods, which \add are\add*
yet no gods? but my people have changed their glory for \add that
which\add* doth not profit.

Be astonished, O ye heavens, at this, and be horribly afraid,
be ye very desolate, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken
me the fountain of living waters, \add and\add* hewed them out cisterns,
broken cisterns, that can hold no water.

\add Is\add* Israel a servant? \add is\add* he a homeborn
\add slave\add*? why is he spoiled?\f + \fr 2.14  \ft spoiled: Heb. become a
spoil?\f*

The young lions roared upon him, \add and\add* yelled, and they
made his land waste: his cities are burned without inhabitant.\f + \fr 2.15 
\ft yelled: Heb. gave out their voice\f*

Also the children of Noph and Tahapanes have broken the crown of thy
head.\f + \fr 2.16  \ft have…: or, feed on thy crown\f*

Hast thou not procured this unto thyself, in that thou hast
forsaken the \nd LORD\nd* thy God, when he led thee by the way?

And now what hast thou to do in the way of Egypt, to drink
the waters of Sihor? or what hast thou to do in the way of Assyria,
to drink the waters of the river?

Thine own wickedness shall correct thee, and thy backslidings
shall reprove thee: know therefore and see that \add it is\add* an
evil \add thing\add* and bitter, that thou hast forsaken the \nd LORD\nd*
thy God, and that my fear \add is\add* not in thee, saith the Lord
\nd GOD\nd* of hosts.

For of old time I have broken thy yoke, \add and\add* burst
thy bands; and thou saidst, I will not transgress; when upon every
high hill and under every green tree thou wanderest, playing the
harlot.\f + \fr 2.20  \ft transgress: or, serve\f*

Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed:
how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?

For though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap,
\add yet\add* thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord
\nd GOD\nd*.

How canst thou say, I am not polluted, I have not gone after
Baalim? see thy way in the valley, know what thou hast done: \add thou
art\add* a swift dromedary traversing her ways;\f + \fr 2.23  \ft thou art…: or, O swift
dromedary\f*

A wild ass used to the wilderness, \add that\add* snuffeth
up the wind at her pleasure; in her occasion who can turn her away?
all they that seek her will not weary themselves; in her month they shall
find her.\f + \fr 2.24  \ft A wild…: or, O wild ass, etc\f*\f + \fr 2.24 
\ft used: Heb. taught\f*\f + \fr 2.24  \ft her pleasure: Heb. the desire of her
heart\f*\f + \fr 2.24  \ft turn…: or, reverse it?\f*

Withhold thy foot from being unshod, and thy throat from thirst:
but thou saidst, There is no hope: no; for I have loved strangers,
and after them will I go.\f + \fr 2.25  \ft There…: or, Is the case
desperate?\f*

As the thief is ashamed when he is found, so is the house
of Israel ashamed; they, their kings, their princes, and their priests,
and their prophets,

Saying to a stock, Thou \add art\add* my father; and to a
stone, Thou hast brought me forth: for they have turned \add their\add*
back unto me, and not \add their\add* face: but in the time of their
trouble they will say, Arise, and save us.\f + \fr 2.27  \ft brought…: or, begotten
me\f*\f + \fr 2.27  \ft their back: Heb. the hinder part of the neck\f*

But where \add are\add* thy gods that thou hast made thee? let them
arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble: for \add according
to\add* the number of thy cities are thy gods, O Judah.\f + \fr 2.28 
\ft trouble: Heb. evil\f*

Wherefore will ye plead with me? ye all have transgressed
against me, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

In vain have I smitten your children; they received no correction:
your own sword hath devoured your prophets, like a destroying lion.

O generation, see ye the word of the \nd LORD\nd*. Have I been a
wilderness unto Israel? a land of darkness? wherefore say my people,
We are lords; we will come no more unto thee?\f + \fr 2.31  \ft We are…: Heb. We have
dominion\f*

Can a maid forget her ornaments, \add or\add* a bride her
attire? yet my people have forgotten me days without number.

Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love? therefore hast thou also
taught the wicked ones thy ways.

Also in thy skirts is found the blood of the souls of the
poor innocents: I have not found it by secret search, but upon all
these.\f + \fr 2.34  \ft secret…: Heb. digging\f*

Yet thou sayest, Because I am innocent, surely his anger shall
turn from me. Behold, I will plead with thee, because thou sayest,
I have not sinned.

Why gaddest thou about so much to change thy way? thou also shalt be
ashamed of Egypt, as thou wast ashamed of Assyria.

Yea, thou shalt go forth from him, and thine hands upon thine
head: for the \nd LORD\nd* hath rejected thy confidences, and thou shalt not
prosper in them.

They say, If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become
another man’s, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land
be greatly polluted? but thou hast played the harlot with many lovers;
yet return again to me, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 3.1  \ft They say: Heb.
Saying\f*

Lift up thine eyes unto the high places, and see where thou hast not been
lien with. In the ways hast thou sat for them, as the Arabian in the
wilderness; and thou hast polluted the land with thy whoredoms and with thy
wickedness.

Therefore the showers have been withholden, and there hath been no latter
rain; and thou hadst a whore’s forehead, thou refusedst to be ashamed.

Wilt thou not from this time cry unto me, My father, thou \add art\add*
the guide of my youth?

Will he reserve \add his anger\add* for ever? will he keep
\add it\add* to the end? Behold, thou hast spoken and done evil things
as thou couldest.

The \nd LORD\nd* said also unto me in the days of Josiah the
king, Hast thou seen \add that\add* which backsliding Israel hath
done? she is gone up upon every high mountain and under every green
tree, and there hath played the harlot.

And I said after she had done all these \add things\add*, Turn
thou unto me. But she returned not. And her treacherous sister Judah
saw \add it\add*.

And I saw, when for all the causes whereby backsliding Israel
committed adultery I had put her away, and given her a bill of divorce;
yet her treacherous sister Judah feared not, but went and played the
harlot also.

And it came to pass through the lightness of her whoredom,
that she defiled the land, and committed adultery with stones and with
stocks.\f + \fr 3.9  \ft lightness: or, fame\f*

And yet for all this her treacherous sister Judah hath not
turned unto me with her whole heart, but feignedly, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 3.10 
\ft feignedly: Heb. in falsehood\f*

And the \nd LORD\nd* said unto me, The backsliding Israel
hath justified herself more than treacherous Judah.

Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, Return,
thou backsliding Israel, saith the \nd LORD\nd*; \add and\add* I will not cause mine
anger to fall upon you: for I \add am\add* merciful, saith the \nd LORD\nd*,
\add and\add* I will not keep \add anger\add* for ever.

Only acknowledge thine iniquity, that thou hast transgressed
against the \nd LORD\nd* thy God, and hast scattered thy ways to the
strangers under every green tree, and ye have not obeyed my voice,
saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

Turn, O backsliding children, saith the \nd LORD\nd*; for I am
married unto you: and I will take you one of a city, and two of a
family, and I will bring you to Zion:

And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall
feed you with knowledge and understanding.

And it shall come to pass, when ye be multiplied and increased
in the land, in those days, saith the \nd LORD\nd*, they shall say
no more, The ark of the covenant of the \nd LORD\nd*: neither shall it
come to mind: neither shall they remember it; neither shall they
visit \add it;\add* neither shall \add that\add* be done any more.\f + \fr 3.16 
\ft come to mind: Heb. come upon the heart\f*\f + \fr 3.16  \ft that…: or, it be
magnified\f*

At that time they shall call Jerusalem the throne of the \nd LORD\nd*;
and all the nations shall be gathered unto it, to the name of the
\nd LORD\nd*, to Jerusalem: neither shall they walk any more after
the imagination of their evil heart.\f + \fr 3.17  \ft imagination: or,
stubbornness\f*

In those days the house of Judah shall walk with the house
of Israel, and they shall come together out of the land of the north
to the land that I have given for an inheritance unto your fathers.\f + \fr 3.18 
\ft with: or, to\f*\f + \fr 3.18  \ft given…: or, caused your fathers to
possess\f*

But I said, How shall I put thee among the children, and give
thee a pleasant land, a goodly heritage of the hosts of nations?
and I said, Thou shalt call me, My father; and shalt not turn away
from me.\f + \fr 3.19  \ft from me: Heb. from after me\f*\f + \fr 3.19 
\ft a goodly…: Heb. an heritage of glory, or, beauty\f*\f + \fr 3.19 
\ft pleasant…: Heb. land of desire\f*

Surely \add as\add* a wife treacherously departeth from her
husband, so have ye dealt treacherously with me, O house of Israel,
saith the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 3.20  \ft husband: Heb. friend\f*

A voice was heard upon the high places, weeping \add and\add*
supplications of the children of Israel: for they have perverted
their way, \add and\add* they have forgotten the \nd LORD\nd* their
God.

Return, ye backsliding children, \add and\add* I will heal
your backslidings. Behold, we come unto thee; for thou \add art\add*
the \nd LORD\nd* our God.

Truly in vain \add is salvation hoped for\add* from the hills,
\add and from\add* the multitude of mountains: truly in the \nd LORD\nd*
our God \add is\add* the salvation of Israel.

For shame hath devoured the labour of our fathers from our
youth; their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters.

We lie down in our shame, and our confusion covereth us: for we have
sinned against the \nd LORD\nd* our God, we and our fathers, from our
youth even unto this day, and have not obeyed the voice of the \nd LORD\nd*
our God.

If thou wilt return, O Israel, saith the \nd LORD\nd*, return
unto me: and if thou wilt put away thine abominations out of my sight,
then shalt thou not remove.

And thou shalt swear, The \nd LORD\nd* liveth, in truth, in
judgment, and in righteousness; and the nations shall bless themselves in him, and in him shall they
glory.

For thus saith the \nd LORD\nd* to the men of Judah and Jerusalem,
Break up your fallow ground, and sow not among thorns.

Circumcise yourselves to the \nd LORD\nd*, and take away the
foreskins of your heart, ye men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem:
lest my fury come forth like fire, and burn that none can quench
\add it\add*, because of the evil of your doings.

Declare ye in Judah, and publish in Jerusalem; and say, Blow
ye the trumpet in the land: cry, gather together, and say, Assemble
yourselves, and let us go into the defenced cities.

Set up the standard toward Zion: retire, stay not: for I will
bring evil from the north, and a great destruction.\f + \fr 4.6 
\ft retire: or, strengthen\f*\f + \fr 4.6  \ft destruction: Heb.
breaking\f*

The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the
Gentiles is on his way; he is gone forth from his place to make thy
land desolate; \add and\add* thy cities shall be laid waste, without an
inhabitant.

For this gird you with sackcloth, lament and howl: for the
fierce anger of the \nd LORD\nd* is not turned back from us.

And it shall come to pass at that day, saith the \nd LORD\nd*,
\add that\add* the heart of the king shall perish, and the heart
of the princes; and the priests shall be astonished, and the prophets
shall wonder.

At that time shall it be said to this people and to Jerusalem,
A dry wind of the high places in the wilderness toward the daughter

them to the king of Babylon to Riblah.

And the king of Babylon smote them, and put them to death
in Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away captive
out of his own land.

This \add is\add* the people whom Nebuchadrezzar carried away
captive: in the seventh year three thousand Jews and three and twenty:

In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar he carried away captive
from Jerusalem eight hundred thirty and two persons:\f + \fr 52.29 
\ft persons: Heb. souls\f*

In the three and twentieth year of Nebuchadrezzar Nebuzar-adan
the captain of the guard carried away captive of the Jews seven hundred
forty and five persons: all the persons \add were\add* four thousand
and six hundred.

And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the
captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the
five and twentieth \add day\add* of the month, \add that\add* Evil-merodach
king of Babylon in the \add first\add* year of his reign lifted up
the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and brought him forth out of
prison,

And spake kindly unto him, and set his throne above the throne
of the kings that \add were\add* with him in Babylon,\f + \fr 52.32 
\ft kindly…: Heb. good things with him\f*

And changed his prison garments: and he did continually eat
bread before him all the days of his life.

And \add for\add* his diet, there was a continual diet given
him of the king of Babylon, every day a portion until the day of his
death, all the days of his life.\f + \fr 52.34  \ft every…: Heb. the matter of the day in his
day\f*

headers.toc1: The Lamentations of Jeremiah
headers.mt1: The Lamentations of Jeremiah

verses.text:
How doth the city sit solitary, \add that was\add* full of
people! \add how\add* is she become as a widow! she \add that was\add*
great among the nations, \add and\add* princess among the provinces,
\add how\add* is she become tributary!

She weepeth sore in the night, and her tears \add are\add*
on her cheeks: among all her lovers she hath none to comfort \add her:\add*
all her friends have dealt treacherously with her, they are become her
enemies.

Judah is gone into captivity because of affliction, and because of
great servitude: she dwelleth among the heathen, she findeth no rest:
all her persecutors overtook her between the straits.\f + \fr 1.3 
\ft because of great…: Heb. for the greatness of servitude\f*

The ways of Zion do mourn, because none come to the solemn
feasts: all her gates are desolate: her priests sigh, her virgins
are afflicted, and she \add is\add* in bitterness.

Her adversaries are the chief, her enemies prosper; for the
\nd LORD\nd* hath afflicted her for the multitude of her transgressions:
her children are gone into captivity before the enemy.

And from the daughter of Zion all her beauty is departed: her
princes are become like harts \add that\add* find no pasture, and they are
gone without strength before the pursuer.

Jerusalem remembered in the days of her affliction and of her
miseries all her pleasant things that she had in the days of old,
when her people fell into the hand of the enemy, and none did help
her: the adversaries saw her, \add and\add* did mock at her sabbaths.\f + \fr 1.7 
\ft pleasant: or, desirable\f*

Jerusalem hath grievously sinned; therefore she is removed:
all that honoured her despise her, because they have seen her nakedness:
yea, she sigheth, and turneth backward.\f + \fr 1.8  \ft is…: Heb. is become a removing, or,
wandering\f*

Her filthiness \add is\add* in her skirts; she remembereth
not her last end; therefore she came down wonderfully: she had no
comforter. O \nd LORD\nd*, behold my affliction: for the enemy hath
magnified \add himself\add*.

The adversary hath spread out his hand upon all her pleasant
things: for she hath seen \add that\add* the heathen entered into her
sanctuary, whom thou didst command \add that\add* they should not
enter into thy congregation.\f + \fr 1.10  \ft pleasant: or, desirable\f*

All her people sigh, they seek bread; they have given their pleasant
things for meat to relieve the soul: see, O \nd LORD\nd*, and consider;
for I am become vile.\f + \fr 1.11  \ft to…: or, to make the soul to come
again\f*

\add Is it\add* nothing to you, all ye that pass by? behold,
and see if there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow, which is done
unto me, wherewith the \nd LORD\nd* hath afflicted \add me\add* in the
day of his fierce anger.\f + \fr 1.12  \ft Is it…: or, It is nothing\f*\f + \fr 1.12 
\ft pass by: Heb. pass by the way?\f*

From above hath he sent fire into my bones, and it prevaileth
against them: he hath spread a net for my feet, he hath turned me
back: he hath made me desolate \add and\add* faint all the day.

The yoke of my transgressions is bound by his hand: they are
wreathed, \add and\add* come up upon my neck: he hath made my strength
to fall, the Lord hath delivered me into \add their\add* hands, \add from
whom\add* I am not able to rise up.

The Lord hath trodden under foot all my mighty \add men\add*
in the midst of me: he hath called an assembly against me to crush
my young men: the Lord hath trodden the virgin, the daughter of Judah,
\add as\add* in a winepress.\f + \fr 1.15  \ft the virgin…: or, the winepress of the virgin,
etc\f*

For these \add things\add* I weep; mine eye, mine eye runneth
down with water, because the comforter that should relieve my soul
is far from me: my children are desolate, because the enemy prevailed.\f + \fr 1.16 
\ft relieve: Heb. bring back\f*

Zion spreadeth forth her hands, \add and there is\add* none to
comfort her: the \nd LORD\nd* hath commanded concerning Jacob, \add that\add*
his adversaries \add should be\add* round about him: Jerusalem is as a menstruous
woman among them.

The \nd LORD\nd* is righteous; for I have rebelled against his
commandment: hear, I pray you, all people, and behold my sorrow:
my virgins and my young men are gone into captivity.\f + \fr 1.18 
\ft commandment: Heb. mouth\f*

I called for my lovers, \add but\add* they deceived me: my
priests and mine elders gave up the ghost in the city, while they
sought their meat to relieve their souls.

Behold, O \nd LORD\nd*; for I \add am\add* in distress: my
bowels are troubled; mine heart is turned within me; for I have grievously
rebelled: abroad the sword bereaveth, at home \add there is\add*
as death.

They have heard that I sigh: \add there is\add* none to comfort
me: all mine enemies have heard of my trouble; they are glad that thou hast
done \add it:\add* thou wilt bring the day \add that\add* thou hast
called, and they shall be like unto me.\f + \fr 1.21  \ft called: or,
proclaimed\f*

Let all their wickedness come before thee; and do unto them, as thou hast
done unto me for all my transgressions: for my sighs \add are\add*
many, and my heart \add is\add* faint.

How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud
in his anger, \add and\add* cast down from heaven unto the earth
the beauty of Israel, and remembered not his footstool in the day
of his anger!

The Lord hath swallowed up all the habitations of Jacob, and hath not
pitied: he hath thrown down in his wrath the strong holds of the
daughter of Judah; he hath brought \add them\add* down to the ground:
he hath polluted the kingdom and the princes thereof.\f + \fr 2.2 
\ft brought…: Heb. made to touch\f*

He hath cut off in \add his\add* fierce anger all the horn
of Israel: he hath drawn back his right hand from before the enemy,
and he burned against Jacob like a flaming fire, \add which\add*
devoureth round about.

He hath bent his bow like an enemy: he stood with his right
hand as an adversary, and slew all \add that were\add* pleasant to the
eye in the tabernacle of the daughter of Zion: he poured out his
fury like fire.\f + \fr 2.4  \ft all…: Heb. all the desirable of the
eye\f*

The Lord was as an enemy: he hath swallowed up Israel, he hath swallowed
up all her palaces: he hath destroyed his strong holds, and hath
increased in the daughter of Judah mourning and lamentation.

And he hath violently taken away his tabernacle, as \add if it were
of\add* a garden: he hath destroyed his places of the assembly: the
\nd LORD\nd* hath caused the solemn feasts and sabbaths to be forgotten
in Zion, and hath despised in the indignation of his anger the king
and the priest.\f + \fr 2.6  \ft tabernacle: or, hedge\f*

The Lord hath cast off his altar, he hath abhorred his sanctuary,
he hath given up into the hand of the enemy the walls of her palaces;
they have made a noise in the house of the \nd LORD\nd*, as in the
day of a solemn feast.\f + \fr 2.7  \ft given up: Heb. shut up\f*

The \nd LORD\nd* hath purposed to destroy the wall of the daughter
of Zion: he hath stretched out a line, he hath not withdrawn his
hand from destroying: therefore he made the rampart and the wall
to lament; they languished together.\f + \fr 2.8  \ft destroying: Heb. swallowing
up\f*

Her gates are sunk into the ground; he hath destroyed and broken
her bars: her king and her princes \add are\add* among the Gentiles:
the law \add is\add* no \add more;\add* her prophets also find no
vision from the \nd LORD\nd*.

The elders of the daughter of Zion sit upon the ground, \add and\add*
keep silence: they have cast up dust upon their heads; they have
girded themselves with sackcloth: the virgins of Jerusalem hang down
their heads to the ground.

Mine eyes do fail with tears, my bowels are troubled, my liver
is poured upon the earth, for the destruction of the daughter of my
people; because the children and the sucklings swoon in the streets
of the city.\f + \fr 2.11  \ft swoon: or, faint\f*

They say to their mothers, Where \add is\add* corn and wine?
when they swooned as the wounded in the streets of the city, when their
soul was poured out into their mothers’ bosom.

What thing shall I take to witness for thee? what thing shall I
liken to thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? what shall I equal to thee, that I may
comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Zion? for thy breach \add is\add*
great like the sea: who can heal thee?

Thy prophets have seen vain and foolish things for thee: and they have not
discovered thine iniquity, to turn away thy captivity; but have seen
for thee false burdens and causes of banishment.

All that pass by clap \add their\add* hands at thee; they
hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem, \add saying,
Is\add* this the city that \add men\add* call The perfection of beauty,
The joy of the whole earth?\f + \fr 2.15  \ft by: Heb. by the way\f*

All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee: they
hiss and gnash the teeth: they say, We have swallowed \add her\add*
up: certainly this \add is\add* the day that we looked for; we have
found, we have seen \add it\add*.

The \nd LORD\nd* hath done \add that\add* which he had devised;
he hath fulfilled his word that he had commanded in the days of old:
he hath thrown down, and hath not pitied: and he hath caused \add thine\add*
enemy to rejoice over thee, he hath set up the horn of thine adversaries.

Their heart cried unto the Lord, O wall of the daughter of
Zion, let tears run down like a river day and night: give thyself no
rest; let not the apple of thine eye cease.

Arise, cry out in the night: in the beginning of the watches
pour out thine heart like water before the face of the Lord: lift
up thy hands toward him for the life of thy young children, that
faint for hunger in the top of every street.

Behold, O \nd LORD\nd*, and consider to whom thou hast done
this. Shall the women eat their fruit, \add and\add* children of a span
long? shall the priest and the prophet be slain in the sanctuary
of the Lord?\f + \fr 2.20  \ft of a span…: or, swaddled with their
hands?\f*

The young and the old lie on the ground in the streets: my
virgins and my young men are fallen by the sword; thou hast slain
\add them\add* in the day of thine anger; thou hast killed, \add and\add*
not pitied.

Thou hast called as in a solemn day my terrors round about,
so that in the day of the \nd LORD’s\nd* anger none escaped nor remained:
those that I have swaddled and brought up hath mine enemy consumed.

I \add am\add* the man \add that\add* hath seen affliction by the
rod of his wrath.

He hath led me, and brought \add me into\add* darkness, but not
\add into\add* light.

Surely against me is he turned; he turneth his hand \add against
me\add* all the day.
My flesh and my skin hath he made old; he hath broken my bones.

He hath builded against me, and compassed \add me\add* with
gall and travail.

He hath set me in dark places, as \add they that be\add* dead
of old.

He hath hedged me about, that I cannot get out: he hath made my
chain heavy.
Also when I cry and shout, he shutteth out my prayer.

He hath inclosed my ways with hewn stone, he hath made my paths
crooked.

He \add was\add* unto me \add as\add* a bear lying in wait,
\add and as\add* a lion in secret places.

He hath turned aside my ways, and pulled me in pieces: he hath
made me desolate.
He hath bent his bow, and set me as a mark for the arrow.

He hath caused the arrows of his quiver to enter into my reins.\f + \fr 3.13 
\ft arrows: Heb. sons\f*

I was a derision to all my people; \add and\add* their song
all the day.

He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken
with wormwood.\f + \fr 3.15  \ft bitterness: Heb. bitternesses\f*

He hath also broken my teeth with gravel stones, he hath covered
me with ashes.\f + \fr 3.16  \ft covered…: or, rolled me in the ashes\f*

And thou hast removed my soul far off from peace: I forgat
prosperity.\f + \fr 3.17  \ft prosperity: Heb. good\f*
And I said, My strength and my hope is perished from the \nd LORD\nd*:

Remembering mine affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the
gall.\f + \fr 3.19  \ft Remembering: or, Remember\f*

My soul hath \add them\add* still in remembrance, and is humbled in
me.\f + \fr 3.20  \ft humbled: Heb. bowed\f*

This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope.\f + \fr 3.21 
\ft recall…: Heb. make to return to my heart\f*

\add It is of\add* the \nd LORD’s\nd* mercies that we are not
consumed, because his compassions fail not.

\add They are\add* new every morning: great \add is\add* thy
faithfulness.

The \nd LORD\nd* \add is\add* my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I
hope in him.

The \nd LORD\nd* \add is\add* good unto them that wait for him, to the
soul \add that\add* seeketh him.

\add It is\add* good that \add a man\add* should both hope
and quietly wait for the salvation of the \nd LORD\nd*.

\add It is\add* good for a man that he bear the yoke in his
youth.

He sitteth alone and keepeth silence, because he hath borne
\add it\add* upon him.
He putteth his mouth in the dust; if so be there may be hope.

He giveth \add his\add* cheek to him that smiteth him: he is filled
full with reproach.
For the Lord will not cast off for ever:

But though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the
multitude of his mercies.

For he doth not afflict willingly nor grieve the children
of men.\f + \fr 3.33  \ft willingly: Heb. from his heart\f*
To crush under his feet all the prisoners of the earth,

To turn aside the right of a man before the face of the most
High,\f + \fr 3.35  \ft the most High: or, a superior\f*

To subvert a man in his cause, the Lord approveth not.\f + \fr 3.36 
\ft approveth not: or, seeth not\f*

Who \add is\add* he \add that\add* saith, and it cometh to pass,
\add when\add* the Lord commandeth \add it\add* not?

Out of the mouth of the most High proceedeth not evil and
good?

Wherefore doth a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his
sins?\f + \fr 3.39  \ft complain: or, murmur\f*
Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the \nd LORD\nd*.

Let us lift up our heart with \add our\add* hands unto God
in the heavens.
We have transgressed and have rebelled: thou hast not pardoned.

Thou hast covered with anger, and persecuted us: thou hast
slain, thou hast not pitied.

Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that \add our\add*
prayer should not pass through.

Thou hast made us \add as\add* the offscouring and refuse
in the midst of the people.
All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.
Fear and a snare is come upon us, desolation and destruction.

Mine eye runneth down with rivers of water for the destruction
of the daughter of my people.
Mine eye trickleth down, and ceaseth not, without any intermission,
Till the \nd LORD\nd* look down, and behold from heaven.

Mine eye affecteth mine heart because of all the daughters
of my city.\f + \fr 3.51  \ft mine heart: Heb. my soul\f*\f + \fr 3.51 
\ft because…: or, more than all\f*
They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me.

Waters flowed over mine head; \add then\add* I said, I am cut
off.
I called upon thy name, O \nd LORD\nd*, out of the low dungeon.

Thou hast heard my voice: hide not thine ear at my breathing,
at my cry.

Thou drewest near in the day \add that\add* I called upon thee: thou
saidst, Fear not.

O Lord, thou hast pleaded the causes of my soul; thou hast
redeemed my life.
O \nd LORD\nd*, thou hast seen my wrong: judge thou my cause.

Thou hast seen all their vengeance \add and\add* all their
imaginations against me.

Thou hast heard their reproach, O \nd LORD\nd*, \add and\add*
all their imaginations against me;

The lips of those that rose up against me, and their device
against me all the day.

Behold their sitting down, and their rising up; I \add am\add*
their musick.

Render unto them a recompence, O \nd LORD\nd*, according to the
work of their hands.

Give them sorrow of heart, thy curse unto them.\f + \fr 3.65 
\ft sorrow…: or, obstinacy of heart\f*

Persecute and destroy them in anger from under the heavens
of the \nd LORD\nd*.

How is the gold become dim! \add how\add* is the most fine
gold changed! the stones of the sanctuary are poured out in the top
of every street.

The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold, how are they
esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!

Even the sea monsters draw out the breast, they give suck to their young
ones: the daughter of my people \add is become\add* cruel, like the
ostriches in the wilderness.\f + \fr 4.3  \ft sea…: or, sea calves\f*

The tongue of the sucking child cleaveth to the roof of his
mouth for thirst: the young children ask bread, \add and\add* no man
breaketh \add it\add* unto them.

They that did feed delicately are desolate in the streets:
they that were brought up in scarlet embrace dunghills.

For the punishment of the iniquity of the daughter of my people
is greater than the punishment of the sin of Sodom, that was overthrown
as in a moment, and no hands stayed on her.\f + \fr 4.6  \ft punishment of the iniquity: or,
iniquity\f*

Her Nazarites were purer than snow, they were whiter than milk,
they were more ruddy in body than rubies, their polishing \add was\add*
of sapphire:

Their visage is blacker than a coal; they are not known in the
streets: their skin cleaveth to their bones; it is withered, it is become like a
stick.\f + \fr 4.8  \ft blacker…: Heb. darker than blackness\f*

\add They that be\add* slain with the sword are better than
\add they that be\add* slain with hunger: for these pine away, stricken through for
\add want of\add* the fruits of the field.\f + \fr 4.9  \ft pine…: Heb. flow
out\f*

The hands of the pitiful women have sodden their own children:
they were their meat in the destruction of the daughter of my people.

The \nd LORD\nd* hath accomplished his fury; he hath poured
out his fierce anger, and hath kindled a fire in Zion, and it hath
devoured the foundations thereof.

The kings of the earth, and all the inhabitants of the world,
would not have believed that the adversary and the enemy should have
entered into the gates of Jerusalem.

For the sins of her prophets, \add and\add* the iniquities
of her priests, that have shed the blood of the just in the midst of her,

They have wandered \add as\add* blind \add men\add* in the
streets, they have polluted themselves with blood, so that men could
not touch their garments.\f + \fr 4.14  \ft so…: or, in that they could not but
touch\f*

They cried unto them, Depart ye; \add it is\add* unclean;
depart, depart, touch not: when they fled away and wandered, they
said among the heathen, They shall no more sojourn \add there\add*.\f + \fr 4.15 
\ft it…: or, ye polluted\f*

The anger of the \nd LORD\nd* hath divided them; he will no
more regard them: they respected not the persons of the priests,
they favoured not the elders.\f + \fr 4.16  \ft anger: or, face\f*

As for us, our eyes as yet failed for our vain help: in our
watching we have watched for a nation \add that\add* could not save
\add us\add*.

They hunt our steps, that we cannot go in our streets: our
end is near, our days are fulfilled; for our end is come.

Our persecutors are swifter than the eagles of the heaven:
they pursued us upon the mountains, they laid wait for us in the
wilderness.

The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the \nd LORD\nd*,
was taken in their pits, of whom we said, Under his shadow we shall
live among the heathen.

Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, that dwellest in the
land of Uz; the cup also shall pass through unto thee: thou shalt be
drunken, and shalt make thyself naked.

The punishment of thine iniquity is accomplished, O daughter
of Zion; he will no more carry thee away into captivity: he will
visit thine iniquity, O daughter of Edom; he will discover thy sins.\f + \fr 4.22 
\ft The…: or, Thine iniquity\f*\f + \fr 4.22  \ft discover…: or, carry thee captive for thy
sins\f*

Remember, O \nd LORD\nd*, what is come upon us: consider, and
behold our reproach.
Our inheritance is turned to strangers, our houses to aliens.

We are orphans and fatherless, our mothers \add are\add* as
widows.

We have drunken our water for money; our wood is sold unto
us.\f + \fr 5.4  \ft is…: Heb. cometh for price\f*

Our necks \add are\add* under persecution: we labour, \add and\add*
have no rest.\f + \fr 5.5  \ft Our…: Heb. On our necks are we persecuted\f*

We have given the hand \add to\add* the Egyptians, \add and
to\add* the Assyrians, to be satisfied with bread.

Our fathers have sinned, \add and are\add* not; and we have
borne their iniquities.

Servants have ruled over us: \add there is\add* none that doth
deliver \add us\add* out of their hand.

We gat our bread with \add the peril of\add* our lives because
of the sword of the wilderness.

Our skin was black like an oven because of the terrible famine.\f + \fr 5.10 
\ft terrible: or, terrors, or, storms\f*

They ravished the women in Zion, \add and\add* the maids in the
cities of Judah.

Princes are hanged up by their hand: the faces of elders were not
honoured.

They took the young men to grind, and the children fell under the
wood.

The elders have ceased from the gate, the young men from their
musick.
The joy of our heart is ceased; our dance is turned into mourning.

The crown is fallen \add from\add* our head: woe unto us, that we have
sinned!\f + \fr 5.16  \ft The…: Heb. The crown of our head is fallen\f*

For this our heart is faint; for these \add things\add* our
eyes are dim.

Because of the mountain of Zion, which is desolate, the foxes
walk upon it.

Thou, O \nd LORD\nd*, remainest  for ever; thy throne from
generation to generation.

Wherefore dost thou forget us for ever, \add and\add* forsake
us so long time?\f + \fr 5.20  \ft so…: Heb. for length of days?\f*

Turn thou us unto thee, O \nd LORD\nd*, and we shall be turned;
renew our days as of old.

But thou hast utterly rejected us; thou art very wroth against
us.\f + \fr 5.22  \ft But…: or, For wilt thou utterly reject us?\f*

headers.toc1: The Book of the Prophet Ezekiel
headers.mt1: The Book of the Prophet Ezekiel

verses.text:
Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth \add month\add*,
in the fifth \add day\add* of the month, as I \add was\add* among
the captives by the river of Chebar, \add that\add* the heavens were
opened, and I saw visions of God.\f + \fr 1.1  \ft captives: Heb.
captivity\f*

In the fifth \add day\add* of the month, which \add was\add*
the fifth year of king Jehoiachin’s captivity,

The word of the \nd LORD\nd* came expressly unto Ezekiel the
priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river
Chebar; and the hand of the \nd LORD\nd* was there upon him.\f + \fr 1.3 
\ft Ezekiel: Heb. Jehezkel\f*

And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north,
a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness \add was\add*
about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the
midst of the fire.\f + \fr 1.4  \ft infolding…: Heb. catching itself\f*

Also out of the midst thereof \add came\add* the likeness of
four living creatures. And this \add was\add* their appearance; they
had the likeness of a man.
And every one had four faces, and every one had four wings.

And their feet \add were\add* straight feet; and the sole of their
feet \add was\add* like the sole of a calf’s foot: and they sparkled
like the colour of burnished brass.\f + \fr 1.7  \ft straight…: Heb. a straight
foot\f*

And \add they had\add* the hands of a man under their wings
on their four sides; and they four had their faces and their wings.

Their wings \add were\add* joined one to another; they turned
not when they went; they went every one straight forward.

As for the likeness of their faces, they four had the face
of a man, and the face of a lion, on the right side: and they four
had the face of an ox on the left side; they four also had the face
of an eagle.

Thus \add were\add* their faces: and their wings \add were\add*
stretched upward; two \add wings\add* of every one \add were\add*
joined one to another, and two covered their bodies.\f + \fr 1.11 
\ft stretched…: or, divided above\f*

And they went every one straight forward: whither the spirit
was to go, they went; \add and\add* they turned not when they went.

As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance
\add was\add* like burning coals of fire, \add and\add* like the
appearance of lamps: it went up and down among the living creatures;

holy \add place:\add* but they shall bear their shame, and their
abominations which they have committed.

But I will make them keepers of the charge of the house, for all the
service thereof, and for all that shall be done therein.

But the priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok, that kept
the charge of my sanctuary when the children of Israel went astray
from me, they shall come near to me to minister unto me, and they shall
stand before me to offer unto me the fat and the blood, saith the
Lord \nd GOD\nd*:

They shall enter into my sanctuary, and they shall come near
to my table, to minister unto me, and they shall keep my charge.

And it shall come to pass, \add that\add* when they enter
in at the gates of the inner court, they shall be clothed with linen
garments; and no wool shall come upon them, whiles they minister
in the gates of the inner court, and within.

They shall have linen bonnets upon their heads, and shall have
linen breeches upon their loins; they shall not gird \add themselves\add*
with any thing that causeth sweat.\f + \fr 44.18  \ft with…: or, in sweating places: Heb. in, or, with
sweat\f*

And when they go forth into the utter court, \add even\add*
into the utter court to the people, they shall put off their garments
wherein they ministered, and lay them in the holy chambers, and they shall
put on other garments; and they shall not sanctify the people with their
garments.

Neither shall they shave their heads, nor suffer their locks
to grow long; they shall only poll their heads.

Neither shall any priest drink wine, when they enter into the
inner court.

Neither shall they take for their wives a widow, nor her that is put
away: but they shall take maidens of the seed of the house of Israel,
or a widow that had a priest before.\f + \fr 44.22  \ft put…: Heb. thrust
forth\f*\f + \fr 44.22  \ft that had…: Heb. from a priest\f*

And they shall teach my people \add the difference\add* between the
holy and profane, and cause them to discern between the unclean and the
clean.

And in controversy they shall stand in judgment; \add and\add*
they shall judge it according to my judgments: and they shall keep
my laws and my statutes in all mine assemblies; and they shall hallow
my sabbaths.

And they shall come at no dead person to defile themselves: but for
father, or for mother, or for son, or for daughter, for brother,
or for sister that hath had no husband, they may defile themselves.

And after he is cleansed, they shall reckon unto him seven
days.

And in the day that he goeth into the sanctuary, unto the
inner court, to minister in the sanctuary, he shall offer his sin
offering, saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*.

And it shall be unto them for an inheritance: I \add am\add*
their inheritance: and ye shall give them no possession in Israel: I
\add am\add* their possession.

They shall eat the meat offering, and the sin offering, and the trespass
offering; and every dedicated thing in Israel shall be theirs.\f + \fr 44.29 
\ft dedicated: or, devoted\f*

And the first of all the firstfruits of all \add things\add*,
and every oblation of all, of every \add sort\add* of your oblations,
shall be the priest’s: ye shall also give unto the priest the first
of your dough, that he may cause the blessing to rest in thine house.\f + \fr 44.30 
\ft And the first: or, And the chief\f*

The priests shall not eat of any thing that is dead of itself,
or torn, whether it be fowl or beast.

Moreover, when ye shall divide by lot the land for inheritance,
ye shall offer an oblation unto the \nd LORD\nd*, an holy portion
of the land: the length \add shall be\add* the length of five and
twenty thousand \add reeds\add*, and the breadth \add shall be\add*
ten thousand. This \add shall be\add* holy in all the borders thereof round
about.\f + \fr 45.1  \ft when…: Heb. when ye cause the land to fall\f*\f + \fr 45.1 
\ft an holy…: Heb. holiness\f*

Of this there shall be for the sanctuary five hundred \add in
length\add*, with five hundred \add in breadth\add*, square round
about; and fifty cubits round about for the suburbs thereof.\f + \fr 45.2 
\ft suburbs: or, void places\f*

And of this measure shalt thou measure the length of five and
twenty thousand, and the breadth of ten thousand: and in it shall be the
sanctuary \add and\add* the most holy \add place\add*.

The holy \add portion\add* of the land shall be for the priests
the ministers of the sanctuary, which shall come near to minister
unto the \nd LORD\nd*: and it shall be a place for their houses,
and an holy place for the sanctuary.

And the five and twenty thousand of length, and the ten thousand
of breadth, shall also the Levites, the ministers of the house, have for themselves, for a
possession for twenty chambers.

And ye shall appoint the possession of the city five thousand
broad, and five and twenty thousand long, over against the oblation
of the holy \add portion:\add* it shall be for the whole house of
Israel.

And a \add portion shall be\add* for the prince on the one side and on the other side of the
oblation of the holy \add portion\add*, and of the possession of the
city, before the oblation of the holy \add portion\add*, and before
the possession of the city, from the west side westward, and from the
east side eastward: and the length \add shall be\add* over against
one of the portions, from the west border unto the east border.

In the land shall be his possession in Israel: and my princes
shall no more oppress my people; and \add the rest of\add* the land
shall they give to the house of Israel according to their tribes.

Thus saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*; Let it suffice you, O princes
of Israel: remove violence and spoil, and execute judgment and justice,
take away your exactions from my people, saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*.\f + \fr 45.9 
\ft exactions: Heb. expulsions\f*

Ye shall have just balances, and a just ephah, and a just
bath.

The ephah and the bath shall be of one measure, that the bath
may contain the tenth part of an homer, and the ephah the tenth part
of an homer: the measure thereof shall be after the homer.

And the shekel \add shall be\add* twenty gerahs: twenty shekels,
five and twenty shekels, fifteen shekels, shall be your maneh.

This \add is\add* the oblation that ye shall offer; the sixth
part of an ephah of an homer of wheat, and ye shall give the sixth
part of an ephah of an homer of barley:

Concerning the ordinance of oil, the bath of oil, \add ye shall
offer\add* the tenth part of a bath out of the cor, \add which is\add*
an homer of ten baths; for ten baths \add are\add* an homer:

And one lamb out of the flock, out of two hundred, out of the fat
pastures of Israel; for a meat offering, and for a burnt offering,
and for peace offerings, to make reconciliation for them, saith the
Lord \nd GOD\nd*.\f + \fr 45.15  \ft lamb: or, kid\f*\f + \fr 45.15 
\ft peace…: or, thank offerings\f*

All the people of the land shall give this oblation for the
prince in Israel.\f + \fr 45.16  \ft shall…: Heb. shall be for\f*\f + \fr 45.16 
\ft for: or, with\f*

And it shall be the prince’s part \add to give\add* burnt
offerings, and meat offerings, and drink offerings, in the feasts,
and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths, in all solemnities of the
house of Israel: he shall prepare the sin offering, and the meat
offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make
reconciliation for the house of Israel.\f + \fr 45.17  \ft peace…: or, thank
offerings\f*

Thus saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*; In the first \add month\add*,
in the first \add day\add* of the month, thou shalt take a young
bullock without blemish, and cleanse the sanctuary:

And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering,
and put \add it\add* upon the posts of the house, and upon the four
corners of the settle of the altar, and upon the posts of the gate
of the inner court.

In the first \add month\add*, in the fourteenth day of the
month, ye shall have the passover, a feast of seven days; unleavened
bread shall be eaten.

And upon that day shall the prince prepare for himself and for all the
people of the land a bullock \add for\add* a sin offering.

And seven days of the feast he shall prepare a burnt offering
to the \nd LORD\nd*, seven bullocks and seven rams without blemish
daily the seven days; and a kid of the goats daily \add for\add*
a sin offering.

And he shall prepare a meat offering of an ephah for a bullock,
and an ephah for a ram, and an hin of oil for an ephah.

In the seventh \add month\add*, in the fifteenth day of the
month, shall he do the like in the feast of the seven days, according to the sin
offering, according to the burnt offering, and according to the meat
offering, and according to the oil.

Thus saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*; The gate of the inner court
that looketh toward the east shall be shut the six working days;
but on the sabbath it shall be opened, and in the day of the new
moon it shall be opened.

And the prince shall enter by the way of the porch of \add that\add*
gate without, and shall stand by the post of the gate, and the priests
shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he shall
worship at the threshold of the gate: then he shall go forth; but the
gate shall not be shut until the evening.

Likewise the people of the land shall worship at the door of this
gate before the \nd LORD\nd* in the sabbaths and in the new moons.

And the burnt offering that the prince shall offer unto the
\nd LORD\nd* in the sabbath day \add shall be\add* six lambs without
blemish, and a ram without blemish.

And the meat offering \add shall be\add* an ephah for a ram,
and the meat offering for the lambs as he shall be able to give,
and an hin of oil to an ephah.\f + \fr 46.5  \ft as he…: Heb. the gift of his
hand\f*

And in the day of the new moon \add it shall be\add* a young
bullock without blemish, and six lambs, and a ram: they shall be without
blemish.

And he shall prepare a meat offering, an ephah for a bullock,
and an ephah for a ram, and for the lambs according as his hand shall
attain unto, and an hin of oil to an ephah.

And when the prince shall enter, he shall go in by the way
of the porch of \add that\add* gate, and he shall go forth by the
way thereof.

But when the people of the land shall come before the \nd LORD\nd*
in the solemn feasts, he that entereth in by the way of the north
gate to worship shall go out by the way of the south gate; and he that
entereth by the way of the south gate shall go forth by the way of the
north gate: he shall not return by the way of the gate whereby he came
in, but shall go forth over against it.

And the prince in the midst of them, when they go in, shall go
in; and when they go forth, shall go forth.

And in the feasts and in the solemnities the meat offering
shall be an ephah to a bullock, and an ephah to a ram, and to the
lambs as he is able to give, and an hin of oil to an ephah.

Now when the prince shall prepare a voluntary burnt offering
or peace offerings voluntarily unto the \nd LORD\nd*, \add one\add*
shall then open him the gate that looketh toward the east, and he shall
prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings, as he did on the
sabbath day: then he shall go forth; and after his going forth \add one\add*
shall shut the gate.

Thou shalt daily prepare a burnt offering unto the \nd LORD\nd*
\add of\add* a lamb of the first year without blemish: thou shalt
prepare it every morning.\f + \fr 46.13  \ft of the…: Heb. a son of his
year\f*\f + \fr 46.13  \ft every…: Heb. morning by morning\f*

And thou shalt prepare a meat offering for it every morning,
the sixth part of an ephah, and the third part of an hin of oil,
to temper with the fine flour; a meat offering continually by a perpetual
ordinance unto the \nd LORD\nd*.

Thus shall they prepare the lamb, and the meat offering, and the
oil, every morning \add for\add* a continual burnt offering.

Thus saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*; If the prince give a gift
unto any of his sons, the inheritance thereof shall be his sons’; it
\add shall be\add* their possession by inheritance.

But if he give a gift of his inheritance to one of his servants,
then it shall be his to the year of liberty; after it shall return
to the prince: but his inheritance shall be his sons’ for them.

Moreover the prince shall not take of the people’s inheritance
by oppression, to thrust them out of their possession; \add but\add*
he shall give his sons inheritance out of his own possession: that my
people be not scattered every man from his possession.

After he brought me through the entry, which \add was\add*
at the side of the gate, into the holy chambers of the priests, which
looked toward the north: and, behold, there \add was\add* a place
on the two sides westward.

Then said he unto me, This \add is\add* the place where the
priests shall boil the trespass offering and the sin offering, where they shall
bake the meat offering; that they bear \add them\add* not out into the
utter court, to sanctify the people.

Then he brought me forth into the utter court, and caused me to pass
by the four corners of the court; and, behold, in every corner of the
court \add there was\add* a court.\f + \fr 46.21  \ft in every…: Heb. a court in a corner of a court, and a court in a corner
of a court\f*

In the four corners of the court \add there were\add* courts
joined of forty \add cubits\add* long and thirty broad: these four
corners \add were\add* of one measure.\f + \fr 46.22  \ft joined: or, made with
chimneys\f*\f + \fr 46.22  \ft corners were…: Heb. cornered, etc\f*

And \add there was\add* a row \add of building\add* round about
in them, round about them four, and \add it was\add* made with boiling
places under the rows round about.

Then said he unto me, These \add are\add* the places of them that
boil, where the ministers of the house shall boil the sacrifice of the
people.

Afterward he brought me again unto the door of the house; and, behold,
waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward:
for the forefront of the house \add stood toward\add* the east, and the
waters came down from under from the right side of the house, at the
south \add side\add* of the altar.

Then brought he me out of the way of the gate northward, and led me
about the way without unto the utter gate by the way that looketh
eastward; and, behold, there ran out waters on the right side.

And when the man that had the line in his hand went forth eastward,
he measured a thousand cubits, and he brought me through the waters;
the waters \add were\add* to the ankles.\f + \fr 47.3  \ft the waters were…: Heb. waters of the
ankles\f*

Afterward he measured a thousand; \add and it was\add* a river
that I could not pass over: for the waters were risen, waters to swim
in, a river that could not be passed over.\f + \fr 47.5  \ft waters to…: Heb. waters of
swimming\f*

And he said unto me, Son of man, hast thou seen \add this\add*?
Then he brought me, and caused me to return to the brink of the river.

Now when I had returned, behold, at the bank of the river \add were\add*
very many trees on the one side and on the other.\f + \fr 47.7  \ft bank: Heb.
lip\f*

Then said he unto me, These waters issue out toward the east
country, and go down into the desert, and go into the sea: \add which
being\add* brought forth into the sea, the waters shall be healed.\f + \fr 47.8 
\ft desert: or, plain\f*

And it shall come to pass, \add that\add* every thing that liveth,
which moveth, whithersoever the rivers shall come, shall live: and there shall be a
very great multitude of fish, because these waters shall come thither: for they shall be
healed; and every thing shall live whither the river cometh.\f + \fr 47.9 
\ft rivers: Heb. two rivers\f*

And it shall come to pass, \add that\add* the fishers shall
stand upon it from En-gedi even unto En-eglaim; they shall be a \add place\add*
to spread forth nets; their fish shall be according to their kinds,
as the fish of the great sea, exceeding many.

But the miry places thereof and the marishes thereof shall not be
healed; they shall be given to salt.\f + \fr 47.11  \ft shall not…: or, and that which shall not be
healed\f*

And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall
grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the
fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his
months, because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the
fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine.\f + \fr 47.12 
\ft shall grow: Heb. shall come up\f*\f + \fr 47.12  \ft new: or,
principal\f*\f + \fr 47.12  \ft for medicine: or, for bruises and
sores\f*

Thus saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*; This \add shall be\add*
the border, whereby ye shall inherit the land according to the twelve
tribes of Israel: Joseph \add shall have two\add* portions.

And ye shall inherit it, one as well as another: \add concerning\add*
the which I lifted up mine hand to give it unto your fathers: and this
land shall fall unto you for inheritance.\f + \fr 47.14  \ft lifted…: or,
swore\f*

Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which \add is\add* between the
border of Damascus and the border of Hamath; Hazar-hatticon, which
\add is\add* by the coast of Hauran.\f + \fr 47.16  \ft Hazar-hatticon: or, the middle
village\f*

And the border from the sea shall be Hazar-enan, the border
of Damascus, and the north northward, and the border of Hamath. And
\add this is\add* the north side.

And the east side ye shall measure from Hauran, and from Damascus,
and from Gilead, and from the land of Israel \add by\add* Jordan,
from the border unto the east sea. And \add this is\add* the east
side.\f + \fr 47.18  \ft from (Hauran, Damascus, Gilead, the land): Heb. from
between\f*

And the south side southward, from Tamar \add even\add* to the
waters of strife \add in\add* Kadesh, the river to the great sea. And
\add this is\add* the south side southward.\f + \fr 47.19  \ft strife: or,
Meribah\f*\f + \fr 47.19  \ft river: or, valley\f*\f + \fr 47.19 
\ft is the south side southward: or, is the south side toward Teman\f*

The west side also \add shall be\add* the great sea from the
border, till a man come over against Hamath. This \add is\add* the
west side.

So shall ye divide this land unto you according to the tribes
of Israel.

And it shall come to pass, \add that\add* ye shall divide
it by lot for an inheritance unto you, and to the strangers that
sojourn among you, which shall beget children among you: and they shall be unto you as
born in the country among the children of Israel; they shall have
inheritance with you among the tribes of Israel.

And it shall come to pass, \add that\add* in what tribe the
stranger sojourneth, there shall ye give \add him\add* his inheritance,
saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*.

Now these \add are\add* the names of the tribes. From the north
end to the coast of the way of Hethlon, as one goeth to Hamath, Hazar-enan,
the border of Damascus northward, to the coast of Hamath; for these are his
sides east \add and\add* west; a \add portion for\add* Dan.\f + \fr 48.1 
\ft a portion: Heb. one portion\f*

And by the border of Dan, from the east side unto the west
side, a \add portion for\add* Asher.

And by the border of Asher, from the east side even unto the
west side, a \add portion for\add* Naphtali.

And by the border of Naphtali, from the east side unto the
west side, a \add portion for\add* Manasseh.

And by the border of Manasseh, from the east side unto the
west side, a \add portion for\add* Ephraim.

And by the border of Ephraim, from the east side even unto the
west side, a \add portion for\add* Reuben.

And by the border of Reuben, from the east side unto the west
side, a \add portion for\add* Judah.

And by the border of Judah, from the east side unto the west
side, shall be the offering which ye shall offer of five and twenty
thousand \add reeds in\add* breadth, and \add in\add* length as one of the
\add other\add* parts, from the east side unto the west side: and the
sanctuary shall be in the midst of it.

The oblation that ye shall offer unto the \nd LORD\nd* \add shall
be\add* of five and twenty thousand in length, and of ten thousand
in breadth.

And for them, \add even\add* for the priests, shall be \add this\add*
holy oblation; toward the north five and twenty thousand \add in
length\add*, and toward the west ten thousand in breadth, and toward the
east ten thousand in breadth, and toward the south five and twenty
thousand in length: and the sanctuary of the \nd LORD\nd* shall be in the
midst thereof.

\add It shall be\add* for the priests that are sanctified
of the sons of Zadok; which have kept my charge, which went not astray
when the children of Israel went astray, as the Levites went astray.\f + \fr 48.11 
\ft It…: or, The sanctified portion shall be for the priests\f*\f + \fr 48.11 
\ft charge: or, ward, or, ordinance\f*

And \add this\add* oblation of the land that is offered shall be unto them a thing
most holy by the border of the Levites.

And over against the border of the priests the Levites \add shall
have\add* five and twenty thousand in length, and ten thousand in
breadth: all the length \add shall be\add* five and twenty thousand,
and the breadth ten thousand.

And they shall not sell of it, neither exchange, nor alienate
the firstfruits of the land: for \add it is\add* holy unto the \nd LORD\nd*.

And the five thousand, that are left in the breadth over
against the five and twenty thousand, shall be a profane \add place\add*
for the city, for dwelling, and for suburbs: and the city shall be in the
midst thereof.

And these \add shall be\add* the measures thereof; the north
side four thousand and five hundred, and the south side four thousand
and five hundred, and on the east side four thousand and five hundred,
and the west side four thousand and five hundred.

And the suburbs of the city shall be toward the north two
hundred and fifty, and toward the south two hundred and fifty, and toward the
east two hundred and fifty, and toward the west two hundred and fifty.

And the residue in length over against the oblation of the
holy \add portion shall be\add* ten thousand eastward, and ten thousand
westward: and it shall be over against the oblation of the holy \add portion;\add*
and the increase thereof shall be for food unto them that serve the
city.

And they that serve the city shall serve it out of all the
tribes of Israel.

All the oblation \add shall be\add* five and twenty thousand
by five and twenty thousand: ye shall offer the holy oblation foursquare,
with the possession of the city.

And the residue \add shall be\add* for the prince, on the one side and on the other of the
holy oblation, and of the possession of the city, over against the
five and twenty thousand of the oblation toward the east border,
and westward over against the five and twenty thousand toward the
west border, over against the portions for the prince: and it shall be the
holy oblation; and the sanctuary of the house \add shall be\add*
in the midst thereof.

Moreover from the possession of the Levites, and from the
possession of the city, \add being\add* in the midst \add of that\add*
which is the prince’s, between the border of Judah and the border
of Benjamin, shall be for the prince.

As for the rest of the tribes, from the east side unto the
west side, Benjamin \add shall have\add* a \add portion\add*.\f + \fr 48.23 
\ft a portion: Heb. one portion\f*

And by the border of Benjamin, from the east side unto the
west side, Simeon \add shall have\add* a \add portion\add*.

And by the border of Simeon, from the east side unto the west
side, Issachar a \add portion\add*.

And by the border of Issachar, from the east side unto the
west side, Zebulun a \add portion\add*.

And by the border of Zebulun, from the east side unto the
west side, Gad a \add portion\add*.

And by the border of Gad, at the south side southward, the
border shall be even from Tamar \add unto\add* the waters of strife
\add in\add* Kadesh, \add and\add* to the river toward the great
sea.\f + \fr 48.28  \ft strife…: or, Meribah-kadesh\f*

This \add is\add* the land which ye shall divide by lot unto the
tribes of Israel for inheritance, and these \add are\add* their portions,
saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*.

And these \add are\add* the goings out of the city on the
north side, four thousand and five hundred measures.

And the gates of the city \add shall be\add* after the names
of the tribes of Israel: three gates northward; one gate of Reuben,
one gate of Judah, one gate of Levi.

And at the east side four thousand and five hundred: and three
gates; and one gate of Joseph, one gate of Benjamin, one gate of
Dan.

And at the south side four thousand and five hundred measures:
and three gates; one gate of Simeon, one gate of Issachar, one gate
of Zebulun.

At the west side four thousand and five hundred, \add with\add*
their three gates; one gate of Gad, one gate of Asher, one gate of
Naphtali.

\add It was\add* round about eighteen thousand \add measures:\add*
and the name of the city from \add that\add* day \add shall be\add*, The
\nd LORD\nd* \add is\add* there.\f + \fr 48.35  \ft The \+nd LORD\+nd*…: Heb.
Jehovah-shammah\f*

headers.toc1: The Book of Daniel
headers.mt1: The Book of Daniel

verses.text:
In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah came
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon unto Jerusalem, and besieged it.

And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, with
part of the vessels of the house of God: which he carried into the
land of Shinar to the house of his god; and he brought the vessels
into the treasure house of his god.

Children in whom \add was\add* no blemish, but well favoured,
and skilful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding
science, and such as \add had\add* ability in them to stand in the
king’s palace, and whom they might teach the learning and the tongue
of the Chaldeans.

And the king appointed them a daily provision of the king’s
meat, and of the wine which he drank: so nourishing them three years,
that at the end thereof they might stand before the king.\f + \fr 1.5 
\ft the wine…: Heb. the wine of his drink\f*

Now among these were of the children of Judah, Daniel, Hananiah,
Mishael, and Azariah:

Unto whom the prince of the eunuchs gave names: for he gave
unto Daniel \add the name\add* of Belteshazzar; and to Hananiah,
of Shadrach; and to Mishael, of Meshach; and to Azariah, of Abed-nego.

But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile
himself with the portion of the king’s meat, nor with the wine which he
drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not
defile himself.

Now God had brought Daniel into favour and tender love with
the prince of the eunuchs.

And the prince of the eunuchs said unto Daniel, I fear my
lord the king, who hath appointed your meat and your drink: for why should he
see your faces worse liking than the children which \add are\add*
of your sort? then shall ye make \add me\add* endanger my head to the
king.\f + \fr 1.10  \ft worse…: Heb. sadder\f*\f + \fr 1.10  \ft sort: or, term, or,
continuance?\f*

Then said Daniel to Melzar, whom the prince of the eunuchs

Then let our countenances be looked upon before thee, and the
