meat: and as thou seest, deal with thy servants.

So he consented to them in this matter, and proved them ten
days.

And at the end of ten days their countenances appeared fairer
and fatter in flesh than all the children which did eat the portion
of the king’s meat.

Thus Melzar took away the portion of their meat, and the wine
that they should drink; and gave them pulse.

As for these four children, God gave them knowledge and skill
in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions
and dreams.\f + \fr 1.17  \ft Daniel…: or, he made Daniel understand\f*

Now at the end of the days that the king had said he should
bring them in, then the prince of the eunuchs brought them in before
Nebuchadnezzar.

And the king communed with them; and among them all was found
none like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah: therefore stood
they before the king.

And in all matters of wisdom \add and\add* understanding,
that the king enquired of them, he found them ten times better than all the
magicians \add and\add* astrologers that \add were\add* in all his
realm.\f + \fr 1.20  \ft wisdom…: Heb. wisdom of understanding\f*

And Daniel continued \add even\add* unto the first year of
king Cyrus.

And in the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar Nebuchadnezzar
dreamed dreams, wherewith his spirit was troubled, and his sleep
brake from him.

Then the king commanded to call the magicians, and the astrologers,
and the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans, for to shew the king his dreams.
So they came and stood before the king.

And the king said unto them, I have dreamed a dream, and my
spirit was troubled to know the dream.

Then spake the Chaldeans to the king in Syriack, O king, live

\ft O king…: (Chaldee, to the end of chapter seven)\f*

The king answered and said to the Chaldeans, The thing is gone

But if ye shew the dream, and the interpretation thereof, ye shall
receive of me gifts and rewards and great honour: therefore shew
me the dream, and the interpretation thereof.\f + \fr 2.6  \ft rewards: or,
fee\f*

They answered again and said, Let the king tell his servants
the dream, and we will shew the interpretation of it.

The king answered and said, I know of certainty that ye would
gain the time, because ye see the thing is gone from me.\f + \fr 2.8 
\ft gain: Chaldee, buy\f*

But if ye will not make known unto me the dream, \add there is
but\add* one decree for you: for ye have prepared lying and corrupt

The Chaldeans answered before the king, and said, There is
not a man upon the earth that can shew the king’s matter: therefore
\add there is\add* no king, lord, nor ruler, \add that\add* asked

And \add it is\add* a rare thing that the king requireth, and there

For this cause the king was angry and very furious, and commanded

And the decree went forth that the wise \add men\add* should be
slain; and they sought Daniel and his fellows to be slain.

Then Daniel answered with counsel and wisdom to Arioch the
captain of the king’s guard, which was gone forth to slay the wise
\add men\add* of Babylon:\f + \fr 2.14  \ft answered…: Chaldee, returned\f*\f + \fr 2.14 
\ft captain…: or, chief marshal: Chaldee, chief of the executioners, or,
slaughtermen\f*

He answered and said to Arioch the king’s captain, Why \add is\add*
the decree \add so\add* hasty from the king? Then Arioch made the

Then Daniel went in, and desired of the king that he would
give him time, and that he would shew the king the interpretation.

Then Daniel went to his house, and made the thing known to
Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions:

That they would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning
this secret; that Daniel and his fellows should not perish with the
rest of the wise \add men\add* of Babylon.\f + \fr 2.18  \ft of the God: Chaldee, from before
God\f*\f + \fr 2.18  \ft that Daniel…: or, that they should not destroy Daniel,
etc\f*

Then was the secret revealed unto Daniel in a night vision.
Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.

Daniel answered and said, Blessed be the name of God for ever
and ever: for wisdom and might are his:

And he changeth the times and the seasons: he removeth kings,
and setteth up kings: he giveth wisdom unto the wise, and knowledge
to them that know understanding:

He revealeth the deep and secret things: he knoweth what \add is\add*

I thank thee, and praise thee, O thou God of my fathers, who hast
given me wisdom and might, and hast made known unto me now what we

Therefore Daniel went in unto Arioch, whom the king had ordained

Then Arioch brought in Daniel before the king in haste, and
said thus unto him, I have found a man of the captives of Judah,

\ft I have…: Chaldee, That I have found\f*\f + \fr 2.25  \ft captives…: Chaldee, children of the captivity of
Judah\f*

The king answered and said to Daniel, whose name \add was\add*
Belteshazzar, Art thou able to make known unto me the dream which I have
seen, and the interpretation thereof?

But there is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets, and maketh
known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days.
Thy dream, and the visions of thy head upon thy bed, are these;\f + \fr 2.28 
\ft maketh…: Chaldee, hath made known\f*

As for thee, O king, thy thoughts came \add into thy mind\add*
upon thy bed, what should come to pass hereafter: and he that revealeth

\ft came: Chaldee, came up\f*

But as for me, this secret is not revealed to me for \add any\add*

the king\f*

Thou, O king, sawest, and behold a great image. This great

This image’s head \add was\add* of fine gold, his breast and his

\ft thighs: or, sides\f*
His legs of iron, his feet part of iron and part of clay.

Thou sawest till that a stone was cut out without hands, which

Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the

This \add is\add* the dream; and we will tell the interpretation

Thou, O king, \add art\add* a king of kings: for the God of

And wheresoever the children of men dwell, the beasts of the

of gold.

And after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee,
and another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all

And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron: forasmuch as
iron breaketh in pieces and subdueth all \add things:\add* and as
iron that breaketh all these, shall it break in pieces and bruise.

And whereas thou sawest the feet and toes, part of potters’
clay, and part of iron, the kingdom shall be divided; but there shall
be in it of the strength of the iron, forasmuch as thou sawest the

And \add as\add* the toes of the feet \add were\add* part of
iron, and part of clay, \add so\add* the kingdom shall be partly
strong, and partly broken.\f + \fr 2.42  \ft broken: or, brittle\f*

And whereas thou sawest iron mixed with miry clay, they shall mingle

this\f*

And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set

\ft the days: Chaldee, their days\f*\f + \fr 2.44  \ft the kingdom: Chaldee, the kingdom
thereof\f*

Forasmuch as thou sawest that the stone was cut out of the

\add is\add* certain, and the interpretation thereof sure.\f + \fr 2.45 
\ft without…: or, which was not in hands\f*\f + \fr 2.45  \ft hereafter: Chaldee, after
this\f*

Then the king Nebuchadnezzar fell upon his face, and worshipped

The king answered unto Daniel, and said, Of a truth \add it

Then the king made Daniel a great man, and gave him many great

Then Daniel requested of the king, and he set Shadrach, Meshach,

\add sat\add* in the gate of the king.

Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height
\add was\add* threescore cubits, \add and\add* the breadth thereof

Then Nebuchadnezzar the king sent to gather together the princes,
the governors, and the captains, the judges, the treasurers, the

Then the princes, the governors, and captains, the judges,
the treasurers, the counsellors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers

image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up; and they stood before
the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

Then an herald cried aloud, To you it is commanded, O people,
nations, and languages,\f + \fr 3.4  \ft aloud: Chaldee, with might\f*\f + \fr 3.4 
\ft it…: Chaldee, they command\f*

\add That\add* at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet,

symphony\f*

And whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall the same hour

Therefore at that time, when all the people heard the sound
of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and all kinds of musick,
all the people, the nations, and the languages, fell down \add and\add*

Wherefore at that time certain Chaldeans came near, and accused

They spake and said to the king Nebuchadnezzar, O king, live
for ever.

Thou, O king, hast made a decree, that every man that shall

dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, shall fall down and worship the
golden image:\f + \fr 3.10  \ft dulcimer: or, singing: Chaldee, symphony\f*

And whoso falleth not down and worshippeth, \add that\add*
he should be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.

There are certain Jews whom thou hast set over the affairs

worship the golden image which thou hast set up.\f + \fr 3.12  \ft have…: Chaldee, have set no regard upon
thee\f*

Then Nebuchadnezzar in \add his\add* rage and fury commanded
to bring Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego. Then they brought these
men before the king.

Nebuchadnezzar spake and said unto them, \add Is it\add* true,
O Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, do not ye serve my gods, nor
worship the golden image which I have set up?\f + \fr 3.14  \ft true: or, of
purpose\f*

Now if ye be ready that at what time ye hear the sound of the

of musick, ye fall down and worship the image which I have made;
\add well:\add* but if ye worship not, ye shall be cast the same
hour into the midst of a burning fiery furnace; and who \add is\add*
that God that shall deliver you out of my hands?\f + \fr 3.15  \ft dulcimer: or, singing: Chaldee,
symphony\f*

Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, answered and said to the

If it be \add so\add*, our God whom we serve is able to deliver
us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver \add us\add*
out of thine hand, O king.

But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not
serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set
up.

Then was Nebuchadnezzar full of fury, and the form of his

filled\f*

And he commanded the most mighty men that \add were\add* in his

mantles\f*\f + \fr 3.21  \ft hats: or, turbans\f*

Therefore because the king’s commandment was urgent, and the

word\f*\f + \fr 3.22  \ft flame: or, spark\f*

And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, fell
down bound into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.

Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonied, and rose up in
haste, \add and\add* spake, and said unto his counsellors, Did not
we cast three men bound into the midst of the fire? They answered
and said unto the king, True, O king.\f + \fr 3.24  \ft counsellors: or,
governors\f*

He answered and said, Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the
midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth
is like the Son of God.\f + \fr 3.25  \ft they…: Chaldee, there is no hurt in
them\f*

Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the mouth of the burning
fiery furnace, \add and\add* spake, and said, Shadrach, Meshach,
and Abed-nego, ye servants of the most high God, come forth, and
come \add hither\add*. Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, came
forth of the midst of the fire.\f + \fr 3.26  \ft mouth: Chaldee,
door\f*

And the princes, governors, and captains, and the king’s counsellors,
being gathered together, saw these men, upon whose bodies the fire
had no power, nor was an hair of their head singed, neither were their
coats changed, nor the smell of fire had passed on them.

\add Then\add* Nebuchadnezzar spake, and said, Blessed \add be\add*
the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, who hath sent his angel,
and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed
the king’s word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve
nor worship any god, except their own God.

Therefore I make a decree, That every people, nation, and
language, which speak any thing amiss against the God of Shadrach,
Meshach, and Abed-nego, shall be cut in pieces, and their houses
shall be made a dunghill: because there is no other God that can

me\f*\f + \fr 3.29  \ft any…: Chaldee, error\f*\f + \fr 3.29  \ft cut…: Chaldee, made
pieces\f*

Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, in the
province of Babylon.\f + \fr 3.30  \ft promoted: Chaldee, made to
prosper\f*

Nebuchadnezzar the king, unto all people, nations, and languages,
that dwell in all the earth; Peace be multiplied unto you.

I thought it good to shew the signs and wonders that the high
God hath wrought toward me.\f + \fr 4.2  \ft I thought…: Chaldee, It was seemly before
me\f*

How great \add are\add* his signs! and how mighty \add are\add*
his wonders! his kingdom \add is\add* an everlasting kingdom, and his
dominion \add is\add* from generation to generation.

I Nebuchadnezzar was at rest in mine house, and flourishing
in my palace:

I saw a dream which made me afraid, and the thoughts upon my
bed and the visions of my head troubled me.

Therefore made I a decree to bring in all the wise \add men\add*
of Babylon before me, that they might make known unto me the interpretation
of the dream.

Then came in the magicians, the astrologers, the Chaldeans,
and the soothsayers: and I told the dream before them; but they did
not make known unto me the interpretation thereof.

But at the last Daniel came in before me, whose name \add was\add*
Belteshazzar, according to the name of my god, and in whom \add is\add*
the spirit of the holy gods: and before him I told the dream, \add saying\add*,

O Belteshazzar, master of the magicians, because I know that the
spirit of the holy gods \add is\add* in thee, and no secret troubleth
thee, tell me the visions of my dream that I have seen, and the interpretation thereof.

Thus \add were\add* the visions of mine head in my bed; I saw,
and behold a tree in the midst of the earth, and the height thereof
\add was\add* great.\f + \fr 4.10  \ft I saw: Chaldee, I was seeing\f*

The tree grew, and was strong, and the height thereof reached
unto heaven, and the sight thereof to the end of all the earth:

The leaves thereof \add were\add* fair, and the fruit thereof
much, and in it \add was\add* meat for all: the beasts of the field
had shadow under it, and the fowls of the heaven dwelt in the boughs

I saw in the visions of my head upon my bed, and, behold,
a watcher and an holy one came down from heaven;

He cried aloud, and said thus, Hew down the tree, and cut

\ft aloud: Chaldee, with might\f*

Nevertheless leave the stump of his roots in the earth, even with a

with the beasts in the grass of the earth:

Let his heart be changed from man’s, and let a beast’s heart
be given unto him; and let seven times pass over him.

This matter \add is\add* by the decree of the watchers, and the

may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth
it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men.

This dream I king Nebuchadnezzar have seen. Now thou, O Belteshazzar,
declare the interpretation thereof, forasmuch as all the wise \add men\add*
of my kingdom are not able to make known unto me the interpretation:
but thou \add art\add* able; for the spirit of the holy gods \add is\add* in thee.

Then Daniel, whose name \add was\add* Belteshazzar, was astonied

said, Belteshazzar, let not the dream, or the interpretation thereof,

Whose leaves \add were\add* fair, and the fruit thereof much, and in it
\add was\add* meat for all; under which the beasts of the field dwelt,
and upon whose branches the fowls of the heaven had their habitation:

It \add is\add* thou, O king, that art grown and become strong:

This \add is\add* the interpretation, O king, and this \add is\add*
the decree of the most High, which is come upon my lord the king:

That they shall drive thee from men, and thy dwelling shall
be with the beasts of the field, and they shall make thee to eat

And whereas they commanded to leave the stump of the tree

Wherefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable unto thee,

All this came upon the king Nebuchadnezzar.

At the end of twelve months he walked in the palace of the

The king spake, and said, Is not this great Babylon, that

While the word \add was\add* in the king’s mouth, there fell

And they shall drive thee from men, and thy dwelling \add shall

\add feathers\add*, and his nails like birds’ \add claws\add*.

And at the end of the days I Nebuchadnezzar lifted up mine

\add among\add* the inhabitants of the earth: and none can stay his

At the same time my reason returned unto me; and for the glory

Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King

Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his

oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make
\add it\add* desolate, even until the consummation, and that determined
shall be poured upon the desolate.\f + \fr 9.27  \ft the covenant: or, a
covenant\f*\f + \fr 9.27  \ft for the…: or, with the abominable armies\f*\f + \fr 9.27 
\ft the desolate: or, the desolator\f*

In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia a thing was revealed
unto Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and the thing \add was\add*
true, but the time appointed \add was\add* long: and he understood
the thing, and had understanding of the vision.\f + \fr 10.1  \ft long: Heb.
great\f*

In those days I Daniel was mourning three full weeks.\f + \fr 10.2 
\ft full…: Heb. weeks of days\f*

I ate no pleasant bread, neither came flesh nor wine in my
mouth, neither did I anoint myself at all, till three whole weeks
were fulfilled.\f + \fr 10.3  \ft pleasant…: Heb. bread of desires\f*

And in the four and twentieth day of the first month, as I was by the
side of the great river, which \add is\add* Hiddekel;

Then I lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and behold a certain
man clothed in linen, whose loins \add were\add* girded with fine
gold of Uphaz:\f + \fr 10.5  \ft a…: Heb. one man\f*

His body also \add was\add* like the beryl, and his face as the
appearance of lightning, and his eyes as lamps of fire, and his arms
and his feet like in colour to polished brass, and the voice of his
words like the voice of a multitude.

And I Daniel alone saw the vision: for the men that were with me
saw not the vision; but a great quaking fell upon them, so that they
fled to hide themselves.

Therefore I was left alone, and saw this great vision, and there
remained no strength in me: for my comeliness was turned in me into
corruption, and I retained no strength.\f + \fr 10.8  \ft comeliness: or,
vigour\f*

Yet heard I the voice of his words: and when I heard the voice
of his words, then was I in a deep sleep on my face, and my face
toward the ground.

And, behold, an hand touched  me, which set me upon my knees and
\add upon\add* the palms of my hands.\f + \fr 10.10  \ft set: Heb.
moved\f*

And he said unto me, O Daniel, a man greatly beloved, understand
the words that I speak unto thee, and stand upright: for unto thee am I now
sent. And when he had spoken this word unto me, I stood trembling.\f + \fr 10.11 
\ft greatly…: Heb. of desires\f*\f + \fr 10.11  \ft upright: Heb. upon thy
standing\f*

Then said he unto me, Fear not, Daniel: for from the first
day that thou didst set thine heart to understand, and to chasten
thyself before thy God, thy words were heard, and I am come for thy
words.

But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood  me one
and twenty days: but, lo, Michael, one of the chief princes, came
to help me; and I remained there with the kings of Persia.\f + \fr 10.13 
\ft chief: or, first\f*

Now I am come to make thee understand what shall befall thy
people in the latter days: for yet the vision \add is\add* for \add many\add*
days.

And when he had spoken such words unto me, I set my face toward the
ground, and I became dumb.

And, behold, \add one\add* like the similitude of the sons
of men touched my lips: then I opened my mouth, and spake, and said
unto him that stood before me, O my lord, by the vision my sorrows
are turned upon me, and I have retained no strength.

For how can the servant of this my lord talk with this my
lord? for as for me, straightway there remained no strength in me, neither is there
breath left in me.\f + \fr 10.17  \ft the…: or, this servant of my
lord\f*

Then there came again and touched me \add one\add* like the
appearance of a man, and he strengthened me,

And said, O man greatly beloved, fear not: peace \add be\add*
unto thee, be strong, yea, be strong. And when he had spoken unto me, I was
strengthened, and said, Let my lord speak; for thou hast strengthened me.

But I will shew thee that which is noted in the scripture
of truth: and \add there is\add* none that holdeth with me in these things, but
Michael your prince.\f + \fr 10.21  \ft holdeth: Heb. strengtheneth
himself\f*

Also I in the first year of Darius the Mede, \add even\add*
I, stood to confirm and to strengthen him.

And now will I shew thee the truth. Behold, there shall stand
up yet three kings in Persia; and the fourth shall be far richer than
\add they\add* all: and by his strength through his riches he shall stir
up all against the realm of Grecia.

And a mighty king shall stand up, that shall rule with great
dominion, and do according to his will.

And when he shall stand up, his kingdom shall be broken, and shall be
divided toward the four winds of heaven; and not to his posterity,
nor according to his dominion which he ruled: for his kingdom shall be plucked
up, even for others beside those.

And in the end of years they shall join themselves together;
for the king’s daughter of the south shall come to the king of the
north to make an agreement: but she shall not retain the power of the
arm; neither shall he stand, nor his arm: but she shall be given
up, and they that brought her, and he that begat her, and he that
strengthened her in \add these\add* times.\f + \fr 11.6  \ft join…: Heb. associate
themselves\f*\f + \fr 11.6  \ft an…: Heb. rights\f*\f + \fr 11.6 
\ft he that begat…: or, whom she brought forth\f*

But out of a branch of her roots shall \add one\add* stand
up in his estate, which shall come with an army, and shall enter
into the fortress of the king of the north, and shall deal against them, and shall
prevail:\f + \fr 11.7  \ft in…: or, in his place, or, office\f*

And shall also carry captives into Egypt their gods, with their
princes, \add and\add* with their precious vessels of silver and of
gold; and he shall continue \add more\add* years than the king of the
north.\f + \fr 11.8  \ft their precious…: Heb. vessels of their desire\f*

So the king of the south shall come into \add his\add* kingdom,
and shall return into his own land.

But his sons shall be stirred up, and shall assemble a multitude
of great forces: and \add one\add* shall certainly come, and overflow,
and pass through: then shall he return, and be stirred up, \add even\add*
to his fortress.\f + \fr 11.10  \ft shall be…: or, shall war\f*\f + \fr 11.10 
\ft return…: or, be stirred up again\f*

And the king of the south shall be moved with choler, and shall come
forth and fight with him, \add even\add* with the king of the north:
and he shall set forth a great multitude; but the multitude shall be
given into his hand.

\add And\add* when he hath taken away the multitude, his heart
shall be lifted up; and he shall cast down \add many\add* ten thousands:
but he shall not be strengthened \add by it\add*.

For the king of the north shall return, and shall set forth
a multitude greater than the former, and shall certainly come after
certain years with a great army and with much riches.\f + \fr 11.13 
\ft after…: Heb. at the end of times, even years\f*

And in those times there shall many stand up against the king
of the south: also the robbers of thy people shall exalt themselves to
establish the vision; but they shall fall.\f + \fr 11.14  \ft the robbers: Heb. the children of
robbers\f*

So the king of the north shall come, and cast up a mount,
and take the most fenced cities: and the arms of the south shall not
withstand, neither his chosen people, neither \add shall there be
any\add* strength to withstand.\f + \fr 11.15  \ft the most…: Heb. the city of
munitions\f*\f + \fr 11.15  \ft his…: Heb. the people of his choices\f*

But he that cometh against him shall do according to his own
will, and none shall stand before him: and he shall stand in the
glorious land, which by his hand shall be consumed.\f + \fr 11.16 
\ft glorious…: or, goodly, etc.: Heb. land of ornament\f*

He shall also set his face to enter with the strength of his whole
kingdom, and upright ones with him; thus shall he do: and he shall
give him the daughter of women, corrupting her: but she shall not
stand \add on his side\add*, neither be for him.\f + \fr 11.17  \ft upright…: or, much uprightness: or, equal
conditions\f*\f + \fr 11.17  \ft corrupting: Heb. to corrupt\f*

After this shall he turn his face unto the isles, and shall
take many: but a prince for his own behalf shall cause the reproach
offered by him to cease; without his own reproach he shall cause
\add it\add* to turn upon him.\f + \fr 11.18  \ft for…: Heb. for
him\f*\f + \fr 11.18  \ft the reproach…: Heb. his reproach\f*

Then he shall turn his face toward the fort of his own land:
but he shall stumble and fall, and not be found.

Then shall stand up in his estate a raiser of taxes \add in\add*
the glory of the kingdom: but within few days he shall be destroyed,
neither in anger, nor in battle.\f + \fr 11.20  \ft estate: or, place\f*\f + \fr 11.20 
\ft a…: Heb. one that causeth an exacter to pass over\f*\f + \fr 11.20 
\ft anger: Heb. angers\f*

And in his estate shall stand up a vile person, to whom they shall not
give the honour of the kingdom: but he shall come in peaceably, and
obtain the kingdom by flatteries.\f + \fr 11.21  \ft estate: or,
place\f*

And with the arms of a flood shall they be overflown from
before him, and shall be broken; yea, also the prince of the covenant.

And after the league \add made\add* with him he shall work
deceitfully: for he shall come up, and shall become strong with a
small people.

He shall enter peaceably even upon the fattest places of the
province; and he shall do \add that\add* which his fathers have not
done, nor his fathers’ fathers; he shall scatter among them the prey,
and spoil, and riches: \add yea\add*, and he shall forecast his devices
against the strong holds, even for a time.\f + \fr 11.24  \ft peaceably…: or, into the peaceable and fat,
etc\f*\f + \fr 11.24  \ft forecast…: Heb. think his thoughts\f*

And he shall stir up his power and his courage against the
king of the south with a great army; and the king of the south shall be stirred
up to battle with a very great and mighty army; but he shall not
stand: for they shall forecast devices against him.

Yea, they that feed of the portion of his meat shall destroy
him, and his army shall overflow: and many shall fall down slain.

And both these kings’ hearts \add shall be\add* to do mischief,
and they shall speak lies at one table; but it shall not prosper:
for yet the end \add shall be\add* at the time appointed.\f + \fr 11.27 
\ft hearts: Heb. their hearts\f*

Then shall he return into his land with great riches; and his
heart \add shall be\add* against the holy covenant; and he shall
do \add exploits\add*, and return to his own land.

At the time appointed he shall return, and come toward the
south; but it shall not be as the former, or as the latter.

For the ships of Chittim shall come against him: therefore he shall be
grieved, and return, and have indignation against the holy covenant:
so shall he do; he shall even return, and have intelligence with them that
forsake the holy covenant.

And arms shall stand on his part, and they shall pollute the
sanctuary of strength, and shall take away the daily \add sacrifice\add*,
and they shall place the abomination that maketh desolate.\f + \fr 11.31 
\ft maketh…: or, astonisheth\f*

And such as do wickedly against the covenant shall he corrupt
by flatteries: but the people that do know their God shall be strong,
and do \add exploits\add*.\f + \fr 11.32  \ft corrupt: or, cause to
dissemble\f*

And they that understand among the people shall instruct many:
yet they shall fall by the sword, and by flame, by captivity, and by
spoil, \add many\add* days.

Now when they shall fall, they shall be holpen with a little
help: but many shall cleave to them with flatteries.

And \add some\add* of them of understanding shall fall, to
try them, and to purge, and to make \add them\add* white, \add even\add*
to the time of the end: because \add it is\add* yet for a time appointed.\f + \fr 11.35 
\ft try them: or, try by them\f*

And the king shall do according to his will; and he shall
exalt himself, and magnify himself above every god, and shall speak
marvellous things against the God of gods, and shall prosper till the
indignation be accomplished: for that that is determined shall be
done.

Neither shall he regard the God of his fathers, nor the desire
of women, nor regard any god: for he shall magnify himself above all.

But in his estate shall he honour the God of forces: and a
god whom his fathers knew not shall he honour with gold, and silver,
and with precious stones, and pleasant things.\f + \fr 11.38  \ft in…: or, as for the Almighty God, in his seat he shall honour
yea, he shall honour a god, whom, etc\f*\f + \fr 11.38  \ft estate: or,
stead\f*\f + \fr 11.38  \ft forces: or, munitions: Heb. Mauzzim, or, God’s
protectors\f*\f + \fr 11.38  \ft pleasant: Heb. things desired\f*

Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god,
whom he shall acknowledge \add and\add* increase with glory: and he shall cause them to
rule over many, and shall divide the land for gain.\f + \fr 11.39 
\ft most…: Heb. fortresses of munitions\f*\f + \fr 11.39  \ft gain: Heb. a
price\f*

And at the time of the end shall the king of the south push
at him: and the king of the north shall come against him like a whirlwind,
with chariots, and with horsemen, and with many ships; and he shall
enter into the countries, and shall overflow and pass over.

He shall enter also into the glorious land, and many \add countries\add*
shall be overthrown: but these shall escape out of his hand, \add even\add*
Edom, and Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon.\f + \fr 11.41 
\ft glorious…: or, goodly, etc.: Heb. land of delight, or, ornament\f*

He shall stretch forth his hand also upon the countries: and the
land of Egypt shall not escape.\f + \fr 11.42  \ft stretch…: Heb. send
forth\f*

But he shall have power over the treasures of gold and of
silver, and over all the precious things of Egypt: and the Libyans
and the Ethiopians \add shall be\add* at his steps.

But tidings out of the east and out of the north shall trouble
him: therefore he shall go forth with great fury to destroy, and utterly to make
away many.

And he shall plant the tabernacles of his palace between the
seas in the glorious holy mountain; yet he shall come to his end,
and none shall help him.\f + \fr 11.45  \ft glorious…: or, goodly, etc.: Heb. mountain of delight of
holiness\f*

And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which
standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time
of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation \add even\add*
to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered,
every one that shall be found written in the book.

And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall
awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame \add and\add*
everlasting contempt.

And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the
firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars
for ever and ever.\f + \fr 12.3  \ft wise: or, teachers\f*

But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, \add even\add*
to the time of the end: many shall run to and fro, and knowledge
shall be increased.

Then I Daniel looked, and, behold, there stood other two,
the one on this side of the bank of the river, and the other on that side of the
bank of the river.\f + \fr 12.5  \ft bank: Heb. lip\f*\f + \fr 12.5 
\ft bank: Heb. lip\f*

And \add one\add* said to the man clothed in linen, which \add was\add*
upon the waters of the river, How long \add shall it be to\add* the
end of these wonders?\f + \fr 12.6  \ft upon…: or, from above\f*

And I heard the man clothed in linen, which \add was\add* upon
the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left
hand unto heaven, and sware by him that liveth for ever that \add it shall
be\add* for a time, times, and an half; and when he shall have accomplished
to scatter the power of the holy people, all these \add things\add*
shall be finished.\f + \fr 12.7  \ft a time…: or, part\f*

And I heard, but I understood not: then said I, O my Lord, what
\add shall be\add* the end of these \add things\add*?

And he said, Go thy way, Daniel: for the words \add are\add*
closed up and sealed till the time of the end.

And from the time \add that\add* the daily \add sacrifice\add*
shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set
up, \add there shall be\add* a thousand two hundred and ninety days.\f + \fr 12.11 
\ft the abomination: Heb. to set up the abomination\f*\f + \fr 12.11 
\ft maketh…: or, astonisheth\f*

Blessed \add is\add* he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand
three hundred and five and thirty days.

But go thou thy way till the end \add be:\add* for thou shalt
rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days.\f + \fr 12.13 
\ft for thou: or, and thou, etc\f*

headers.toc1: Hosea
headers.mt1: Hosea

verses.text:
The word of the \nd LORD\nd* that came unto Hosea, the son
of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, \add and\add* Hezekiah,
kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king
of Israel.

The beginning of the word of the 
d LORD
d* by Hosea. And the

d LORD
d* said to Hosea, Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms
and children of whoredoms: for the land hath committed great whoredom,
\add departing\add* from the 
d LORD
d*.

So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim; which conceived,
and bare him a son.

And the \nd LORD\nd* said unto him, Call his name Jezreel;
for yet a little \add while\add*, and I will avenge the blood of
Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom
of the house of Israel.\f + \fr 1.4  \ft avenge: Heb. visit\f*

And it shall come to pass at that day, that I will break the
bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel.

And she conceived again, and bare a daughter. And \add God\add*
said unto him, Call her name Lo-ruhamah: for I will no more have
mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.\f + \fr 1.6 
\ft Lo-ruhamah: that is, Not having obtained mercy\f*\f + \fr 1.6 
\ft no…: Heb. not add any more to\f*\f + \fr 1.6  \ft but…: or, that I should altogether pardon
them\f*

But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save
them by the \nd LORD\nd* their God, and will not save them by bow,
nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen.

Now when she had weaned Lo-ruhamah, she conceived, and bare
a son.

Then said \add God\add*, Call his name Lo-ammi: for ye \add are\add*
not my people, and I will not be your \add God\add*.\f + \fr 1.9 
\ft Lo-ammi: that is, Not my people\f*

Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the
sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass,
\add that\add* in the place where it was said unto them, Ye \add are\add*
not my people, \add there\add* it shall be said unto them, \add Ye
are\add* the sons of the living God.\f + \fr 1.10  \ft in…: or, instead of
that\f*

Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel
be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come
up out of the land: for great \add shall be\add* the day of Jezreel.

Say ye unto your brethren, Ammi; and to your sisters, Ru-hamah.
\f + \fr 2.1  \ft Ammi: that is, My people\f*\f + \fr 2.1  \ft Ru-hamah: that is, Having obtained
mercy\f*

Plead with your mother, plead: for she \add is\add* not my
wife, neither \add am\add* I her husband: let her therefore put away
her whoredoms out of her sight, and her adulteries from between her
breasts;

Lest I strip her naked, and set her as in the day that she was
born, and make her as a wilderness, and set her like a dry land,
and slay her with thirst.

And I will not have mercy upon her children; for they \add be\add*
the children of whoredoms.

For their mother hath played the harlot: she that conceived
them hath done shamefully: for she said, I will go after my lovers,
that give \add me\add* my bread and my water, my wool and my flax,
mine oil and my drink.\f + \fr 2.5  \ft drink: Heb. drinks\f*

Therefore, behold, I will hedge up thy way with thorns, and
make a wall, that she shall not find her paths.\f + \fr 2.6  \ft make…: Heb. wall a
wall\f*

And she shall follow after her lovers, but she shall not overtake
them; and she shall seek them, but shall not find \add them:\add*
then shall she say, I will go and return to my first husband; for then
\add was it\add* better with me than now.

For she did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil,
and multiplied her silver and gold, \add which\add* they prepared
for Baal.\f + \fr 2.8  \ft wine: Heb. new wine\f*\f + \fr 2.8  \ft which…: or, wherewith they made
Baal\f*

Therefore will I return, and take away my corn in the time
thereof, and my wine in the season thereof, and will recover my wool
and my flax \add given\add* to cover her nakedness.\f + \fr 2.9 
\ft recover: or, take away\f*

And now will I discover her lewdness in the sight of her lovers,
and none shall deliver her out of mine hand.\f + \fr 2.10  \ft lewdness: Heb. folly, or,
villany\f*

I will also cause all her mirth to cease, her feast days,
her new moons, and her sabbaths, and all her solemn feasts.

And I will destroy her vines and her fig trees, whereof she hath
said, These \add are\add* my rewards that my lovers have given me: and I will
make them a forest, and the beasts of the field shall eat them.\f + \fr 2.12 
\ft destroy: Heb. make desolate\f*

And I will visit upon her the days of Baalim, wherein she burned
incense to them, and she decked herself with her earrings and her
jewels, and she went after her lovers, and forgat me, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

Therefore, behold, I will allure her, and bring her into the
wilderness, and speak comfortably unto her.\f + \fr 2.14  \ft comfortably: or, friendly: Heb. to her
heart\f*

And I will give her her vineyards from thence, and the valley
of Achor for a door of hope: and she shall sing there, as in the
days of her youth, and as in the day when she came up out of the
land of Egypt.

And it shall be at that day, saith the \nd LORD\nd*, \add that\add*
thou shalt call me Ishi; and shalt call me no more Baali.\f + \fr 2.16 
\ft Ishi: that is, My husband\f*\f + \fr 2.16  \ft Baali: that is, My
lord\f*

For I will take away the names of Baalim out of her mouth,
and they shall no more be remembered by their name.

And in that day will I make a covenant for them with the beasts
of the field, and with the fowls of heaven, and \add with\add* the creeping
things of the ground: and I will break the bow and the sword and the
battle out of the earth, and will make them to lie down safely.

And I will betroth thee unto me for ever; yea, I will betroth
thee unto me in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness,
and in mercies.

I will even betroth thee unto me in faithfulness: and thou shalt
know the \nd LORD\nd*.

And the earth shall hear the corn, and the wine, and the oil;
and they shall hear Jezreel.

And I will sow her unto me in the earth; and I will have mercy
upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to \add them which
were\add* not my people, Thou \add art\add* my people; and they shall
say, \add Thou art\add* my God.

Then said the \nd LORD\nd* unto me, Go yet, love a woman beloved of
\add her\add* friend, yet an adulteress, according to the love of the
\nd LORD\nd* toward the children of Israel, who look to other gods,
and love flagons of wine.\f + \fr 3.1  \ft of wine: Heb. of grapes\f*

So I bought her to me for fifteen \add pieces\add* of silver, and
\add for\add* an homer of barley, and an half homer of barley:\f + \fr 3.2 
\ft half…: Heb. lethech\f*

And I said unto her, Thou shalt abide for me many days; thou shalt not play the
harlot, and thou shalt not be for \add another\add* man: so \add will\add* I also
\add be\add* for thee.

For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a
king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an
image, and without an ephod, and \add without\add* teraphim:\f + \fr 3.4 
\ft image: Heb. a standing, or, statue, or, pillar\f*

Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the

d LORD
d* their God, and David their king; and shall fear the

d LORD
d* and his goodness in the latter days.

Hear the word of the \nd LORD\nd*, ye children of Israel: for the
\nd LORD\nd* hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because
\add there is\add* no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the
land.

By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing
adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.\f + \fr 4.2 
\ft blood: Heb. bloods\f*

Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth
therein shall languish, with the beasts of the field, and with the
fowls of heaven; yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be taken away.

Yet let no man strive, nor reprove another: for thy people
\add are\add* as they that strive with the priest.

Therefore shalt thou fall in the day, and the prophet also shall
fall with thee in the night, and I will destroy thy mother.\f + \fr 4.5 
\ft destroy: Heb. cut off\f*

My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast
rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no
priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also
forget thy children.\f + \fr 4.6  \ft destroyed: Heb. cut off\f*

As they were increased, so they sinned against me: \add therefore\add*
will I change their glory into shame.

They eat up the sin of my people, and they set their heart
on their iniquity.\f + \fr 4.8  \ft set…: Heb. lift up their soul
to\f*

And there shall be, like people, like priest: and I will punish
them for their ways, and reward them their doings.\f + \fr 4.9  \ft punish: Heb. visit
upon\f*\f + \fr 4.9  \ft reward: Heb. cause to return\f*

Who \add is\add* wise, and he shall understand these \add things\add*?
prudent, and he shall know them? for the ways of the \nd LORD\nd*
\add are\add* right, and the just shall walk in them: but the transgressors
shall fall therein.

headers.toc1: Joel
headers.mt1: Joel

verses.text: The word of the \nd LORD\nd* that came to Joel the son of Pethuel.

Hear this, ye old men, and give ear, all ye inhabitants of the
land. Hath this been in your days, or even in the days of your fathers?

Tell ye your children of it, and \add let\add* your children
\add tell\add* their children, and their children another generation.

That which the palmerworm hath left hath the locust eaten;
and that which the locust hath left hath the cankerworm eaten; and that which the
cankerworm hath left hath the caterpiller eaten.\f + \fr 1.4  \ft That which the palmerworm…: Heb. The residue of the
palmerworm\f*

Awake, ye drunkards, and weep; and howl, all ye drinkers of
wine, because of the new wine; for it is cut off from your mouth.

For a nation is come up upon my land, strong, and without number,
whose teeth \add are\add* the teeth of a lion, and he hath the cheek
teeth of a great lion.

He hath laid my vine waste, and barked my fig tree: he hath made it
clean bare, and cast \add it\add* away; the branches thereof are made
white.\f + \fr 1.7  \ft barked…: Heb. laid my fig tree for a barking\f*

Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband
of her youth.

The meat offering and the drink offering is cut off from the
house of the 
d LORD
d*; the priests, the 
d LORD’s
d* ministers,
mourn.

The field is wasted, the land mourneth; for the corn is wasted:
the new wine is dried up, the oil languisheth.

Be ye ashamed, O ye husbandmen; howl, O ye vinedressers, for the
wheat and for the barley; because the harvest of the field is perished.

The vine is dried up, and the fig tree languisheth; the pomegranate
tree, the palm tree also, and the apple tree, \add even\add* all the
trees of the field, are withered: because joy is withered away from the
sons of men.

Gird yourselves, and lament, ye priests: howl, ye ministers
of the altar: come, lie all night in sackcloth, ye ministers of my
God: for the meat offering and the drink offering is withholden from the
house of your God.

Sanctify ye a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders
\add and\add* all the inhabitants of the land \add into\add* the
house of the \nd LORD\nd* your God, and cry unto the \nd LORD\nd*,\f + \fr 1.14 
\ft solemn…: or, day of restraint\f*

Alas for the day! for the day of the \nd LORD\nd* \add is\add*
at hand, and as a destruction from the Almighty shall it come.

Is not the meat cut off before our eyes, \add yea\add*, joy
and gladness from the house of our God?

The seed is rotten under their clods, the garners are laid
desolate, the barns are broken down; for the corn is withered.\f + \fr 1.17 
\ft seed: Heb. grains\f*

How do the beasts groan! the herds of cattle are perplexed,
because they have no pasture; yea, the flocks of sheep are made desolate.

O \nd LORD\nd*, to thee will I cry: for the fire hath devoured
the pastures of the wilderness, and the flame hath burned all the
trees of the field.\f + \fr 1.19  \ft pastures: or, habitations\f*

The beasts of the field cry also unto thee: for the rivers
of waters are dried up, and the fire hath devoured the pastures of the
wilderness.

Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy
mountain: let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: for the day
of the \nd LORD\nd* cometh, for \add it is\add* nigh at hand;\f + \fr 2.1 
\ft trumpet: or, cornet\f*

A day of darkness and of gloominess, a day of clouds and of thick
darkness, as the morning spread upon the mountains: a great people
and a strong; there hath not been ever the like, neither shall be any
more after it, \add even\add* to the years of many generations.\f + \fr 2.2 
\ft of many…: Heb. of generation and generation\f*

A fire devoureth before them; and behind them a flame burneth:
the land \add is\add* as the garden of Eden before them, and behind
them a desolate wilderness; yea, and nothing shall escape them.

The appearance of them \add is\add* as the appearance of horses;
and as horsemen, so shall they run.

Like the noise of chariots on the tops of mountains shall they
leap, like the noise of a flame of fire that devoureth the stubble,
as a strong people set in battle array.

Before their face the people shall be much pained: all faces
shall gather blackness.\f + \fr 2.6  \ft blackness: Heb. pot\f*

They shall run like mighty men; they shall climb the wall like
men of war; and they shall march every one on his ways, and they shall not
break their ranks:

Neither shall one thrust another; they shall walk every one
in his path: and \add when\add* they fall upon the sword, they shall not be
wounded.\f + \fr 2.8  \ft sword: or, dart\f*

They shall run to and fro in the city; they shall run upon the
wall, they shall climb up upon the houses; they shall enter in at the
windows like a thief.

The earth shall quake before them; the heavens shall tremble:
the sun and the moon shall be dark, and the stars shall withdraw
their shining:

And the \nd LORD\nd* shall utter his voice before his army:
for his camp \add is\add* very great: for \add he is\add* strong
that executeth his word: for the day of the \nd LORD\nd* \add is\add*
great and very terrible; and who can abide it?

Therefore also now, saith the \nd LORD\nd*, turn ye \add even\add*
to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with
mourning:

And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the
\nd LORD\nd* your God: for he \add is\add* gracious and merciful,
slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.

Who knoweth \add if\add* he will return and repent, and leave
a blessing behind him; \add even\add* a meat offering and a drink
offering unto the \nd LORD\nd* your God?

Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn
assembly:

Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the
elders, gather the children, and those that suck the breasts: let the
bridegroom go forth of his chamber, and the bride out of her closet.

Let the priests, the ministers of the \nd LORD\nd*, weep between the
porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O \nd LORD\nd*,
and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule
over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where \add is\add*
their God?\f + \fr 2.17  \ft rule over: or, use a byword against\f*

Then will the \nd LORD\nd* be jealous for his land, and pity
his people.

Yea, the \nd LORD\nd* will answer and say unto his people,
Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil, and ye shall be
satisfied therewith: and I will no more make you a reproach among the
heathen:

But I will remove far off from you the northern \add army\add*,
and will drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face
toward the east sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea, and his
stink shall come up, and his ill savour shall come up, because he hath
done great things.\f + \fr 2.20  \ft hath…: Heb. hath magnified to
do\f*

Fear not, O land; be glad and rejoice: for the \nd LORD\nd*
will do great things.\f + \fr 2.21  \ft will…: Heb. hath magnified to
do\f*

Be not afraid, ye beasts of the field: for the pastures of the
wilderness do spring, for the tree beareth  her fruit, the fig tree
and the vine do yield their strength.

Be glad then, ye children of Zion, and rejoice in the \nd LORD\nd*
your God: for he hath given you the former rain moderately, and he will cause to come
down for you the rain, the former rain, and the latter rain in the
first \add month\add*.\f + \fr 2.23  \ft the former rain moderately: or, a teacher of
righteousness\f*\f + \fr 2.23  \ft moderately: Heb. according to
righteousness\f*

And the floors shall be full of wheat, and the fats shall
overflow with wine and oil.

And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten,
the cankerworm, and the caterpiller, and the palmerworm, my great
army which I sent among you.

And ye shall eat in plenty, and be satisfied, and praise the
name of the \nd LORD\nd* your God, that hath dealt wondrously with you: and my
people shall never be ashamed.

And ye shall know that I \add am\add* in the midst of Israel, and
\add that\add* I \add am\add* the \nd LORD\nd* your God, and none else: and my
people shall never be ashamed.

And it shall come to pass afterward, \add that\add* I will pour
out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall
prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see
visions:

And also upon the servants and upon the handmaids in those
days will I pour out my spirit.

And I will shew wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood,
and fire, and pillars of smoke.

The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood,
before the great and the terrible day of the \nd LORD\nd* come.

And it shall come to pass, \add that\add* whosoever shall call
on the name of the 
d LORD
d* shall be delivered: for in mount
Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the 
d LORD
d* hath
said, and in the remnant whom the 
d LORD
d* shall call.

For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring
again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,

I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the
valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and
\add for\add* my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the
nations, and parted my land.

And they have cast lots for my people; and have given a boy
for an harlot, and sold a girl for wine, that they might drink.

Yea, and what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the
coasts of Palestine? will ye render me a recompence? and if ye recompense
me, swiftly \add and\add* speedily will I return your recompence
upon your own head;

Because ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried
into your temples my goodly pleasant things:\f + \fr 3.5  \ft pleasant: Heb.
desirable\f*

The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye
sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their
border.\f + \fr 3.6  \ft the Grecians: Heb. the sons of the Grecians\f*

Behold, I will raise them out of the place whither ye have
sold them, and will return your recompence upon your own head:

And I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand
of the children of Judah, and they shall sell them to the Sabeans,
to a people far off: for the \nd LORD\nd* hath spoken \add it\add*.

Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare  war, wake up
the mighty men, let all the men of war draw near; let them come up:\f + \fr 3.9 
\ft Prepare: Heb. Sanctify\f*

Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruninghooks into
spears: let the weak say, I \add am\add* strong.\f + \fr 3.10  \ft pruninghooks: or,
scythes\f*

Assemble yourselves, and come, all ye heathen, and gather yourselves
together round about: thither cause thy mighty ones to come down,
O \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 3.11  \ft cause…: or, the \+nd LORD\+nd* shall bring
down\f*

Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat:
for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about.

Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe: come, get you
down; for the press is full, the fats overflow; for their wickedness
\add is\add* great.

Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision: for the
day of the \nd LORD\nd* \add is\add* near in the valley of decision.\f + \fr 3.14 
\ft decision: or, concision, or, threshing\f*

The sun and the moon shall be darkened, and the stars shall
withdraw their shining.

The \nd LORD\nd* also shall roar out of Zion, and utter his
voice from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth shall shake:
but the \nd LORD\nd* \add will be\add* the hope of his people, and the
strength of the children of Israel.\f + \fr 3.16  \ft hope: Heb. place of repair, or,
harbour\f*

So shall ye know that I \add am\add* the \nd LORD\nd* your
God dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain: then shall Jerusalem be holy,
and there shall no strangers pass through her any more.\f + \fr 3.17 
\ft holy: Heb. holiness\f*

And it shall come to pass in that day, \add that\add* the
mountains shall drop down new wine, and the hills shall flow with
milk, and all the rivers of Judah shall flow with waters, and a fountain
shall come forth of the house of the \nd LORD\nd*, and shall water
the valley of Shittim.\f + \fr 3.18  \ft flow: Heb. go\f*

Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom shall be a desolate
wilderness, for the violence \add against\add* the children of Judah,
because they have shed innocent blood in their land.

But Judah shall dwell for ever, and Jerusalem from generation
to generation.\f + \fr 3.20  \ft dwell: or, abide\f*

For I will cleanse their blood \add that\add* I have not cleansed:
for the \nd LORD\nd* dwelleth in Zion.\f + \fr 3.21  \ft for the…: or, even I the
\+nd LORD\+nd* that\f*

headers.toc1: Amos
headers.mt1: Amos

verses.text:
The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he
saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the
days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before
the earthquake.

And he said, The \nd LORD\nd* will roar from Zion, and utter
his voice from Jerusalem; and the habitations of the shepherds shall
mourn, and the top of Carmel shall wither.

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd*; For three transgressions of Damascus,
and for four, I will not turn away \add the punishment\add* thereof; because they have
threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron:\f + \fr 1.3 
\ft and…: or, yea, for four\f*\f + \fr 1.3  \ft turn…: or, convert it, or, let it be
quiet\f*

But I will send a fire into the house of Hazael, which shall
devour the palaces of Ben-hadad.

I will break also the bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitant
from the plain of Aven, and him that holdeth the sceptre from the
house of Eden: and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto
Kir, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 1.5  \ft the plain…: or, Bikathaven\f*\f + \fr 1.5 
\ft the house…: or, Beth-eden\f*

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd*; For three transgressions of Gaza,
and for four, I will not turn away \add the punishment\add* thereof; because they carried away
captive the whole captivity, to deliver \add them\add* up to Edom:\f + \fr 1.6 
\ft away captive…: or, them away with an entire\f*

But I will send a fire on the wall of Gaza, which shall devour
the palaces thereof:

And I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod, and him that
holdeth the sceptre from Ashkelon, and I will turn mine hand against
Ekron: and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish, saith the
Lord \nd GOD\nd*.

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd*; For three transgressions of Tyrus,
and for four, I will not turn away \add the punishment\add* thereof; because they delivered
up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly
covenant:\f + \fr 1.9  \ft the brotherly…: Heb. the covenant of brethren\f*

But I will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus, which shall devour
the palaces thereof.

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd*; For three transgressions of
Edom, and for four, I will not turn away \add the punishment\add*
thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast
off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his
wrath for ever:\f + \fr 1.11  \ft did cast…: Heb. corrupted his compassions\f*

But I will send a fire upon Teman, which shall devour the
palaces of Bozrah.

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd*; For three transgressions of the
children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away \add the punishment\add*
thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead,
that they might enlarge their border:\f + \fr 1.13  \ft ripped…: or, divided the
mountains\f*

But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall
devour the palaces thereof, with shouting in the day of battle, with a
tempest in the day of the whirlwind:

And their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes
together, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd*; For three transgressions of Moab,
and for four, I will not turn away \add the punishment\add* thereof; because he
burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime:

But I will send a fire upon Moab, and it shall devour the palaces
of Kerioth: and Moab shall die with tumult, with shouting, \add and\add*
with the sound of the trumpet:

And I will cut off the judge from the midst thereof, and will
slay all the princes thereof with him, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd*; For three transgressions of Judah,
and for four, I will not turn away \add the punishment\add* thereof; because they have
despised the law of the \nd LORD\nd*, and have not kept his commandments,
and their lies caused them to err, after the which their fathers
have walked:

But I will send a fire upon Judah, and it shall devour the
palaces of Jerusalem.

That pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor,
and turn aside the way of the meek: and a man and his father will
go in unto the \add same\add* maid, to profane my holy name:\f + \fr 2.7 
\ft maid: or, young woman\f*

And they lay \add themselves\add* down upon clothes laid to
pledge by every altar, and they drink the wine of the condemned \add in\add*
the house of their god.\f + \fr 2.8  \ft the condemned: or, such as have fined, or,
mulcted\f*

Yet destroyed I the Amorite before them, whose height \add was\add*
like the height of the cedars, and he \add was\add* strong as the
oaks; yet I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots from beneath.

Also I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and led you
forty years through the wilderness, to possess the land of the Amorite.

And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young
men for Nazarites. \add Is it\add* not even thus, O ye children of
Israel? saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

But ye gave the Nazarites wine to drink; and commanded the
prophets, saying, Prophesy not.

Behold, I am pressed under you, as a cart is pressed \add that
is\add* full of sheaves.\f + \fr 2.13  \ft I am…: or, I will press your place, as a cart full of sheaves
presseth\f*

Therefore the flight shall perish from the swift, and the
strong shall not strengthen his force, neither shall the mighty deliver
himself:\f + \fr 2.14  \ft himself: Heb. his soul, or, life\f*

Neither shall he stand that handleth the bow; and \add he that
is\add* swift of foot shall not deliver \add himself:\add* neither shall he that
rideth the horse deliver himself.

And \add he that is\add* courageous among the mighty shall flee
away naked in that day, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 2.16  \ft courageous: Heb. strong of his
heart\f*

Hear this word that the \nd LORD\nd* hath spoken against you, O
children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the
land of Egypt, saying,

You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will
punish you for all your iniquities.\f + \fr 3.2  \ft punish: Heb. visit
upon\f*
Can two walk together, except they be agreed?

Will a lion roar in the forest, when he hath no prey? will a young
lion cry out of his den, if he have taken nothing?\f + \fr 3.4  \ft cry: Heb. give forth his
voice\f*

Can a bird fall in a snare upon the earth, where no gin \add is\add* for him? shall
\add one\add* take up a snare from the earth, and have taken nothing at
all?

Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be
afraid? shall there be evil in a city, and the \nd LORD\nd* hath not
done \add it\add*?\f + \fr 3.6  \ft be afraid: or, run together?\f*\f + \fr 3.6 
\ft the \+nd LORD\+nd*…: or, shall not the \+nd LORD\+nd* do somewhat?\f*

Surely the Lord \nd GOD\nd* will do nothing, but he revealeth
his secret unto his servants the prophets.

The lion hath roared, who will not fear? the Lord \nd GOD\nd*
hath spoken, who can but prophesy?

Publish in the palaces at Ashdod, and in the palaces in the
land of Egypt, and say, Assemble yourselves upon the mountains of
Samaria, and behold the great tumults in the midst thereof, and the
oppressed in the midst thereof.\f + \fr 3.9  \ft oppressed: or, oppressions\f*

For they know not to do right, saith the \nd LORD\nd*, who
store up violence and robbery in their palaces.\f + \fr 3.10  \ft robbery: or,
spoil\f*

Therefore thus saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*; An adversary \add there shall
be\add* even round about the land; and he shall bring down thy strength
from thee, and thy palaces shall be spoiled.

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd*; As the shepherd taketh out of the
mouth of the lion two legs, or a piece of an ear; so shall the children
of Israel be taken out that dwell in Samaria in the corner of a bed,
and in Damascus \add in\add* a couch.\f + \fr 3.12  \ft taketh: Heb.
delivereth\f*\f + \fr 3.12  \ft in Damascus…: or, on the bed’s feet\f*

Hear ye, and testify in the house of Jacob, saith the Lord
\nd GOD\nd*, the God of hosts,

That in the day that I shall visit the transgressions of Israel
upon him I will also visit the altars of Beth-el: and the horns of the
altar shall be cut off, and fall to the ground.\f + \fr 3.14  \ft visit: or, punish Israel
for\f*

And I will smite the winter house with the summer house; and the
houses of ivory shall perish, and the great houses shall have an
end, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

Hear this word, ye kine of Bashan, that \add are\add* in the
mountain of Samaria, which oppress the poor, which crush the needy,
which say to their masters, Bring, and let us drink.

The Lord \nd GOD\nd* hath sworn by his holiness, that, lo, the
days shall come upon you, that he will take you away with hooks,
and your posterity with fishhooks.

And ye shall go out at the breaches, every \add cow at that which
is\add* before her; and ye shall cast \add them\add* into the palace,
saith the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 4.3  \ft cast…: or, cast away the things of the
palace\f*

And offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving with leaven, and proclaim
\add and\add* publish the free offerings: for this liketh you, O ye
children of Israel, saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*.\f + \fr 4.5  \ft offer: Heb. offer by
burning\f*\f + \fr 4.5  \ft this…: Heb. so ye love\f*

And I also have given you cleanness of teeth in all your cities,
and want of bread in all your places: yet have ye not returned unto me,
saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

And also I have withholden the rain from you, when \add there
were\add* yet three months to the harvest: and I caused it to rain
upon one city, and caused it not to rain upon another city: one piece
was rained upon, and the piece whereupon it rained not withered.

So two \add or\add* three cities wandered unto one city, to
drink water; but they were not satisfied: yet have ye not returned
unto me, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

I have smitten you with blasting and mildew: when your gardens
and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees increased,
the palmerworm devoured \add them:\add* yet have ye not returned
unto me, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 4.9  \ft when…: or, the multitude of your gardens, etc. did the
palmerworm\f*

I have sent among you the pestilence after the manner of Egypt:
your young men have I slain with the sword, and have taken away your
horses; and I have made the stink of your camps to come up unto your
nostrils: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 4.10 
\ft after…: or, in the way\f*\f + \fr 4.10  \ft and have…: Heb. with the captivity of your
horses\f*

I have overthrown \add some\add* of you, as God overthrew
Sodom and Gomorrah, and ye were as a firebrand plucked out of the
burning: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

Therefore thus will I do unto thee, O Israel: \add and\add*
because I will do this unto thee, prepare to meet thy God, O Israel.

For, lo, he that formeth the mountains, and createth the wind,
and declareth unto man what \add is\add* his thought, that maketh
the morning darkness, and treadeth upon the high places of the earth,
The \nd LORD\nd*, The God of hosts, \add is\add* his name.\f + \fr 4.13 
\ft wind: or, spirit\f*

Hear ye this word which I take up against you, \add even\add*
a lamentation, O house of Israel.

The virgin of Israel is fallen; she shall no more rise: she is
forsaken upon her land; \add there is\add* none to raise her up.

For thus saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*; The city that went out
\add by\add* a thousand shall leave an hundred, and that which went
forth \add by\add* an hundred shall leave ten, to the house of Israel.

For thus saith the \nd LORD\nd* unto the house of Israel,
Seek ye me, and ye shall live:

But seek not Beth-el, nor enter into Gilgal, and pass not to
Beer-sheba: for Gilgal shall surely go into captivity, and Beth-el
shall come to nought.

Seek the \nd LORD\nd*, and ye shall live; lest he break out
like fire in the house of Joseph, and devour \add it\add*, and \add there
be\add* none to quench \add it\add* in Beth-el.

Ye who turn judgment to wormwood, and leave off righteousness
in the earth,

\add Seek him\add* that maketh the seven stars and Orion, and
turneth the shadow of death into the morning, and maketh the day
dark with night: that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them
out upon the face of the earth: The \nd LORD\nd* \add is\add* his
name:

That strengtheneth the spoiled against the strong, so that the
spoiled shall come against the fortress.\f + \fr 5.9  \ft spoiled: Heb.
spoil\f*

They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that
speaketh uprightly.

Forasmuch therefore as your treading \add is\add* upon the
poor, and ye take from him burdens of wheat: ye have built houses
of hewn stone, but ye shall not dwell in them; ye have planted pleasant
vineyards, but ye shall not drink wine of them.\f + \fr 5.11  \ft pleasant…: Heb. vineyards of
desire\f*

For I know your manifold transgressions and your mighty sins:
they afflict the just, they take a bribe, and they turn aside the
poor in the gate \add from their right\add*.\f + \fr 5.12  \ft a bribe: or, a
ransom\f*

Therefore the prudent shall keep silence in that time; for it
\add is\add* an evil time.

Seek good, and not evil, that ye may live: and so the \nd LORD\nd*,
the God of hosts, shall be with you, as ye have spoken.

Hate the evil, and love the good, and establish judgment in the
gate: it may be that the \nd LORD\nd* God of hosts will be gracious
unto the remnant of Joseph.

Therefore the \nd LORD\nd*, the God of hosts, the Lord, saith
thus; Wailing \add shall be\add* in all streets; and they shall say
in all the highways, Alas! alas! and they shall call the husbandman
to mourning, and such as are skilful of lamentation to wailing.

And in all vineyards \add shall be\add* wailing: for I will
pass through thee, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

Woe unto you that desire the day of the 
d LORD
d*! to what
end \add is\add* it for you? the day of the 
d LORD
d* \add is\add*
darkness, and not light.

As if a man did flee from a lion, and a bear met him; or went
into the house, and leaned his hand on the wall, and a serpent bit him.

\add Shall\add* not the day of the \nd LORD\nd* \add be\add*
darkness, and not light? even very dark, and no brightness in it?

I hate, I despise your feast days, and I will not smell in your solemn
assemblies.\f + \fr 5.21  \ft in…: or, your holy days\f*

Though ye offer me burnt offerings and your meat offerings,
I will not accept \add them:\add* neither will I regard the peace
offerings of your fat beasts.\f + \fr 5.22  \ft peace…: or, thank
offerings\f*

Take thou away from me the noise of thy songs; for I will not
hear the melody of thy viols.

But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a
mighty stream.\f + \fr 5.24  \ft run: Heb. roll\f*

Have ye offered unto me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness
forty years, O house of Israel?

But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun
your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.\f + \fr 5.26 
\ft the tabernacle…: or, Siccuth your king\f*

Therefore will I cause you to go into captivity beyond Damascus,
saith the \nd LORD\nd*, whose name \add is\add* The God of hosts.

Woe to them \add that are\add* at ease in Zion, and trust in the
mountain of Samaria, \add which are\add* named chief of the nations,
to whom the house of Israel came!\f + \fr 6.1  \ft are at…: or, are
secure\f*\f + \fr 6.1  \ft chief: or, firstfruits\f*

Pass ye unto Calneh, and see; and from thence go ye to Hamath
the great: then go down to Gath of the Philistines: \add be they\add*
better than these kingdoms? or their border greater than your border?

Ye that put far away the evil day, and cause the seat of violence
to come near;\f + \fr 6.3  \ft seat: or, habitation\f*

That lie upon beds of ivory, and stretch themselves upon their
couches, and eat the lambs out of the flock, and the calves out of the
midst of the stall;\f + \fr 6.4  \ft stretch…: or, abound with superfluities\f*

That chant to the sound of the viol, \add and\add* invent to themselves
instruments of musick, like David;\f + \fr 6.5  \ft chant: or, quaver\f*

That drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief
ointments: but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph.\f + \fr 6.6 
\ft wine…: or, in bowls of wine\f*\f + \fr 6.6  \ft affliction: Heb.
breach\f*

Therefore now shall they go captive with the first that go
captive, and the banquet of them that stretched themselves shall be
removed.

The Lord \nd GOD\nd* hath sworn by himself, saith the \nd LORD\nd*
the God of hosts, I abhor the excellency of Jacob, and hate his palaces:
therefore will I deliver up the city with all that is therein.\f + \fr 6.8 
\ft that…: Heb. the fulness thereof\f*

And it shall come to pass, if there remain ten men in one house,
that they shall die.

And a man’s uncle shall take him up, and he that burneth him, to bring
out the bones out of the house, and shall say unto him that \add is\add*
by the sides of the house, \add Is there\add* yet \add any\add* with thee? and he shall
say, No. Then shall he say, Hold thy tongue: for we may not make
mention of the name of the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 6.10  \ft we…: or, they will not, or, have
not\f*

For, behold, the \nd LORD\nd* commandeth, and he will smite
the great house with breaches, and the little house with clefts.\f + \fr 6.11 
\ft breaches: or, droppings\f*

Shall horses run upon the rock? will \add one\add* plow \add there\add*
with oxen? for ye have turned judgment into gall, and the fruit of
righteousness into hemlock:

Ye which rejoice in a thing of nought, which say, Have we not
taken to us horns by our own strength?

But, behold, I will raise up against you a nation, O house
of Israel, saith the \nd LORD\nd* the God of hosts; and they shall
afflict you from the entering in of Hemath unto the river of the
wilderness.\f + \fr 6.14  \ft river: or, valley\f*

Thus hath the Lord \nd GOD\nd* shewed unto me; and, behold, he
formed grasshoppers in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter
growth; and, lo, \add it was\add* the latter growth after the king’s
mowings.\f + \fr 7.1  \ft grasshoppers: or, green worms\f*

And it came to pass, \add that\add* when they had made an end
of eating the grass of the land, then I said, O Lord \nd GOD\nd*,
forgive, I beseech thee: by whom shall Jacob arise? for he \add is\add*
small.\f + \fr 7.2  \ft by…: or, who of (or, for,) Jacob shall stand?\f*

The 
d LORD
d* repented for this: It shall not be, saith
the 
d LORD
d*.

Thus hath the Lord 
d GOD
d* shewed unto me: and, behold, the
Lord 
d GOD
d* called to contend by fire, and it devoured the great
deep, and did eat up a part.

Then said I, O Lord \nd GOD\nd*, cease, I beseech thee: by whom shall
Jacob arise? for he \add is\add* small.\f + \fr 7.5  \ft by…: or, who of (or, for,) Jacob shall
stand?\f*

The 
d LORD
d* repented for this: This also shall not be,
saith the Lord 
d GOD
d*.

Thus he shewed me: and, behold, the Lord stood upon a wall
\add made\add* by a plumbline, with a plumbline in his hand.

And the \nd LORD\nd* said unto me, Amos, what seest thou? And I
said, A plumbline. Then said the Lord, Behold, I will set a plumbline
in the midst of my people Israel: I will not again pass by them any more:

And the high places of Isaac shall be desolate, and the sanctuaries
of Israel shall be laid waste; and I will rise against the house
of Jeroboam with the sword.

Then Amaziah the priest of Beth-el sent to Jeroboam king
of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst
of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.

For thus Amos saith, Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and
Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land.

Also Amaziah said unto Amos, O thou seer, go, flee thee away
into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there:

But prophesy not again any more at Beth-el: for it \add is\add*
the king’s chapel, and it \add is\add* the king’s court.\f + \fr 7.13 
\ft chapel: or, sanctuary\f*\f + \fr 7.13  \ft king’s court: Heb. house of the
kingdom\f*

Then answered Amos, and said to Amaziah, I \add was\add*
no prophet, neither \add was\add* I a prophet’s son; but I \add was\add*
an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit:\f + \fr 7.14  \ft sycomore…: or, wild
figs\f*

And the \nd LORD\nd* took me as I followed the flock, and the
\nd LORD\nd* said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.\f + \fr 7.15 
\ft as…: Heb. from behind\f*

Now therefore hear thou the word of the \nd LORD\nd*: Thou
sayest, Prophesy not against Israel, and drop not \add thy word\add*
against the house of Isaac.

Therefore thus saith the \nd LORD\nd*; Thy wife shall be an
harlot in the city, and thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the
sword, and thy land shall be divided by line; and thou shalt die
in a polluted land: and Israel shall surely go into captivity forth of his
land.

Thus hath the Lord \nd GOD\nd* shewed unto me: and behold a
basket of summer fruit.

And he said, Amos, what seest thou? And I said, A basket of summer
fruit. Then said the \nd LORD\nd* unto me, The end is come upon my
people of Israel; I will not again pass by them any more.

And the songs of the temple shall be howlings in that day,
saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*: \add there shall be\add* many dead bodies
in every place; they shall cast \add them\add* forth with silence.\f + \fr 8.3 
\ft shall be howlings: Heb. shall howl\f*\f + \fr 8.3  \ft with…: Heb. be
silent\f*

Hear this, O ye that swallow up the needy, even to make the
poor of the land to fail,

Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn?
and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small,
and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?\f + \fr 8.5 
\ft new…: or, month\f*\f + \fr 8.5  \ft set…: Heb. open\f*\f + \fr 8.5 
\ft falsifying…: Heb. perverting the balances of deceit\f*

That we may buy the poor for silver, and the needy for a pair of
shoes; \add yea\add*, and sell the refuse of the wheat?

The \nd LORD\nd* hath sworn by the excellency of Jacob, Surely I will
never forget any of their works.

Shall not the land tremble for this, and every one mourn that
dwelleth therein? and it shall rise up wholly as a flood; and it shall be cast
out and drowned, as \add by\add* the flood of Egypt.

And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd*,
that I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the
earth in the clear day:

And I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs
into lamentation; and I will bring up sackcloth upon all loins, and
baldness upon every head; and I will make it as the mourning of an
only \add son\add*, and the end thereof as a bitter day.

Behold, the days come, saith the Lord 
d GOD
d*, that I will
send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for
water, but of hearing the words of the 
d LORD
d*:

And they shall wander from sea to sea, and from the north
even to the east, they shall run to and fro to seek the word of the
\nd LORD\nd*, and shall not find \add it\add*.

In that day shall the fair virgins and young men faint for
thirst.

They that swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, Thy god, O
Dan, liveth; and, The manner of Beer-sheba liveth; even they shall
fall, and never rise up again.\f + \fr 8.14  \ft manner: Heb. way\f*

I saw the Lord standing upon the altar: and he said, Smite
the lintel of the door, that the posts may shake: and cut them in the
head, all of them; and I will slay the last of them with the sword:
he that fleeth of them shall not flee away, and he that escapeth
of them shall not be delivered.\f + \fr 9.1  \ft lintel: or, chapiter, or,
knop\f*\f + \fr 9.1  \ft cut…: or, wound them\f*

Though they dig into hell, thence shall mine hand take them; though they climb
up to heaven, thence will I bring them down:

And though they hide themselves in the top of Carmel, I will
search and take them out thence; and though they be hid from my sight
