in the bottom of the sea, thence will I command the serpent, and he shall
bite them:

And though they go into captivity before their enemies, thence will I
command the sword, and it shall slay them: and I will set mine eyes
upon them for evil, and not for good.

And the Lord \nd GOD\nd* of hosts \add is\add* he that toucheth
the land, and it shall melt, and all that dwell therein shall mourn:
and it shall rise up wholly like a flood; and shall be drowned, as
\add by\add* the flood of Egypt.

\add It is\add* he that buildeth his stories in the heaven,
and hath founded his troop in the earth; he that calleth for the
waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth:
The \nd LORD\nd* \add is\add* his name.\f + \fr 9.6  \ft stories: or, spheres: Heb.
ascensions\f*\f + \fr 9.6  \ft troop: or, bundle\f*

\add Are\add* ye not as children of the Ethiopians unto me, O
children of Israel? saith the \nd LORD\nd*. Have not I brought up
Israel out of the land of Egypt? and the Philistines from Caphtor,
and the Syrians from Kir?

Behold, the eyes of the Lord \nd GOD\nd* \add are\add* upon the
sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth;
saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, saith
the \nd LORD\nd*.

For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel
among all nations, like as \add corn\add* is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least
grain fall upon the earth.\f + \fr 9.9  \ft sift: Heb. cause to move\f*\f + \fr 9.9 
\ft grain: Heb. stone\f*

All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which
say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.

In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is
fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his
ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old:\f + \fr 9.11  \ft close: Heb. hedge, or,
wall\f*

That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the
heathen, which are called by my name, saith the \nd LORD\nd* that
doeth this.\f + \fr 9.12  \ft which…: Heb. upon whom my name is called\f*

Behold, the days come, saith the \nd LORD\nd*, that the plowman
shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him that soweth
seed; and the mountains shall drop sweet wine, and all the hills
shall melt.\f + \fr 9.13  \ft soweth: Heb. draweth forth\f*\f + \fr 9.13 
\ft sweet: or, new\f*

And I will bring again the captivity of my people of Israel,
and they shall build the waste cities, and inhabit \add them;\add*
and they shall plant vineyards, and drink the wine thereof; they shall also
make gardens, and eat the fruit of them.

And I will plant them upon their land, and they shall no more be pulled
up out of their land which I have given them, saith the \nd LORD\nd*
thy God.

headers.toc1: Obadiah
headers.mt1: Obadiah

verses.text:
The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord \nd GOD\nd* concerning
Edom; We have heard a rumour from the \nd LORD\nd*, and an ambassador
is sent among the heathen, Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in
battle.

Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art
greatly despised.

The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest
in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation \add is\add* high; that
saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?

Though thou exalt \add thyself\add* as the eagle, and though thou
set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith
the \nd LORD\nd*.

If thieves came to thee, if robbers by night, (how art thou cut
off!) would they not have stolen till they had enough? if the grapegatherers
came to thee, would they not leave \add some\add* grapes?\f + \fr 1.5 
\ft some…: or, gleanings?\f*

How are \add the things\add* of Esau searched out! \add how\add*
are his hidden things sought up!

All the men of thy confederacy have brought thee \add even\add*
to the border: the men that were at peace with thee have deceived thee,
\add and\add* prevailed against thee; \add they that eat\add* thy
bread have laid a wound under thee: \add there is\add* none understanding in
him.\f + \fr 1.7  \ft that were…: Heb. of thy peace\f*\f + \fr 1.7 
\ft they…: Heb. the men of thy bread\f*\f + \fr 1.7  \ft in him: or, of
it\f*

Shall I not in that day, saith the \nd LORD\nd*, even destroy
the wise \add men\add* out of Edom, and understanding out of the
mount of Esau?

And thy mighty \add men\add*, O Teman, shall be dismayed, to the end that every
one of the mount of Esau may be cut off by slaughter.

For \add thy\add* violence against thy brother Jacob shame
shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.

In the day that thou stoodest on the other side, in the day
that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners
entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou \add wast\add*
as one of them.\f + \fr 1.11  \ft captive…: or, his substance\f*

But thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother
in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have
rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction;
neither shouldest thou have spoken proudly in the day of distress.\f + \fr 1.12 
\ft spoken…: Heb. magnified thy mouth\f*

Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people
in the day of their calamity; yea, thou shouldest not have looked
on their affliction in the day of their calamity, nor have laid \add hands\add*
on their substance in the day of their calamity;\f + \fr 1.13  \ft substance: or,
forces\f*

Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut
off those of his that did escape; neither shouldest thou have delivered
up those of his that did remain in the day of distress.\f + \fr 1.14 
\ft delivered up: or, shut up\f*

For the day of the \nd LORD\nd* \add is\add* near upon all the
heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward
shall return upon thine own head.

For as ye have drunk upon my holy mountain, \add so\add* shall all the
heathen drink continually, yea, they shall drink, and they shall swallow
down, and they shall be as though they had not been.\f + \fr 1.16 
\ft swallow…: or, sup up\f*

But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be
holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions.\f + \fr 1.17 
\ft deliverance: or, they that escape\f*\f + \fr 1.17  \ft there…: or, it shall be
holy\f*

And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph
a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle
in them, and devour them; and there shall not be \add any\add* remaining
of the house of Esau; for the \nd LORD\nd* hath spoken \add it\add*.

And \add they of\add* the south shall possess the mount of
Esau; and \add they of\add* the plain the Philistines: and they shall
possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria: and Benjamin
\add shall possess\add* Gilead.

And the captivity of this host of the children of Israel \add shall
possess\add* that of the Canaanites, \add even\add* unto Zarephath;
and the captivity of Jerusalem, which \add is\add* in Sepharad, shall
possess the cities of the south.\f + \fr 1.20  \ft which…: or, shall possess that which is
in\f*

And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount
of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the \nd LORD’s\nd*.

headers.toc1: Jonah
headers.mt1: Jonah

verses.text:
Now the word of the \nd LORD\nd* came unto Jonah the son of
Amittai, saying,\f + \fr 1.1  \ft Jonah: Gr. Jonas\f*

Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their
wickedness is come up before me.

But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the
\nd LORD\nd*, and went down to Joppa; and he found a ship going to
Tarshish: so he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to
go with them unto Tarshish from the presence of the \nd LORD\nd*.

But the \nd LORD\nd* sent out a great wind into the sea, and there was a
mighty tempest in the sea, so that the ship was like to be broken.\f + \fr 1.4 
\ft sent out: Heb. cast forth\f*\f + \fr 1.4  \ft was like…: Heb. thought to be
broken\f*

Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his
god, and cast forth the wares that \add were\add* in the ship into the
sea, to lighten \add it\add* of them. But Jonah was gone down into the
sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.

So the shipmaster came to him, and said unto him, What meanest thou, O
sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we
perish not.

And they said every one to his fellow, Come, and let us cast
lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil \add is\add* upon us. So they
cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.

Then said they unto him, Tell us, we pray thee, for whose cause this
evil \add is\add* upon us; What \add is\add* thine occupation? and
whence comest thou? what \add is\add* thy country? and of what people
\add art\add* thou?

And he said unto them, I \add am\add* an Hebrew; and I fear
the \nd LORD\nd*, the God of heaven, which hath made the sea and the
dry \add land\add*.\f + \fr 1.9  \ft the \+nd LORD\+nd*: or, \+nd JEHOVAH\+nd*\f*

Then were the men exceedingly afraid, and said unto him, Why hast thou
done this? For the men knew that he fled from the presence of the
\nd LORD\nd*, because he had told them.\f + \fr 1.10  \ft exceedingly…: Heb. with great
fear\f*

Then said they unto him, What shall we do unto thee, that the
sea may be calm unto us? for the sea wrought, and was tempestuous.\f + \fr 1.11 
\ft may…: Heb. may be silent from us\f*\f + \fr 1.11  \ft wrought…: or, grew more and more tempestuous: Heb.
went\f*

And he said unto them, Take me up, and cast me forth into the
sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake
this great tempest \add is\add* upon you.

Nevertheless the men rowed hard to bring \add it\add* to the
land; but they could not: for the sea wrought, and was tempestuous against
them.\f + \fr 1.13  \ft rowed: Heb. digged\f*\f + \fr 1.13  \ft wrought…: or, grew more and more tempestuous: Heb.
went\f*

Wherefore they cried unto the 
d LORD
d*, and said, We beseech
thee, O 
d LORD
d*, we beseech thee, let us not perish for this
man’s life, and lay not upon us innocent blood: for thou, O 
d LORD
d*,
hast done as it pleased thee.

So they took up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea: and the
sea ceased from her raging.\f + \fr 1.15  \ft ceased: Heb. stood\f*

Then the men feared the \nd LORD\nd* exceedingly, and offered
a sacrifice unto the \nd LORD\nd*, and made vows.\f + \fr 1.16  \ft offered…: Heb. sacrifice unto the
\+nd LORD\+nd*, and vowed vows\f*

Now the \nd LORD\nd* had prepared a great fish to swallow
up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three
nights.\f + \fr 1.17  \ft belly: Heb. bowels\f*

Then Jonah prayed unto the \nd LORD\nd* his God out of the
fish’s belly,

And said, I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the \nd LORD\nd*,
and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, \add and\add*
thou heardest my voice.\f + \fr 2.2  \ft by…: or, out of mine affliction\f*\f + \fr 2.2 
\ft hell: or, the grave\f*

Then I said, I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again
toward thy holy temple.

The waters compassed me about, \add even\add* to the soul:
the depth closed me round about, the weeds were wrapped about my
head.

I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her
bars \add was\add* about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my
life from corruption, O \nd LORD\nd* my God.\f + \fr 2.6  \ft bottoms: Heb. cuttings
off\f*\f + \fr 2.6  \ft corruption: or, the pit\f*

When my soul fainted within me I remembered the \nd LORD\nd*:
and my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple.
They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy.

And the \nd LORD\nd* spake unto the fish, and it vomited
out Jonah upon the dry \add land\add*.

And the word of the \nd LORD\nd* came unto Jonah the second
time, saying,

Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the
preaching that I bid thee.

So Jonah arose, and went unto Nineveh, according to the word
of the \nd LORD\nd*. Now Nineveh was an exceeding great city of three
days’ journey.\f + \fr 3.3  \ft exceeding: Heb. of God\f*

And Jonah began to enter into the city a day’s journey, and he
cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.

So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast,
and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.

For word came unto the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his
throne, and he laid his robe from him, and covered \add him\add*
with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.

And he caused \add it\add* to be proclaimed and published through
Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither
man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed,
nor drink water:\f + \fr 3.7  \ft published: Heb. said\f*\f + \fr 3.7 
\ft nobles: Heb. great men\f*

But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily
unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the
violence that \add is\add* in their hands.

Who can tell \add if\add* God will turn and repent, and turn
away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?

And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil
way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would
do unto them; and he did \add it\add* not.
But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry.

And he prayed unto the \nd LORD\nd*, and said, I pray thee, O
\nd LORD\nd*, \add was\add* not this my saying, when I was yet in my
country? Therefore I fled before unto Tarshish: for I knew that thou
\add art\add* a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of
great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil.

Therefore now, O \nd LORD\nd*, take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for
\add it is\add* better for me to die than to live.

Then said the \nd LORD\nd*, Doest thou well to be angry?\f + \fr 4.4 
\ft Doest…: or, Art thou greatly angry?\f*

So Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the
city, and there made him a booth, and sat under it in the shadow,
till he might see what would become of the city.

And the \nd LORD\nd* God prepared a gourd, and made \add it\add*
to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shadow over his head, to
deliver him from his grief. So Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd.\f + \fr 4.6 
\ft gourd: or, palmcrist: Heb. Kikajon\f*\f + \fr 4.6  \ft was…: Heb. rejoiced with great
joy\f*

But God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day,
and it smote the gourd that it withered.

And it came to pass, when the sun did arise, that God prepared
a vehement east wind; and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he
fainted, and wished in himself to die, and said, \add It is\add*
better for me to die than to live.\f + \fr 4.8  \ft vehement: or,
silent\f*

And God said to Jonah, Doest thou well to be angry for the
gourd? And he said, I do well to be angry, \add even\add* unto death.\f + \fr 4.9 
\ft Doest…: or, Art thou greatly angry?\f*\f + \fr 4.9  \ft I do well…: or, I am greatly
angry\f*

Then said the \nd LORD\nd*, Thou hast had pity on the gourd,
for the which thou hast not laboured, neither madest it grow; which came up in a
night, and perished in a night:\f + \fr 4.10  \ft had pity: or, spared\f*\f + \fr 4.10 
\ft came…: Heb. was the son of the night\f*

And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are
more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right
hand and their left hand; and \add also\add* much cattle?

headers.toc1: Micah
headers.mt1: Micah

verses.text:
The word of the \nd LORD\nd* that came to Micah the Morasthite
in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, \add and\add* Hezekiah, kings of Judah,
which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.

Hear, all ye people; hearken, O earth, and all that therein
is: and let the Lord \nd GOD\nd* be witness against you, the Lord
from his holy temple.\f + \fr 1.2  \ft all ye…: Heb. ye people, all of
them\f*\f + \fr 1.2  \ft all that…: Heb. the fulness thereof\f*

For, behold, the \nd LORD\nd* cometh forth out of his place,
and will come down, and tread upon the high places of the earth.

And the mountains shall be molten under him, and the valleys
shall be cleft, as wax before the fire, \add and\add* as the waters
\add that are\add* poured down a steep place.\f + \fr 1.4  \ft a steep…: Heb. a
descent\f*

For the transgression of Jacob \add is\add* all this, and for the
sins of the house of Israel. What \add is\add* the transgression
of Jacob? \add is it\add* not Samaria? and what \add are\add* the high
places of Judah? \add are they\add* not Jerusalem?

Therefore I will make Samaria as an heap of the field, \add and\add*
as plantings of a vineyard: and I will pour down the stones thereof into the
valley, and I will discover the foundations thereof.

And all the graven images thereof shall be beaten to pieces,
and all the hires thereof shall be burned with the fire, and all the
idols thereof will I lay desolate: for she gathered \add it\add*
of the hire of an harlot, and they shall return to the hire of an
harlot.

Therefore I will wail and howl, I will go stripped and naked:
I will make a wailing like the dragons, and mourning as the owls.\f + \fr 1.8 
\ft owls: Heb. daughters of the owl\f*

Declare ye \add it\add* not at Gath, weep ye not at all:
in the house of Aphrah roll thyself in the dust.\f + \fr 1.10  \ft Aphrah: that is,
Dust\f*

Pass ye away, thou inhabitant of Saphir, having thy shame
naked: the inhabitant of Zaanan came not forth in the mourning of
Beth-ezel; he shall receive of you his standing.\f + \fr 1.11  \ft thou…: or, thou that dwellest
fairly\f*\f + \fr 1.11  \ft inhabitant: Heb. inhabitress\f*\f + \fr 1.11 
\ft Zaanan: or, The country of flocks\f*\f + \fr 1.11  \ft Beth-ezel: or, A place
near\f*

For the inhabitant of Maroth waited carefully for good: but
evil came down from the \nd LORD\nd* unto the gate of Jerusalem.\f + \fr 1.12 
\ft inhabitant: Heb. inhabitress\f*\f + \fr 1.12  \ft waited…: or, was
grieved\f*

O thou inhabitant of Lachish, bind the chariot to the swift
beast: she \add is\add* the beginning of the sin to the daughter
of Zion: for the transgressions of Israel were found in thee.\f + \fr 1.13 
\ft inhabitant: Heb. inhabitress\f*

Therefore shalt thou give presents to Moresheth-gath: the
houses of Achzib \add shall be\add* a lie to the kings of Israel.\f + \fr 1.14 
\ft to…: or, for Moresheth-gath\f*\f + \fr 1.14  \ft Achzib: that is, A
lie\f*

Yet will I bring an heir unto thee, O inhabitant of Mareshah:
he shall come unto Adullam the glory of Israel.\f + \fr 1.15  \ft inhabitant: Heb.
inhabitress\f*\f + \fr 1.15  \ft he…: or, the glory of Israel shall,
etc\f*

Make thee bald, and poll thee for thy delicate children; enlarge
thy baldness as the eagle; for they are gone into captivity from thee.

Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their
beds! when the morning is light, they practise it, because it is
in the power of their hand.

And they covet fields, and take \add them\add* by violence;
and houses, and take \add them\add* away: so they oppress a man and his
house, even a man and his heritage.\f + \fr 2.2  \ft oppress: or,
defraud\f*

In that day shall \add one\add* take up a parable against you, and
lament with a doleful lamentation, \add and\add* say, We be utterly
spoiled: he hath changed the portion of my people: how hath he removed
\add it\add* from me! turning away he hath divided our fields.\f + \fr 2.4 
\ft a doleful…: Heb. a lamentation of lamentations\f*\f + \fr 2.4 
\ft turning…: or, instead of restoring\f*

Therefore thou shalt have none that shall cast a cord by lot
in the congregation of the \nd LORD\nd*.

Prophesy ye not, \add say they to them that\add* prophesy:
they shall not prophesy to them, \add that\add* they shall not take
shame.\f + \fr 2.6  \ft Prophesy ye…: or, Prophesy not as they prophesy: Heb. Drop,
etc\f*

O \add thou that art\add* named the house of Jacob, is the
spirit of the \nd LORD\nd* straitened? \add are\add* these his doings?
do not my words do good to him that walketh uprightly?\f + \fr 2.7 
\ft straitened: or, shortened?\f*\f + \fr 2.7  \ft uprightly: Heb.
upright?\f*

Even of late my people is risen up as an enemy: ye pull off
the robe with the garment from them that pass by securely as men
averse from war.\f + \fr 2.8  \ft of late: Heb. yesterday\f*\f + \fr 2.8 
\ft with the: Heb. over against a\f*

The women of my people have ye cast out from their pleasant
houses; from their children have ye taken away my glory for ever.\f + \fr 2.9 
\ft women: or, wives\f*

Arise ye, and depart; for this \add is\add* not \add your\add*
rest: because it is polluted, it shall destroy \add you\add*, even with a
sore destruction.

If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, \add saying\add*,
I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the
prophet of this people.\f + \fr 2.11  \ft walking…: or, walk with the wind, and lie
falsely\f*

I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee; I will surely
gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together as the sheep
of Bozrah, as the flock in the midst of their fold: they shall make great
noise by reason of \add the multitude of\add* men.

The breaker is come up before them: they have broken up, and have passed
through the gate, and are gone out by it: and their king shall pass
before them, and the \nd LORD\nd* on the head of them.

And I said, Hear, I pray you, O heads of Jacob, and ye princes
of the house of Israel; \add Is it\add* not for you to know judgment?

Who hate the good, and love the evil; who pluck off their skin
from off them, and their flesh from off their bones;

Who also eat the flesh of my people, and flay their skin from off them; and they
break their bones, and chop them in pieces, as for the pot, and as
flesh within the caldron.

Then shall they cry unto the \nd LORD\nd*, but he will not
hear them: he will even hide his face from them at that time, as they have behaved themselves
ill in their doings.

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd* concerning the prophets that make my
people err, that bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace; and he that
putteth not into their mouths, they even prepare war against him.

Therefore night \add shall be\add* unto you, that ye shall not have a
vision; and it shall be dark unto you, that ye shall not divine;
and the sun shall go down over the prophets, and the day shall be
dark over them.\f + \fr 3.6  \ft that…: vision: Heb. from a vision\f*\f + \fr 3.6 
\ft that…: divine: Heb. from divining\f*

Then shall the seers be ashamed, and the diviners confounded:
yea, they shall all cover their lips; for \add there is\add* no answer
of God.\f + \fr 3.7  \ft lips: Heb. upper lip\f*

But truly I am full of power by the spirit of the \nd LORD\nd*,
and of judgment, and of might, to declare unto Jacob his transgression,
and to Israel his sin.

Hear this, I pray you, ye heads of the house of Jacob, and
princes of the house of Israel, that abhor judgment, and pervert
all equity.

They build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity.\f + \fr 3.10 
\ft blood: Heb. bloods\f*

The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof
teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they
lean upon the \nd LORD\nd*, and say, \add Is\add* not the \nd LORD\nd*
among us? none evil can come upon us.\f + \fr 3.11  \ft and say: Heb.
saying\f*

Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed \add as\add*
a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the
house as the high places of the forest.

But in the last days it shall come to pass, \add that\add*
the mountain of the house of the \nd LORD\nd* shall be established
in the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills;
and people shall flow unto it.

And many nations shall come, and say, Come, and let us go up
to the mountain of the \nd LORD\nd*, and to the house of the God
of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his
paths: for the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the \nd LORD\nd*
from Jerusalem.

And he shall judge among many people, and rebuke strong nations
afar off; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their
spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up a sword against
nation, neither shall they learn war any more.\f + \fr 4.3  \ft pruninghooks: or,
scythes\f*

But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig
tree; and none shall make \add them\add* afraid: for the mouth of the
\nd LORD\nd* of hosts hath spoken \add it\add*.

For all people will walk every one in the name of his god,
and we will walk in the name of the \nd LORD\nd* our God for ever
and ever.

And I will make her that halted a remnant, and her that was cast far
off a strong nation: and the \nd LORD\nd* shall reign over them in
mount Zion from henceforth, even for ever.

And thou, O tower of the flock, the strong hold of the daughter
of Zion, unto thee shall it come, even the first dominion; the kingdom
shall come to the daughter of Jerusalem.

Now why dost thou cry out aloud? \add is there\add* no king
in thee? is thy counsellor perished? for pangs have taken thee as a woman in
travail.

Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion,
like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city,
and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go \add even\add*
to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered; there the \nd LORD\nd*
shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies.

Now also many nations are gathered against thee, that say,
Let her be defiled, and let our eye look upon Zion.

But they know not the thoughts of the \nd LORD\nd*, neither
understand they his counsel: for he shall gather them as the sheaves
into the floor.

Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion: for I will make thine
horn iron, and I will make thy hoofs brass: and thou shalt beat in
pieces many people: and I will consecrate their gain unto the \nd LORD\nd*,
and their substance unto the Lord of the whole earth.

Now gather thyself in troops, O daughter of troops: he hath
laid siege against us: they shall smite the judge of Israel with a
rod upon the cheek.

But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah, \add though\add* thou be little
among the thousands of Judah, \add yet\add* out of thee shall he come
forth unto me \add that is\add* to be ruler in Israel; whose goings
forth \add have been\add* from of old, from everlasting.\f + \fr 5.2 
\ft everlasting: Heb. the days of eternity\f*

Therefore will he give them up, until the time \add that\add*
she which travaileth hath brought forth: then the remnant of his
brethren shall return unto the children of Israel.

And he shall stand and feed in the strength of the \nd LORD\nd*,
in the majesty of the name of the \nd LORD\nd* his God; and they shall
abide: for now shall he be great unto the ends of the earth.\f + \fr 5.4 
\ft feed: or, rule\f*

And this \add man\add* shall be the peace, when the Assyrian
shall come into our land: and when he shall tread in our palaces,
then shall we raise against him seven shepherds, and eight principal
men.\f + \fr 5.5  \ft principal: Heb. princes of\f*

And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the
land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof: thus shall he deliver \add us\add*
from the Assyrian, when he cometh into our land, and when he treadeth
within our borders.\f + \fr 5.6  \ft waste: Heb. eat up\f*\f + \fr 5.6 
\ft in the…: or, with her own naked swords\f*

And the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many people
as a dew from the \nd LORD\nd*, as the showers upon the grass, that
tarrieth not for man, nor waiteth for the sons of men.

And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles in the
midst of many people as a lion among the beasts of the forest, as a young
lion among the flocks of sheep: who, if he go through, both treadeth
down, and teareth in pieces, and none can deliver.\f + \fr 5.8  \ft sheep: or,
goats\f*

Thine hand shall be lifted up upon thine adversaries, and all thine
enemies shall be cut off.

And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the \nd LORD\nd*,
that I will cut off thy horses out of the midst of thee, and I will
destroy thy chariots:

And I will cut off the cities of thy land, and throw down
all thy strong holds:

And I will cut off witchcrafts out of thine hand; and thou shalt have no
\add more\add* soothsayers:

Thy graven images also will I cut off, and thy standing images
out of the midst of thee; and thou shalt no more worship the work
of thine hands.\f + \fr 5.13  \ft standing…: or, statues\f*

And I will pluck up thy groves out of the midst of thee: so will I
destroy thy cities.\f + \fr 5.14  \ft cities: or, enemies\f*

And I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen,
such as they have not heard.

Hear ye now what the \nd LORD\nd* saith; Arise, contend thou before the
mountains, and let the hills hear thy voice.\f + \fr 6.1  \ft before: or,
with\f*

Hear ye, O mountains, the 
d LORD’s
d* controversy, and ye
strong foundations of the earth: for the 
d LORD
d* hath a controversy
with his people, and he will plead with Israel.

O my people, what have I done unto thee? and wherein have I
wearied thee? testify against me.

For I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed
thee out of the house of servants; and I sent before thee Moses,
Aaron, and Miriam.

Wherewith shall I come before the \nd LORD\nd*, \add and\add*
bow myself before the high God? shall I come before him with burnt
offerings, with calves of a year old?\f + \fr 6.6  \ft of a…: Heb. sons of a
year?\f*

Will the \nd LORD\nd* be pleased with thousands of rams, \add or\add*
with ten thousands of rivers of oil? shall I give my firstborn \add for\add*
my transgression, the fruit of my body \add for\add* the sin of my
soul?\f + \fr 6.7  \ft body: Heb. belly\f*

He hath shewed thee, O man, what \add is\add* good; and what doth the
\nd LORD\nd* require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy,
and to walk humbly with thy God?\f + \fr 6.8  \ft walk…: Heb. humble thyself to
walk\f*

The \nd LORD’s\nd* voice crieth unto the city, and \add the man
of\add* wisdom shall see thy name: hear ye the rod, and who hath
appointed it.\f + \fr 6.9  \ft the man…: or, thy name shall see that which
is\f*

Are there yet the treasures of wickedness in the house of the
wicked, and the scant measure \add that is\add* abominable?\f + \fr 6.10 
\ft Are…: or, Is there yet unto every man an house of the, etc\f*\f + \fr 6.10 
\ft scant…: Heb. measure of leanness\f*

Shall I count \add them\add* pure with the wicked balances,
and with the bag of deceitful weights?\f + \fr 6.11  \ft count…: or, be pure with,
etc\f*

For the rich men thereof are full of violence, and the inhabitants
thereof have spoken lies, and their tongue \add is\add* deceitful
in their mouth.

Therefore also will I make \add thee\add* sick in smiting thee, in making
\add thee\add* desolate because of thy sins.

Thou shalt eat, but not be satisfied; and thy casting down
\add shall be\add* in the midst of thee; and thou shalt take hold,
but shalt not deliver; and \add that\add* which thou deliverest will I give
up to the sword.

Thou shalt sow, but thou shalt not reap; thou shalt tread
the olives, but thou shalt not anoint thee with oil; and sweet wine,
but shalt not drink wine.

For the statutes of Omri are kept, and all the works of the
house of Ahab, and ye walk in their counsels; that I should make
thee a desolation, and the inhabitants thereof an hissing: therefore ye shall
bear the reproach of my people.\f + \fr 6.16  \ft For the…: or, For he doth much keep the,
etc\f*\f + \fr 6.16  \ft desolation: or, astonishment\f*

Woe is me! for I am as when they have gathered the summer fruits,
as the grapegleanings of the vintage: \add there is\add* no cluster
to eat: my soul desired the firstripe fruit.\f + \fr 7.1  \ft when…: Heb. the gatherings of
summer\f*

The good \add man\add* is perished out of the earth: and \add there
is\add* none upright among men: they all lie in wait for blood; they
hunt every man his brother with a net.\f + \fr 7.2  \ft good: or, godly, or,
merciful\f*

That they may do evil with both hands earnestly, the prince
asketh, and the judge \add asketh\add* for a reward; and the great
\add man\add*, he uttereth his mischievous desire: so they wrap it
up.\f + \fr 7.3  \ft his…: Heb. the mischief of his soul\f*

The best of them \add is\add* as a brier: the most upright
\add is sharper\add* than a thorn hedge: the day of thy watchmen
\add and\add* thy visitation cometh; now shall be their perplexity.

Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide:
keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom.

Therefore I will look unto the \nd LORD\nd*; I will wait for the
God of my salvation: my God will hear me.

Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall
arise; when I sit in darkness, the \nd LORD\nd* \add shall be\add*
a light unto me.

I will bear the indignation of the \nd LORD\nd*, because I have
sinned against him, until he plead my cause, and execute judgment
for me: he will bring me forth to the light, \add and\add* I shall
behold his righteousness.

Then \add she that is\add* mine enemy shall see \add it\add*,
and shame shall cover her which said unto me, Where is the \nd LORD\nd*
thy God? mine eyes shall behold her: now shall she be trodden down
as the mire of the streets.\f + \fr 7.10  \ft Then…: or, And thou wilt see her that is mine enemy, and cover her with
shame\f*\f + \fr 7.10  \ft shall she…: Heb. she shall be for a treading
down\f*

\add In\add* the day that thy walls are to be built, \add in\add*
that day shall the decree be far removed.

\add In\add* that day \add also\add* he shall come even to thee from
Assyria, and \add from\add* the fortified cities, and from the fortress
even to the river, and from sea to sea, and \add from\add* mountain
to mountain.\f + \fr 7.12  \ft and from the fortified cities: or, even to the fortified
cities\f*

Notwithstanding the land shall be desolate because of them that
dwell therein, for the fruit of their doings.\f + \fr 7.13  \ft Notwithstanding: or, After that it hath
been\f*

Feed thy people with thy rod, the flock of thine heritage,
which dwell solitarily \add in\add* the wood, in the midst of Carmel:
let them feed \add in\add* Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old.\f + \fr 7.14 
\ft Feed: or, Rule\f*

According to the days of thy coming out of the land of Egypt
will I shew unto him marvellous \add things\add*.

The nations shall see and be confounded at all their might:
they shall lay \add their\add* hand upon \add their\add* mouth, their
ears shall be deaf.

They shall lick the dust like a serpent, they shall move out of their
holes like worms of the earth: they shall be afraid of the \nd LORD\nd*
our God, and shall fear because of thee.\f + \fr 7.17  \ft worms: or, creeping
things\f*

Who \add is\add* a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity,
and passeth by the transgression of the remnant of his heritage?
he retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth \add in\add*
mercy.

He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us; he will
subdue our iniquities; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the
depths of the sea.

Thou wilt perform the truth to Jacob, \add and\add* the mercy
to Abraham, which thou hast sworn unto our fathers from the days
of old.

headers.toc1: Nahum
headers.mt1: Nahum

verses.text:
The burden of Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the
Elkoshite.

God \add is\add* jealous, and the 
d LORD
d* revengeth; the

d LORD
d* revengeth, and \add is\add* furious; the 
d LORD
d*
will take vengeance on his adversaries, and he reserveth \add wrath\add*
for his enemies.  +  r 1.2   t God…: or, The \+nd LORD\+nd* is a jealous God, and a revenger,
etc *  +  r 1.2   t is furious: Heb. that hath fury *

The \nd LORD\nd* \add is\add* slow to anger, and great in power,
and will not at all acquit \add the wicked:\add* the \nd LORD\nd*
hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds \add are\add*
the dust of his feet.

He rebuketh the sea, and maketh it dry, and drieth up all the
rivers: Bashan languisheth, and Carmel, and the flower of Lebanon
languisheth.

The mountains quake at him, and the hills melt, and the earth
is burned at his presence, yea, the world, and all that dwell therein.

Who can stand before his indignation? and who can abide in the
fierceness of his anger? his fury is poured out like fire, and the
rocks are thrown down by him.\f + \fr 1.6  \ft abide: Heb. stand
up\f*

The \nd LORD\nd* \add is\add* good, a strong hold in the day
of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.\f + \fr 1.7  \ft strong hold: or,
strength\f*

But with an overrunning flood he will make an utter end of the
place thereof, and darkness shall pursue his enemies.

What do ye imagine against the \nd LORD\nd*? he will make an utter
end: affliction shall not rise up the second time.

For while \add they be\add* folden together \add as\add* thorns,
and while they are drunken \add as\add* drunkards, they shall be
devoured as stubble fully dry.

There is \add one\add* come out of thee, that imagineth evil
against the \nd LORD\nd*, a wicked counsellor.\f + \fr 1.11  \ft a wicked…: Heb. a counsellor of
Belial\f*

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd*; Though \add they be\add* quiet,
and likewise many, yet thus shall they be cut down, when he shall pass
through. Though I have afflicted thee, I will afflict thee no more.\f + \fr 1.12 
\ft Though…: or, If they would have been at peace, so should they have been many, and so should they have been shorn, and he
should have passed away\f*\f + \fr 1.12  \ft cut down: Heb. shorn\f*

For now will I break his yoke from off thee, and will burst
thy bonds in sunder.

And the \nd LORD\nd* hath given a commandment concerning thee,
\add that\add* no more of thy name be sown: out of the house of thy
gods will I cut off the graven image and the molten image: I will
make thy grave; for thou art vile.

Behold upon the mountains the feet of him that bringeth good
tidings, that publisheth peace! O Judah, keep thy solemn feasts,
perform thy vows: for the wicked shall no more pass through thee; he is utterly cut
off.\f + \fr 1.15  \ft keep…: Heb. feast\f*\f + \fr 1.15  \ft the wicked: Heb.
Belial\f*

He that dasheth in pieces is come up before thy face: keep
the munition, watch the way, make \add thy\add* loins strong, fortify
\add thy\add* power mightily.\f + \fr 2.1  \ft He…: or, The disperser, or,
hammer\f*

For the \nd LORD\nd* hath turned away the excellency of Jacob,
as the excellency of Israel: for the emptiers have emptied them out,
and marred their vine branches.\f + \fr 2.2  \ft the excellency of Jacob…: or, the pride of Jacob as the pride,
etc\f*

The shield of his mighty men is made red, the valiant men \add are\add*
in scarlet: the chariots \add shall be\add* with flaming torches
in the day of his preparation, and the fir trees shall be terribly
shaken.\f + \fr 2.3  \ft in scarlet: or, dyed scarlet\f*\f + \fr 2.3 
\ft flaming: or, fiery\f*

The chariots shall rage in the streets, they shall justle one against
another in the broad ways: they shall seem like torches, they shall
run like the lightnings.\f + \fr 2.4  \ft they: Heb. their show\f*

He shall recount his worthies: they shall stumble in their
walk; they shall make haste to the wall thereof, and the defence
shall be prepared.\f + \fr 2.5  \ft worthies: or, gallants\f*\f + \fr 2.5 
\ft defence: Heb. covering, or, coverer\f*

The gates of the rivers shall be opened, and the palace shall be
dissolved.\f + \fr 2.6  \ft dissolved: or, molten\f*

And Huzzab shall be led away captive, she shall be brought
up, and her maids shall lead \add her\add* as with the voice of doves,
tabering upon their breasts.\f + \fr 2.7  \ft Huzzab: or, that which was established, or, there was a stand
made\f*\f + \fr 2.7  \ft led…: or, discovered\f*

But Nineveh \add is\add* of old like a pool of water: yet they shall flee
away. Stand, stand, \add shall they cry;\add* but none shall look
back.\f + \fr 2.8  \ft of old: or, from the days that she hath been\f*\f + \fr 2.8 
\ft look back: or, cause them to turn\f*

Take ye the spoil of silver, take the spoil of gold: for \add there
is\add* none end of the store \add and\add* glory out of all the
pleasant furniture.\f + \fr 2.9  \ft for…: or, and their infinite store,
etc\f*\f + \fr 2.9  \ft pleasant…: Heb. vessels of desire\f*

She is empty, and void, and waste: and the heart melteth,
and the knees smite together, and much pain \add is\add* in all loins,
and the faces of them all gather blackness.

Where \add is\add* the dwelling of the lions, and the feedingplace
of the young lions, where the lion, \add even\add* the old lion,
walked, \add and\add* the lion’s whelp, and none made \add them\add*
afraid?

The lion did tear in pieces enough for his whelps, and strangled
for his lionesses, and filled his holes with prey, and his dens with
ravin.

Behold, I \add am\add* against thee, saith the \nd LORD\nd*
of hosts, and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword
shall devour thy young lions: and I will cut off thy prey from the
earth, and the voice of thy messengers shall no more be heard.

Woe to the bloody city! it \add is\add* all full of lies \add and\add*
robbery; the prey departeth not;\f + \fr 3.1  \ft bloody…: Heb. city of
bloods\f*

The noise of a whip, and the noise of the rattling of the wheels,
and of the pransing horses, and of the jumping chariots.

The horseman lifteth up both the bright sword and the glittering
spear: and \add there is\add* a multitude of slain, and a great number of
carcases; and \add there is\add* none end of \add their\add* corpses;
they stumble upon their corpses:\f + \fr 3.3  \ft the bright…: Heb. the flame of the sword, and the lightning of the
spear\f*

Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured
harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her
whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts.

Behold, I \add am\add* against thee, saith the \nd LORD\nd*
of hosts; and I will discover thy skirts upon thy face, and I will
shew the nations thy nakedness, and the kingdoms thy shame.

And I will cast abominable filth upon thee, and make thee vile,
and will set thee as a gazingstock.

And it shall come to pass, \add that\add* all they that look
upon thee shall flee from thee, and say, Nineveh is laid waste: who will
bemoan her? whence shall I seek comforters for thee?

Art thou better than populous No, that was situate among the
rivers, \add that had\add* the waters round about it, whose rampart
\add was\add* the sea, \add and\add* her wall \add was\add* from the
sea?\f + \fr 3.8  \ft populous…: or, nourishing, etc: Heb. No Amon\f*

Ethiopia and Egypt \add were\add* her strength, and \add it
was\add* infinite; Put and Lubim were thy helpers.\f + \fr 3.9  \ft thy helpers: Heb. in thy
help\f*

Yet \add was\add* she carried away, she went into captivity:
her young children also were dashed in pieces at the top of all the
streets: and they cast lots for her honourable men, and all her great
men were bound in chains.

Thou also shalt be drunken: thou shalt be hid, thou also shalt
seek strength because of the enemy.

All thy strong holds \add shall be like\add* fig trees with the firstripe
figs: if they be shaken, they shall even fall into the mouth of the
eater.

Behold, thy people in the midst of thee \add are\add* women:
the gates of thy land shall be set wide open unto thine enemies:
the fire shall devour thy bars.

Draw thee waters for the siege, fortify thy strong holds:
go into clay, and tread the morter, make strong the brickkiln.

There shall the fire devour thee; the sword shall cut thee
off, it shall eat thee up like the cankerworm: make thyself many
as the cankerworm, make thyself many as the locusts.

Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven:
the cankerworm spoileth, and flieth away.\f + \fr 3.16  \ft spoileth: or, spreadeth
himself\f*

Thy crowned \add are\add* as the locusts, and thy captains
as the great grasshoppers, which camp in the hedges in the cold day,
\add but\add* when the sun ariseth they flee away, and their place
is not known where they \add are\add*.

Thy shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria: thy nobles shall
dwell \add in the dust:\add* thy people is scattered upon the mountains,
and no man gathereth \add them\add*.\f + \fr 3.18  \ft nobles: or, valiant
ones\f*

\add There is\add* no healing of thy bruise; thy wound is
grievous: all that hear the bruit of thee shall clap the hands over thee: for upon whom hath not thy
wickedness passed continually?\f + \fr 3.19  \ft healing: Heb. wrinkling\f*

headers.toc1: Habakkuk
headers.mt1: Habakkuk

verses.text: The burden which Habakkuk the prophet did see.

O \nd LORD\nd*, how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear!
\add even\add* cry out unto thee \add of\add* violence, and thou wilt not
save!

Why dost thou shew me iniquity, and cause \add me\add* to behold
grievance? for spoiling and violence \add are\add* before me: and there are
\add that\add* raise up strife and contention.

Therefore the law is slacked, and judgment doth never go forth:
for the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore wrong
judgment proceedeth.\f + \fr 1.4  \ft wrong: or, wrested\f*

Behold ye among the heathen, and regard, and wonder marvellously: for
\add I\add* will work a work in your days, \add which\add* ye will not
believe, though it be told \add you\add*.

For, lo, I raise up the Chaldeans, \add that\add* bitter and
hasty nation, which shall march through the breadth of the land,
to possess the dwellingplaces \add that are\add* not theirs.\f + \fr 1.6 
\ft breadth: Heb. breadths\f*

They \add are\add* terrible and dreadful: their judgment and their
dignity shall proceed of themselves.\f + \fr 1.7  \ft their judgment…: or, from them shall proceed the judgment of these, and
the captivity of these\f*

Their horses also are swifter than the leopards, and are more
fierce than the evening wolves: and their horsemen shall spread themselves, and their
horsemen shall come from far; they shall fly as the eagle \add that\add*
hasteth to eat.\f + \fr 1.8  \ft fierce: Heb. sharp\f*

They shall come all for violence: their faces shall sup up
\add as\add* the east wind, and they shall gather the captivity as the
sand.\f + \fr 1.9  \ft their…: or, the supping up of their faces, etc: or, their faces shall look (Heb. the opposition of their
faces) toward the east\f*

And they shall scoff at the kings, and the princes shall be a
scorn unto them: they shall deride every strong hold; for they shall
heap dust, and take it.

Then shall \add his\add* mind change, and he shall pass over,
and offend, \add imputing\add* this his power unto his god.

\add Art\add* thou not from everlasting, O \nd LORD\nd* my
God, mine Holy One? we shall not die. O \nd LORD\nd*, thou hast ordained
them for judgment; and, O mighty God, thou hast established them for
correction.\f + \fr 1.12  \ft mighty…: Heb. rock\f*\f + \fr 1.12 
\ft established: Heb. founded\f*

\add Thou art\add* of purer eyes than to behold evil, and
canst not look on iniquity: wherefore lookest thou upon them that deal
treacherously, \add and\add* holdest thy tongue when the wicked devoureth
\add the man that is\add* more righteous than he?\f + \fr 1.13  \ft iniquity: or,
grievance\f*

And makest men as the fishes of the sea, as the creeping things,
\add that have\add* no ruler over them?\f + \fr 1.14  \ft creeping: or,
moving\f*

They take up all of them with the angle, they catch them in their
net, and gather them in their drag: therefore they rejoice and are
glad.\f + \fr 1.15  \ft drag: or, flue net\f*

Therefore they sacrifice unto their net, and burn incense
unto their drag; because by them their portion \add is\add* fat,
and their meat plenteous.\f + \fr 1.16  \ft plenteous: or, dainty: Heb.
fat\f*

Shall they therefore empty their net, and not spare continually
to slay the nations?

I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will
watch to see what he will say unto me, and what I shall answer when I am
reproved.\f + \fr 2.1  \ft tower: Heb. fenced place\f*\f + \fr 2.1 
\ft unto me: or, in me\f*\f + \fr 2.1  \ft when…: or, when I am argued with: Heb. upon my reproof, or,
arguing\f*

And the \nd LORD\nd* answered  me, and said, Write the vision, and make
\add it\add* plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.

For the vision \add is\add* yet for an appointed time, but at the
end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will
surely come, it will not tarry.

Behold, his soul \add which\add* is lifted up is not upright
in him: but the just shall live by his faith.

Yea also, because he transgresseth by wine, \add he is\add*
a proud man, neither keepeth at home, who enlargeth his desire as
hell, and \add is\add* as death, and cannot be satisfied, but gathereth
unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all people:\f + \fr 2.5 
\ft Yea…: or, How much more\f*

Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting
proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increaseth \add that which
is\add* not his! how long? and to him that ladeth himself with thick
clay!\f + \fr 2.6  \ft Woe…: or, Ho, he\f*

Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee, and awake
that shall vex thee, and thou shalt be for booties unto them?

Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the
people shall spoil thee; because of men’s blood, and \add for\add*
the violence of the land, of the city, and of all that dwell therein.\f + \fr 2.8 
\ft blood: Heb. bloods\f*

Woe to him that coveteth an evil covetousness to his house,
that he may set his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the
power of evil!\f + \fr 2.9  \ft coveteth…: or, gaineth and evil gain\f*\f + \fr 2.9 
\ft power…: Heb. palm of the hand\f*

Thou hast consulted shame to thy house by cutting off many
people, and hast sinned \add against\add* thy soul.

For the stone shall cry out of the wall, and the beam out
of the timber shall answer it.\f + \fr 2.11  \ft beam: or, piece, or,
fastening\f*\f + \fr 2.11  \ft answer it: or, witness against it\f*

Woe to him that buildeth a town with blood, and stablisheth
a city by iniquity!\f + \fr 2.12  \ft blood: Heb. bloods\f*

Behold, \add is it\add* not of the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts that the
people shall labour in the very fire, and the people shall weary
themselves for very vanity?\f + \fr 2.13  \ft for…: or, in vain?\f*

For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory
of the \nd LORD\nd*, as the waters cover the sea.\f + \fr 2.14  \ft with…: or, by knowing the
glory\f*

Woe unto him that giveth his neighbour drink, that puttest
thy bottle to \add him\add*, and makest \add him\add* drunken also, that thou mayest
look on their nakedness!

Thou art filled with shame for glory: drink thou also, and let thy foreskin be
uncovered: the cup of the \nd LORD’s\nd* right hand shall be turned
unto thee, and shameful spewing \add shall be\add* on thy glory.\f + \fr 2.16 
\ft with…: or, more with shame than with glory\f*

For the violence of Lebanon shall cover thee, and the spoil
of beasts, \add which\add* made them afraid, because of men’s blood,
and for the violence of the land, of the city, and of all that dwell therein.

What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath
graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies, that the maker
of his work trusteth therein, to make dumb idols?\f + \fr 2.18  \ft maker of…: Heb. fashioner of his
fashion\f*

Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone,
Arise, it shall teach! Behold, it \add is\add* laid over with gold
and silver, and \add there is\add* no breath at all in the midst of it.

But the \nd LORD\nd* \add is\add* in his holy temple: let all the
earth keep silence before him.\f + \fr 2.20  \ft let…: Heb. be silent all the earth before
him\f*

A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet upon Shigionoth.\f + \fr 3.1 
\ft upon…: or, according to variable songs, or, tunes, called in Hebrew,
Shigionoth\f*

O \nd LORD\nd*, I have heard thy speech, \add and\add* was
afraid: O \nd LORD\nd*, revive thy work in the midst of the years,
in the midst of the years make known; in wrath remember mercy.\f + \fr 3.2 
\ft speech: Heb. report, or, hearing\f*\f + \fr 3.2  \ft revive: or, preserve
alive\f*

God came from Teman, and the Holy One from mount Paran. Selah.
His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise.\f + \fr 3.3 
\ft Teman: or, the south\f*

And \add his\add* brightness was as the light; he had horns
\add coming\add* out of his hand: and there \add was\add* the hiding
of his power.\f + \fr 3.4  \ft horns…: or, bright beams out of his
side\f*

Before him went the pestilence, and burning coals went forth
at his feet.\f + \fr 3.5  \ft coals: or, diseases\f*

He stood, and measured the earth: he beheld, and drove asunder
the nations; and the everlasting mountains were scattered, the perpetual
hills did bow: his ways \add are\add* everlasting.

I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction: \add and\add* the
curtains of the land of Midian did tremble.\f + \fr 3.7  \ft Cushan: or,
Ethiopia\f*\f + \fr 3.7  \ft in…: or, under affliction, or, vanity\f*

Was the \nd LORD\nd* displeased  against the rivers? \add was\add*
thine anger against the rivers? \add was\add* thy wrath against the
sea, that thou didst ride upon thine horses \add and\add* thy chariots
of salvation?\f + \fr 3.8  \ft of…: or, were salvation?\f*

Thy bow was made quite naked, \add according\add* to the oaths
of the tribes, \add even thy\add* word. Selah. Thou didst cleave
the earth with rivers.\f + \fr 3.9  \ft earth…: or, rivers of the
earth\f*

The mountains saw thee, \add and\add* they trembled: the overflowing
of the water passed by: the deep uttered his voice, \add and\add*
lifted up his hands on high.

The sun \add and\add* moon stood still in their habitation:
at the light of thine arrows they went, \add and\add* at the shining
of thy glittering spear.\f + \fr 3.11  \ft at the light…: or, thine arrows walked in the
light\f*

Thou didst march through the land in indignation, thou didst
thresh the heathen in anger.

Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, \add even\add*
for salvation with thine anointed; thou woundedst the head out of the
house of the wicked, by discovering the foundation unto the neck.
Selah.\f + \fr 3.13  \ft by…: Heb. making naked\f*

Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his
villages: they came out as a whirlwind to scatter me: their rejoicing
\add was\add* as to devour the poor secretly.\f + \fr 3.14  \ft came…: Heb. were
tempestuous\f*

Thou didst walk through the sea with thine horses, \add through\add*
the heap of great waters.\f + \fr 3.15  \ft heap: or, mud\f*

When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice:
rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself, that I might
rest in the day of trouble: when he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his
troops.\f + \fr 3.16  \ft invade…: or, cut them in pieces\f*

Although the fig tree shall not blossom, neither \add shall\add*
fruit \add be\add* in the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail,
and the fields shall yield no meat; the flock shall be cut off from the
fold, and \add there shall be\add* no herd in the stalls:\f + \fr 3.17 
\ft fail: Heb. lie\f*

Yet I will rejoice in the \nd LORD\nd*, I will joy in the
God of my salvation.

The \nd LORD\nd* God \add is\add* my strength, and he will
make my feet like hinds’ \add feet\add*, and he will make me to walk
upon mine high places. To the chief singer on my stringed instruments.\f + \fr 3.19 
\ft chief…: or, overseer\f*\f + \fr 3.19  \ft stringed…: Heb. Neginoth\f*

headers.toc1: Zephaniah
headers.mt1: Zephaniah

verses.text:
The word of the \nd LORD\nd* which came unto Zephaniah the
son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of
Hizkiah, in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah.

I will utterly consume all \add things\add* from off the land,
saith the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 1.2  \ft I will…: Heb. By taking away I will make an
end\f*\f + \fr 1.2  \ft the land: Heb. the face of the land\f*

I will consume man and beast; I will consume the fowls of the
heaven, and the fishes of the sea, and the stumblingblocks with the
wicked; and I will cut off man from off the land, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.\f + \fr 1.3 
\ft stumblingblocks: or, idols\f*

I will also stretch out mine hand upon Judah, and upon all the
inhabitants of Jerusalem; and I will cut off the remnant of Baal
from this place, \add and\add* the name of the Chemarims with the
priests;

And them that are turned back from the 
d LORD
d*; and \add those\add*
that have not sought the 
d LORD
d*, nor enquired for him.

Hold thy peace at the presence of the Lord 
d GOD
d*: for the
day of the 
d LORD
d* \add is\add* at hand: for the 
d LORD
d*
hath prepared a sacrifice, he hath bid his guests.  +  r 1.7   t bid: Heb. sanctified, or,
prepared *

And it shall come to pass in the day of the \nd LORD’s\nd*
sacrifice, that I will punish the princes, and the king’s children,
and all such as are clothed with strange apparel.\f + \fr 1.8  \ft punish: Heb. visit
upon\f*

In the same day also will I punish all those that leap on the
threshold, which fill their masters’ houses with violence and deceit.

And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the \nd LORD\nd*,
\add that there shall be\add* the noise of a cry from the fish gate,
and an howling from the second, and a great crashing from the hills.

Howl, ye inhabitants of Maktesh, for all the merchant people
are cut down; all they that bear silver are cut off.

And it shall come to pass at that time, \add that\add* I will
search Jerusalem with candles, and punish the men that are settled
on their lees: that say in their heart, The \nd LORD\nd* will not do
good, neither will he do evil.\f + \fr 1.12  \ft settled: Heb. curded, or,
thickened\f*

Therefore their goods shall become a booty, and their houses
a desolation: they shall also build houses, but not inhabit \add them;\add*
and they shall plant vineyards, but not drink the wine thereof.

The great day of the 
d LORD
d* \add is\add* near, \add it
is\add* near, and hasteth greatly, \add even\add* the voice of the
day of the 
d LORD
d*: the mighty man shall cry there bitterly.

That day \add is\add* a day of wrath, a day of trouble and
distress, a day of wasteness and desolation, a day of darkness and
gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness,

A day of the trumpet and alarm against the fenced cities,
and against the high towers.

And I will bring distress upon men, that they shall walk like blind
men, because they have sinned against the \nd LORD\nd*: and their
blood shall be poured out as dust, and their flesh as the dung.

Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver
them in the day of the \nd LORD’s\nd* wrath; but the whole land shall be
devoured by the fire of his jealousy: for he shall make even a speedy
riddance of all them that dwell in the land.

Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation
not desired;\f + \fr 2.1  \ft not…: or, not desirous\f*

Before the decree bring forth, \add before\add* the day pass
as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the 
d LORD
d* come upon you, before the
day of the 
d LORD’s
d* anger come upon you.

Seek ye the \nd LORD\nd*, all ye meek of the earth, which have
wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be
ye shall be hid in the day of the \nd LORD’s\nd* anger.

For Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation: they shall drive
out Ashdod at the noon day, and Ekron shall be rooted up.

Woe unto the inhabitants of the sea coast, the nation of the
Cherethites! the word of the \nd LORD\nd* \add is\add* against you; O
Canaan, the land of the Philistines, I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no
inhabitant.

And the sea coast shall be dwellings \add and\add* cottages
for shepherds, and folds for flocks.

And the coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah;
they shall feed thereupon: in the houses of Ashkelon shall they lie
down in the evening: for the \nd LORD\nd* their God shall visit them, and turn
away their captivity.\f + \fr 2.7  \ft for the \+nd LORD\+nd*: or, when,
etc\f*

I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the
children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people, and magnified
\add themselves\add* against their border.

Therefore \add as\add* I live, saith the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts,
the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children
of Ammon as Gomorrah, \add even\add* the breeding of nettles, and
saltpits, and a perpetual desolation: the residue of my people shall
spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them.

This shall they have for their pride, because they have reproached
and magnified \add themselves\add* against the people of the \nd LORD\nd*
of hosts.

The \nd LORD\nd* \add will be\add* terrible unto them: for he will
famish all the gods of the earth; and \add men\add* shall worship
him, every one from his place, \add even\add* all the isles of the
heathen.\f + \fr 2.11  \ft famish: Heb. make lean\f*
Ye Ethiopians also, ye \add shall be\add* slain by my sword.

And he will stretch out his hand against the north, and destroy
Assyria; and will make Nineveh a desolation, \add and\add* dry like a
wilderness.

And flocks shall lie down in the midst of her, all the beasts
of the nations: both the cormorant and the bittern shall lodge in the upper
lintels of it; \add their\add* voice shall sing in the windows; desolation
\add shall be\add* in the thresholds: for he shall uncover the cedar
work.\f + \fr 2.14  \ft cormorant: or, pelican\f*\f + \fr 2.14  \ft upper…: or, knops, or,
chapiters\f*\f + \fr 2.14  \ft for…: or, when he hath uncovered\f*

This \add is\add* the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly,
that said in her heart, I \add am\add*, and \add there is\add* none
beside me: how is she become a desolation, a place for beasts to lie down
in! every one that passeth by her shall hiss, \add and\add* wag his
hand.

Woe to her that is filthy and polluted, to the oppressing city!\f + \fr 3.1 
\ft her…: or, gluttonous: Heb. craw\f*

She obeyed not the voice; she received not correction; she
trusted not in the \nd LORD\nd*; she drew not near to her God.\f + \fr 3.2 
\ft correction: or, instruction\f*

Her princes within her \add are\add* roaring lions; her judges
\add are\add* evening wolves; they gnaw not the bones till the morrow.

Her prophets \add are\add* light \add and\add* treacherous
persons: her priests have polluted the sanctuary, they have done
violence to the law.

The just \nd LORD\nd* \add is\add* in the midst thereof; he will not
do iniquity: every morning doth he bring his judgment to light, he
faileth not; but the unjust knoweth no shame.\f + \fr 3.5  \ft every…: Heb. morning by
morning\f*

I have cut off the nations: their towers are desolate; I made their
streets waste, that none passeth by: their cities are destroyed,
so that there is no man, that there is none inhabitant.\f + \fr 3.6 
\ft towers: or, corners\f*

Therefore wait ye upon me, saith the \nd LORD\nd*, until the
day that I rise up to the prey: for my determination \add is\add*
to gather the nations, that I may assemble the kingdoms, to pour
upon them mine indignation, \add even\add* all my fierce anger: for all the
earth shall be devoured with the fire of my jealousy.

For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all
call upon the name of the \nd LORD\nd*, to serve him with one consent.\f + \fr 3.9 
\ft language: Heb. lip\f*\f + \fr 3.9  \ft consent: Heb. shoulder\f*

From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia my suppliants, \add even\add*
the daughter of my dispersed, shall bring mine offering.

In that day shalt thou not be ashamed for all thy doings,
wherein thou hast transgressed against me: for then I will take away
out of the midst of thee them that rejoice in thy pride, and thou shalt no
more be haughty because of my holy mountain.\f + \fr 3.11  \ft because…: Heb. in my
holy\f*

I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor
people, and they shall trust in the name of the \nd LORD\nd*.

Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel; be glad and rejoice
with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem.

The 
d LORD
d* hath taken away thy judgments, he hath cast
out thine enemy: the king of Israel, \add even\add* the 
d LORD
d*,
\add is\add* in the midst of thee: thou shalt not see evil any more.

In that day it shall be said to Jerusalem, Fear thou not:
\add and to\add* Zion, Let not thine hands be slack.\f + \fr 3.16 
\ft slack: or, faint\f*

The \nd LORD\nd* thy God in the midst of thee \add is\add*
mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will
rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.\f + \fr 3.17 
\ft rest: Heb. be silent\f*

I will gather \add them that are\add* sorrowful for the solemn
assembly, \add who\add* are of thee, \add to whom\add* the reproach of it
\add was\add* a burden.\f + \fr 3.18  \ft reproach…: Heb. the burden upon it was
reproach\f*

Behold, at that time I will undo all that afflict thee: and I will
save her that halteth, and gather her that was driven out; and I will
get them praise and fame in every land where they have been put to
shame.\f + \fr 3.19  \ft get…: Heb. set them for a praise\f*\f + \fr 3.19 
\ft where…: Heb. of their shame\f*

At that time will I bring you \add again\add*, even in the
time that I gather you: for I will make you a name and a praise among all
people of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your
eyes, saith the \nd LORD\nd*.

verses.text:
In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month,
in the first day of the month, came the word of the \nd LORD\nd*
by Haggai the prophet unto Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor
of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, saying,
\f + \fr 1.1  \ft by: Heb. by the hand of\f*\f + \fr 1.1  \ft governor: or,
captain\f*

Thus speaketh the 
d LORD
d* of hosts, saying, This people
say, The time is not come, the time that the 
d LORD’s
d* house
should be built.

Then came the word of the \nd LORD\nd* by Haggai the prophet,
saying,

\add Is it\add* time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled
houses, and this house \add lie\add* waste?

Now therefore thus saith the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts; Consider
your ways.\f + \fr 1.5  \ft Consider…: Heb. Set your heart on your
ways\f*

Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not
enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none
warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages \add to put it\add*
into a bag with holes.\f + \fr 1.6  \ft with holes: Heb. pierced
through\f*

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts; Consider your ways.\f + \fr 1.7 
\ft Consider…: Heb. Set your heart on your ways\f*

Ye looked for much, and, lo, \add it came\add* to little; and when ye
brought \add it\add* home, I did blow upon it. Why? saith the \nd LORD\nd*
of hosts. Because of mine house that \add is\add* waste, and ye run
every man unto his own house.\f + \fr 1.9  \ft blow…: or, blow it
away\f*

Therefore the heaven over you is stayed from dew, and the
earth is stayed \add from\add* her fruit.

And I called for a drought upon the land, and upon the mountains,
and upon the corn, and upon the new wine, and upon the oil, and upon
\add that\add* which the ground bringeth forth, and upon men, and upon
cattle, and upon all the labour of the hands.

Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son
of Josedech, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people,
obeyed the voice of the 
d LORD
d* their God, and the words of
Haggai the prophet, as the 
d LORD
d* their God had sent him, and the
people did fear before the 
d LORD
d*.

Then spake Haggai the 
d LORD’s
d* messenger in the 
d LORD’s
d*
message unto the people, saying, I \add am\add* with you, saith the

d LORD
d*.

And the \nd LORD\nd* stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel the
son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua the
son of Josedech, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant
of the people; and they came and did work in the house of the \nd LORD\nd*
of hosts, their God,

In the four and twentieth day of the sixth month, in the second
year of Darius the king.

In the seventh \add month\add*, in the one and twentieth \add day\add*
of the month, came the word of the \nd LORD\nd* by the prophet Haggai,
saying, \f + \fr 2.1  \ft by: Heb. by the hand of\f*

Speak now to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah,
and to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, and to the residue
of the people, saying,

Who \add is\add* left among you that saw this house in her first
glory? and how do ye see it now? \add is it\add* not in your eyes
in comparison of it as nothing?

Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel, saith the 
d LORD
d*; and be
strong, O Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and be strong,
all ye people of the land, saith the 
d LORD
d*, and work: for I
\add am\add* with you, saith the 
d LORD
d* of hosts:

\add According to\add* the word that I covenanted with you when ye
came out of Egypt, so my spirit remaineth among you: fear ye not.

For thus saith the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts; Yet once, it \add is\add*
a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the
sea, and the dry \add land;\add*

And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations
shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the \nd LORD\nd*
of hosts.

The silver \add is\add* mine, and the gold \add is\add* mine,
saith the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts.

The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the
former, saith the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts: and in this place will I
give peace, saith the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts.

In the four and twentieth \add day\add* of the ninth \add month\add*,
in the second year of Darius, came the word of the \nd LORD\nd* by
Haggai the prophet, saying,

Thus saith the \nd LORD\nd* of hosts; Ask now the priests
\add concerning\add* the law, saying,

If one bear holy flesh in the skirt of his garment, and with his
skirt do touch bread, or pottage, or wine, or oil, or any meat, shall it be
holy? And the priests answered and said, No.

Then said Haggai, If \add one that is\add* unclean by a dead
body touch any of these, shall it be unclean? And the priests answered
and said, It shall be unclean.

Then answered Haggai, and said, So \add is\add* this people, and so
\add is\add* this nation before me, saith the \nd LORD\nd*; and so
\add is\add* every work of their hands; and that which they offer there
\add is\add* unclean.

And now, I pray you, consider from this day and upward, from
before a stone was laid upon a stone in the temple of the \nd LORD\nd*:

Since those \add days\add* were, when \add one\add* came to an
heap of twenty \add measures\add*, there were \add but\add* ten: when
\add one\add* came to the pressfat for to draw out fifty \add vessels\add*
out of the press, there were \add but\add* twenty.

I smote you with blasting and with mildew and with hail in all the
labours of your hands; yet ye \add turned\add* not to me, saith the
\nd LORD\nd*.

Consider now from this day and upward, from the four and twentieth
day of the ninth \add month, even\add* from the day that the foundation
of the \nd LORD’s\nd* temple was laid, consider \add it\add*.

Is the seed yet in the barn? yea, as yet the vine, and the fig
tree, and the pomegranate, and the olive tree, hath not brought forth:
from this day will I bless \add you\add*.

And again the word of the \nd LORD\nd* came unto Haggai in the
four and twentieth \add day\add* of the month, saying,

Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying, I will shake
the heavens and the earth;

And I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms, and I will destroy
the strength of the kingdoms of the heathen; and I will overthrow
the chariots, and those that ride in them; and the horses and their
riders shall come down, every one by the sword of his brother.

In that day, saith the 
d LORD
d* of hosts, will I take
thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the 
d LORD
d*,
and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith the

d LORD
d* of hosts.
